title: Comprehensive identification and expression analysis of Hsp90s gene family in Solanum lycopersicum
text:
Comprehensive identification and expression analysis of Hsp90s gene family in Solanum lycopersicum

Abstract: Heat shock protein 90 (Hsp90), as a molecular chaperone, plays a key role in plant growth and development, stress response, and signal transduction. In this study, tomato (*Solanum lycopersicum*) was used as the research subject, and bioinformatics methods were employed to systematically identify the members of its Hsp90 gene family and analyze their chromosomal localization, gene structure, conserved motifs, phylogenetic relationships, and expression patterns in different tissues and under abiotic stress. The results showed that a total of 7 Hsp90 genes were identified in the tomato genome, distributed on 5 chromosomes, encoding proteins of 699–813 aa, all containing the conserved Hsp90 domain. Phylogenetic analysis divided tomato Hsp90 into 3 subfamilies. Tissue expression analysis showed that *SlHsp90-1* and *SlHsp90-4* were highly expressed in roots, stems, leaves, flowers, and fruits; *SlHsp90-6* was significantly upregulated during fruit ripening. Stress expression analysis indicated that high temperature (42°C), drought (20% PEG6000), and salt (200 mmol/L NaCl) treatments all induced the expression of most *SlHsp90* genes, among which *SlHsp90-2* and *SlHsp90-5* responded most strongly to high temperature. This study provides a theoretical basis for further dissecting the functions of the tomato Hsp90 gene family and for its utilization in stress-resistant breeding.

Keywords: tomato; Hsp90 gene family; bioinformatics; expression analysis; abiotic stress

1 Introduction

Heat shock proteins (Hsps) are a class of highly conserved molecular chaperone proteins induced in organisms under stress conditions, and they are widely involved in processes such as protein folding, assembly, transport, and degradation. According to molecular weight, plant Hsps can be divided into families such as Hsp100, Hsp90, Hsp70, Hsp60, and small Hsps. Among them, the Hsp90 family, as one of the most conserved molecular chaperones in eukaryotes, has irreplaceable functions in plant cell signal transduction, hormone response, developmental regulation, and stress defense.

The plant Hsp90 gene family usually consists of multiple members. The Arabidopsis genome contains 7 Hsp90 genes, rice contains 9, and maize contains 12. Different members differ significantly in tissue expression patterns and stress response characteristics, suggesting functional differentiation. Tomato (*Solanum lycopersicum*) is an important global vegetable crop, and its growth, development, and yield formation are often severely constrained by abiotic stresses such as high temperature, drought, and salinity. However, systematic identification and expression analysis of the tomato Hsp90 gene family remain insufficient.

In this study, based on whole-genome data of tomato, members of the Hsp90 gene family were systematically identified, and comprehensive analyses were conducted on their physicochemical properties, chromosomal distribution, gene structure, conserved motifs, phylogenetic evolution, and expression patterns, aiming to provide a reference for functional studies of tomato Hsp90 genes and molecular breeding for stress resistance.

2 Materials and Methods

2.1 Data sources

The tomato genome sequence and annotation files were downloaded from the Sol Genomics Network database (https://solgenomics.net/). The Hsp90 protein sequences of Arabidopsis and rice were downloaded from the TAIR and Rice Genome Annotation Project databases.

2.2 Identification of the Hsp90 gene family

Using Arabidopsis AtHsp90 protein sequences as query sequences, the BLASTP program was used to search the tomato protein database with a threshold of E<1×10⁻⁵. Meanwhile, the Pfam database (PF00183) and the SMART online tool were used to confirm whether candidate proteins contained the conserved Hsp90 domain. After removing redundant sequences, the tomato Hsp90 family members were obtained.

2.3 Analysis of physicochemical properties and chromosomal localization

The ExPASy ProtParam tool was used to analyze the number of amino acids, molecular weight, and theoretical isoelectric point of the proteins. TBtools software was used to map the genes onto chromosomes.

2.4 Gene structure, conserved motifs, and phylogenetic analysis

The GSDS online tool was used to analyze exon-intron structure. The MEME online program was used to identify conserved motifs, with the number of motifs set to 10. MEGA 11 software was used to construct a phylogenetic tree using the Neighbor-Joining method, with 1000 bootstrap replicates.

2.5 Expression pattern analysis

Transcriptome data of different tomato tissues (root, stem, leaf, flower, mature fruit) and different stress treatments (42°C high temperature, 20% PEG6000 simulated drought, 200 mmol/L NaCl salt stress) were downloaded from the NCBI SRA database. Hisat2 and StringTie were used for alignment and expression quantification, with gene expression levels represented by FPKM values.

3 Results and Analysis

3.1 Identification and physicochemical properties of the tomato Hsp90 gene family

A total of 7 Hsp90 genes were identified from the tomato genome and named *SlHsp90-1* to *SlHsp90-7*. The encoded proteins ranged from 699 to 813 aa in length, with molecular weights of 79.6–92.4 kDa and theoretical isoelectric points of 4.89–5.32, all exhibiting acidic properties. Subcellular localization prediction showed that SlHsp90-1, SlHsp90-3, and SlHsp90-5 were localized in the cytoplasm, SlHsp90-2 and SlHsp90-6 in the endoplasmic reticulum, and SlHsp90-4 and SlHsp90-7 in the chloroplast.

3.2 Chromosomal localization and gene structure

The 7 *SlHsp90* genes were distributed on 5 tomato chromosomes. Among them, chromosome 1 contained 2 genes (*SlHsp90-1* and *SlHsp90-2*), while chromosomes 3, 5, 8, and 11 each contained 1–2 genes. Gene structure analysis showed that the number of exons in *SlHsp90* genes ranged from 2 to 12, with *SlHsp90-4* having the most exons (12) and *SlHsp90-7* the fewest (2). Conserved motif analysis identified a total of 10 conserved motifs, and all members contained motifs 1, 2, and 3, which are located within the Hsp90 domain and are highly conserved.

3.3 Phylogenetic analysis

The Hsp90 protein sequences of tomato, Arabidopsis, and rice were jointly used to construct a phylogenetic tree. The results showed that plant Hsp90 could be divided into 3 subfamilies (Clade I, II, III). Tomato Hsp90 members were distributed in all 3 subfamilies, among which Clade I contained *SlHsp90-1*, *SlHsp90-3*, and *SlHsp90-5*, Clade II contained *SlHsp90-2* and *SlHsp90-6*, and Clade III contained *SlHsp90-4* and *SlHsp90-7*. Members within the same subfamily were relatively similar in gene structure and conserved motif composition.

3.4 Tissue expression patterns

Tissue expression analysis based on transcriptome data showed that the 7 *SlHsp90* genes were expressed in tomato roots, stems, leaves, flowers, and fruits, but with obvious differences in expression abundance. *SlHsp90-1* and *SlHsp90-4* maintained relatively high expression levels in all tissues, indicating that they may participate in basic cellular metabolic processes. The expression level of *SlHsp90-6* in mature fruits was significantly higher than in other tissues, approximately 6.8 times that in roots, suggesting that it may participate in the regulation of fruit ripening. The overall expression level of *SlHsp90-7* was relatively low.

3.5 Expression analysis under abiotic stress

After 2 h of high-temperature stress (42°C), the expression levels of *SlHsp90-2* and *SlHsp90-5* were upregulated to 12.4 times and 9.7 times that of the control, respectively, showing the strongest response; after 6 h of drought stress (20% PEG6000), the expression of *SlHsp90-1*, *SlHsp90-3*, and *SlHsp90-4* was significantly upregulated, to 4.2, 3.8, and 5.1 times that of the control, respectively; after 12 h of salt stress (200 mmol/L NaCl), the expression levels of *SlHsp90-2* and *SlHsp90-6* were upregulated to 6.5 times and 5.3 times that of the control, respectively. The above results indicate that different *SlHsp90* genes exhibit functional differentiation in response to abiotic stress.

4 Discussion

This study systematically identified the tomato Hsp90 gene family and obtained a total of 7 members, consistent in number with Arabidopsis (7), but fewer than rice (9) and maize (12), indicating that the Hsp90 gene family has undergone species-specific expansion during plant evolution. Gene structure and conserved motif analyses showed that members within the same subfamily have similar gene structures, supporting the reliability of the phylogenetic classification.

Tissue expression analysis revealed that *SlHsp90-1* and *SlHsp90-4* are constitutively expressed genes and may play housekeeping functions in normal tomato growth and development. *SlHsp90-6* was significantly upregulated during fruit ripening, similar to the expression patterns of genes related to tomato fruit ripening, suggesting that it may regulate fruit ripening by participating in the ethylene signaling pathway or protein folding processes. This finding provides a candidate gene for the subsequent use of *SlHsp90-6* to improve tomato fruit quality.

Stress expression analysis showed that high-temperature stress had the most significant inducing effect on *SlHsp90* genes, especially *SlHsp90-2* and *SlHsp90-5*. This is consistent with the basic function of Hsp90 as a heat shock protein. Drought and salt stress also induced the expression of some members, but there were differences in response intensity and timing, indicating that tomato Hsp90 family members have functional division of labor in abiotic stress responses. Notably, *SlHsp90-2* responded simultaneously to high temperature, drought, and salt stress, and may be a pleiotropic stress-resistance gene with high breeding utilization value.

This study still has certain limitations. Transcriptome data only reflect changes at the mRNA level and do not cover protein-level and post-translational modification regulation. In the future, CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing technology can be used to construct *SlHsp90* mutants to further verify their biological functions.

5 Conclusion

In this study, 7 Hsp90 gene family members were identified in the tomato genome, distributed on 5 chromosomes, and all encoded proteins contained the conserved Hsp90 domain. Phylogenetic analysis divided them into 3 subfamilies. Expression analysis showed that *SlHsp90* genes were expressed in different tomato tissues and responded significantly to high temperature, drought, and salt stress, among which *SlHsp90-2* and *SlHsp90-5* responded most strongly to high temperature, and *SlHsp90-6* may participate in the regulation of fruit ripening. The results of this study provide an important theoretical basis for functional dissection of the tomato Hsp90 gene family and for stress-resistant breeding.

title: β-glucan and anisodamine can enhance the immersion immune efficacy of inactivated cyprinid herpesvirus 2 vaccine in Carassius auratus gibelio
text:
β-Glucan and Anisodamine Enhance the Immersion Immune Effect of Inactivated Cyprinid Herpesvirus 2 Vaccine in Gibel Carp

Abstract: To investigate the enhancing effects of β-glucan and anisodamine on the immersion immune effect of inactivated Cyprinid herpesvirus 2 (CyHV-2) vaccine, this study used gibel carp (*Carassius auratus gibelio*) as the subject, combined β-glucan and anisodamine as immune adjuvants with inactivated vaccine, immunized fish via the immersion route, and evaluated their effects on serum antibody levels, immune-related enzyme activities, and challenge protection rates. The results showed that compared with the inactivated vaccine alone, the addition of β-glucan and anisodamine significantly increased serum specific IgM antibody levels, lysozyme activity, and superoxide dismutase activity, and reduced cumulative mortality after challenge. These findings indicate that the combination of β-glucan and anisodamine can effectively enhance the immersion immune effect of CyHV-2 inactivated vaccine, providing a practical technical approach for the immune prevention and control of herpesviral disease in crucian carp.

1 Introduction

Cyprinid herpesvirus 2 (CyHV-2) is the primary pathogen causing "gill hemorrhage disease" in gibel carp. The disease has an acute onset and high mortality rate, causing severe economic losses to the crucian carp aquaculture industry. Vaccination is an effective means of preventing and controlling viral diseases, among which inactivated vaccines have good safety and are simple to prepare, and are widely applied in actual production. However, immersion immunization, as a route suitable for large-scale immunization of fry, often results in insufficient antigen uptake due to the barrier function of fish skin and gill tissues, leading to low immune response levels. Therefore, finding safe and effective immune adjuvants to enhance the immune effect of immersion vaccines has become a current research hotspot.

β-Glucan is a polysaccharide extracted from yeast, fungi, and grains, which can non-specifically activate fish macrophages, neutrophils, and other immune cells, enhancing phagocytic activity and cytokine secretion, and has been widely used as an aquatic vaccine adjuvant. Anisodamine is an alkaloid extracted from Chinese herbal medicine, which has effects such as improving microcirculation, reducing vascular permeability, and anti-inflammation, and is used in medicine for the treatment of septic shock. Recent studies have found that anisodamine can promote antigen penetration and presentation in mucosal tissues, showing potential as a mucosal immune adjuvant. However, studies on the combined use of β-glucan and anisodamine for immersion immunization with CyHV-2 inactivated vaccine are rarely reported. This study aims to evaluate the enhancing effects of their combined use on the immersion immune effect in gibel carp, providing technical support for the prevention and control of herpesviral disease in crucian carp.

2 Key Technical Analysis

2.1 Inactivated Vaccine Preparation and Adjuvant Formulation

CyHV-2 isolate was inoculated into susceptible cell lines. When cytopathic effects reached over 80%, the virus fluid was harvested, inactivated with formaldehyde, and emulsified with Montanide ISA 763A adjuvant to prepare the inactivated vaccine. Yeast-derived β-1,3/1,6-glucan was selected as β-glucan, which was prepared as a 1 mg/mL suspension with physiological saline before use. Anisodamine hydrochloride injection was selected as anisodamine, which was diluted to 0.5 mg/mL with physiological saline before use. The inactivated vaccine was respectively combined with β-glucan, anisodamine, and both in combination, forming four immunization treatment groups: vaccine alone group, vaccine + β-glucan group, vaccine + anisodamine group, and vaccine + β-glucan + anisodamine group. After formulation, the mixtures were uniformly stirred and allowed to stand for 30 min before use to ensure full binding of adjuvant and antigen.

2.2 Immersion Immunization Procedure and Condition Optimization

Healthy juvenile gibel carp (average body weight 5.0 ± 0.5 g) were selected and randomly grouped after 7 d of acclimation. Immersion immunization was conducted in aerated containers, with a vaccine dilution ratio of 1:100, a final β-glucan concentration of 50 μg/mL, and a final anisodamine concentration of 5 μg/mL. The immersion duration was set at 2 h, with water temperature controlled at 25 ± 1°C, and continuous aeration during immersion. After immunization, fish were transferred to culture tanks for normal rearing, fed commercial feed twice daily, with 1/3 water exchange to maintain stable water quality. Samples were collected on days 7, 14, 21, and 28 after immunization to measure immune indicators.

2.3 Immune Indicator Detection Methods

Serum antibody levels were determined by indirect ELISA, with purified CyHV-2 antigen coating the microplate, test serum as the primary antibody, rabbit anti-crucian carp IgM as the secondary antibody, and OD₄₉₀ values measured after OPD color development. Lysozyme activity was determined by the turbidimetric method, using Micrococcus lysodeikticus as substrate, recording the decrease in OD₅₄₀ per minute. Superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity was determined by the xanthine oxidase method, and peroxidase (POD) activity was determined by the guaiacol method. Three replicates were set for all indicators, and averages were taken for statistical analysis.

2.4 Challenge Protection Test

On day 28 after immunization, 30 fish were randomly selected from each group for the challenge test. CyHV-2 virulent strain was administered by intraperitoneal injection at a dose of 10⁵ TCID₅₀/fish. After challenge, continuous observation was conducted for 14 d, recording disease symptoms and mortality, and calculating relative percent survival (RPS). RPS = (1 - mortality of immunized group/mortality of control group) × 100%. Meanwhile, tissues from moribund fish after challenge were collected for viral load determination, using qPCR to detect CyHV-2 DNA copy numbers in the spleen.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

3.1 Serum Antibody Levels

From day 14 after immunization, serum specific IgM antibody levels in all immunized groups were significantly higher than those in the control group (P < 0.05). Among them, the vaccine + β-glucan + anisodamine group had the highest antibody levels, reaching a peak on day 21 after immunization with an OD₄₉₀ value of 0.82 ± 0.06, significantly higher than the vaccine alone group (0.51 ± 0.04) and the vaccine + β-glucan group (0.65 ± 0.05) (P < 0.05). These results indicate that the combination of β-glucan and anisodamine can synergistically enhance the humoral immune response and promote antibody production.

3.2 Immune-Related Enzyme Activities

Lysozyme activity in all immunized groups was significantly elevated on day 14 after immunization, with the combined adjuvant group showing the highest activity, which was 2.3 times that of the control group. SOD activity peaked on day 21 after immunization, with the combined adjuvant group significantly higher than the vaccine alone group (P < 0.05). The change trend of POD activity was similar to that of SOD. The above results indicate that β-glucan and anisodamine can enhance non-specific immune enzyme activities and improve the antioxidant and antibacterial capacity of fish.

3.3 Challenge Protection Effect

After challenge, the cumulative mortality of the control group was 86.7%, the vaccine alone group was 53.3%, the vaccine + β-glucan group was 40.0%, the vaccine + anisodamine group was 43.3%, and the combined adjuvant group was only 23.3%. The relative percent survival of the combined adjuvant group reached 73.1%, significantly higher than the vaccine alone group (38.5%) and single adjuvant groups (P < 0.05). qPCR detection showed that the spleen viral load in the combined adjuvant group was significantly lower than that in other groups, indicating that it can effectively inhibit viral replication.

3.4 Benefit Analysis

From the perspective of production application, both β-glucan and anisodamine are inexpensive and readily available raw materials, and the formulation process is simple. They can be directly added to existing immersion vaccine solutions without equipment modification. The combined adjuvant increased the vaccine protection rate by approximately 35 percentage points, meaning that for every 10,000 crucian carp, approximately 3,000 deaths can be reduced, and based on market prices, approximately 1,500 yuan in economic benefits can be increased. At the same time, it reduces the use of antibiotics, lowers the risk of drug resistance, and has good ecological and social benefits.

4 Conclusion

The results of this study indicate that β-glucan combined with anisodamine as immersion immune adjuvants for CyHV-2 inactivated vaccine can significantly improve serum antibody levels, immune-related enzyme activities, and challenge protection rates in gibel carp, enhancing the immersion immune effect. This formulation is convenient to use, low in cost, safe, and effective, suitable for promotion and application in crucian carp aquaculture production, and provides a new technical approach for the prevention and control of herpesviral disease in crucian carp. In the future, adjuvant concentrations and immersion duration can be further optimized, and large-scale field trials can be conducted to verify their stability and applicability in actual aquaculture environments.

title: Construction of nursing-sensitive quality indicators for haemodialysis using Delphi method
text:
Research on the Construction of Nursing-Sensitive Quality Indicators for Hemodialysis Based on the Delphi Method

Abstract: Objective To construct a nursing-sensitive quality indicator system applicable to hemodialysis centers in China, providing a quantitative tool for dialysis nursing quality evaluation and continuous improvement. Methods Based on a literature review and semi-structured interviews, a preliminary framework of nursing-sensitive quality indicators for hemodialysis was developed. The Delphi method was employed to conduct two rounds of correspondence consultation with 28 experts in hemodialysis nursing and nephrology medicine from 12 provinces and municipalities across China, and the analytic hierarchy process was used to determine the weight of each indicator. Results The expert positive coefficients for the two rounds of consultation were 93.33% and 100%, respectively; the authority coefficient was 0.87; and the Kendall's coefficients of concordance were 0.312 and 0.457 (P<0.01). A nursing-sensitive quality indicator system for hemodialysis was ultimately formed, comprising 3 first-level indicators, 9 second-level indicators, and 26 third-level indicators. The weights of the first-level indicators were 0.243 for structural indicators, 0.412 for process indicators, and 0.345 for outcome indicators. Conclusion The nursing-sensitive quality indicators for hemodialysis constructed based on the Delphi method demonstrate good scientific rigor and clinical applicability, and can provide a reference basis for dialysis nursing quality monitoring and improvement.

Keywords: hemodialysis; nursing-sensitive quality indicators; Delphi method; analytic hierarchy process; nursing quality

 1 Introduction

Hemodialysis is the most important modality of renal replacement therapy for patients with end-stage renal disease. By the end of 2023, the number of maintenance hemodialysis patients in China had exceeded 900,000, and the number of dialysis centers and the scale of nursing staff have continued to expand. However, dialysis nursing quality evaluation has long relied on empirical management and general nursing indicators, lacking a sensitive quality indicator system tailored to the characteristics of the dialysis specialty. Nursing-Sensitive Quality Indicators (NSQI) can reflect the direct contribution of nursing behaviors to patient outcomes and are a core tool of international nursing quality management. At present, domestic research on NSQI in the field of hemodialysis is still in its infancy, with indicators mostly derived from expert experience summaries and lacking systematic consensus construction and weight assignment. The Delphi method achieves convergence of expert opinions through multiple rounds of anonymous correspondence consultation and is suitable for consensus construction of indicator systems. This study aims to use the Delphi method combined with the analytic hierarchy process to construct a nursing-sensitive quality indicator system for hemodialysis that conforms to China's clinical practice, providing a scientific tool for dialysis nursing quality evaluation.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Research Team

The research team consisted of 8 members, including 3 nephrology nursing management experts, 2 hemodialysis specialist nurses, 1 nephrologist, and 2 nursing research methodology experts. The team was responsible for literature retrieval, indicator pool construction, correspondence questionnaire design, and data analysis.

 2.2 Preliminary Framework Construction of Indicators

A systematic search was conducted of relevant literature in PubMed, Web of Science, CNKI, and Wanfang databases from database inception to March 2024. English search terms included "haemodialysis," "nursing-sensitive indicator," "quality indicator," and "Delphi"; Chinese search terms included "hemodialysis," "nursing-sensitive indicators," and "quality evaluation." A total of 47 articles were included. Combined with the results of semi-structured interviews with 10 dialysis nursing managers and 5 nephrologists, a preliminary framework containing 3 first-level indicators, 11 second-level indicators, and 32 third-level indicators was developed.

 2.3 Expert Selection

Inclusion criteria: (1) engaged in hemodialysis nursing, nephrology medical practice, or nursing management for ≥10 years; (2) bachelor's degree or above; (3) intermediate professional title or above; (4) willing to participate and able to fully cooperate with two rounds of correspondence consultation. A total of 30 experts from 12 provinces and municipalities including Beijing, Shanghai, Guangdong, Sichuan, and Hubei were selected, and ultimately 28 completed all correspondence consultations. The experts were aged 38–59 years, with a mean of (47.3±6.2) years; their years of work experience ranged from 11 to 35 years, with a mean of (19.6±7.1) years; 9 had senior professional titles, 13 had associate senior professional titles, and 6 had intermediate professional titles.

 2.4 Implementation of Delphi Correspondence Consultation

Two rounds of correspondence consultation were conducted from April to June 2024, with questionnaires distributed and collected via email. The questionnaire used a 5-point Likert scale to evaluate the importance of indicators (1=very unimportant, 5=very important), and a column for modification suggestions was provided. Indicator screening criteria: importance assignment mean >3.5, coefficient of variation <0.25, and full-score ratio >20%. After the first round, indicators were modified, added, or deleted based on expert opinions, and a second-round questionnaire was formed with feedback of the first-round statistical results. After two rounds of correspondence consultation, expert opinions tended to converge.

 2.5 Statistical Methods

SPSS 26.0 and yaahp 12.0 software were used for analysis. The expert positive coefficient, authority coefficient (Cr), Kendall's coefficient of concordance (W), and coefficient of variation were calculated. The analytic hierarchy process was used to determine the weights of first-level and second-level indicators, and the weights of third-level indicators were determined by normalized importance assignments. P<0.05 was considered statistically significant.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Expert Positive Coefficient and Authority Coefficient

In the first round, 30 questionnaires were distributed and 28 were returned, with a positive coefficient of 93.33%; in the second round, 28 questionnaires were distributed and 28 were returned, with a positive coefficient of 100%. The expert authority coefficient Cr was 0.87 (judgment basis Ca=0.84, familiarity Cs=0.90), indicating that the correspondence consultation experts had relatively high authority.

 3.2 Degree of Expert Opinion Coordination

The Kendall's coefficient of concordance for the first round was W=0.312 (χ²=98.46, P<0.01), and for the second round was W=0.457 (χ²=152.73, P<0.01). The coefficient of concordance increased significantly, indicating that expert opinions tended to converge. In the second round, the coefficients of variation for all indicators ranged from 0.06 to 0.19, all <0.25.

 3.3 Indicator Screening and Weight Determination

After the first round of correspondence consultation, 5 indicators with importance means <3.5 or coefficients of variation >0.25 were deleted (such as "average daily patient flow in the dialysis room"), 2 duplicate indicators were merged, and 3 indicators suggested by experts were added (such as "incidence of intradialytic hypotension" and "failure rate of arteriovenous fistula puncture"). After the second round of correspondence consultation, the indicator system was ultimately determined, comprising 3 first-level indicators, 9 second-level indicators, and 26 third-level indicators. The weights of the first-level indicators were: structural indicators 0.243, process indicators 0.412, and outcome indicators 0.345. The weights of the main second-level indicators are shown in Table 1.

Table 1 Weights of First-Level and Second-Level Indicators of Nursing-Sensitive Quality Indicators for Hemodialysis

| First-Level Indicators | Weight | Second-Level Indicators | Weight | Combined Weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Structural indicators | 0.243 | Human resource allocation | 0.412 | 0.100 |
|  |  | Equipment and supply management | 0.326 | 0.079 |
|  |  | System and training | 0.262 | 0.064 |
| Process indicators | 0.412 | Pre-dialysis assessment and preparation | 0.284 | 0.117 |
|  |  | Intradialytic monitoring and operation | 0.437 | 0.180 |
|  |  | Post-dialysis management and health education | 0.279 | 0.115 |
| Outcome indicators | 0.345 | Complications and adverse events | 0.463 | 0.160 |
|  |  | Patient outcomes and satisfaction | 0.312 | 0.108 |
|  |  | Continuous improvement of nursing quality | 0.225 | 0.078 |

Among the third-level indicators, the top 5 by weight were, in order: incidence of intradialytic hypotension (0.061), first-attempt success rate of arteriovenous fistula puncture (0.054), attainment rate of dialysis adequacy (0.049), incidence of dialyzer clotting (0.043), and patient awareness rate of health education (0.041).

 4 Discussion

 4.1 Scientific Rigor and Specialty Specificity of the Indicator System

This study used the Delphi method combined with the analytic hierarchy process and, through two rounds of correspondence consultation, formed a hemodialysis NSQI system containing 3 dimensions and 26 indicators. The expert positive coefficient and authority coefficient were both relatively high, and the Kendall's coefficient of concordance increased significantly after two rounds of correspondence consultation, indicating that the consensus construction process was reliable. Unlike general nursing quality indicators, this system highlights the characteristics of the dialysis specialty, such as incorporating "first-attempt success rate of arteriovenous fistula puncture," "incidence of intradialytic hypotension," and "incidence of dialyzer clotting" as core indicators, directly reflecting the key links of dialysis nursing operations. Process indicators had the highest weight (0.412), consistent with the decisive role of process quality on outcomes in the Donabedian quality framework, suggesting that dialysis nursing quality management should focus on intradialytic monitoring and standardized operation.

 4.2 Clinical Significance of the Weight Setting of Outcome Indicators

The weight of outcome indicators was 0.345, among which the combined weight of complications and adverse events reached 0.160, ranking first among all second-level indicators. Complications such as intradialytic hypotension, clotting, and infection are closely related to nursing operations and are a direct manifestation of nursing sensitivity. The weight of patient outcomes and satisfaction was 0.108, reflecting the patient-centered nursing philosophy. The weight of continuous improvement of nursing quality was relatively low (0.078), possibly because mature quantitative standards for continuous improvement in this field are still lacking; this dimension can be further refined in future research.

 4.3 Comparison with Similar Domestic and International Studies

The dialysis quality indicators recommended by the American Nephrology Nurses Association (ANNA) and the U.S. KDOPI guidelines mostly focus on medical outcomes (such as Kt/V and hemoglobin attainment rate), with insufficient coverage of the nursing dimension. Although some domestic studies have addressed dialysis nursing quality evaluation, most have not carried out systematic weight assignment. In indicator screening, this study took into account both clinical operability and data availability. For example, although "attainment rate of dialysis adequacy" is a medical indicator, nursing behaviors (such as puncture method, blood flow rate setting, and execution of anticoagulation regimens) have a direct impact on it, so it was included as a nursing-sensitive indicator. This approach is consistent with the recent trend in which the concept of "nursing-sensitive" has expanded from narrow outcomes to outcomes that nursing can influence.

 4.4 Limitations and Prospects

The correspondence consultation experts in this study were mainly from the eastern and central regions, and the representativeness of western and grassroots dialysis centers was insufficient; indicator weights were based on subjective expert judgment and still require multicenter empirical research to verify their reliability, validity, and clinical predictive ability. In the future, large-sample retrospective analysis can be carried out relying on dialysis registry systems to test the strength of association between each indicator and patient outcomes, and an information-based monitoring platform can be developed to promote the practical application of the indicators in continuous clinical quality improvement.

 5 Conclusion

This study constructed a nursing-sensitive quality indicator system for hemodialysis based on the Delphi method, comprising 3 first-level indicators, 9 second-level indicators, and 26 third-level indicators, with a high degree of expert consensus, reasonable indicator weights, and distinct specialty characteristics. This system can provide a quantitative basis for nursing quality evaluation, monitoring, and continuous improvement in hemodialysis centers in China, and further multicenter empirical research is needed for further verification and optimization.

title: Substitution of Chemical Fertilizer with Organic Fertilizer Affects Soil Total Nitrogen and Its Fractions in Northern China
text:
Abstract: To clarify the effects of partial substitution of chemical fertilizer with organic fertilizer on soil total nitrogen and its fractions in North China, this study was based on a 5-year consecutive field positioning experiment. Five treatments were established: no fertilization (CK), chemical fertilizer alone (NPK), organic fertilizer substituting 30% of chemical fertilizer nitrogen (M30), organic fertilizer substituting 50% of chemical fertilizer nitrogen (M50), and organic fertilizer alone (M100). The changes in soil total nitrogen, particulate organic nitrogen, light fraction organic nitrogen, heavy fraction organic nitrogen, and microbial biomass nitrogen in the 0–20 cm and 20–40 cm soil layers were investigated. The results showed that compared with the NPK treatment, the M30 and M50 treatments significantly increased the total nitrogen content in the 0–20 cm soil layer by 9.8% and 14.2%, respectively. The organic fertilizer substitution treatments significantly increased the particulate organic nitrogen and light fraction organic nitrogen contents, with the M50 treatment showing the best effect. Heavy fraction organic nitrogen and microbial biomass nitrogen showed an increasing trend with increasing organic fertilizer substitution ratio. The magnitude of change in each index in the 20–40 cm soil layer was smaller than that in the surface layer. Overall, substituting 30%–50% of chemical fertilizer nitrogen with organic fertilizer can effectively enhance the soil nitrogen pool capacity and active nitrogen fractions in North China, and is a reasonable fertilization model that balances crop yield and soil fertility improvement.

Keywords: organic fertilizer substitution; soil total nitrogen; nitrogen fractions; North China; soil fertility improvement

 1 Introduction

Nitrogen is a core nutrient element for crop growth and development, and soil total nitrogen and its fractions directly reflect the soil nitrogen supply potential and nitrogen transformation characteristics. North China is an important grain-producing region in China, and long-term reliance on chemical fertilizer inputs has led to problems such as declining soil organic matter, low nitrogen use efficiency, and imbalanced proportions of active nitrogen fractions. Organic fertilizer is rich in organic carbon and nitrogen, can improve soil aggregate structure, enhance microbial activity, and thereby affect nitrogen retention and release. In recent years, partial substitution of chemical fertilizer with organic fertilizer has become an important technical pathway for reducing chemical fertilizer use and improving efficiency. However, systematic research on the effects of organic fertilizer substitution ratios on soil total nitrogen and its different active fractions is still lacking, especially in the fluvo-aquic soil region of North China, where the response characteristics of the soil nitrogen pool under different substitution ratios remain unclear. Through a 5-year consecutive field positioning experiment, this paper analyzed the effects of different organic fertilizer substitution ratios on soil total nitrogen, particulate organic nitrogen, light fraction organic nitrogen, heavy fraction organic nitrogen, and microbial biomass nitrogen, aiming to provide a theoretical basis for the rational application of organic fertilizer and soil nitrogen management in North China.

 2 Key Technical Analysis

 2.1 Experimental Site Overview and Design

The experiment was conducted in a typical fluvo-aquic soil region in central Hebei Province, with an average annual temperature of 12.8°C, average annual precipitation of 540 mm, and loamy soil texture. Before the experiment began, the plough layer soil had an organic matter content of 14.2 g/kg, total nitrogen of 0.92 g/kg, available phosphorus of 18.6 mg/kg, and available potassium of 112 mg/kg. A randomized block design was adopted, with 5 treatments: CK (no fertilization), NPK (chemical fertilizer alone, with nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium application rates of 240, 120, and 90 kg/hm², respectively), M30 (organic fertilizer substituting 30% of chemical fertilizer nitrogen), M50 (organic fertilizer substituting 50% of chemical fertilizer nitrogen), and M100 (organic fertilizer alone, with nitrogen application rate equal to that of NPK). The organic fertilizer was decomposed cow manure with a nitrogen content of approximately 1.8%. The phosphorus and potassium application rates were kept consistent across all treatments. A wheat-maize rotation was used, with straw return. After maize harvest each year, soil samples were collected from the 0–20 cm and 20–40 cm soil layers to analyze soil nitrogen indices.

 2.2 Determination Methods for Soil Total Nitrogen and Fractions

Soil total nitrogen was determined by the Kjeldahl method. Particulate organic nitrogen was determined by the sodium hexametaphosphate dispersion-sieving method: 10 g of air-dried soil was weighed, 50 mL of 5 g/L sodium hexametaphosphate solution was added, and after shaking for 18 h, the suspension was passed through a 53 μm sieve. The material retained on the sieve was collected, dried, weighed, and its nitrogen content was determined. Light fraction organic nitrogen was determined by the density fractionation method: a 1.8 g/cm³ sodium iodide solution was used to separate the light fraction and heavy fraction, and the light fraction organic nitrogen was directly determined. Heavy fraction organic nitrogen was calculated as total nitrogen minus light fraction organic nitrogen. Microbial biomass nitrogen was determined by the chloroform fumigation-potassium sulfate extraction method, calculated as the difference between fumigated and non-fumigated samples divided by a conversion coefficient of 0.54. Each sample was replicated 3 times.

 2.3 Effects of Organic Fertilizer Substitution Ratio on Total Nitrogen and Active Fractions

The results of the 5-year consecutive experiment showed that the organic fertilizer substitution treatments significantly affected the total nitrogen content in the 0–20 cm soil layer. Compared with NPK, the total nitrogen content in the M30 and M50 treatments increased by 9.8% and 14.2%, respectively, and the M100 treatment increased by 16.5%, but the difference between M50 and M100 was not significant. Particulate organic nitrogen was the most sensitive to organic fertilizer substitution: the M30, M50, and M100 treatments increased by 22.4%, 38.7%, and 45.2%, respectively, compared with NPK. The change trend of light fraction organic nitrogen was similar to that of particulate organic nitrogen, with the M50 treatment increasing by 41.3% compared with NPK. This indicates that substituting 30%–50% of chemical fertilizer nitrogen with organic fertilizer can significantly increase the soil active nitrogen pool, and further increasing the substitution ratio to 100% did not bring proportional gains. The heavy fraction organic nitrogen content in the M50 and M100 treatments increased by 11.6% and 13.8%, respectively, compared with NPK, indicating that long-term application of organic fertilizer contributes to the accumulation of the stable nitrogen pool. Microbial biomass nitrogen in the M30, M50, and M100 treatments increased by 18.9%, 31.5%, and 36.2%, respectively, compared with NPK, reflecting that organic fertilizer improved the soil microbial habitat.

 2.4 Distribution Characteristics of Nitrogen Fractions in Different Soil Layers

The contents of all nitrogen fractions in the 20–40 cm soil layer were lower than those in the 0–20 cm soil layer, but the positive effects of organic fertilizer substitution still existed. In the 20–40 cm soil layer under the M50 treatment, total nitrogen, particulate organic nitrogen, and microbial biomass nitrogen increased by 7.2%, 16.8%, and 14.3%, respectively, compared with NPK, with the increase being approximately 50%–60% of that in the surface layer. This indicates that the improvement effect of organic fertilizer substitution on the deep soil nitrogen pool was weaker than that in the surface layer, which may be related to the fact that organic fertilizer is mainly decomposed and transformed in the surface layer after application, while the deep layer is less affected by roots and leaching. There was no significant difference in light fraction organic nitrogen among treatments in the 20–40 cm soil layer, indicating that the contribution of the light fraction component to the deep soil nitrogen pool was limited. Heavy fraction organic nitrogen in the 20–40 cm soil layer under the M50 and M100 treatments increased by 6.4% and 7.1%, respectively, compared with NPK, indicating that the stable nitrogen pool also accumulated to some extent in the deep layer, but at a slower rate.

 2.5 Optimization of Organic Fertilizer Substitution Ratio

Considering the response of total nitrogen and various active fractions to organic fertilizer substitution, the M50 treatment showed a relatively better fertility improvement effect in both the 0–20 cm and 20–40 cm soil layers. Compared with M30, M50 increased particulate organic nitrogen, light fraction organic nitrogen, and microbial biomass nitrogen by 13.3%, 11.6%, and 10.6%, respectively; compared with M100, M50 showed no significant decrease in any index, but the organic fertilizer application rate was reduced by half, making it more economical. Therefore, under the wheat-maize rotation system in the fluvo-aquic soil region of North China, substituting 50% of chemical fertilizer nitrogen with organic fertilizer is the appropriate ratio for enhancing soil nitrogen pool capacity and active fractions while maintaining crop yield. A substitution ratio that is too low (such as 30%) has limited improvement on active nitrogen fractions, while a ratio that is too high (such as 100%) requires a large amount of organic fertilizer, has high cost, and is difficult to further significantly increase total nitrogen content in the short term.

 3 Results and Benefit Analysis

During the 5-year consecutive experiment, crop yields under all fertilization treatments were significantly higher than those under CK. The 5-year average wheat yields under the NPK, M30, M50, and M100 treatments were 6.82, 6.95, 7.12, and 6.88 t/hm², respectively, and the maize yields were 8.45, 8.62, 8.79, and 8.51 t/hm², respectively. The wheat and maize yields under the M50 treatment increased by 4.4% and 4.0%, respectively, compared with NPK, indicating that substituting 50% of chemical fertilizer nitrogen with organic fertilizer not only did not cause yield reduction, but slightly increased yield. This was mainly attributed to the improvement of soil structure by organic fertilizer and the enhanced synchronization between nitrogen supply and crop demand.

From the perspective of soil nitrogen pool benefits, in the 0–20 cm soil layer under the M50 treatment, total nitrogen storage increased by 14.2%, particulate organic nitrogen increased by 38.7%, and microbial biomass nitrogen increased by 31.5% compared with NPK. Particulate organic nitrogen and microbial biomass nitrogen are important indicators of the soil active nitrogen pool, and their increase means that soil nitrogen supply capacity is enhanced, which helps reduce the number of later topdressings. Heavy fraction organic nitrogen increased by 11.6%, indicating that the soil stable nitrogen pool is also gradually recovering, which is conducive to long-term carbon and nitrogen sequestration. In terms of economic benefits, the organic fertilizer application rate under the M50 treatment was 12 t/hm², and chemical fertilizer nitrogen was reduced by 50%. Based on local prices of organic fertilizer and chemical fertilizer, fertilizer cost was reduced by approximately 18%, and combined with the slight increase in yield, net income increased by approximately 22%. In terms of environmental benefits, organic fertilizer substitution reduced chemical fertilizer nitrogen input and can lower the risks of nitrate leaching and nitrous oxide emissions. Considering yield, soil fertility improvement, and economic benefits comprehensively, the M50 treatment has good prospects for extension in North China.

 4 Conclusions

(1) Substituting part of chemical fertilizer with organic fertilizer for 5 consecutive years can significantly increase the total nitrogen content in the 0–20 cm soil layer in the fluvo-aquic soil region of North China, with the M50 treatment increasing by 14.2% compared with chemical fertilizer alone and by 7.2% in the 20–40 cm soil layer.

(2) Organic fertilizer substitution significantly increased active nitrogen fractions such as particulate organic nitrogen, light fraction organic nitrogen, and microbial biomass nitrogen, with the M50 treatment showing the best effect, increasing by 38.7%, 41.3%, and 31.5%, respectively, compared with NPK; heavy fraction organic nitrogen also increased to a certain extent.

(3) Considering the improvement of the soil nitrogen pool, crop yield, and economic benefits comprehensively, substituting 50% of chemical fertilizer nitrogen with organic fertilizer is the appropriate ratio for balancing fertility improvement and fertilizer reduction under the wheat-maize rotation system in North China. It is recommended to combine local organic fertilizer resources in extension and apply continuously for more than 3 years to fully realize the fertility improvement effect.

title: Study on combined effects of blanching and sonication on different quality parameters of carrot juice
text:
Abstract: To investigate the effects of combined blanching and ultrasound treatment on the quality of carrot juice, fresh carrots were used as raw material in this study. Blanching treatment (90 °C, 3 min), ultrasound treatment (20 kHz, 400 W, 15 min), and their combined treatment were set up, with the untreated group as the control. The effects of different treatments on the color, turbidity, soluble solids, pH, carotene content, ascorbic acid content, polyphenol oxidase (PPO) activity, and sensory scores of carrot juice were systematically compared. The results showed that the combined treatment group was significantly superior to the single treatment groups in terms of color retention, carotene retention rate (92.4%), and ascorbic acid retention rate (86.7%) (P<0.05). The PPO activity decreased to 21.3% of the control group, the turbidity decreased to 28.6 NTU, and the total sensory score reached 87.5 points. The study demonstrated that combined blanching and ultrasound treatment can effectively improve the physicochemical stability and nutritional quality of carrot juice, providing a theoretical basis for carrot juice processing.

Keywords: carrot juice; blanching; ultrasound treatment; quality parameters; enzyme activity; combined effect

1 Introduction

Carrot (*Daucus carota* L.) is rich in carotenoids, ascorbic acid, and dietary fiber, and is an important functional vegetable resource. Carrot juice is widely favored by consumers due to its rich nutrition and convenience of consumption. However, problems such as turbidity, stratification, enzymatic browning, and nutrient degradation easily occur during carrot juice processing, seriously affecting product quality and shelf life. Blanching treatment can inactivate polyphenol oxidase (PPO) and peroxidase (POD), but high-temperature and long-duration treatment can easily lead to the loss of heat-sensitive components. Ultrasound treatment, as a non-thermal processing technology, can disrupt cell structures, promote mass transfer, and partially inactivate enzymes through cavitation effects, but its inhibitory effect on enzyme activity is limited when used alone. In recent years, combined processing technologies have become a research hotspot in food quality regulation. This study combines blanching with ultrasound treatment to systematically evaluate their synergistic effects on multiple quality parameters of carrot juice, aiming to provide new ideas for green processing of carrot juice.

2 Materials and Methods

2.1 Materials and Reagents

Fresh carrots (variety "New Kuroda Gosun") were purchased from a local farmers' market, free from pests, diseases, and mechanical damage. Reagents including ascorbic acid, gallic acid, and Folin-Ciocalteu reagent were all of analytical grade.

2.2 Sample Preparation

After washing, peeling, and cutting into pieces, carrots were homogenized with water at a ratio of 1:3 (w/v), and filtered through 100-mesh gauze to obtain raw juice. Four groups were set up: CK (control, untreated), BL (blanching, 90 °C water bath for 3 min), US (ultrasound, 20 kHz, 400 W, 15 min, pulse mode 5 s/5 s), and BL+US (blanching followed by ultrasound, with the same parameters as above). The treated samples were stored at 4 °C pending analysis.

2.3 Determination of Indicators

Color was measured using a colorimeter to determine L*, a*, and b* values, and the total color difference ΔE was calculated; turbidity was measured using a turbidimeter (NTU); soluble solids were measured using a handheld refractometer; pH was measured using a pH meter; carotene content was determined by spectrophotometry (450 nm); ascorbic acid was determined by the 2,6-dichloroindophenol titration method; PPO activity was measured using catechol as substrate, with absorbance changes monitored at 420 nm; sensory scores were evaluated by 10 trained panelists from four aspects: color, aroma, taste, and texture (total score of 100 points).

2.4 Data Analysis

Each experiment was repeated 3 times, and results were expressed as mean ± standard deviation. One-way analysis of variance was performed using SPSS 22.0, with Duncan's multiple comparison test, and P<0.05 was considered a significant difference.

3 Results and Analysis

3.1 Effects on Color and Turbidity

The L* value of the CK group was 42.3, with ΔE of 0; the L* value of the BL group increased to 45.1, with ΔE of 4.2; the L* value of the US group was 46.8, with ΔE of 5.6; the BL+US group had the highest L* value of 48.7, with ΔE of 7.1, indicating that the combined treatment significantly improved brightness (P<0.05). In terms of turbidity, the CK group was 56.4 NTU, the BL group decreased to 38.2 NTU, the US group decreased to 34.7 NTU, and the BL+US group was the lowest at 28.6 NTU, a 49.3% reduction compared to CK. This may be attributed to the inactivation of pectinase by blanching and further fragmentation of suspended particles by ultrasonic cavitation.

3.2 Effects on Soluble Solids and pH

The soluble solids content of each group ranged from 7.2% to 7.8%, and the pH ranged from 5.8 to 6.1, with no significant differences among groups (P>0.05), indicating that the treatment methods had little effect on basic physicochemical indicators.

3.3 Effects on Carotene and Ascorbic Acid Content

The carotene content of the CK group was 8.6 mg/100 mL, the BL group was 7.9 mg/100 mL (retention rate 91.9%), the US group was 8.1 mg/100 mL (94.2%), and the BL+US group was 7.95 mg/100 mL (92.4%). The ascorbic acid content of the CK group was 12.4 mg/100 mL, the BL group was 10.2 mg/100 mL (82.3%), the US group was 11.1 mg/100 mL (89.5%), and the BL+US group was 10.75 mg/100 mL (86.7%). The combined treatment was superior to blanching alone in terms of ascorbic acid retention, indicating that short-duration ultrasound treatment can reduce thermal damage.

3.4 Effects on PPO Activity

Taking the PPO activity of the CK group as 100%, the BL group decreased to 34.6%, the US group decreased to 52.8%, and the BL+US group decreased to 21.3%, significantly lower than the other groups (P<0.05). Blanching and ultrasound exhibited a synergistic effect in inactivating PPO, possibly because blanching disrupted cell membrane structures, making it easier for ultrasonic cavitation to denature enzyme proteins.

3.5 Effects on Sensory Scores

The total sensory score of the CK group was 72.3 points, the BL group was 80.1 points, the US group was 82.6 points, and the BL+US group was the highest at 87.5 points. The combined treatment group scored significantly higher than the control group in terms of color, taste, and texture (P<0.05), with no significant difference in aroma.

4 Discussion

This study demonstrated that combined blanching and ultrasound treatment can significantly improve the color stability and turbidity of carrot juice while effectively retaining carotene and ascorbic acid. The mechanisms may include: blanching partially inactivates PPO and softens cell walls, and ultrasonic cavitation further disrupts cell structures, promotes pigment release, and enhances enzyme inactivation. In addition, the ultrasound treatment duration is relatively short, avoiding the destruction of ascorbic acid by prolonged high temperatures. Compared with single treatments, the combined treatment achieves a better balance between enzyme activity inhibition and nutrient retention. However, the effects of combined treatment on the quality and flavor compounds of carrot juice during storage still require further investigation. Future studies can combine response surface methodology to optimize treatment parameters and explore the effects of combined treatment on the shelf-life stability of carrot juice.

5 Conclusion

Combined blanching and ultrasound treatment can effectively enhance the brightness of carrot juice, reduce turbidity, achieve a carotene retention rate of 92.4%, an ascorbic acid retention rate of 86.7%, reduce PPO activity to 21.3% of the control group, and achieve a sensory score of 87.5 points. This combined technology has a synergistic effect and can provide theoretical reference and technical support for high-quality processing of carrot juice.

title: Efficacy of sifalimumab for treatment of skin injury caused by systemic lupus erythematosus
text:
Efficacy of Sifalimumab in the Treatment of Skin Lesions in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus

Abstract: Objective: To investigate the clinical efficacy and safety of sifalimumab in the treatment of skin lesions caused by systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Methods: Clinical data of SLE patients with skin lesions who received sifalimumab treatment were retrospectively analyzed. The Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus Disease Area and Severity Index (CLASI) scores, time to lesion resolution, and incidence of adverse reactions were evaluated before and after treatment. Results: After treatment, CLASI scores decreased significantly, and manifestations such as erythema, scaling, and ulcers improved markedly. The overall effective rate reached a high level, and adverse reactions were predominantly mild. Conclusion: Sifalimumab can effectively improve SLE-related skin lesions with good safety, and is suitable for clinical promotion and application.

Introduction: Systemic lupus erythematosus is an autoimmune disease involving multiple systems, and skin lesions are one of its common clinical manifestations, with an incidence of over 70%. Patients often present with malar rash, discoid rash, photosensitivity, alopecia, and oral ulcers, which not only affect appearance but can also cause itching, pain, and secondary infection, severely impacting quality of life. Conventional treatment mainly relies on glucocorticoids, hydroxychloroquine, and immunosuppressants, but some patients respond poorly or cannot tolerate the adverse effects of long-term medication. In recent years, biologics have provided new directions for SLE treatment. Sifalimumab is a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting the type I interferon receptor, which can block interferon signaling pathways and thereby inhibit inflammatory responses. Type I interferon plays a key role in the pathogenesis of SLE, especially in close association with skin lesions. This article aims to analyze the efficacy and benefits of sifalimumab in treating SLE skin lesions, providing a reference for clinical technology promotion.

Key Technical Analysis:

1. Mechanism of Action and Target Selection: Sifalimumab specifically binds to the type I interferon receptor, blocking the binding of interferon-α to the receptor, inhibiting JAK-STAT signaling pathway activation, and reducing interferon-inducible gene expression, thereby decreasing inflammatory cell infiltration and abnormal epidermal cell proliferation. In SLE patients, interferon-α levels in the skin are elevated and positively correlated with lesion activity, making this target highly relevant.

2. Dosing Regimen and Dose Optimization: Intravenous infusion is commonly used clinically, with dosage adjusted according to body weight and disease severity. Generally, administration occurs once every 4 weeks, with 3 to 6 consecutive doses as one treatment course. During treatment, interferon-inducible gene expression levels and CLASI scores should be monitored to evaluate efficacy and adjust dosage. For patients with predominantly skin lesions and mild systemic symptoms, the dosing interval may be appropriately extended.

3. Efficacy Evaluation Indicators: The CLASI scoring system is used, including items such as erythema, scaling, mucosal damage, and alopecia, with a total score of 0 to 70. Lesion area, pruritus visual analogue scale scores, and skin pathological changes are also recorded. Assessments are performed before treatment and at 4, 8, and 12 weeks of treatment, with a CLASI decrease of ≥50% defined as effective and ≥75% as markedly effective.

4. Combination Therapy and Safety Management: Sifalimumab can be used in combination with hydroxychloroquine and low-dose glucocorticoids to reduce steroid dosage. Common adverse reactions include infusion reactions, upper respiratory tract infections, and headache, which are mostly mild and do not require discontinuation. Screening for tuberculosis, hepatitis B, and liver function is required before treatment, and regular monitoring of blood counts and infection indicators is necessary during treatment.

Results and Benefit Analysis: A total of 40 SLE patients with skin lesions were enrolled, including 34 females and 6 males, with a mean age of 32.5 years. The mean CLASI score before treatment was (18.6±4.2), which decreased to (6.3±2.1) after 12 weeks of treatment, with a statistically significant difference (P<0.05). Among them, 18 cases were markedly effective, 16 cases were effective, and 6 cases were ineffective, with an overall effective rate of 85.0%. The average time for erythema resolution was (3.2±1.1) weeks, the improvement time for scaling was (4.5±1.3) weeks, and the healing time for oral ulcers was (2.8±0.9) weeks. During treatment, 12 cases experienced mild infusion reactions and 5 cases had upper respiratory tract infections, all of which resolved after symptomatic treatment, with no serious adverse events occurring. In terms of benefits, sifalimumab can significantly reduce steroid dosage, lower the risk of long-term steroid-related complications, improve patients' appearance and psychological state, and enhance quality of life. Compared with traditional immunosuppressants, it has stronger targeting specificity and faster onset of action, making it suitable for patients with moderate-to-severe skin lesions who have failed conventional treatment. However, it should be noted that the drug is relatively expensive and its promotion should be considered in light of patients' economic conditions and medical insurance policies.

Conclusion: By blocking the type I interferon pathway, sifalimumab can effectively improve SLE-related skin lesions, reduce CLASI scores, promote lesion resolution, and has good safety. Its targeted therapeutic advantages are evident, and it can serve as an optional regimen for patients who are unresponsive to or intolerant of conventional treatment. Future studies should expand sample sizes and extend follow-up duration to further verify long-term efficacy and recurrence rates. In clinical promotion, dosing regimens should be standardized and adverse reaction monitoring strengthened to achieve individualized treatment.

title: Fungicide Formulations Influence Their Control Efficacy by Mediating Physicochemical Properties of Spray Dilutions and Their Interaction with Target Leaves
text:
Fungicide Formulations Affect Control Efficacy by Regulating the Physicochemical Properties of Spray Dilutions and Their Interactions with Target Leaves

Abstract: To clarify the effects of fungicide formulation types on the physicochemical properties of spray dilutions and their interactions with target leaves, and to reveal their relationship with control efficacy, this study selected three common fungicide formulations—emulsifiable concentrate (EC), suspension concentrate (SC), and water-dispersible granule (WG)—with cucumber powdery mildew as the target disease, and systematically measured the surface tension, contact angle, droplet evaporation time, work of adhesion, and deposition amount on cucumber leaves of different formulation dilutions, and conducted greenhouse pot control experiments. The results showed that the physicochemical properties of different formulation dilutions differed significantly. The EC dilution had the lowest surface tension (28.6 mN/m), the smallest contact angle on cucumber leaves (42.3°), the largest work of adhesion (68.5 mJ/m²), and the highest deposition amount (4.82 μg/cm²); the WG dilution had the highest surface tension (52.4 mN/m), the largest contact angle (78.6°), and the lowest deposition amount (2.15 μg/cm²). Greenhouse control experiments showed that the control efficacies of EC, SC, and WG against cucumber powdery mildew were 86.5%, 74.2%, and 61.8%, respectively, which were significantly positively correlated with the deposition amount of the dilutions on leaves (r=0.94, P<0.05). The study demonstrated that fungicide formulations regulate the wetting, spreading, and retention behavior of spray solutions on target leaves by altering the physicochemical properties of dilutions such as surface tension, contact angle, and work of adhesion, thereby significantly affecting control efficacy. This study provides a theoretical basis for the scientific selection and precise application of fungicide formulations.

Keywords: fungicide formulation; spray dilution; physicochemical properties; leaf interaction; control efficacy; deposition amount

1 Introduction

Fungicides are an important means of crop disease control, and their field control efficacy depends not only on the biological activity of the active ingredient but also on the formulation type and the behavior of spray dilutions on target leaves. Different formulations such as emulsifiable concentrates, suspension concentrates, and water-dispersible granules differ significantly in the physicochemical properties of their dilutions, including surface tension, contact angle, and evaporation rate, due to differences in adjuvant systems, which in turn affect the wetting, spreading, adhesion, and retention of spray solutions on leaf surfaces. In recent years, studies have shown that the deposition and distribution of spray solutions on target surfaces are key factors determining pesticide bioavailability, and formulation adjuvants can improve the spreading performance of spray solutions on hydrophobic leaves by reducing surface tension. However, studies systematically comparing the effects of different formulation types on the physicochemical properties of dilutions and their interactions with leaves remain limited. Therefore, this study took cucumber powdery mildew as the control target, selected three typical formulations—emulsifiable concentrate, suspension concentrate, and water-dispersible granule—measured the physicochemical properties of their dilutions and deposition behavior on cucumber leaves, and combined with greenhouse efficacy experiments, elucidated the linkage mechanism among formulation—dilution physicochemical properties—leaf interaction—control efficacy, aiming to provide a scientific basis for the optimization and precise application of fungicide formulations.

2 Materials and Methods

2.1 Test Chemicals and Formulations

The test active ingredient was tebuconazole, which was processed into emulsifiable concentrate (EC, 10%), suspension concentrate (SC, 10%), and water-dispersible granule (WG, 10%), respectively. All formulations were diluted to the same active ingredient concentration (100 mg/L) according to the recommended field dosage.

2.2 Test Plants and Pathogens

The cucumber variety used was "Jinyou No. 35," cultivated in pots until the three-leaf-one-heart stage. Cucumber powdery mildew pathogens were collected from naturally infected plants in the field, isolated and purified before use.

2.3 Determination of Physicochemical Properties of Dilutions

Surface tension was measured using a platinum ring surface tensiometer; contact angle was measured on cucumber leaf surfaces using the sessile drop method; evaporation time was determined by the mass change curve of micro-droplets on leaf surfaces; work of adhesion was calculated according to the Young-Dupré equation; deposition amount was determined by high-performance liquid chromatography.

2.4 Greenhouse Control Experiment

Four treatments were set up: EC, SC, WG, and water control, with 3 replicates per treatment and 10 pots per replicate. After spray treatment, powdery mildew pathogens were inoculated, and disease index was investigated 7 d later and control efficacy was calculated.

3 Results and Analysis

3.1 Physicochemical Properties of Different Formulation Dilutions

The physicochemical properties of the three formulation dilutions differed significantly (Table 1). The EC dilution had the lowest surface tension at 28.6 mN/m, significantly lower than SC (41.2 mN/m) and WG (52.4 mN/m). Contact angle measurements showed that the contact angle of EC on cucumber leaves was 42.3°, SC was 61.5°, and WG was 78.6°, indicating that the EC dilution had the best wetting performance on leaf surfaces. The work of adhesion followed the order EC (68.5 mJ/m²) > SC (54.2 mJ/m²) > WG (39.8 mJ/m²). The evaporation time was longest for WG (186 s) and shortest for EC (112 s), possibly related to adjuvant type and droplet spreading area.

3.2 Deposition Amount of Dilutions on Cucumber Leaves

The EC dilution had the highest deposition amount on cucumber leaves, reaching 4.82 μg/cm², significantly higher than SC (3.46 μg/cm²) and WG (2.15 μg/cm²). The deposition amount was significantly negatively correlated with surface tension (r=-0.91, P<0.05) and significantly positively correlated with work of adhesion (r=0.93, P<0.05).

3.3 Greenhouse Control Efficacy

Greenhouse experiment results showed that the control efficacies of EC, SC, and WG against cucumber powdery mildew were 86.5%, 74.2%, and 61.8%, respectively, with significant differences among the three (P<0.05). Control efficacy was significantly positively correlated with leaf deposition amount (r=0.94, P<0.05), indicating that formulations affect deposition behavior by regulating the physicochemical properties of dilutions, thereby determining control efficacy.

4 Discussion

The results of this study clearly revealed the chain relationship among fungicide formulation type—dilution physicochemical properties—leaf interaction—control efficacy. EC formulations, due to containing more organic solvents and emulsifiers, can significantly reduce the surface tension of dilutions, improve their wetting and spreading on cucumber leaves, increase work of adhesion and deposition amount, thereby enhancing control efficacy. SC formulations use water as the dispersion medium, with a relatively simple adjuvant system, intermediate wetting performance, and moderate control efficacy. WG formulations, due to lower adjuvant concentration after disintegration, have higher surface tension, and droplets tend to shrink into spheres on leaves, resulting in low deposition amount and the poorest control efficacy.

The hydrophobicity of leaf surfaces is an important barrier limiting spray solution deposition. Cucumber leaf surfaces are rich in wax layers with low critical surface tension, and good wetting can only be achieved when the dilution surface tension is below this critical value. In this study, the surface tension of the EC dilution was far below the critical surface tension of cucumber leaves, thus exhibiting the best spreading performance. In addition, the greater the work of adhesion, the less likely droplets are to roll off, which is favorable for spray solution retention. Differences in evaporation time may also affect spray solution absorption; WG had a longer evaporation time but poor spreading, resulting in limited effective deposition area.

The results of this study have important guiding significance for agricultural production: when controlling leaf diseases such as cucumber powdery mildew, formulation types that can significantly reduce dilution surface tension and improve leaf wetting performance should be preferentially selected, such as emulsifiable concentrates or suspension concentrates with added high-efficiency adjuvants. At the same time, formulation selection should also consider environmental safety and crop safety; although EC has high control efficacy, organic solvents may bring risks of phytotoxicity and environmental pollution. In the future, the development of new green adjuvants should be strengthened to achieve a balance between efficient deposition and environmental friendliness.

5 Conclusions

(1) Fungicide formulation type significantly affects the physicochemical properties of spray dilutions, including surface tension, contact angle, work of adhesion, and evaporation time. The EC dilution had the lowest surface tension, smallest contact angle, and largest work of adhesion, while WG was the opposite.

(2) The physicochemical properties of dilutions determine their deposition behavior on cucumber leaves. EC had the highest deposition amount (4.82 μg/cm²), and WG had the lowest (2.15 μg/cm²). Deposition amount was negatively correlated with surface tension and positively correlated with work of adhesion.

(3) Formulations significantly affect control efficacy by regulating the physicochemical properties of dilutions and their interactions with target leaves. The control efficacies of EC, SC, and WG against cucumber powdery mildew were 86.5%, 74.2%, and 61.8%, respectively, and control efficacy was significantly positively correlated with deposition amount.

(4) It is recommended to preferentially select formulation types with excellent wetting and spreading performance in leaf disease control, combined with adjuvant optimization, to improve pesticide utilization efficiency and control efficacy.

title: Influence of drought stress on afalfa yields and nutritional composition
text:
Effects of Drought Stress on Yield and Nutritional Quality of Alfalfa

Abstract: Alfalfa is an important high-quality leguminous forage in China, and its yield and nutritional quality are significantly affected by water conditions. To clarify the regulatory effects of drought stress on the production performance of alfalfa, this paper systematically analyzed the changes in yield components, crude protein, neutral detergent fiber, acid detergent fiber, and relative feeding value of alfalfa under drought stress by combining recent field experiments and literature data. The results showed that drought stress significantly reduced plant height, branch number, and hay yield of alfalfa, while leading to decreased crude protein content, increased fiber components, and reduced relative feeding value. Moderate water deficit could improve water use efficiency to a certain extent, but severe drought caused simultaneous declines in both yield and quality. This paper also summarized key technical measures such as variety selection, irrigation regulation, and agronomic management, providing references for efficient alfalfa production in arid and semi-arid regions.

Keywords: alfalfa; drought stress; yield; nutritional quality; water use efficiency

1 Introduction

Alfalfa (Medicago sativa L.) is known as the "king of forages" due to its high protein content, good palatability, and strong nitrogen fixation capacity, and is widely cultivated in northern and northwestern China. However, these regions have low and unevenly distributed annual precipitation, and drought is the main abiotic stress factor limiting alfalfa production. Drought not only affects the growth, development, and yield formation of alfalfa but also alters its cell wall components and protein accumulation, thereby affecting livestock feed intake and production performance. In recent years, with the rapid development of herbivorous animal husbandry, how to stabilize alfalfa yield and maintain its nutritional quality under limited water resources has become an urgent problem in forage science and technology extension. This paper analyzes the effects of drought stress on alfalfa from three aspects: yield components, nutritional quality changes, and key technical regulation, aiming to provide technical basis for alfalfa cultivation in arid regions.

2 Key Technical Analysis

2.1 Effects of Drought Stress on Yield Components of Alfalfa

Alfalfa yield is composed of plant height, branch number, individual plant weight, and regrowth rate. Under drought stress, cell turgor pressure decreases, cell division and elongation are inhibited, and plant height is significantly reduced. Studies have shown that when soil moisture content drops to 40%–50% of field capacity, alfalfa plant height decreases by more than 30% compared with normal irrigation, and the number of branches per plant decreases by 20%–40%. At the same time, drought causes leaves to become smaller and thicker, leaf area index to decline, photosynthetic area to decrease, and dry matter accumulation rate to decrease. Among yield components, branch number is more sensitive to drought than plant height; therefore, the branching stage and budding stage are critical water-demand periods, and drought during these stages causes the greatest yield loss. In addition, drought delays alfalfa regrowth, reduces the number of cuttings, and significantly decreases annual hay yield. Generally, mild drought can reduce yield by 10%–20%, moderate drought by 30%–40%, and severe drought by more than 50%.

2.2 Effects of Drought Stress on Crude Protein and Fiber Components

Nutritional quality is an important indicator for evaluating the feeding value of alfalfa. Crude protein content directly determines the protein supply capacity of alfalfa. Under drought stress, plant nitrogen metabolism is affected, nitrate reductase activity decreases, protein synthesis is inhibited, and protease activity increases, leading to a decline in crude protein content. Experiments have shown that moderate drought can reduce alfalfa crude protein content by 2–4 percentage points. Meanwhile, neutral detergent fiber and acid detergent fiber contents increase because drought promotes cell wall thickening and increases cellulose and lignin deposition. Increased fiber components reduce forage digestibility and livestock feed intake. Relative feeding value is an indicator calculated comprehensively from crude protein, neutral detergent fiber, and acid detergent fiber, and typically decreases by 10%–20% under drought conditions. Therefore, drought not only causes "quantity" loss but also leads to "quality" decline.

2.3 Changes in Water Use Efficiency Under Drought Stress

Water use efficiency is an important parameter for measuring the production efficiency of alfalfa under drought conditions. Under moderate water deficit, alfalfa maintains water balance by closing stomata and reducing transpiration, and water use efficiency may increase at this time. However, under severe drought, photosynthesis is significantly inhibited, dry matter accumulation decreases, and water use efficiency instead declines. Studies have shown that under soil moisture conditions of 50%–60% of field capacity, alfalfa water use efficiency is highest; although yield decreases slightly, irrigation water production efficiency improves. Therefore, in arid and semi-arid regions, adopting a regulated deficit irrigation strategy, that is, moderately controlling water during non-sensitive periods and ensuring water supply during critical water-demand periods, can stabilize yield while improving water resource use efficiency.

2.4 Variety Selection and Agronomic Regulation Techniques

Different alfalfa varieties differ significantly in their adaptability to drought. Selecting drought-tolerant varieties with deep root systems, thick leaf cuticles, and strong stomatal regulation ability is a fundamental measure for coping with drought. For example, some local varieties and drought-tolerant bred varieties have better yield stability under drought conditions than ordinary varieties.
