In terms of agronomic regulation, rational close planting can reduce ineffective tillering and water competition; increasing phosphorus and potassium fertilizer application can improve cell osmotic adjustment ability; covering with straw or plastic film can reduce soil evaporation; adopting water-saving irrigation methods such as furrow irrigation and drip irrigation can deliver water directly to the root zone and reduce ineffective losses. In addition, in drought-prone areas, mixed sowing of alfalfa with gramineous forages can be promoted, utilizing the shallow root system and low water consumption characteristics of gramineous forages to improve overall grassland yield and stability.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

Based on the comprehensive results of multiple experiments, the effects of drought stress on alfalfa yield and nutritional quality exhibit an obvious threshold effect. Under mild drought, hay yield decreases by 10%–20%, crude protein content decreases by 1–2 percentage points, and relative feeding value decreases by 5%–10%, but water use efficiency may increase. Under moderate drought, yield decreases by 30%–40%, crude protein decreases by 2–4 percentage points, fiber components increase by 5–8 percentage points, and relative feeding value decreases by 10%–20%. Under severe drought, yield decreases by more than 50%, quality deteriorates significantly, and plants may even die. Adopting drought-tolerant varieties combined with regulated deficit irrigation and mulching for moisture conservation can stabilize alfalfa hay yield in drought years at 70%–80% of normal years, maintain crude protein content above 16%, keep relative feeding value above 120, and increase water use efficiency by 15%–25%. From an economic benefit perspective, although water-saving irrigation and drought-tolerant varieties increase some inputs, they reduce irrigation frequency and water consumption, lower production costs, and at the same time stabilize forage yield and quality and improve breeding benefits. In the arid region of northwestern China, alfalfa fields using comprehensive regulation techniques can save 80–120 cubic meters of water per mu per year, increase hay yield by 10%–15%, and increase net income by 200–300 yuan.

4 Conclusion

Drought stress has significant negative effects on the yield and nutritional quality of alfalfa, mainly manifested as reduced plant height and branch number, decreased hay yield, lower crude protein content, increased fiber components, and reduced relative feeding value. Mild drought can improve water use efficiency, but moderate or more severe drought causes simultaneous deterioration of yield and quality. Through comprehensive technical measures such as selecting drought-tolerant varieties, optimizing irrigation schedules, rational fertilization, and mulching for moisture conservation, alfalfa yield can be stabilized and relatively good nutritional quality maintained under drought conditions. It is recommended to promote regulated deficit irrigation and supporting technologies for drought-tolerant varieties in arid and semi-arid regions to achieve efficient and sustainable alfalfa production. In the future, research on drought thresholds and precision irrigation indicators in different ecological regions should be strengthened to provide stronger technical support for the alfalfa industry in responding to climate change.

title: Nitrous oxide emissions in response to straw incorporation is regulated by historical fertilization
text:
Abstract: To investigate the regulatory effects of long-term fertilization history on nitrous oxide (N₂O) emissions following straw return, this study was based on a 12-year long-term positioning experiment in the North China Plain. Three treatments were established: no fertilization (CK), chemical fertilizer alone (NPK), and chemical fertilizer combined with straw (NPKS). During the 2023–2024 wheat season, N₂O emission fluxes were monitored using the static chamber-gas chromatography method, and soil physicochemical properties and functional gene abundances were measured. The results showed that the cumulative N₂O emissions under NPKS were significantly reduced by 27.6% compared with NPK (P<0.05), while CK had the lowest emissions. Historical fertilization significantly altered the emission reduction effect of straw return: the N₂O reduction magnitude of straw return on the basis of long-term chemical fertilization (27.6%) was significantly higher than that under a no-fertilization history (12.4%). Soil nitrate nitrogen content was significantly positively correlated with N₂O emissions (r=0.73, P<0.01), while nosZ gene abundance was negatively correlated with N₂O emissions (r=-0.68, P<0.05). Structural equation modeling showed that historical fertilization indirectly affected N₂O emissions after straw return by regulating the soil carbon-to-nitrogen ratio and nosZ community abundance. This study indicates that long-term fertilization history is a key factor determining the N₂O emission reduction potential of straw return, and optimizing fertilization management can synergistically achieve carbon sequestration and emission reduction.

Keywords: nitrous oxide; straw return; long-term fertilization; nosZ gene; emission reduction

1 Introduction

Nitrous oxide (N₂O) is a potent greenhouse gas, with a 100-year global warming potential 298 times that of carbon dioxide, and it also participates in stratospheric ozone depletion. Agricultural activities contribute approximately 60% of global anthropogenic N₂O emissions, with farmland soils being the main emission source. As a measure promoted in China to improve cultivated land quality, straw return still has controversial effects on N₂O emissions: some studies report that return increases N₂O emissions, while others find emission reductions or no significant effect. This inconsistency may arise from differences in soil background conditions, especially the legacy effects of soil fertility formed by historical fertilization. Long-term fertilization can alter the soil organic carbon pool, microbial community structure, and the abundance of nitrogen-cycling functional genes, thereby regulating nitrogen transformation pathways during straw decomposition. However, systematic research is still lacking on how historical fertilization regulates the effect of straw return on N₂O emissions. Relying on a long-term positioning experiment, this study hypothesized that historical fertilization regulates N₂O emissions after straw return by changing the soil carbon-to-nitrogen ratio and the abundance of denitrification functional genes. By comparing the N₂O emission characteristics of straw return under different fertilization histories, this study aims to provide a theoretical basis for optimizing regional straw management strategies.

2 Materials and Methods

2.1 Experimental Site and Design

The experiment was located at the long-term positioning experimental station in Quzhou County, Hebei Province (36°52′N, 115°01′E), which has a warm temperate semi-humid monsoon climate, with an average annual temperature of 13.2°C and annual precipitation of 542 mm. The soil is fluvo-aquic soil, with 28% sand, 46% silt, and 26% clay, and initial organic matter of 12.3 g·kg⁻¹, total nitrogen of 0.78 g·kg⁻¹, and pH 8.1. The long-term experiment began in 2012 and included three treatments: CK (no fertilization), NPK (chemical fertilizer alone, N 240 kg·hm⁻², P₂O₅ 120 kg·hm⁻², K₂O 60 kg·hm⁻²), and NPKS (chemical fertilizer combined with straw, straw return amount 6 t·hm⁻²). Each treatment had 3 replicates, arranged in a randomized block design, with a plot area of 30 m². During the 2023–2024 wheat season, all treatments were set up with two microplots, straw return (6 t·hm⁻²) and no return, forming 6 treatment combinations, denoted as CK-S, CK-NS, NPK-S, NPK-NS, NPKS-S, and NPKS-NS. The wheat variety was Jimai 22, sown in October 2023 and harvested in June 2024.

2.2 Gas Sampling and Measurement

N₂O emission fluxes were monitored using the static chamber-gas chromatography method (Agilent 7890B). The sampling chamber was made of opaque PVC material (length × width × height = 50 cm × 50 cm × 50 cm), with a temperature sensor installed inside. Sampling was conducted every 7 d after sowing, with intensified sampling for 3 consecutive d after fertilization. Sampling time was from 9:00 to 11:00 a.m., and gas samples were collected at 0, 15, and 30 min. The formula for calculating N₂O emission flux was: F = ρ × (V/A) × (Δc/Δt) × (273/(273+T)), where ρ is the density of N₂O under standard conditions, V is the chamber volume, A is the base area, Δc/Δt is the rate of concentration change, and T is the chamber temperature. Cumulative emissions were integrated using linear interpolation.

2.3 Soil Sample Collection and Analysis

At wheat maturity, 0–20 cm topsoil samples were collected, with 5 points mixed per plot. Soil nitrate nitrogen and ammonium nitrogen were determined by 2 mol·L⁻¹ KCl extraction and continuous flow analyzer; organic carbon was determined by the potassium dichromate external heating method; total nitrogen was determined by the Kjeldahl method. Soil DNA was extracted using the FastDNA SPIN Kit, and the abundances of amoA, nirK, nirS, and nosZ genes were determined by real-time fluorescence quantitative PCR, with primers and conditions referring to published literature.

2.4 Data Analysis

SPSS 26.0 was used for one-way analysis of variance and Pearson correlation analysis, and structural equation modeling (SEM) was constructed using AMOS 24.0. Figures were drawn using Origin 2021.

3 Results and Analysis

3.1 N₂O Emission Dynamics

N₂O emission fluxes during the wheat season showed a double-peak pattern, with peaks appearing after basal fertilization following sowing and after topdressing at the jointing stage, respectively. The emission flux under NPK-NS was the highest (average 78.3 μg·m⁻²·h⁻¹), and that under NPKS-S was the lowest (32.6 μg·m⁻²·h⁻¹). Cumulative emissions were as follows: NPK-NS (2.14 kg·hm⁻²) > NPK-S (1.78 kg·hm⁻²) > NPKS-NS (1.52 kg·hm⁻²) > CK-NS (1.21 kg·hm⁻²) > NPKS-S (1.10 kg·hm⁻²) > CK-S (1.06 kg·hm⁻²). Compared with NPK-NS, NPKS-S and NPK-S reduced emissions by 48.6% and 16.8%, respectively. Under a long-term chemical fertilization history, straw return reduced N₂O by 27.6%, while under a no-fertilization history it reduced N₂O by only 12.4%.

3.2 Soil Physicochemical Properties and Functional Genes

Soil organic carbon (15.6 g·kg⁻¹) and total nitrogen (1.12 g·kg⁻¹) under NPKS were significantly higher than those under NPK and CK (P<0.05). After straw return, soil nitrate nitrogen content under NPKS-S (18.4 mg·kg⁻¹) was significantly lower than that under NPK-S (32.7 mg·kg⁻¹). The abundance of the nosZ gene was highest in NPKS-S (3.2×10⁸ copies·g⁻¹ dry soil), 86.4% higher than that in NPK-NS. The nirK/nosZ ratio was significantly positively correlated with cumulative N₂O emissions (r=0.81, P<0.01).

3.3 Correlation Analysis and Structural Equation Modeling

Cumulative N₂O emissions were positively correlated with soil nitrate nitrogen (r=0.73, P<0.01) and the nirK/nosZ ratio (r=0.81, P<0.01), and negatively correlated with nosZ abundance (r=-0.68, P<0.05) and soil carbon-to-nitrogen ratio (r=-0.59, P<0.05). SEM analysis showed that historical fertilization affected N₂O emissions through two pathways: first, directly increasing the soil carbon-to-nitrogen ratio and promoting the growth of the nosZ community (path coefficient 0.42); second, reducing nitrate nitrogen accumulation and indirectly inhibiting denitrification substrate supply (path coefficient -0.37). The total explanatory power of the model was 72%.

4 Discussion

This study found that the N₂O emission reduction effect of straw return was highly dependent on the historical fertilization background. In the "fertile" soil formed by long-term combined application of chemical fertilizer and straw, return further reduced N₂O emissions by 27.6%, whereas in soil with a no-fertilization history it reduced emissions by only 12.4%. This is consistent with the hypothesis that historical fertilization regulates the return effect by reshaping the soil carbon-nitrogen balance and microbial functional communities. Possible mechanisms include the following: First, long-term combined application of organic and inorganic fertilizers increased the soil carbon-to-nitrogen ratio, providing sufficient carbon sources for nosZ-type denitrifiers and promoting the reduction of N₂O to N₂. In this study, the nosZ abundance in the NPKS-S treatment was significantly the highest, supporting this explanation. Second, historical fertilization changed soil nitrogen transformation pathways. Long-term application of chemical fertilizer alone in the NPK treatment led to nitrate nitrogen accumulation, and straw return stimulated denitrification, producing more N₂O; in contrast, due to carbon-nitrogen synergy in the NPKS treatment, inorganic nitrogen was immobilized by microorganisms after return, reducing the availability of denitrification substrates. In addition, straw return improved soil structure and increased aeration, which may inhibit the denitrification process. It is worth noting that CK had the lowest N₂O emissions, but this was low emissions under low productivity, not an ideal management goal. Overall, implementing straw return on the basis of long-term chemical fertilization can both maintain crop yield and achieve N₂O emission reduction, making it a relatively superior management strategy. The limitation of this study is that it monitored only one wheat season, and future multi-year and multi-site verification is needed.

5 Conclusions

(1) The effect of straw return on N₂O emissions was significantly regulated by historical fertilization. The emission reduction magnitude of return under a history of long-term combined application of chemical fertilizer and straw (27.6%) was significantly higher than that under a no-fertilization history (12.4%). (2) N₂O emissions were positively correlated with soil nitrate nitrogen content and the nirK/nosZ ratio, and negatively correlated with nosZ gene abundance and the carbon-to-nitrogen ratio. (3) Historical fertilization indirectly inhibited N₂O emissions after straw return by increasing the soil carbon-to-nitrogen ratio and nosZ community abundance. It is recommended to promote straw return on the basis of long-term combined application of chemical fertilizers and organic materials, so as to synergistically achieve soil carbon sequestration and greenhouse gas emission reduction.

title: Unveiling the comparative efficacy and tolerability of comprehensive treatments for migraine: A protocol of systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis
text:
Revealing the Comparative Efficacy and Tolerability of Comprehensive Treatment Regimens for Migraine: A Study Protocol for Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis

Abstract

Objective: Migraine is a highly disabling primary headache disorder with diverse clinical treatment approaches, including acute-phase medication and preventive treatment. However, the relative efficacy and tolerability among different comprehensive treatment regimens lack systematic comparison. This study aims to comprehensively evaluate the comparative efficacy and tolerability of multiple comprehensive treatment regimens for migraine through systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis, providing evidence-based support for clinical decision-making. Methods: Randomized controlled trials on migraine treatment will be systematically searched in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, and other databases. Primary outcomes include headache attack frequency, acute-phase pain relief rate, monthly headache days, and adverse event withdrawal rate. The Cochrane risk of bias assessment tool will be used to evaluate the quality of included studies, and Bayesian network meta-analysis will be employed for indirect comparison among multiple regimens, calculating the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA). Expected Results: This study will clarify the relative advantages and disadvantages of different comprehensive treatment regimens in terms of efficacy and tolerability, and identify the optimal intervention combinations. Conclusion: This study protocol is expected to provide high-level evidence support for individualized treatment of migraine and promote optimization of clinical practice.

1. Introduction

Migraine is a recurrent neurovascular disorder with a global prevalence of approximately 14%, and is listed by the World Health Organization as one of the disabling diseases. Its typical features include unilateral pulsating headache, often accompanied by nausea, vomiting, photophobia, and phonophobia, severely affecting patients' quality of life and causing significant socioeconomic burden. Current clinical treatment strategies are divided into two major categories: acute-phase analgesia and preventive treatment. Acute-phase medications include nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, triptans, gepants, etc.; preventive medications include beta-blockers, antiepileptic drugs, CGRP monoclonal antibodies, and botulinum toxin, etc. In addition, non-pharmacological therapies such as cognitive behavioral therapy, acupuncture, and neuromodulation are gradually being applied in comprehensive management.

Despite the abundance of treatment options, direct comparison studies among different regimens are limited. Traditional meta-analysis can only handle pairwise direct comparisons and is difficult to integrate evidence from multiple regimens. Bayesian network meta-analysis, by constructing a mixed treatment comparison model, can achieve indirect and mixed comparisons among multiple interventions and provide probabilistic rankings, having become an important tool for comparative efficacy research. However, there is currently a lack of systematic review and network meta-analysis protocols targeting comprehensive treatment regimens for migraine. This study intends to develop a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis protocol aimed at comparing the efficacy and tolerability of different comprehensive treatment regimens, providing reference for clinical guideline development and individualized treatment.

2. Key Technical Analysis

2.1 Literature Search and Screening Strategy

This study will follow the PRISMA-P statement to develop the systematic review protocol. Databases to be searched include PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, as well as Chinese databases such as CNKI, Wanfang, and VIP. The search period will be from database inception to December 2025. English search terms include "migraine," "treatment," "randomized controlled trial," "network meta-analysis," etc.; Chinese search terms correspond to "偏头痛," "治疗," "随机对照试验," etc. Inclusion criteria are: ① Participants are migraine patients meeting the International Classification of Headache Disorders criteria; ② Interventions include at least one pharmacological or non-pharmacological comprehensive treatment regimen; ③ Controls are placebo, usual care, or other active interventions; ④ Outcomes include at least headache frequency, acute-phase relief rate, monthly headache days, or adverse event withdrawal rate; ⑤ Study design is randomized controlled trial. Duplicate publications, incomplete data, and non-randomized studies will be excluded. Two researchers will independently screen and extract data, with disagreements resolved through third-party arbitration.

2.2 Risk of Bias Assessment and Quality of Evidence Grading

The risk of bias assessment tool recommended by the Cochrane Collaboration (RoB 2.0) will be used to evaluate the quality of included randomized controlled trials, covering five domains: randomization process, deviations from intended interventions, missing outcome data, outcome measurement, and selective reporting of results. Simultaneously, the GRADE system will be used to grade the quality of evidence bodies formed by network meta-analysis, classified into four levels: high, moderate, low, and very low. Evidence quality will consider factors such as limitations, indirectness, inconsistency, imprecision, and publication bias. Through the above assessments, the reliability of study conclusions and clinical applicability will be ensured.

2.3 Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis Model Construction

A random effects model under the Bayesian framework will be used for network meta-analysis. Assuming heterogeneity exists among studies, parameter estimation will be performed through Markov chain Monte Carlo methods. Model consistency will be tested through the node-splitting method; if inconsistency exists, an inconsistency model or meta-regression will be used to explore the sources. For binary outcomes (such as relief rate and withdrawal rate), odds ratios and their 95% credible intervals will be calculated; for continuous outcomes (such as headache frequency and monthly headache days), mean differences or standardized mean differences and their 95% credible intervals will be calculated. Interventions will be ranked through the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA), with SUCRA values closer to 1 indicating a better regimen. All analyses will be completed using R software (gemtc, rjags packages) or Stata software.

2.4 Heterogeneity, Sensitivity, and Publication Bias Analysis

The I² statistic will be used to assess between-study heterogeneity, with I² > 50% considered as significant heterogeneity. If heterogeneity is high, subgroup analyses (e.g., stratified by migraine type, age, sex, treatment duration) and meta-regression analysis will be conducted to explore potential effect modifiers. Sensitivity analysis will test the robustness of results by sequentially excluding studies or changing model assumptions (such as replacing the random effects model with a fixed effects model). Publication bias will be assessed using comparison-adjusted funnel plots and Egger's test. If significant publication bias is found, the trim-and-fill method will be used for correction. Through the above analyses, the credibility and generalizability of results will be enhanced.

3. Results and Benefit Analysis

This study is expected to include approximately 50 to 80 randomized controlled trials, involving more than 20 intervention regimens. Main results will include: ① Relative efficacy ranking of different comprehensive treatment regimens in reducing monthly headache days; ② Comparison of complete acute-phase pain relief rates; ③ Ranking of treatment withdrawal rates due to adverse events; ④ SUCRA probabilistic ranking plots and cluster ranking plots, visually displaying the trade-off between efficacy and tolerability. It is expected that CGRP monoclonal antibodies combined with acute-phase triptans may perform better in terms of efficacy and tolerability; non-pharmacological therapies such as cognitive behavioral therapy combined with conventional preventive medications may have advantages in medium- to long-term management. The benefits of this study are reflected in: First, providing clinicians with quantitative evidence for multi-regimen comparison to assist individualized decision-making; Second, providing indirect evidence for cost-effectiveness analysis for health policy makers; Third, identifying current evidence gaps to guide future research directions; Fourth, promoting the application and dissemination of Bayesian network meta-analysis methods in the headache field.

4. Conclusion

This study protocol designs a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis aimed at comprehensively comparing the efficacy and tolerability of comprehensive treatment regimens for migraine. Through rigorous literature search, quality assessment, and statistical modeling, it is expected to generate probabilistic rankings of relative efficacy among multiple interventions, providing high-level evidence-based evidence for clinical practice. This protocol has characteristics of methodological rigor, intuitive results, and strong generalizability, and is expected to promote the optimization and individualized development of migraine treatment strategies. Future research can further integrate real-world data and cost-effectiveness analysis to improve the evidence system.

title: Deficit irrigation and sustainable water-resource strategies in agriculture for China's food security
text:
Impact of Deficit Irrigation and Sustainable Agricultural Water Resource Strategies on China's Food Security

Abstract: Objective: To explore the role and potential of deficit irrigation (DI) technology and sustainable water resource management strategies in ensuring China's food security. Methods: Based on field experiments and regional statistical data from 2018–2023 in the North China Plain, the arid region of Northwest China, and Northeast China, a water use efficiency (WUE) and grain yield response model was constructed. Three treatments were established: full irrigation (FI), moderate deficit irrigation (MDI, 65% ETc), and severe deficit irrigation (SDI, 50% ETc), to analyze the effects of different irrigation strategies on wheat and maize yields and water resource consumption. Results: Compared with FI, wheat and maize yields under MDI decreased by 8.3% and 10.7%, respectively, but WUE increased by 22.4% and 18.9%, respectively, and irrigation water use decreased by 31.6%; under SDI, yield reductions reached 21.5%–26.8%, with no significant improvement in WUE. Regional simulations indicated that if MDI were extended to 60% of the irrigated area in the North China Plain, approximately 4.8 billion m³ of water could be saved annually, with total grain production losses controlled within 4.2%. Conclusion: Moderate deficit irrigation can significantly enhance water resource sustainability while ensuring food security. It is recommended to integrate regional water resource endowments, crop variety optimization, and smart irrigation technologies to establish a differentiated deficit irrigation strategy system.

Keywords: deficit irrigation; sustainable water resource utilization; food security; water use efficiency; North China Plain

 1 Introduction

China supports nearly 18% of the global population with approximately 6% of the world's freshwater resources and 9% of its arable land, and food security has always been an important cornerstone of national security. However, issues such as the uneven spatiotemporal distribution of water resources, the excessively high proportion of agricultural water use (approximately 62%), and groundwater overexploitation are becoming increasingly severe. The area of groundwater depression cones in the North China Plain has exceeded 70,000 km², and ecological water use in the inland river basins of Northwest China has been severely encroached upon. Against this background, how to ensure stable and increased grain production under limited water resource constraints has become a core proposition in agricultural water resource management.

Deficit irrigation (DI), as a strategy of actively regulating irrigation water volume, achieves the goal of "trading water for efficiency" by imposing moderate water stress during non-sensitive periods or tolerant stages of crop growth. Numerous studies have shown that DI can significantly improve water use efficiency (WUE) while causing only a small decrease in yield, but systematic quantification of its applicability, thresholds, and macro-level effects on food security across different ecological zones in China is still lacking. Through multi-site field experiments and regional scenario simulations, this paper evaluates the effects of DI strategies on grain yield, WUE, and regional water resource balance, and proposes sustainable water resource management countermeasures.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Experimental Sites and Design

Experiments were conducted from 2018 to 2023 in three typical ecological zones: Shijiazhuang, Hebei (North China Plain, winter wheat–summer maize rotation), Wuwei, Gansu (arid region of Northwest China, monoculture spring maize), and Harbin, Heilongjiang (semi-humid region of Northeast China, monoculture spring maize). The soil types were fluvo-aquic soil, gray desert soil, and black soil, respectively. Three irrigation treatments were established at each site: full irrigation (FI, 100% ETc), moderate deficit irrigation (MDI, 65% ETc), and severe deficit irrigation (SDI, 50% ETc), using a randomized complete block design with 4 replications. Irrigation was applied by drip irrigation, and ETc was calculated according to the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith method.

 2.2 Measurement Indicators and Methods

Yield: Actual harvest yields were measured at maturity and converted to standard moisture content (13% for wheat, 14% for maize). WUE = grain yield / total water consumption (ET). Water consumption was calculated using the water balance method. Meteorological data were obtained from automatic weather stations at each site. Regional simulations used the CROPWAT model and GIS spatial analysis, based on county-level statistical yearbook data from 2018–2023, with scenarios set for MDI extension proportions (30%, 60%, 90%).

 2.3 Data Processing

SPSS 26.0 was used for analysis of variance (ANOVA), with Duncan's multiple range test (P<0.05). Regional simulations were calculated using Python 3.9.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Effects of Deficit Irrigation on Crop Yield

As shown in Table 1, compared with FI, under MDI treatment the winter wheat yield in Shijiazhuang decreased from 8.42 t/hm² to 7.72 t/hm² (-8.3%), and summer maize decreased from 9.15 t/hm² to 8.17 t/hm² (-10.7%); spring maize in Wuwei decreased from 12.36 t/hm² to 10.98 t/hm² (-11.2%); and spring maize in Harbin decreased from 11.87 t/hm² to 10.72 t/hm² (-9.7%). Under SDI treatment, yield reductions expanded significantly, reaching 21.5%–26.8%. ANOVA showed that the yield difference between MDI and FI was significant (P<0.05), but the difference between MDI and SDI was also significant (P<0.05), indicating that 65% ETc is the critical threshold at which yield loss remains controllable.

 3.2 Water Use Efficiency and Water-Saving Effects

Under MDI treatment, WUE improved significantly: wheat WUE in Shijiazhuang increased from 1.42 kg/m³ to 1.74 kg/m³ (+22.4%), and summer maize increased from 1.68 kg/m³ to 2.00 kg/m³ (+18.9%); spring maize WUE in Wuwei increased from 1.85 kg/m³ to 2.21 kg/m³ (+19.5%). In terms of irrigation water use, MDI reduced water use by 31.6%–34.2% compared with FI, and SDI reduced it by 48.7%–51.3%. Notably, the WUE improvement under SDI (+8.2%–12.4%) was far lower than that under MDI, indicating that excessive deficit caused yield losses exceeding water-saving benefits.

 3.3 Scenario Simulation of Regional Water Resources and Food Security

Taking the North China Plain as an example, if MDI covered 60% of the irrigated area (approximately 7.2 million hm²), annual irrigation water use could be reduced by approximately 4.8 billion m³, equivalent to 1.2 times the annual water transfer volume of the middle route of the South-to-North Water Diversion Project; total grain production loss would be approximately 4.2%, but groundwater overexploitation could be reduced by 37%. If extended to 90% of the area, water savings would reach 7.2 billion m³, but yield loss would rise to 6.8%, requiring offsetting through variety improvement and agronomic compensatory measures. Under the scenario of 60% MDI extension in the arid region of Northwest China, water savings would be approximately 1.9 billion m³, yield loss would be 5.1%, and the rate of ecological water encroachment would decrease by 12%.

 4 Discussion

This study confirms that moderate deficit irrigation (65% ETc) can achieve an 18%–22% increase in WUE and more than 30% water savings while keeping yield loss below 12%, which is consistent with the conclusions of most DI studies domestically and internationally. The physiological mechanism lies in the fact that moderate water stress can promote deeper root growth, improve stomatal regulation capacity, optimize assimilate distribution to grains, and reduce ineffective transpiration. However, the effects of DI are significantly influenced by crop type, growth stage, soil texture, and climatic conditions. For example, wheat is sensitive to water during the jointing stage, and MDI should avoid this stage; for maize, moderate deficit during the grain-filling stage is more beneficial.

From the macro perspective of food security, the DI strategy is not "zero-cost." If MDI were extended to 60% of China's major irrigation districts, total grain production could decline by 3.5%–5.0%, which would need to be offset through yield improvement (varieties + dense planting + precision fertilization) and reserve regulation. At the same time, the sustainability of DI depends on smart irrigation systems, soil moisture monitoring, and farmer acceptance. At the policy level, it is recommended to incorporate water-saving indicators into the food security assessment system, establish a "water-saving compensation + yield insurance" linkage mechanism, and prioritize the extension of MDI in water resource overloaded areas.

The limitations of this study are: the field experiment period was relatively short and did not fully consider extreme climate years; the regional simulation did not couple socioeconomic and farmer behavioral factors. Future research should conduct long-term positioned experiments and multi-scale integrated modeling.

 5 Conclusions

(1) Moderate deficit irrigation (65% ETc) can achieve yield losses of 8.3%–11.2%, WUE improvements of 18.9%–22.4%, and irrigation water savings of 31.6%–34.2% in China's major grain-producing regions, making it a feasible strategy that balances food security and water resource sustainability. (2) Although severe deficit irrigation (50% ETc) saves more water, yield losses exceed 21% and WUE improvement is limited, making it unsuitable for large-scale extension. (3) Regional simulations show that under the scenario of 60% MDI extension in the North China Plain, annual water savings of approximately 4.8 billion m³ can be achieved, with total grain production losses controlled within 4.2%, significantly alleviating groundwater overexploitation. (4) It is recommended to build an integrated management system of "regionally differentiated deficit irrigation + intelligent monitoring + variety adaptation + policy incentives" to support the dual goals of China's food security and sustainable agricultural water resource utilization.

title: Non-symbolic and symbolic number lines are dissociated
text:
The Separation of Non-Symbolic and Symbolic Number Lines

Abstract: The number line estimation task is widely used to study human numerical representation. The traditional view holds that non-symbolic (e.g., dot arrays) and symbolic (e.g., Arabic numerals) quantity processing share the same mental number line. This paper systematically reviews recent behavioral and neuroscience evidence to analyze the dissociation between the two in spatial mapping. Key technical analysis indicates that the non-symbolic number line is governed by the approximate number system and exhibits logarithmic compression characteristics, whereas the symbolic number line relies on language and educational experience and shows a linearization trend. The two exhibit significant dissociation in developmental trajectories, task effects, and brain region activation. Analysis of results and benefits points out that this dissociation has important implications for mathematics education, dyscalculia intervention, and human-computer interaction design. The conclusion holds that non-symbolic and symbolic number lines are not a single representation but separable processing systems.

Keywords: number line; non-symbolic quantity; symbolic quantity; approximate number system; mental representation

1 Introduction

The number line estimation task requires participants to locate a presented quantity (e.g., a set of dots or an Arabic numeral) on a line segment. This task is widely used to assess the precision of numerical representation and spatial mapping ability. Early research tended to assume that whether processing non-symbolic dot arrays or symbolic numerals, individuals rely on a common mental number line, whose mapping follows logarithmic or linear rules. However, in recent years, increasing evidence indicates that non-symbolic and symbolic number lines exhibit systematic dissociation in behavioral performance, developmental trajectories, and neural mechanisms. This dissociation challenges the "single number line" hypothesis and has important implications for mathematical cognition and educational practice.

This paper aims to systematically analyze the key technical evidence for the dissociation between non-symbolic and symbolic number lines, elaborating from five aspects: task effects, developmental trajectories, neural foundations, individual differences, and computational models, and to discuss their applied benefits.

2 Key Technical Analysis

2.1 Dissociation of Task Effects and Estimation Patterns

In the number line estimation task, non-symbolic quantities are typically presented as dot arrays or sequences, whereas symbolic quantities are presented as Arabic numerals. Behavioral studies have found that non-symbolic number line estimation conforms more to a logarithmic compression model, in which the subjective distance between small quantities is larger and the subjective distance between large quantities is smaller. For example, participants tend to locate 10 dots near the middle of the line segment rather than at one-tenth of the line according to linear proportion. In contrast, symbolic number line estimation is closer to a linear model in adults, especially after receiving formal education, with linear fit goodness significantly improving.

This dissociation of task effects indicates that non-symbolic quantity processing depends on the approximate number system, whose representation has inherent compressibility; symbolic number processing is acquired through cultural learning, gradually establishing a linear spatial mapping. The two are not different input forms of the same system but separable processing pathways.

2.2 Dissociation of Developmental Trajectories

Longitudinal studies show that non-symbolic number line estimation ability emerges in early childhood, and its precision improves slowly with age, mainly constrained by non-symbolic quantity discrimination ability. Symbolic number line estimation ability develops rapidly during school age and is closely related to number order and number line instruction in the mathematics curriculum. For example, 5-year-old children already exhibit stable logarithmic mapping on the non-symbolic number line but remain close to chance level on the symbolic number line; by age 8, symbolic number line estimation has become significantly linearized, whereas the non-symbolic number line still maintains logarithmic characteristics.

This developmental asynchrony further supports the dissociation hypothesis: the non-symbolic number line is a product of early intuitive quantity representation, whereas the symbolic number line is a construction of later cultural learning.

2.3 Dissociation of Neural Foundations

Functional magnetic resonance imaging studies show that non-symbolic quantity processing mainly activates the right intraparietal sulcus and prefrontal regions, related to spatial attention and approximate quantity comparison. Symbolic number processing relies more on the left intraparietal sulcus, angular gyrus, and language-related brain regions (such as the left superior temporal gyrus). Transcranial magnetic stimulation studies further indicate that inhibiting the left intraparietal sulcus selectively impairs symbolic number line estimation without affecting non-symbolic number line tasks; inhibiting the right intraparietal sulcus produces the opposite pattern.

In addition, event-related potential studies have found that non-symbolic quantity deviation appears early (approximately 200 ms) as a right-hemisphere negative wave, whereas symbolic number deviation appears late (approximately 400 ms) as a left-hemisphere positive wave. These neural findings indicate that the two are dissociated in both temporal course and spatial localization.

2.4 Individual Differences and Dyscalculia

In children with dyscalculia, non-symbolic number line estimation is usually normal or mildly impaired, whereas symbolic number line estimation is significantly behind. Conversely, some children with developmental language disorder perform poorly on the symbolic number line but are relatively intact on the non-symbolic number line. This double dissociation pattern provides strong individual-difference evidence for the dissociation hypothesis.

Moreover, in normal adults, non-symbolic number line estimation precision correlates with approximate number system acuity, whereas symbolic number line estimation precision correlates with mathematical achievement and number order knowledge. The correlation between the two is low, further indicating their separability.

2.5 Differentiation of Computational Models

Regarding computational models, the non-symbolic number line often adopts a logarithmic Gaussian model or a scalar variability model, emphasizing the noise and compression characteristics of quantity representation. The symbolic number line often adopts a linear regression model or a Bayesian learning model, emphasizing the calibrating role of educational experience on mapping. Recent hybrid models have attempted to integrate the two, but comparisons of goodness of fit show that dissociation models outperform single models. For example, in adult data, the prediction error of the dual-system model for non-symbolic and symbolic number line estimation is significantly lower than that of the single-system model.

3 Analysis of Results and Benefits

The above dissociation phenomena bring multiple benefits. First, in mathematics education, teachers should distinguish training strategies for non-symbolic and symbolic number lines. The non-symbolic number line can enhance intuitive number sense through dot array comparison and approximate estimation games; the symbolic number line requires number line and number order exercises to promote linear mapping. The two cannot substitute for each other.

Second, in dyscalculia intervention, assessment should include both non-symbolic and symbolic number line tasks to identify different subtypes. For non-symbolic number line deficits, approximate quantity training can be used; for symbolic number line deficits, number line positioning and verbal coding training can be used.

Third, in human-computer interaction design, quantity interfaces for children or non-literate users should prioritize the non-symbolic number line, whereas data visualization for educated adults can adopt the symbolic number line. The dissociation principle helps optimize interface mapping and reduce cognitive load.

Finally, in the field of artificial intelligence, simulating the dissociation between non-symbolic and symbolic number lines can provide inspiration for developing neural networks closer to human numerical cognition, such as separate approximate quantity modules and symbolic mapping modules.

4 Conclusion

Non-symbolic and symbolic number lines exhibit systematic dissociation in task effects, developmental trajectories, neural foundations, individual differences, and computational models. This dissociation indicates that human numerical representation is not a single mental number line but separable processing pathways jointly constituted by the approximate number system and the symbolic number system. Future research should further explore the interaction mechanisms between the two and how educational experience modulates this dissociation. At the applied level, acknowledging the dissociation helps design more precise mathematics education programs, dyscalculia intervention strategies, and human-computer interaction interfaces. Therefore, the separation of non-symbolic and symbolic number lines is not only a theoretical issue but also has broad practical significance.

title: RNAi-mediated SMV P3 cistron silencing confers significantly enhanced resistance to multiple Potyvirus strains and isolates in transgenic soybean
text:
Abstract: Soybean mosaic virus (SMV) is one of the most devastating viruses affecting soybean production, and breeding broad-spectrum resistant cultivars is an effective approach to controlling this disease. In this study, targeting the SMV P3 cistron, we constructed an RNAi plant expression vector pCAMBIA3301-P3hp containing an inverted repeat sequence of the conserved region of the P3 gene, and transformed soybean cultivar Williams 82 via Agrobacterium-mediated transformation, obtaining 12 independent transgenic lines. Molecular detection of the T3 generation showed that the target siRNA was stably expressed in transgenic lines, and no P3 protein accumulation was detected. Disease resistance evaluation revealed that transgenic lines exhibited significantly enhanced resistance to four strains/isolates including SMV-SC3, SMV-SC7, SMV-SC15, and SMV-N, with disease indices reduced by 62.3%–81.7% compared to wild type, and viral accumulation decreased by more than 70%. Under field natural infection conditions, the yield loss rate of transgenic lines was reduced by approximately 45 percentage points compared to the control. These results demonstrate that RNAi-mediated silencing of the SMV P3 cistron confers broad-spectrum resistance to multiple Potyvirus strains/isolates in soybean, providing a new strategy for antiviral breeding in soybean.

Keywords: Soybean mosaic virus; RNA interference; P3 cistron; Broad-spectrum resistance; Transgenic soybean

 1 Introduction

Soybean (Glycine max (L.) Merr.) is an important oilseed and food crop in China, and its production security is directly related to national food security and oil supply. However, soybean mosaic disease occurs in all major soybean-producing regions worldwide, causing yield reductions of 10%–30% in normal years and over 50% in severe disease years, with significant deterioration in seed quality of diseased plants. SMV belongs to the genus Potyvirus within the family Potyviridae, and its genome is a single-stranded positive-sense RNA encoding a polyprotein that is cleaved by self-encoded proteases into multiple mature proteins including P1, HC-Pro, P3, P3N-PIPO, CI, 6K1, 6K2, NIa-VPg, NIa-Pro, NIb, and CP. Among these, the P3 protein not only participates in the formation of the viral replication complex but is also closely associated with viral movement in the host and pathogenicity, and the P3 coding region is relatively conserved among Potyviruses, making it an ideal antiviral target.

Traditional disease resistance breeding mainly relies on natural resistance genes (such as the Rsv series), but such genes often exhibit strain-specific resistance and are prone to losing resistance due to viral strain variation when facing the highly variable population structure of SMV. RNA interference (RNAi) technology induces sequence-specific gene silencing by introducing hairpin RNA (hpRNA) homologous to the viral genome, enabling efficient degradation of homologous viruses. Studies have shown that RNAi strategies targeting Potyvirus CP, HC-Pro, NIb, and other genes can significantly improve plant disease resistance; however, RNAi research targeting the P3 cistron in soybean has rarely been reported, and whether it can provide broad-spectrum resistance against multiple strains still requires systematic evaluation.

In this study, targeting the conserved region of the SMV P3 cistron, we constructed an RNAi expression vector and transformed soybean, and systematically evaluated the resistance performance of transgenic lines against multiple SMV strains/isolates, aiming to provide theoretical basis and germplasm materials for broad-spectrum antiviral breeding in soybean.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Plant Materials and Virus Strains

The soybean cultivar used was Williams 82 (SMV-susceptible cultivar), preserved in our laboratory. SMV strains SMV-SC3, SMV-SC7, SMV-SC15, and SMV-N were kindly provided by the National Center for Soybean Improvement, Nanjing Agricultural University, representing the major epidemic strains in the Huang-Huai-Hai region, Yangtze River basin, and Northeast production areas of China, respectively. Viruses were purified by single-lesion isolation and propagated and maintained on the susceptible soybean cultivar Nannong 1138-2.

 2.2 RNAi Vector Construction

Based on SMV P3 gene sequences in the NCBI database (accession numbers: NC_002634.1, etc.), multiple sequence alignment was performed using DNAMAN software, and a highly conserved 312 bp fragment at the 5′ end of the P3 coding region (corresponding to nucleotides 45–356 of P3) was selected as the RNAi target. Using SMV-SC3 cDNA as template, specific primers containing Xho I and Kpn I restriction sites were designed for PCR amplification. The amplified products were cloned in forward and reverse orientations into the pKANNIBAL intermediate vector to form an intron-spaced inverted repeat sequence, and the P3hp fragment was excised by Not I digestion and inserted downstream of the 35S promoter of the plant expression vector pCAMBIA3301 to construct pCAMBIA3301-P3hp. After confirmation by restriction digestion and sequencing, the construct was transformed into Agrobacterium tumefaciens EHA105.

 2.3 Soybean Genetic Transformation and Regeneration

The Agrobacterium-mediated cotyledonary node transformation method was used. Cotyledonary node explants from 5–7 d-old sterile seedlings were co-cultured with Agrobacterium suspension at OD₆₀₀=0.6 for 30 min, then transferred to co-cultivation medium containing 200 μmol/L acetosyringone for 3 d in the dark. Subsequently, they were transferred to shoot induction medium containing 5 mg/L glufosinate (PPT) for selective culture for 4 weeks. After 2–3 rounds of subculture selection, resistant shoots were transferred to rooting medium. Rooted plantlets were acclimatized and transplanted to the greenhouse with routine water and fertilizer management.

 2.4 Molecular Detection of Transgenic Plants

Young leaves from T1–T3 generation transgenic plants were collected, and genomic DNA was extracted by the CTAB method. PCR detection was performed using specific primers for the 35S promoter and P3hp fragment. Total RNA was extracted by the Trizol method, and stem-loop RT-PCR was used to detect P3-specific siRNA expression levels, with U6 snRNA as internal reference. Total protein was also extracted, and Western blot analysis was performed using SMV P3 polyclonal antibody.

 2.5 Disease Resistance Evaluation

The rub inoculation method was used to inoculate SMV at the first true leaf stage of T3 generation transgenic lines and wild-type plants. Thirty plants were inoculated per line, with 3 replicates. Disease indices were investigated 21 d after inoculation, with grading standards as follows: grade 0, no symptoms; grade 1, mild mosaic; grade 2, obvious mosaic; grade 3, severe mosaic with dwarfing; grade 4, death. Disease index = ∑ (number of diseased plants at each grade × grade value) / (total number of plants investigated × 4) × 100. Meanwhile, qRT-PCR was used to detect SMV CP gene expression in systemic leaves, with soybean Actin as internal reference, to calculate relative viral accumulation.

 2.6 Field Yield Trait Evaluation

Field plot trials were conducted in an isolated screen house. Each line was planted in 3 rows, with a row length of 3 m and row spacing of 0.6 m, arranged in a randomized complete block design with 3 replicates. After artificial inoculation with SMV-SC7, plants were harvested at maturity for yield component measurement, and pod number per plant, 100-seed weight, and plot yield were determined to calculate yield loss rate.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Obtainment and Molecular Identification of Transgenic Soybean Plants

Through Agrobacterium-mediated transformation, a total of 38 PPT-resistant regenerated plants were obtained. PCR detection showed that 12 of them could amplify target bands of expected size, with a positive rate of 31.6%. After T1 generation self-pollination harvest, T2 generation underwent PPT screening and PCR verification, yielding 9 positive lines, designated P3i-1 to P3i-9. Molecular detection of the T3 generation showed that all 9 lines were stably inherited, and stem-loop RT-PCR detected high-level expression of P3-specific siRNA, with lines P3i-3 and P3i-7 showing the highest relative siRNA expression levels at 18.6-fold and 16.3-fold that of wild type, respectively. Western blot analysis showed that no P3 protein accumulation was detected in transgenic lines, while P3 protein expression was evident in inoculated wild-type plants.

 3.2 Resistance Performance of Transgenic Lines Against Multiple SMV Strains

Investigation results at 21 d after inoculation showed that wild-type control plants exhibited high susceptibility to all 4 SMV strains, with disease indices ranging from 68.5 to 79.3, and leaves showing typical mosaic, crinkling, and dwarfing symptoms. In contrast, transgenic lines showed significantly reduced disease indices (P<0.01), with line P3i-3 exhibiting disease indices of 14.2, 18.6, 16.8, and 21.3 against SMV-SC3, SMV-SC7, SMV-SC15, and SMV-N, respectively, representing reductions of 76.2%–81.7% compared to wild type; line P3i-7 showed disease indices of 16.5–24.7, representing reductions of 62.3%–76.8%. Some variation in resistance existed among different lines, but all exhibited high resistance to disease resistance levels.

qRT-PCR analysis showed that the relative expression of SMV CP gene in systemic leaves of transgenic lines decreased by 70.3%–89.6% compared to wild type. Among them, line P3i-3 had the lowest viral accumulation against SMV-SC7, at only 10.4% of wild type. Correlation analysis revealed a significant negative correlation between siRNA expression level and viral accumulation (r=-0.83, P<0.05), indicating that RNAi silencing efficiency is closely related to disease resistance.

 3.3 Field Yield Traits of Transgenic Lines

Under field inoculation conditions, wild-type control plants had pod number per plant, 100-seed weight, and plot yield of 18.6, 14.2 g, and 286.5 g, respectively, with a yield loss rate of 52.3%. Transgenic lines P3i-3 and P3i-7 had pod numbers per plant of 32.4 and 29.8, 100-seed weights of 17.8 g and 17.1 g, and plot yields of 498.6 g and 472.3 g, with yield loss rates of 8.7% and 13.5%, respectively, representing reductions of approximately 45 percentage points compared to wild-type control. Agronomic trait observations showed no significant differences between transgenic lines and wild type in plant height, growth period, and other aspects, with no adverse agronomic effects observed.

 4 Discussion

The P3 protein of Potyvirus is a key factor in viral replication and movement, and its coding region has relatively high sequence conservation among different SMV strains. In this study, the 312 bp conserved region at the 5′ end of the P3 gene was selected as the RNAi target, which covers the N-terminal transmembrane domain of the P3 protein and part of the P3N-PIPO overlapping region, playing important functions in viral replication complex assembly and intercellular movement. Results showed that this strategy could simultaneously target multiple SMV strains, and the induced siRNA could efficiently degrade P3 mRNA, thereby blocking the viral infection process. This is consistent with previous studies on RNAi targeting HC-Pro or CP genes, but P3 cistron silencing may have greater advantages in broad-spectrum resistance because its sequence variability is lower than that of the CP gene.

It is noteworthy that resistance varied among different transgenic lines, with P3i-3 performing best, having the highest siRNA expression and lowest viral accumulation. This indicates that RNAi-mediated disease resistance has a dose effect, and efficient accumulation of siRNA is key to achieving strong resistance. Furthermore, no P3 protein accumulation was detected in this study, indicating that the post-transcriptional gene silencing (PTGS) mechanism was effectively activated rather than protein-level inhibition.

Compared with Rsv-mediated strain-specific resistance, the RNAi strategy does not depend on recognition between host resistance genes and viral effectors, but directly degrades viral RNA based on sequence homology, making it less prone to losing resistance due to viral strain variation. However, long-term cultivation of transgenic resistant cultivars may exert selection pressure on viral populations, leading to target sequence variation. Therefore, it is recommended to adopt multi-target (e.g., combined P3 and HC-Pro) RNAi strategies to delay the risk of resistance breakdown.

This study still has certain limitations: only 4 SMV strains were evaluated, not covering all epidemic strains; field trials were conducted for only one year and require multi-year and multi-location validation. Additionally, food safety and environmental safety evaluation of transgenic soybean still need to be systematically carried out.

 5 Conclusion

In this study, we successfully constructed an RNAi plant expression vector targeting the SMV P3 cistron and obtained 9 stably inherited transgenic soybean lines. P3-specific siRNA was expressed at high levels in transgenic lines, and P3 protein accumulation was completely suppressed. Disease resistance evaluation showed that transgenic lines exhibited significantly enhanced resistance to four strains/isolates including SMV-SC3, SMV-SC7, SMV-SC15, and SMV-N, with disease indices reduced by 62.3%–81.7%, viral accumulation decreased by more than 70%, and field yield loss rate reduced by approximately 45 percentage points. These results demonstrate that RNAi-mediated silencing of the SMV P3 cistron confers broad-spectrum resistance to multiple Potyvirus strains/isolates in soybean, providing an effective strategy and germplasm resources for antiviral molecular breeding in soybean.

title: Slc7a11 Modulated by POU2F1 is Involved in Pigmentation in Rabbit
text:
Slc7a11 Is Regulated by POU2F1 and Participates in Rabbit Coat Color Formation

Abstract: To investigate the function and transcriptional regulatory mechanism of solute carrier family 7 member 11 (Slc7a11) in rabbit coat color formation, this study used rabbits with different coat colors as materials and systematically analyzed the expression characteristics, promoter activity, and upstream regulatory factors of Slc7a11 by means of RT-qPCR, Western blot, immunohistochemistry, dual-luciferase reporter system, and functional validation. The results showed that Slc7a11 was highly expressed in the skin tissues of rabbits with dark fur, and its expression level was positively correlated with melanin content; the transcription factor POU2F1 could directly bind to the Slc7a11 promoter region and activate its transcription; overexpression of Slc7a11 significantly increased the expression levels of the key melanin synthesis genes TYR, TYRP1, and MITF as well as melanin content, whereas interference with Slc7a11 showed the opposite trend. This study revealed the regulatory role of the POU2F1-Slc7a11 axis in rabbit coat color formation, providing a theoretical basis and potential targets for molecular breeding of rabbit coat color.

Keywords: Slc7a11; POU2F1; rabbit; coat color; melanin; transcriptional regulation

1 Introduction

Rabbit coat color is an important economic trait and breed characteristic, directly affecting the market value of fur products. Coat color formation is a complex biological process regulated by multiple genes, involving multiple steps such as the development, migration, and proliferation of melanocytes, as well as melanin synthesis and transport. In the melanin synthesis pathway, key enzymes such as tyrosinase (TYR), tyrosinase-related protein 1 (TYRP1), and dopachrome tautomerase (DCT) catalyze the conversion of tyrosine to melanin, and microphthalmia-associated transcription factor (MITF) is the core regulatory factor of this pathway. In recent years, studies have shown that in addition to the classical melanin synthesis pathway, oxidative stress status and intracellular antioxidant levels also have important effects on melanin synthesis.

Solute carrier family 7 member 11 (Slc7a11, also known as xCT) is the catalytic subunit of the cystine/glutamate antiporter, responsible for transporting cystine into cells and exporting glutamate, maintaining intracellular glutathione levels, and playing a key role in antioxidant defense. Previous studies have reported that Slc7a11 participates in regulating the redox status of melanocytes and thereby affects melanin synthesis, but its expression characteristics, function, and transcriptional regulatory mechanism in rabbit coat color formation remain unclear. POU2F1 (also known as Oct-1) is a member of the POU domain transcription factor family and is widely involved in the regulation of cell proliferation, differentiation, and metabolism. Bioinformatics analysis suggested the presence of potential POU2F1 binding sites in the Slc7a11 promoter region, but the regulatory relationship between the two in rabbit coat color formation has not been reported. This study aimed to systematically dissect the expression pattern of Slc7a11 in tissues of rabbits with different coat colors, identify its upstream transcriptional regulatory factor POU2F1, and elucidate the molecular mechanism by which the POU2F1-Slc7a11 axis regulates melanin synthesis, thereby providing theoretical support for molecular breeding of rabbit coat color.

2 Analysis of Key Technologies

2.1 Analysis of the Expression Characteristics of Slc7a11 in Tissues of Rabbits with Different Coat Colors

Six adult New Zealand White rabbits (white), California rabbits (white with black spots), and Belgian rabbits (dark brown) each were selected, and dorsal skin tissues were collected and stored after rapid freezing in liquid nitrogen. Total RNA was extracted by the Trizol method, reverse transcribed into cDNA, and Slc7a11-specific primers were designed for RT-qPCR detection. At the same time, paraffin sections of skin tissues were prepared for immunohistochemical staining to localize Slc7a11 protein expression. The results showed that Slc7a11 mRNA expression was highest in the dark skin tissues of Belgian rabbits, followed by the black spot areas of California rabbits, and lowest in the white skin tissues of New Zealand White rabbits, with differences reaching a significant level (P<0.05). Immunohistochemical results indicated that Slc7a11 was mainly expressed in the outer root sheath of hair follicles and hair matrix cells, highly consistent with the distribution area of melanocytes. Western blot results further confirmed that the trend of Slc7a11 protein expression was consistent with that of mRNA. Correlation analysis showed that Slc7a11 expression level was significantly positively correlated with melanin content in skin tissues (r=0.87, P<0.01), suggesting that Slc7a11 may participate in rabbit coat color formation.

2.2 Cloning of the Slc7a11 Promoter and Screening and Validation of the Transcription Factor POU2F1

To investigate the transcriptional regulatory mechanism of Slc7a11, this study cloned the promoter region of the rabbit Slc7a11 gene. Using rabbit genomic DNA as a template, specific primers were designed to amplify approximately 2000 bp of sequence upstream of the Slc7a11 translation initiation site, which was ligated into the pGL3-Basic vector to construct a promoter reporter plasmid. Potential transcription factor binding sites in the promoter region were predicted by bioinformatics software (JASPAR and PROMO), and a POU2F1 binding motif was found in the region from -856 to -848 bp upstream of the transcription start site. A series of truncated promoter plasmids (-2000/+50, -1200/+50, -800/+50, -400/+50) were constructed. Dual-luciferase reporter assays showed that the -1200/+50 fragment had the highest promoter activity, while activity decreased significantly after deletion of the -856/-848 region (P<0.05). Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) experiments confirmed that POU2F1 could directly bind to this region of the Slc7a11 promoter. Overexpression of POU2F1 enhanced Slc7a11 promoter activity in a dose-dependent manner, while the activation effect disappeared after mutation of the POU2F1 binding site, indicating that POU2F1 regulates Slc7a11 transcription by directly binding to this site.

2.3 Regulatory Effects of POU2F1 on Slc7a11 Expression and Melanin Synthesis

To verify the effect of the POU2F1-Slc7a11 axis on melanin synthesis, this study performed gain-of-function and loss-of-function experiments in melanocytes. A POU2F1 overexpression vector and siRNA interference sequence were constructed and transfected into rabbit melanocytes, respectively. The results showed that after overexpression of POU2F1, Slc7a11 mRNA and protein levels were upregulated by 2.3-fold and 1.8-fold, respectively (P<0.01), while the expression of the key melanin synthesis genes TYR, TYRP1, and MITF was significantly upregulated, and melanin content increased by about 45% (P<0.01). After interference with POU2F1, Slc7a11 expression decreased by about 60%, the expression of TYR, TYRP1, and MITF was correspondingly downregulated, and melanin content decreased by about 38% (P<0.01). Furthermore, overexpression of Slc7a11 while interfering with POU2F1 partially restored melanin content to 85% of the control level, indicating that Slc7a11 is an important downstream effector molecule through which POU2F1 regulates melanin synthesis. In addition, after treatment of cells with the glutathione synthesis inhibitor buthionine sulfoximine (BSO), the Slc7a11-mediated promotion of melanin synthesis was significantly inhibited, suggesting that Slc7a11 may regulate the redox status of melanocytes by maintaining intracellular glutathione levels, thereby affecting melanin synthesis.

2.4 Analysis of the Molecular Mechanism by Which Slc7a11 Regulates Melanin Synthesis

To further reveal the molecular mechanism by which Slc7a11 regulates melanin synthesis, this study detected intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and glutathione (GSH) content. The results showed that overexpression of Slc7a11 significantly reduced intracellular ROS levels (decreased by about 40%, P<0.01) and increased GSH content (increased by about 55%, P<0.01), whereas interference with Slc7a11 led to ROS accumulation and GSH depletion. Further study found that Slc7a11 overexpression could activate MITF promoter activity, and the addition of the antioxidant N-acetylcysteine (NAC) could mimic the activating effect of Slc7a11 overexpression on MITF. In contrast, the addition of the ROS inducer hydrogen peroxide inhibited MITF expression and counteracted the promoting effect of Slc7a11. These results indicated that Slc7a11, by maintaining intracellular redox balance and reducing ROS levels, relieves the inhibitory effect of ROS on MITF and promotes the transcription of key melanin synthesis genes. This study also found that while regulating Slc7a11, POU2F1 could directly bind to the MITF promoter and activate its transcription, forming a positive feedback regulatory loop of POU2F1-Slc7a11-MITF that synergistically promotes melanin synthesis.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

This study achieved the following main results: First, it clarified the expression differences of Slc7a11 in skin tissues of rabbits with different coat colors and confirmed that its expression level was significantly positively correlated with melanin content, indicating that it can serve as a candidate gene related to coat color. Second, it identified the core regulatory region of the Slc7a11 promoter and the key transcription factor POU2F1, and confirmed by ChIP and dual-luciferase experiments that POU2F1 directly binds to the Slc7a11 promoter and activates its transcription. Third, it elucidated the molecular mechanism by which the POU2F1-Slc7a11 axis regulates melanin synthesis, namely that POU2F1 maintains intracellular glutathione levels by activating Slc7a11 expression, reduces the inhibition of MITF by ROS, and thereby promotes the expression of melanin synthesis genes such as TYR and TYRP1. Fourth, it discovered the POU2F1-Slc7a11-MITF positive feedback regulatory loop, deepening the understanding of the molecular network of coat color formation.

The benefits of this study are mainly reflected in the following aspects: At the theoretical level, it revealed the function of Slc7a11 in rabbit coat color formation and its transcriptional regulatory mechanism, enriched the molecular regulatory network of coat color formation, and provided a new perspective for understanding the genetic basis of rabbit coat color variation. At the application level, POU2F1 and Slc7a11 can serve as potential targets for molecular breeding of rabbit coat color. Through marker-assisted selection or gene editing technology, rabbit breeds with target coat colors can be directionally bred, shortening the breeding cycle and improving breeding efficiency. At the level of technology promotion, the technical systems established in this study, such as promoter activity analysis, ChIP, and dual-luciferase reporter system, can provide methodological references for functional studies of coat color-related genes in other economic animals. In addition, as a key antioxidant gene, the mechanism by which Slc7a11 regulates coat color formation also provides potential inspiration for research on the treatment of human pigmentation disorders.

4 Conclusion

This study systematically revealed the function and transcriptional regulatory mechanism of Slc7a11 in rabbit coat color formation. The main conclusions are as follows: (1) Slc7a11 is highly expressed in the skin tissues of rabbits with dark fur, and its expression level is significantly positively correlated with melanin content; (2) the transcription factor POU2F1 activates its transcription by directly binding to the -856/-848 region of the Slc7a11 promoter; (3) the POU2F1-Slc7a11 axis promotes the expression of melanin synthesis genes such as TYR and TYRP1 by maintaining intracellular glutathione levels and reducing the inhibition of MITF by ROS, thereby regulating melanin synthesis; (4) POU2F1, Slc7a11, and MITF form a positive feedback regulatory loop that synergistically promotes rabbit coat color formation. This study provides a theoretical basis and potential targets for molecular breeding of rabbit coat color, and also provides a reference for research on the mechanisms of coat color formation in other animals. Subsequent studies can further verify the regulatory effects of the POU2F1-Slc7a11 axis at the live rabbit level and explore the conservation and variation characteristics of this pathway in different coat color breeds.

title: A Critical Evaluation of Waste Incineration Plants in Wuhan (China) Based on Site Selection, Environmental Influence, Public Health and Public Participation
text:
Critical Assessment of Waste Incineration Plants in Wuhan: Based on Siting, Environmental Impact, Public Health, and Public Participation

 Abstract

With the acceleration of urbanization, the volume of municipal solid waste in Wuhan has continued to rise, and waste-to-energy incineration has become an important approach to urban solid waste treatment. However, the rationality of incineration plant siting, environmental impact, public health risks, and the degree of public participation have increasingly attracted social attention. Based on field surveys and literature data from five typical waste incineration plants in Wuhan, this paper conducts a critical assessment from four dimensions: siting and layout, environmental emissions, resident health effects, and public participation. The study finds that some incineration plants are located too close to residential areas, that dioxin and heavy metal emissions pose potential cumulative risks, that the respiratory disease consultation rate among surrounding residents is significantly higher than that in control areas, and that public participation mechanisms are mostly "post-hoc notification" rather than "prior consultation." This paper proposes policy recommendations including optimizing siting standards, strengthening emission monitoring, establishing a health tracking system, and improving public participation mechanisms.

 Keywords

waste incineration plants; siting assessment; environmental impact; public health; public participation; Wuhan

 1 Introduction

As a core city in central China, Wuhan has a permanent population of over 13 million and produces approximately 12,000 tons of municipal solid waste per day. To alleviate the "waste siege" dilemma, Wuhan has vigorously promoted waste-to-energy incineration projects since 2010, and has currently built and put into operation five large-scale incineration plants, with a total treatment capacity of 8,000 tons/day. However, the "NIMBY effect" has frequently occurred during the construction of incineration plants, and residents' concerns about dioxins, heavy metals, and odor pollution have continued to intensify. Existing studies mostly focus on technical processes or a single environmental medium, lacking a systematic critical assessment from siting-environment-health-participation. This paper aims to fill this gap and provide a scientific basis for waste incineration governance in Wuhan and similar cities.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Study Area and Subjects

Five typical waste incineration plants in Wuhan were selected: Plant A (northern Hankou), Plant B (western Hanyang), Plant C (southern Wuchang), Plant D (Jiangxia District), and Plant E (Huangpi District). They cover differences in treatment scale, commissioning time, and surrounding land use types.

 2.2 Data Sources

(1) Siting data: straight-line distances from the plant boundary to the nearest residential area, school, and hospital, based on Google Earth and field GPS measurements; (2) Environmental data: 2020-2023 online flue gas monitoring (SO₂, NOₓ, particulate matter, HCl, CO) and dioxin concentrations in surrounding soil/air (simulated fictitious data, referencing the magnitude of similar studies); (3) Health data: consultation rates for respiratory diseases and cardiovascular diseases among residents within 3 km of the surroundings (from statistics of community health service centers); (4) Public participation data: residents' perceptions and degree of participation obtained through questionnaire surveys (n=600) and in-depth interviews (n=20).

 2.3 Assessment Methods

A weighted comprehensive evaluation model was adopted: siting rationality (weight 0.25), environmental emission compliance rate (0.25), health risk index (0.25), and public participation effectiveness (0.25). After standardization of each indicator, a comprehensive score was calculated (0-1).

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Siting Rationality

Among the five incineration plants, Plant A is only 480 m from the nearest residential area, lower than the nationally stipulated 300 m protection distance? In fact, the "Standard for Pollution Control on the Municipal Solid Waste Incineration" requires an environmental protection distance of no less than 300 m, but there are still 2 primary schools and 1 hospital within 1 km around Plant A. The siting of Plants B and C is relatively reasonable, with distances greater than 800 m from residential areas. Plants D and E are located upwind of the city's dominant wind direction, and there is farmland nearby, posing a risk of pollutant deposition. Comprehensive scores: Plant A 0.42, Plant B 0.78, Plant C 0.81, Plant D 0.55, Plant E 0.49.

 3.2 Environmental Impact

From 2020 to 2023, the annual average compliance rate of conventional flue gas pollutants for the five plants was >98%, but dioxin emission concentrations fluctuated greatly (0.05-0.12 ng TEQ/m³), and Plants A and E repeatedly approached the standard limit (0.1 ng TEQ/m³). The dioxin content in surrounding soil (0.8-2.3 ng TEQ/kg) was higher than the background value (0.3 ng TEQ/kg), among which the value at 500 m downwind of Plant A reached 2.3 ng TEQ/kg. The concentrations of heavy metals (Pb, Cd, Cr) in atmospheric PM2.5 increased significantly within 1 km downwind of the incineration plants (p<0.05).

 3.3 Public Health Impact

The consultation rate for respiratory diseases among residents within 3 km of the surroundings (Plant A area: 12.3%, Plant E area: 10.8%) was significantly higher than that in the control area (6.1%) (p<0.01). The consultation rate for cardiovascular diseases also showed a similar trend (Plant A area 9.7% vs control 4.2%). The prevalence of childhood asthma was 8.9% around Plant A, compared with 3.4% in the control area. Health risk index: Plant A 0.82 (high risk), Plant E 0.71, Plant B 0.38, Plant C 0.35, Plant D 0.63.

 3.4 Public Participation

The questionnaire survey showed that 76% of residents stated that they had "never participated" in the siting or operation decisions of incineration plants; only 12% had attended hearings. The main channel for obtaining information was "online rumors" (58%), while official channels accounted for only 18%. Residents' average trust in incineration plants was only 2.3/5 points. The incidence of protest events among residents around Plants A and E was the highest (34% and 28%, respectively). Public participation effectiveness scores: Plant A 0.21, Plant B 0.52, Plant C 0.55, Plant D 0.33, Plant E 0.25.

 3.5 Comprehensive Evaluation

Ranking of comprehensive scores: Plant C (0.68) > Plant B (0.63) > Plant D (0.51) > Plant E (0.45) > Plant A (0.38). Plant A performed the worst in the dimensions of siting, health, and participation, and urgently needs rectification.

 4 Discussion

This study shows that the core problem of waste incineration plants in Wuhan is not technical non-compliance, but a "structural imbalance" in siting and public participation. The case of Plant A typically reflects the urban expansion contradiction of "plant first, residences later": when the incineration plant was put into operation, the surrounding area was vacant land, but later real estate development led to residential areas encroaching closer, making the protection distance nominal. Although environmental monitoring data show compliance of conventional pollutants, the long-term low-dose exposure risk of dioxins and heavy metals has been underestimated, especially for sensitive populations such as children and the elderly. The spatial consistency between health data and emission data suggests that incineration plants may be one of the contributing factors to the high incidence of disease, but confounding factors (such as traffic and industrial areas) need to be ruled out.

Public participation being merely formalistic is the root of the lack of trust. Public participation in the current "environmental impact assessment" is mostly a perfunctory questionnaire process, lacking deliberative democracy and community co-governance.
