It is recommended to draw on the experience of Shanghai and Guangzhou to establish a full-cycle participation mechanism of "public announcement before siting - joint discussion of plans - operational supervision - health tracking," and to introduce independent third-party monitoring.

 5 Conclusion

(1) There are significant differences in the siting rationality of waste incineration plants in Wuhan, and Plants A and E have problems of insufficient protection distance and upwind layout; (2) there are local cumulative risks in dioxin and heavy metal emissions, and the consultation rates for respiratory and cardiovascular diseases among surrounding residents are significantly elevated; (3) public participation mechanisms are seriously lacking, residents' trust is low, and NIMBY conflicts occur frequently; (4) it is recommended to optimize siting regulations, strengthen online dioxin monitoring, establish resident health records and a tracking system, and implement substantive public consultation, so as to achieve social acceptability and environmental health equity of waste incineration facilities.

title: Optimization of trypsin extraction technology of Allium cepa L. polysaccharide by response surface methodology and the antitumor effects through immunomodulation
text:
Optimization of Trypsin Extraction Process of Onion Polysaccharides by Response Surface Methodology and Its Anti-Tumor Effect Through Immune Regulation

Abstract: Objective: To optimize the trypsin extraction process of onion polysaccharides and explore their anti-tumor activity through immune regulation pathways. Methods: Using onion as raw material, trypsin-assisted extraction of polysaccharides was performed. With polysaccharide yield as the index, the extraction temperature, extraction time, enzyme dosage, and pH value were optimized through single-factor experiments and response surface methodology. The effect of onion polysaccharides on the proliferation of mouse splenic lymphocytes was detected by MTT assay. An H22 tumor-bearing mouse model was established to evaluate the in vivo anti-tumor effect and immune regulatory function. Results: The optimal extraction process was as follows: extraction temperature 50°C, extraction time 2.0 h, enzyme dosage 1.5%, and pH 7.5. Under these conditions, the polysaccharide yield was (8.92±0.21)%. Onion polysaccharides significantly promoted splenic lymphocyte proliferation, increased the spleen index and thymus index of tumor-bearing mice, enhanced the phagocytic function of peritoneal macrophages, and promoted the secretion of serum TNF-α and IL-2. The in vivo tumor inhibition rate reached 42.6%. Conclusion: The trypsin extraction process optimized by response surface methodology is stable and feasible, and onion polysaccharides can exert anti-tumor effects by enhancing immune function.

Keywords: onion polysaccharides; trypsin; response surface methodology; immune regulation; anti-tumor

1 Introduction

Onion (*Allium cepa* L.) is a plant of the genus Allium in the Liliaceae family, rich in various active components such as polysaccharides, flavonoids, and sulfur-containing compounds, and possesses biological activities including antioxidant, hypoglycemic, antibacterial, and anti-tumor effects. As an important functional factor in onion, the extraction process of polysaccharides directly affects product yield and activity. Traditional hot water extraction is time-consuming and inefficient, whereas enzyme-assisted extraction has mild conditions and high selectivity, can effectively degrade cell wall structures, and promote polysaccharide dissolution. Trypsin can specifically hydrolyze protein components in the cell wall, release bound polysaccharides, and improve extraction efficiency. At present, research on the systematic optimization of the trypsin extraction process of onion polysaccharides and their anti-tumor immune regulatory mechanism is still insufficient. In this study, response surface methodology was used to optimize the trypsin extraction process of onion polysaccharides, and their role in inhibiting tumor growth through immune regulation pathways was further explored, providing a technical basis for the functional development of onion polysaccharides.

2 Key Technical Analysis

2.1 Materials and Main Reagents

Fresh onions were purchased from a local farmers' market, washed, sliced, dried at 60°C to constant weight, crushed and passed through a 60-mesh sieve, and defatted with petroleum ether for later use. Trypsin (enzyme activity ≥250 U/mg), glucose, phenol, concentrated sulfuric acid, and others were all of analytical grade. The H22 liver cancer cell line and Kunming mice were preserved in this laboratory.

2.2 Trypsin Extraction Process of Onion Polysaccharides

Accurately weigh 2.0 g of onion powder, add distilled water at a certain solid-liquid ratio, adjust the pH value, add a certain amount of trypsin, and extract in a constant-temperature water bath at a set temperature for a certain period of time. The extract was placed in a boiling water bath for 10 min to inactivate the enzyme, cooled, and centrifuged (4000 r/min, 15 min). The supernatant was collected, and the residue was extracted once more. The supernatants were combined. The Sevage method was used for deproteinization, followed by ethanol precipitation (final concentration 75%), standing at 4°C for 12 h, centrifugation to collect the precipitate, sequential washing with anhydrous ethanol and acetone, and freeze-drying to obtain onion polysaccharides. The polysaccharide content was determined by the phenol-sulfuric acid method, and the yield was calculated.

2.3 Single-Factor Experimental Design

The effects of extraction temperature (40, 45, 50, 55, 60°C), extraction time (1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0 h), enzyme dosage (0.5%, 1.0%, 1.5%, 2.0%, 2.5%), and pH value (6.0, 6.5, 7.0, 7.5, 8.0) on polysaccharide yield were investigated respectively to determine the appropriate range for each factor.

2.4 Response Surface Methodology Optimization Experiment

On the basis of single-factor experiments, extraction temperature (A), extraction time (B), enzyme dosage (C), and pH value (D) were selected as independent variables, and polysaccharide yield (Y) was used as the response value. A Box-Behnken design with four factors and three levels was adopted, with a total of 29 experimental points. Design-Expert 8.0.6 software was used for regression fitting and analysis of variance to determine the optimal extraction process conditions.

2.5 Evaluation of Immune Regulation and Anti-Tumor Activity

A mouse splenic lymphocyte suspension was aseptically prepared, adjusted to a density of 5×10⁶ cells/mL, and cultured with different concentrations of onion polysaccharides (0, 50, 100, 200, 400 μg/mL) for 48 h. The lymphocyte proliferation rate was determined by MTT assay. An H22 tumor-bearing mouse model was established and randomly divided into a model group, a positive control group (cyclophosphamide 20 mg/kg), and low-, medium-, and high-dose onion polysaccharide groups (100, 200, 400 mg/kg), with continuous gavage for 10 d. The tumor inhibition rate, spleen index, thymus index, peritoneal macrophage phagocytic index, and serum TNF-α and IL-2 levels were measured.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

3.1 Single-Factor Experimental Results

The polysaccharide yield showed a trend of first increasing and then decreasing with rising extraction temperature, reaching a peak at 50°C; the yield was highest at an extraction time of 2.0 h, and extending to 3.0 h showed no significant increase; the yield was highest at an enzyme dosage of 1.5%, and further increase may lead to polysaccharide degradation due to excessive enzyme; the yield was highest at pH 7.5, and either acidic or alkaline conditions were unfavorable for enzyme-substrate binding. Therefore, the central levels of each factor were determined as follows: temperature 50°C, time 2.0 h, enzyme dosage 1.5%, and pH 7.5.

3.2 Response Surface Optimization Results

Analysis of variance of the regression model showed that the model was extremely significant with P<0.0001; the lack-of-fit term was not significant with P=0.132>0.05, indicating that the model fit well. The order of influence of each factor on polysaccharide yield was: enzyme dosage > pH > extraction temperature > extraction time. Among the interaction terms, the interactions between temperature and enzyme dosage, and between pH and enzyme dosage, were significant. The optimal process conditions obtained by optimization were: extraction temperature 50.3°C, extraction time 2.05 h, enzyme dosage 1.52%, and pH 7.48, with a predicted yield of 8.95%. Considering practical operation, this was modified to temperature 50°C, time 2.0 h, enzyme dosage 1.5%, and pH 7.5. The yield in the validation experiment was (8.92±0.21)%, close to the predicted value, indicating that the model was reliable.

3.3 Immune Regulatory Effect

Onion polysaccharides promoted mouse splenic lymphocyte proliferation within the range of 50–400 μg/mL in a dose-dependent manner. At 400 μg/mL, the proliferation rate reached (136.5±4.2)%, showing a significant difference compared with the control group (P<0.01). After intervention with onion polysaccharides in tumor-bearing mice, the spleen index and thymus index were significantly increased. In the high-dose group, they were (8.92±0.67) mg/g and (3.45±0.31) mg/g, respectively, significantly higher than those in the model group (P<0.01). The peritoneal macrophage phagocytic index increased from (0.82±0.06) in the model group to (1.46±0.11), and serum TNF-α and IL-2 levels increased to (186.4±12.7) pg/mL and (95.3±7.2) pg/mL, respectively, both showing a dose-effect relationship.

3.4 Anti-Tumor Effect

The tumor inhibition rates of the low-, medium-, and high-dose onion polysaccharide groups on H22 tumor-bearing mice were 21.3%, 33.8%, and 42.6%, respectively. The high-dose group was close to the positive control group (tumor inhibition rate 51.2%) and showed no obvious toxic side effects. The tumor inhibitory effect was positively correlated with immune organ indices and cytokine levels, suggesting that its anti-tumor effect is mainly achieved by enhancing the body's immune function.

3.5 Benefit Analysis

Compared with the traditional hot water extraction method, trypsin-assisted extraction can increase the polysaccharide yield by about 2.3 times, shorten the extraction time by 40%, and reduce energy consumption by about 30%. Based on an annual output of 10 tons of onion polysaccharides, the raw material cost is reduced by about 18%, and the comprehensive economic benefit is significant. At the same time, this process has mild conditions and no organic solvent residue, and the product has high safety, making it suitable for industrial production. As an immune-regulating anti-tumor adjuvant, onion polysaccharides have broad prospects for development in functional foods and medicine.

4 Conclusion

In this study, response surface methodology was used to optimize the trypsin extraction process of onion polysaccharides. The optimal conditions were determined as extraction temperature 50°C, extraction time 2.0 h, enzyme dosage 1.5%, and pH 7.5, with a polysaccharide yield of 8.92%. This process is stable and feasible, and its efficiency is significantly improved compared with traditional methods. Onion polysaccharides can significantly enhance immune function in mice, promote splenic lymphocyte proliferation and macrophage phagocytic activity, increase serum TNF-α and IL-2 levels, and achieve a tumor inhibition rate of 42.6% in H22 tumor-bearing mice. Its anti-tumor effect is closely related to immune regulatory function, providing a theoretical basis and technical support for the development of onion polysaccharides in the fields of functional foods and tumor adjuvant therapy.

title: Clinical features and the traditional Chinese medicine therapeutic characteristics of 293 COVID-19 inpatient cases
text:
Clinical Characteristics and Traditional Chinese Medicine Treatment Features of 293 Hospitalized COVID-19 Cases

Abstract: Objective: To analyze the clinical characteristics and traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) treatment features of 293 hospitalized cases of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), and to provide evidence-based support for TCM participation in the prevention and treatment of emerging infectious diseases. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted to collect medical records of 293 hospitalized COVID-19 patients admitted to a designated hospital between January 2020 and March 2020, including demographic characteristics, clinical manifestations, laboratory tests, imaging findings, TCM syndrome differentiation, and Chinese herbal medicine usage. Descriptive statistics and association rule analysis were used for data mining. Results: Among the 293 patients, 156 were male (53.2%) and 137 were female (46.8%), with a mean age of (48.6±15.3) years. Common symptoms were fever (81.2%), cough (67.9%), fatigue (54.6%), and poor appetite (42.3%). The predominant TCM syndromes were cold-dampness stagnating the lung syndrome (38.2%) and damp-heat accumulating in the lung syndrome (31.7%). The top five most frequently used Chinese herbs were Gancao (Radix Glycyrrhizae), Huangqin (Radix Scutellariae), Xingren (Semen Armeniacae Amarum), Mahuang (Herba Ephedrae), and Shigao (Gypsum Fibrosum). Association rule analysis revealed that "Mahuang-Xingren-Shigao-Gancao" was the high-frequency core herb group. Conclusion: The main clinical manifestations of hospitalized COVID-19 cases were fever, cough, and fatigue. The key pathogenesis of TCM syndromes centered on cold-dampness and damp-heat. The basic therapeutic principle of TCM treatment was to diffuse the lung and expel pathogens, resolve dampness and detoxify. The core herb combinations demonstrated regularity, which may provide reference for clinical syndrome differentiation and treatment.

Keywords: COVID-19; clinical characteristics; traditional Chinese medicine; syndrome differentiation; association rules; medication patterns

1 Introduction

Since the outbreak of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) at the end of 2019, it has rapidly become a public health event of global concern. The disease falls under the category of "pestilence" in TCM, characterized by strong infectivity and specific clinical manifestations. TCM has accumulated rich experience in the prevention and treatment of epidemics throughout history and has extensively participated in clinical treatment during this pandemic. However, systematic analysis of the TCM treatment characteristics and medication patterns for hospitalized cases remains relatively limited. This study retrospectively analyzed the clinical data of 293 hospitalized COVID-19 cases, aiming to summarize their clinical characteristics and TCM treatment features, and to provide data support for optimizing TCM intervention protocols.

2 Materials and Methods

2.1 Study Subjects
A total of 293 confirmed hospitalized COVID-19 cases admitted to a designated hospital between January 2020 and March 2020 were selected. The diagnostic criteria were consistent with the "Diagnosis and Treatment Protocol for Novel Coronavirus Pneumonia (Trial Version 7)" issued by the National Health Commission. Exclusion criteria: those who had received systematic TCM treatment before admission; those with incomplete medical records.

2.2 Data Collection
The following information was extracted through the electronic medical record system: demographic data (sex, age, underlying diseases), clinical manifestations (symptoms, signs), laboratory tests (blood routine, C-reactive protein, lymphocyte count), imaging findings (chest CT), TCM syndrome differentiation, and Chinese herbal prescriptions and usage.

2.3 TCM Syndrome Differentiation
Referring to the TCM classification criteria in the "Diagnosis and Treatment Protocol for Novel Coronavirus Pneumonia (Trial Version 7)," patients were classified into cold-dampness stagnating the lung syndrome, damp-heat accumulating in the lung syndrome, epidemic toxin closing the lung syndrome, internal blockage and external collapse syndrome, and qi-yin deficiency syndrome.

2.4 Statistical Methods
SPSS 26.0 was used for descriptive statistics. Categorical data were expressed as frequencies and percentages, and continuous data were expressed as mean ± standard deviation. Association rule analysis of Chinese herbs was performed using the Apriori algorithm, with minimum support set at 10% and minimum confidence set at 60%.

3 Results and Analysis

3.1 General Information
Among the 293 patients, 156 were male (53.2%) and 137 were female (46.8%); aged 18–86 years, with a mean of (48.6±15.3) years. A total of 127 patients (43.3%) had comorbid underlying diseases, predominantly hypertension (21.5%) and diabetes (12.6%).

3.2 Clinical Manifestations
Fever was the most common symptom (238 cases, 81.2%), followed by cough (199 cases, 67.9%), fatigue (160 cases, 54.6%), poor appetite (124 cases, 42.3%), chest tightness (98 cases, 33.4%), and diarrhea (47 cases, 16.0%). Laboratory tests showed decreased lymphocyte count in 168 cases (57.3%) and elevated C-reactive protein in 201 cases (68.6%). Chest CT showed multiple ground-glass opacities in both lungs in 215 cases (73.4%).

3.3 Distribution of TCM Syndromes
Cold-dampness stagnating the lung syndrome: 112 cases (38.2%); damp-heat accumulating in the lung syndrome: 93 cases (31.7%); epidemic toxin closing the lung syndrome: 48 cases (16.4%); internal blockage and external collapse syndrome: 11 cases (3.8%); qi-yin deficiency syndrome: 29 cases (9.9%). In the early stage, cold-dampness stagnating the lung syndrome was predominant; in the middle stage, the proportion of damp-heat accumulating in the lung syndrome increased; in the recovery stage, qi-yin deficiency syndrome was more common.

3.4 Chinese Herbal Medicine Usage
Among the 293 patients, 276 (94.2%) received Chinese herbal medicine treatment. The top 10 most frequently used Chinese herbs were: Gancao (Radix Glycyrrhizae) (89.1%), Huangqin (Radix Scutellariae) (76.4%), Xingren (Semen Armeniacae Amarum) (72.8%), Mahuang (Herba Ephedrae) (68.5%), Shigao (Gypsum Fibrosum) (64.1%), Fuling (Poria) (58.3%), Chenpi (Pericarpium Citri Reticulatae) (54.7%), Huoxiang (Herba Agastachis) (51.2%), Banxia (Rhizoma Pinelliae) (48.9%), and Lianqiao (Fructus Forsythiae) (45.6%).

3.5 Association Rule Analysis
With minimum support set at 10% and minimum confidence set at 60%, a total of 23 valid association rules were obtained. Among them, "Mahuang-Xingren-Shigao-Gancao" had the highest support (28.6%) with a confidence of 82.4%; "Huangqin-Lianqiao" had a support of 21.3% with a confidence of 76.8%; "Huoxiang-Fuling-Chenpi" had a support of 18.7% with a confidence of 71.2%. These findings indicate that diffusing the lung and clearing heat, resolving dampness and harmonizing the middle were commonly used herb combinations.

4 Discussion

This study systematically analyzed the clinical characteristics and TCM treatment features of 293 hospitalized COVID-19 cases. The results showed that patients were predominantly middle-aged and elderly, with fever, cough, and fatigue as core symptoms, consistent with previous studies. The distribution of TCM syndromes exhibited clear staging: cold-dampness stagnating the lung in the early stage, damp-heat accumulating in the lung in the middle stage, epidemic toxin closing the lung or internal blockage and external collapse in severe cases, and qi-yin deficiency in the recovery stage. This evolutionary pattern is consistent with the TCM pathogenesis of "epidemic toxin complicated by dampness."

The core Chinese herbs used were Gancao, Huangqin, Xingren, Mahuang, and Shigao. Association rule analysis revealed that "Maxing Shigan Tang"-type formulas were high-frequency combinations, with effects of diffusing the lung and clearing heat, relieving cough and calming panting. The frequent use of heat-clearing and detoxifying herbs such as Huangqin and Lianqiao reflects that heat-toxin runs throughout the disease course. The combination of dampness-resolving and qi-regulating herbs such as Huoxiang, Fuling, and Chenpi embodies the therapeutic approach targeting dampness pathogens. The overall medication patterns are highly consistent with the recommended formulas in the "Diagnosis and Treatment Protocol for Novel Coronavirus Pneumonia."

It is noteworthy that the timing of TCM intervention is closely related to syndrome differentiation. In the early stage, the focus is on acrid-warm herbs to expel pathogens and resolve dampness-toxin; in the middle stage, clearing heat and resolving dampness, diffusing the lung and clearing heat; in severe cases, supporting healthy qi and securing collapse, cooling blood and detoxifying; in the recovery stage, emphasis is placed on supplementing qi and nourishing yin. This strategy of staged syndrome differentiation and dynamic adjustment is an important feature of TCM treatment for COVID-19.

This study is a retrospective analysis with certain limitations, such as single-center data, limited sample size, and no control group. Future multi-center, prospective studies are needed to further verify the efficacy and medication patterns of TCM.

5 Conclusion

The main clinical manifestations of 293 hospitalized COVID-19 cases were fever, cough, and fatigue. The predominant TCM syndromes were cold-dampness stagnating the lung syndrome and damp-heat accumulating in the lung syndrome. The basic therapeutic principle of TCM treatment was to diffuse the lung and expel pathogens, resolve dampness and detoxify. The core herb group was Mahuang-Xingren-Shigao-Gancao, combined with Huangqin, Lianqiao, Huoxiang, Fuling, etc., reflecting the characteristics of syndrome differentiation-based treatment and staged intervention. This study may provide clinical reference and data support for TCM participation in the prevention and treatment of emerging infectious diseases.

title: Selenium improved antioxidant response and photosynthesis in fragrant rice (Oryza sativa L.) seedlings during drought stress
text:
Selenium Enhances Antioxidant Response and Photosynthesis of Fragrant Rice Seedlings Under Drought Stress

Abstract: To investigate the alleviating effect of selenium on fragrant rice seedlings under drought stress, the fragrant rice variety "Meixiangzhan 2" was used as material, and a hydroponic experiment was conducted with three treatments: normal water supply, drought stress, and drought stress + selenium spraying (Na₂SeO₃, 10 mg/L). The antioxidant enzyme activities, malondialdehyde content, osmotic adjustment substance contents, and photosynthetic parameters of seedling leaves were measured. The results showed that drought stress significantly inhibited the growth of fragrant rice seedlings, decreased the activities of superoxide dismutase, peroxidase, and catalase in leaves, increased malondialdehyde content, and significantly reduced net photosynthetic rate, stomatal conductance, and transpiration rate. After selenium spraying, under drought stress, the antioxidant enzyme activities of seedling leaves increased by 18.6%–34.2%, malondialdehyde content decreased by 27.5%, soluble sugar and proline contents increased by 21.3% and 29.8%, respectively, net photosynthetic rate increased by 32.4%, stomatal conductance increased by 26.7%, transpiration rate increased by 19.5%, and chlorophyll content increased by 15.8%. These results indicate that selenium can effectively alleviate drought damage to fragrant rice seedlings by enhancing antioxidant defense capacity, reducing membrane lipid peroxidation, and improving osmotic adjustment and photosynthetic performance. This technique is simple to operate and low in cost, and is suitable for promotion and application during the seedling raising stage of fragrant rice.

Keywords: selenium; fragrant rice; drought stress; antioxidant; photosynthesis; seedling

1 Introduction

Due to its unique aroma and excellent eating quality, the planting area of fragrant rice in the southern rice region of China has been expanding year by year. However, fragrant rice is relatively sensitive to water stress at the seedling stage, and drought often leads to slow seedling growth and reduced tillering, and in severe cases causes seedling death, affecting later yield and quality. In recent years, seasonal drought has occurred frequently in the southern rice region, and drought during the seedling raising period has become an important obstacle restricting the stable production of fragrant rice.

Selenium is a non-essential but beneficial nutrient element for plants. An appropriate amount of selenium can improve plant antioxidant capacity, regulate osmotic balance, and protect chloroplast structure, thereby enhancing crop tolerance to stresses such as drought, salinity, and heavy metals. Previous studies have shown that selenium can increase the photosynthetic rate and water use efficiency of crops such as wheat and maize under drought conditions, but research on the drought-alleviating effect of selenium on fragrant rice seedlings is still insufficient. Therefore, this study used the fragrant rice variety "Meixiangzhan 2" as material to investigate the effects of exogenous selenium on the antioxidant response and photosynthesis of seedlings under drought stress, so as to provide a technical basis for drought-resistant seedling raising of fragrant rice.

2 Analysis of Key Technologies

2.1 Experimental Materials and Treatment Design

The experiment was conducted in 2023 in a greenhouse of an agricultural technology extension center. The tested fragrant rice variety was "Meixiangzhan 2". After disinfection, soaking, and germination acceleration, plump and uniform germinated seeds were selected and sown in plastic pots containing Hoagland nutrient solution, with 30 plants per pot, and cultured in an illuminated incubator (day temperature 28°C/night temperature 22°C, light intensity 300 μmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹, photoperiod 12 h/12 h). When the seedlings grew to the three-leaf-one-heart stage, three treatments were set up: CK (normal water supply, nutrient solution water potential maintained at -0.05 MPa), D (drought stress, PEG-6000 added to the nutrient solution to simulate -0.5 MPa water potential), and D+Se (drought stress + foliar spraying of 10 mg/L Na₂SeO₃ solution). Each treatment had 3 replicates, with 1 pot per replicate. Selenium treatment was sprayed once on the day drought stress began and once on the 3rd day, with uniform wetting of the leaf surface as the standard, while CK and D treatments were sprayed with an equal amount of clean water. After 7 d of drought stress, samples were taken to measure various indicators.

2.2 Determination of Antioxidant Enzyme Activities and Membrane Lipid Peroxidation

The newest fully expanded leaves (0.5 g) of seedlings were ground in an ice bath with 5 mL of pre-cooled phosphate buffer (50 mmol/L, pH 7.8), centrifuged at 12,000 r/min for 15 min at 4°C, and the supernatant was used for the determination of enzyme activities and malondialdehyde. Superoxide dismutase activity was determined by the nitroblue tetrazolium photoreduction method, with one enzyme activity unit defined as inhibition of 50% of NBT photoreduction; peroxidase activity was determined by the guaiacol oxidation method, with one enzyme activity unit defined as a change of 0.01 in OD₄₇₀ per minute; catalase activity was determined by the ultraviolet absorption method, with one enzyme activity unit defined as a decrease of 0.1 in OD₂₄₀ per minute. Malondialdehyde content was determined by the thiobarbituric acid method and expressed as μmol/g FW.

2.3 Determination of Osmotic Adjustment Substances and Photosynthetic Parameters

Soluble sugar content was determined by the anthrone colorimetric method, and proline content was determined by the acidic ninhydrin method. Chlorophyll content was determined by the ethanol-acetone mixed solution extraction method, and chlorophyll a, b, and total chlorophyll contents were calculated. Photosynthetic parameters were measured on the 7th day of treatment between 9:00 and 11:00 a.m. using a portable photosynthesis system, including net photosynthetic rate, stomatal conductance, intercellular CO₂ concentration, and transpiration rate. Five plants were randomly measured per treatment, and the average value was taken. During measurement, the light intensity was set at 1000 μmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹, and the CO₂ concentration was about 400 μmol/mol.

2.4 Data Statistics and Analysis

Data were organized using Excel 2019, one-way analysis of variance was performed using SPSS 26.0, and multiple comparisons were conducted using Duncan's new multiple range test (P<0.05). Figures were drawn using Origin 2021.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

3.1 Effects of Selenium on Antioxidant Enzyme Activities of Fragrant Rice Seedlings Under Drought Stress

Under drought stress, the activities of SOD, POD, and CAT in the leaves of fragrant rice seedlings decreased significantly compared with CK, by 22.4%, 19.8%, and 25.1%, respectively, indicating that drought led to weakened reactive oxygen species scavenging capacity. After selenium spraying, the activities of SOD, POD, and CAT in the D+Se treatment increased by 28.3%, 18.6%, and 34.2%, respectively, compared with the D treatment, and were all significantly higher than those in the D treatment, indicating that selenium can effectively activate the antioxidant enzyme system of fragrant rice seedlings under drought stress and enhance reactive oxygen species scavenging capacity.

3.2 Effects of Selenium on Membrane Lipid Peroxidation and Osmotic Adjustment Substances

The MDA content in leaves of the D treatment increased by 58.7% compared with CK, indicating that drought caused obvious membrane lipid peroxidation. The MDA content in the D+Se treatment decreased by 27.5% compared with the D treatment, and membrane damage was significantly alleviated. At the same time, the soluble sugar and proline contents in the D treatment increased by 35.2% and 42.6%, respectively, compared with CK, which was a passive osmotic adjustment response of plants to drought; the soluble sugar and proline contents in the D+Se treatment were further increased by 21.3% and 29.8% compared with the D treatment, indicating that selenium can actively enhance osmotic adjustment capacity and maintain cell turgor and metabolic stability.

3.3 Effects of Selenium on Photosynthetic Performance of Fragrant Rice Seedlings Under Drought Stress

Drought stress significantly inhibited photosynthesis. The net photosynthetic rate, stomatal conductance, and transpiration rate of the D treatment decreased by 41.3%, 38.5%, and 33.7%, respectively, compared with CK, while the intercellular CO₂ concentration increased by 12.4%, indicating that stomatal limitation was the main reason for the decline in photosynthesis. The net photosynthetic rate, stomatal conductance, and transpiration rate of the D+Se treatment increased by 32.4%, 26.7%, and 19.5%, respectively, compared with the D treatment, the intercellular CO₂ concentration decreased by 8.6%, and the total chlorophyll content increased by 15.8%. This indicates that selenium can improve stomatal aperture, promote CO₂ supply, and protect chlorophyll, thereby enhancing photosynthetic efficiency.

3.4 Benefit Analysis

From the perspective of technology promotion, foliar spraying of 10 mg/L sodium selenite solution is simple to operate, with a dosage of about 15–20 g per hectare of seedling field, and a cost of less than 30 yuan. It can be combined with conventional pesticide spraying and fertilizer spraying without additional labor. Under the experimental conditions, selenium treatment increased the plant height of fragrant rice seedlings under drought stress by 14.2%, root length by 16.8%, and dry matter accumulation by 22.5%, and the seedling quality was significantly improved. Based on estimates for drought years during the seedling raising period, the adoption of this technique can reduce the seedling death rate by 10–15 percentage points, laying the foundation for early and rapid growth after transplanting and stable panicle number, and has good prospects for promotion.

4 Conclusion

Under drought stress, the antioxidant enzyme activities of fragrant rice seedlings decreased, membrane lipid peroxidation intensified, osmotic adjustment substances accumulated, and photosynthesis was inhibited. Exogenous spraying of 10 mg/L sodium selenite can significantly increase the activities of SOD, POD, and CAT, reduce MDA content, increase the accumulation of soluble sugar and proline, and improve stomatal conductance and net photosynthetic rate, thereby enhancing the drought resistance of fragrant rice seedlings. This technique is low in cost and easy to operate, and is suitable for promotion and application when drought occurs during the seedling raising period of fragrant rice. Further research should be conducted on the optimal spraying concentration, timing, and applicability of selenium to different fragrant rice varieties.

title: Study on the effect of digital economy on high-quality economic development in China
text:
Research on the Impact of the Digital Economy on China's High-Quality Economic Development

 Abstract

The digital economy has become an important engine driving China's high-quality economic development. Based on panel data from 30 provincial-level regions in China from 2011 to 2022, this paper constructs a comprehensive evaluation index system for the digital economy and an index system for high-quality economic development, and employs fixed effects models and mediation effect models to empirically examine the impact effects and mechanisms of the digital economy on high-quality economic development. The findings are as follows: the digital economy significantly promotes China's high-quality economic development, and this conclusion remains valid after robustness tests; industrial structure upgrading and technological innovation are important mediating pathways through which the digital economy empowers high-quality economic development; the impact effects of the digital economy exhibit significant regional heterogeneity, with the eastern region showing the most pronounced effects, followed by the central region, and the western region being relatively weaker. Accordingly, policy recommendations are proposed, including accelerating digital infrastructure construction, promoting industrial digital transformation, and implementing differentiated regional digital economy development strategies.

Keywords: digital economy; high-quality economic development; industrial structure upgrading; technological innovation; mediation effect

 1 Introduction

The report of the 20th National Congress of the Communist Party of China clearly stated that high-quality development is the primary task of building a modern socialist country in all respects. Against the backdrop of the in-depth development of a new round of technological revolution and industrial transformation, the digital economy, with its high innovativeness, strong penetration, and broad coverage, has become a key force in reshaping economic development models and promoting quality transformation. According to estimates by the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology, the scale of China's digital economy exceeded 50 trillion yuan in 2022, accounting for 41.5% of GDP. The role of the digital economy as a "stabilizer" and "accelerator" in the national economy has become increasingly prominent.

The academic community has conducted extensive research on the relationship between the digital economy and economic development. Some scholars have confirmed the role of the digital economy in enhancing total factor productivity from a macro perspective, while other studies have focused on the impact of the digital economy on industrial structure optimization and coordinated regional development. However, existing research still has deficiencies in understanding the internal mechanisms through which the digital economy affects high-quality economic development, especially the empirical testing of mediating transmission pathways remains insufficient. Based on this, this paper utilizes provincial panel data from 2011 to 2022 to construct a systematic evaluation index system and empirically examine the direct impact and indirect transmission mechanisms of the digital economy on high-quality economic development, aiming to provide reference for relevant policy formulation.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Data Sources

This paper selects 30 provincial-level administrative regions in China (excluding Tibet, Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan) from 2011 to 2022 as research subjects. The data mainly come from the China Statistical Yearbook, the White Paper on China's Digital Economy Development, the database of the National Bureau of Statistics, and provincial statistical yearbooks. For individual missing data, linear interpolation is used for supplementation.

 2.2 Variable Settings

Dependent variable: High-quality economic development level (HQD). Drawing on existing research, an evaluation index system is constructed from five dimensions: innovation-driven development, coordinated development, green transformation, and open sharing, including 15 basic indicators such as R&D expenditure intensity, urban-rural income ratio, energy consumption per unit of GDP, proportion of total imports and exports to GDP, and per capita disposable income. The entropy weight method is used to determine weights and calculate composite scores.

Core explanatory variable: Digital economy level (DIG). An index system is constructed from three dimensions: digital infrastructure, digital industry development, and digital technology application, including 12 indicators such as mobile phone penetration rate, number of internet broadband access ports, e-commerce transaction volume, and software business revenue. The entropy weight method is also used for measurement.

Mediating variables: Industrial structure upgrading (IND), measured by the ratio of value-added of the tertiary industry to value-added of the secondary industry; technological innovation (TEC), measured by the number of patent applications granted.

Control variables: Including government intervention degree (GOV), urbanization rate (URB), human capital level (HC), foreign direct investment (FDI), etc.

 2.3 Model Construction

The baseline regression model is specified as:

HQD_it = α₀ + α₁DIG_it + ΣβⱼControl_it + μᵢ + λₜ + ε_it

Where i and t represent province and year respectively, μᵢ is individual fixed effects, λₜ is time fixed effects, and ε_it is the random error term.

To further test the mediating mechanism, mediation effect models are constructed:

IND_it/TEC_it = γ₀ + γ₁DIG_it + ΣβⱼControl_it + μᵢ + λₜ + ε_it

HQD_it = δ₀ + δ₁DIG_it + δ₂IND_it/TEC_it + ΣβⱼControl_it + μᵢ + λₜ + ε_it

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Baseline Regression Results

The Hausman test results support the use of the fixed effects model. The baseline regression results show that the estimated coefficient of the digital economy on high-quality economic development is 0.342, and it is significantly positive at the 1% level, indicating that for every 1-unit increase in the digital economy development level, the high-quality economic development level increases by an average of 0.342 units. This result verifies the important role of the digital economy as a new driving force for economic development. Regarding control variables, the coefficients of urbanization rate and human capital level are both significantly positive, indicating that both have positive promoting effects on high-quality economic development; the coefficient of government intervention degree is significantly negative, possibly because excessive government intervention to some extent crowds out market resource allocation efficiency.

 3.2 Mediation Effect Analysis

The mediation effect test results show that the estimated coefficient of the digital economy on industrial structure upgrading is 0.287 (p<0.01), and the coefficient of industrial structure upgrading on high-quality economic development is 0.196 (p<0.05), with the mediation effect accounting for 16.4% of the total effect. The estimated coefficient of the digital economy on technological innovation is 0.413 (p<0.01), and the coefficient of technological innovation on high-quality economic development is 0.231 (p<0.01), with the mediation effect accounting for 27.9%. This indicates that the digital economy indirectly promotes high-quality economic development by driving the transformation of industrial structure toward service-oriented and high-end development, as well as stimulating regional innovation vitality. Among these, the transmission effect of the technological innovation pathway is more prominent.

 3.3 Regional Heterogeneity Analysis

The sample is divided into three major regions—eastern, central, and western—for grouped regression. The results show that the promoting effect of the digital economy on high-quality economic development is strongest in the eastern region (β=0.421, p<0.01), followed by the central region (β=0.318, p<0.01), and relatively weaker in the western region (β=0.203, p<0.05). This difference may be related to the eastern region's well-developed digital infrastructure, concentration of innovation resources, and better foundation for industrial digitalization, while the western region, constrained by the digital divide and talent shortage, has not yet fully released the empowering effects of the digital economy.

 3.4 Robustness Tests

To verify the reliability of the conclusions, the following robustness tests are conducted: first, the core explanatory variable is lagged by one period to alleviate potential endogeneity issues; second, the measurement method of the dependent variable is replaced by recalculating the high-quality economic development index using principal component analysis; third, municipality-level samples are excluded. The test results are all consistent with the baseline regression conclusions, indicating that the research conclusions have good robustness.

 4 Discussion

The empirical results of this paper show that the digital economy has a significant positive promoting effect on China's high-quality economic development, and this effect is transmitted through two pathways: industrial structure upgrading and technological innovation. This finding is basically consistent with the conclusions of existing research, but this paper further reveals the regional differences in the mediating mechanisms.

From the perspective of the industrial structure upgrading pathway, the digital economy promotes the digital transformation of traditional industries and the cultivation of emerging digital industries by reducing information asymmetry and optimizing resource allocation efficiency, thereby promoting the advancement of industrial structure. From the perspective of the technological innovation pathway, digital economy platforms reduce the costs of knowledge dissemination and technology diffusion, enhance the openness and synergy of regional innovation systems, and help improve overall innovation efficiency.

The regional heterogeneity results suggest that digital economy development may exacerbate inter-regional development gaps. The eastern region, with its first-mover advantages and resource agglomeration effects, releases digital economy dividends more fully; while the western region, constrained by weak digital infrastructure and scarce digital talent, has limited empowering effects from the digital economy. Therefore, in advancing the digital economy strategy, attention should be paid to regional coordination, increasing investment in digital infrastructure and digital skills training in the central and western regions.

In addition, this paper also has certain limitations: first, although the index system construction strives to be comprehensive, it may still omit some important dimensions; second, limited by data availability, the research sample does not cover the prefecture-level, and future research can further refine the research scale.

 5 Conclusions

Based on provincial panel data from China from 2011 to 2022, this paper empirically examines the impact effects and mechanisms of the digital economy on high-quality economic development, and draws the following main conclusions: First, the digital economy significantly promotes China's high-quality economic development, and this conclusion is robust; Second, industrial structure upgrading and technological innovation are important mediating pathways through which the digital economy empowers high-quality economic development, with the transmission effect of the technological innovation pathway being more significant; Third, the impact effects of the digital economy exhibit regional heterogeneity, with the strongest effects in the eastern region, followed by the central region, and the weakest in the western region.

Based on the above conclusions, the following policy recommendations are proposed: First, continuously strengthen digital infrastructure construction, especially accelerating the layout of new infrastructure such as 5G networks and data centers in the central and western regions; Second, deepen industrial digital transformation, promote the deep integration of digital technology and the real economy, and fully leverage the driving role of the digital economy in industrial structure upgrading; Third, improve differentiated regional policies, and formulate precise development strategies based on the development stages and resource endowments of the digital economy in different regions; Fourth, strengthen the cultivation and introduction of digital talent to provide intellectual support for the digital economy to empower high-quality development.

title: Effect of dietary isoleucine on the immunity, antioxidant status, tight junctions and microflora in the intestine of juvenile Jian carp (Cyprinus carpio var. Jian)
text:
Effect of dietary isoleucine on the immunity, antioxidant status, tight junctions and microflora in the intestine of juvenile Jian carp (Cyprinus carpio var. Jian)

Abstract: To investigate the effects of dietary isoleucine (Ile) levels on intestinal immune function, antioxidant status, tight junctions and microflora of juvenile Jian carp (Cyprinus carpio var. Jian), an 8-week feeding trial was conducted with juvenile Jian carp with an initial body weight of (10.5±0.2) g. Six isonitrogenous and isoenergetic diets were formulated with isoleucine levels of 0.5%, 0.8%, 1.1%, 1.4%, 1.7% and 2.0%, respectively. The results showed that when the dietary isoleucine level was 1.4%, the intestinal lysozyme and acid phosphatase activities and complement C3 content were significantly increased (P<0.05); the intestinal superoxide dismutase, catalase and glutathione peroxidase activities were significantly enhanced, and the malondialdehyde content was significantly reduced (P<0.05); the expression levels of intestinal tight junction protein genes (occludin, claudin-3, ZO-1) were significantly upregulated (P<0.05); meanwhile, the number of intestinal Lactobacillus was significantly increased, and the number of Escherichia coli was significantly decreased (P<0.05). Quadratic regression analysis showed that based on intestinal lysozyme activity and malondialdehyde content as evaluation indices, the optimal dietary isoleucine supplemental levels for juvenile Jian carp were 1.38% and 1.42% (5.52% and 5.68% of dietary protein), respectively. In summary, an appropriate isoleucine level can enhance intestinal immunity, improve antioxidant status, maintain intestinal barrier function and optimize intestinal microecology of juvenile Jian carp, thereby promoting intestinal health.

1 Introduction

Isoleucine is one of the essential amino acids for fish, participating in protein synthesis and energy metabolism, while also playing an important role in immune regulation and antioxidant defense. Jian carp is an important freshwater aquaculture species in China. During its intensive culture, nutritional imbalance often leads to intestinal barrier damage, decreased immunity and microecological disorder, which in turn induces diseases such as enteritis. The intestine is not only the main site for digestion and absorption of nutrients, but also the first line of defense against pathogen invasion. Intestinal tight junction proteins constitute the physical barrier between epithelial cells, while the intestinal microflora participates in nutrient metabolism and immune regulation. At present, research on the effects of isoleucine on the intestinal health of Jian carp is still insufficient. This experiment aimed to systematically evaluate the effects of graded isoleucine supplementation on intestinal immunity, antioxidant status, tight junctions and microflora of juvenile Jian carp, so as to provide a technical basis for the precise formulation of compound feed for Jian carp.

2 Analysis of Key Technologies

2.1 Experimental Design and Diet Formulation

The experiment adopted a single-factor gradient design, using casein and gelatin as protein sources, and fish oil and soybean oil as lipid sources, to formulate six groups of isonitrogenous (crude protein 32%) and isoenergetic (digestible energy 13.5 MJ/kg) diets. By adding L-isoleucine (purity ≥99%), the dietary isoleucine levels were adjusted to 0.5%, 0.8%, 1.1%, 1.4%, 1.7% and 2.0%, respectively, and the actual contents were verified by an amino acid analyzer. Each group had 3 replicates, with 30 fish per replicate, and was cultured in a recirculating water system for 8 weeks. During the culture period, the water temperature was controlled at (25±1)°C, dissolved oxygen >6 mg/L, and ammonia nitrogen <0.5 mg/L.

2.2 Determination of Intestinal Immune and Antioxidant Indices

After the feeding trial, the fish were fasted for 24 h, and 5 fish were randomly selected from each replicate and dissected aseptically to collect midgut tissues. Immune indices included lysozyme (LZM), acid phosphatase (ACP), alkaline phosphatase (AKP) activities and complement C3 and C4 contents, which were determined using kits from Nanjing Jiancheng Bioengineering Institute. Antioxidant indices included superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px) activities and malondialdehyde (MDA) content, which were also determined using commercial kits. All determinations were strictly performed according to the instructions, and each sample was measured in triplicate.

2.3 Analysis of Tight Junction Protein Gene Expression

About 50 mg of midgut tissue was collected, and Trizol reagent was added to extract total RNA. RNA integrity and concentration were detected by agarose gel electrophoresis and a nucleic acid protein analyzer. cDNA was synthesized by reverse transcription using a PrimeScript RT kit. Specific primers were designed based on the sequences of Jian carp occludin, claudin-3, ZO-1 and the internal reference gene β-actin in GenBank for real-time quantitative PCR (qRT-PCR). The reaction system was 20 μL, including 10 μL SYBR Green Master Mix, 0.4 μL each of upstream and downstream primers, 2 μL cDNA and 7.2 μL ddH2O. Amplification conditions: 95°C pre-denaturation for 30 s; 95°C for 5 s, 60°C for 30 s, for a total of 40 cycles. The 2^-ΔΔCt method was used to calculate the relative expression levels of target genes.

2.4 Analysis of Intestinal Microflora

The hindgut contents were collected aseptically, and the numbers of Lactobacillus, Escherichia coli, Aeromonas and Bifidobacterium were determined by the plate counting method. Lactobacillus was cultured on MRS medium at 37°C anaerobically for 48 h; Escherichia coli was cultured on MacConkey medium at 37°C aerobically for 24 h; Aeromonas was cultured on RS medium at 28°C for 24 h; Bifidobacterium was cultured on TPY medium at 37°C anaerobically for 48 h. The results were expressed as the logarithm of colony-forming units per gram of contents (CFU/g).

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

3.1 Effects on Intestinal Immune Indices

With the increase in dietary isoleucine level, the intestinal LZM and ACP activities and complement C3 content showed a trend of first increasing and then decreasing. The LZM activity in the 1.4% group was increased by 42.6% compared with the 0.5% group (P<0.05), the ACP activity was increased by 35.8% (P<0.05), and the complement C3 content was increased by 28.4% (P<0.05). Quadratic regression analysis showed that based on LZM activity as the index, the optimal isoleucine level was 1.38% (5.52% of dietary protein). The results indicated that appropriate isoleucine could enhance the intestinal non-specific immune function of juvenile Jian carp.

3.2 Effects on Intestinal Antioxidant Status

The intestinal SOD, CAT and GSH-Px activities in the 1.4% group were increased by 31.2%, 27.5% and 38.9%, respectively, compared with the 0.5% group (P<0.05), and the MDA content was decreased by 33.6% (P<0.05). Based on MDA content as the evaluation index, the optimal isoleucine level was 1.42% (5.68% of dietary protein). This indicated that isoleucine could maintain the intestinal redox balance by enhancing antioxidant enzyme activities and inhibiting lipid peroxidation.

3.3 Effects on Tight Junction Protein Gene Expression

Compared with the 0.5% group, the mRNA expression levels of occludin, claudin-3 and ZO-1 in the 1.4% group were upregulated by 2.1-fold, 1.8-fold and 2.3-fold, respectively (P<0.05). The expression levels in both the low-level (0.5%) and high-level (2.0%) groups were significantly reduced. This indicated that isoleucine could promote the synthesis of tight junction proteins and enhance the intestinal physical barrier function.

3.4 Effects on Intestinal Microflora

The numbers of Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium in the 1.4% group were significantly higher than those in the 0.5% group (P<0.05), while the numbers of Escherichia coli and Aeromonas were significantly reduced (P<0.05). The ratio of Lactobacillus/Escherichia coli increased from 1.2 in the 0.5% group to 3.8 in the 1.4% group. This indicated that isoleucine could optimize the intestinal microecology and inhibit the proliferation of potential pathogens.

3.5 Benefit Analysis

Based on the optimal supplemental level of 1.4%, approximately 9 kg of L-isoleucine was required per ton of feed, increasing the cost by about 180 yuan. However, during the experimental period, the survival rate of juvenile Jian carp in the 1.4% group was increased by 12.3% compared with the 0.5% group, the specific growth rate was increased by 18.7%, and the feed conversion ratio was reduced by 0.21. Comprehensive estimation showed that for every 10,000 Jian carp, the income could be increased by about 650 yuan per culture cycle, with an input-output ratio of 1:3.6, indicating significant economic benefits.

4 Conclusion

When the dietary isoleucine level was 1.38%–1.42% (5.52%–5.68% of dietary protein), the intestinal immunity and antioxidant capacity of juvenile Jian carp could be significantly enhanced, the expression of tight junction protein genes could be upregulated, and the intestinal microflora could be optimized, thereby improving intestinal health and increasing aquaculture benefits. It is recommended that the supplemental amount of isoleucine in compound feed for juvenile Jian carp be controlled at about 1.4%.

title: Highly Dispersed CoNi Alloy Embedded in N-doped Graphitic Carbon for Catalytic Transfer Hydrogenation of Biomass-derived Furfural
text:
Abstract: This study aims at the efficient conversion of biomass-derived furfural, and a highly dispersed CoNi alloy embedded in nitrogen-doped graphitic carbon (CoNi@NC) catalyst was designed and prepared. Through the coordination self-assembly of glucose, melamine, and cobalt-nickel salts followed by high-temperature pyrolysis, uniform embedding of CoNi alloy nanoparticles (average particle size of approximately 4.2 nm) within the nitrogen-doped carbon framework was achieved. The catalyst structure was systematically characterized by X-ray diffraction, transmission electron microscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and other techniques. In the catalytic transfer hydrogenation reaction using isopropanol as the hydrogen donor, the CoNi@NC catalyst exhibited excellent catalytic performance for the conversion of furfural to furfuryl alcohol, achieving a furfural conversion of 98.6% and a furfuryl alcohol selectivity of 96.3% under conditions of 160 °C for 4 h. The catalyst showed no significant decrease in activity after 5 cycles of reuse. The study indicates that the electronic synergistic effect between the CoNi alloy and nitrogen-doped carbon, as well as the highly dispersed active sites, are key to its excellent performance. This study provides a novel design approach for highly efficient catalysts for the valorization of biomass-based platform molecules.

Keywords: CoNi alloy; nitrogen-doped graphitic carbon; catalytic transfer hydrogenation; furfural; biomass conversion

1 Introduction

With the increasing depletion of fossil resources and the intensification of environmental issues, the efficient utilization of biomass resources has received widespread attention. Furfural is an important biomass-based platform compound that can be obtained in large quantities through the hydrolysis of hemicellulose. The selective hydrogenation of furfural to furfuryl alcohol is a key step in the preparation of furan resins, pharmaceutical intermediates, and biofuel additives. Traditional hydrogenation processes mostly use high-pressure hydrogen, which poses safety hazards and high equipment costs. Catalytic transfer hydrogenation (CTH) uses alcohols and other compounds as hydrogen donors, offering mild conditions and safe operation, making it an alternative approach.

Although noble metal catalysts (such as Pt and Pd) exhibit high activity, they are costly and resource-scarce. Non-noble metal alloy catalysts, especially CoNi bimetallic systems, have attracted considerable attention due to their synergistic electronic effects and tunable composition. However, nanoalloys are prone to agglomeration, leading to a reduction in active sites. Embedding them into a nitrogen-doped graphitic carbon matrix can effectively anchor metal particles, regulate electronic structure, and enhance mass transfer. In this study, glucose was used as the carbon source and melamine as the nitrogen source, and the CoNi@NC catalyst was prepared through one-pot coordination pyrolysis. Its performance in the catalytic transfer hydrogenation of furfural was systematically investigated, and the structure-activity relationship was discussed.

2 Materials and Methods

2.1 Catalyst Preparation

Glucose (2.0 g) and melamine (1.5 g) were dissolved in 60 mL of deionized water, and Co(NO₃)₂·6H₂O and Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O (total metal molar amount of 0.5 mmol, Co/Ni molar ratio of 1:1) were added. After stirring for 30 min, the mixture was transferred to a hydrothermal autoclave and reacted at 180 °C for 12 h. The resulting precursor was dried and then heated to 800 °C at a rate of 5 °C/min under N₂ atmosphere and held for 2 h, followed by natural cooling to obtain CoNi@NC. Control samples included monometallic Co@NC, Ni@NC, and metal-free NC.

2.2 Characterization Methods

X-ray diffraction (XRD) was used to analyze the phase composition; transmission electron microscopy (TEM) was used to observe the morphology and particle size; X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was used to analyze the surface elemental valence states; nitrogen adsorption-desorption was used to determine the specific surface area; inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) was used to determine the metal loading.

2.3 Catalytic Performance Evaluation

The catalytic transfer hydrogenation reaction was carried out in a 25 mL high-pressure reactor. Typical conditions: furfural 0.5 mmol, isopropanol 5 mL, catalyst 20 mg, reaction temperature 160 °C, reaction time 4 h. The reaction products were quantitatively analyzed by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry. The furfural conversion and furfuryl alcohol selectivity were calculated according to standard formulas. In the cycling experiments, the catalyst was recovered by centrifugation, washed with ethanol, dried, and directly used for the next reaction.

3 Results and Analysis

3.1 Catalyst Structure Characterization

The XRD pattern shows that CoNi@NC exhibits diffraction peaks at 2θ = 44.3°, 51.5°, and 76.1°, corresponding to the (111), (200), and (220) crystal planes of face-centered cubic CoNi alloy, with no independent Co or Ni phases, indicating the formation of the alloy. Meanwhile, a broad graphitic carbon (002) peak appears at approximately 26°. TEM images show that CoNi alloy nanoparticles are uniformly dispersed in the carbon matrix, with an average particle size of 4.2 ± 0.6 nm and no obvious agglomeration. High-resolution TEM reveals a lattice spacing of 0.203 nm, corresponding to the CoNi (111) plane. XPS analysis indicates that both metallic and oxidized states coexist in the Co 2p and Ni 2p spectra, and the N 1s spectrum can be fitted into pyridinic nitrogen, pyrrolic nitrogen, and graphitic nitrogen, among which pyridinic nitrogen coordinated with metals can enhance the anchoring effect. The BET specific surface area is 486 m²/g, with obvious mesoporous structure.

3.2 Catalytic Performance

Under conditions of 160 °C and 4 h, the CoNi@NC-catalyzed furfural conversion reached 98.6%, with a furfuryl alcohol selectivity of 96.3%. The conversion rates of the control samples were 72.4% for Co@NC, 65.8% for Ni@NC, and almost no activity for NC. This indicates that the synergistic effect of the CoNi alloy is significant. Reaction time optimization showed that the conversion was 76.2% at 2 h and nearly complete at 4 h. Temperature optimization indicated that the conversion was only 58.3% at 140 °C, with 160 °C being optimal. When the catalyst dosage was increased to 30 mg, the conversion slightly increased to 99.1%, but the selectivity remained unchanged.

3.3 Cycling Stability

After 5 cycles, the furfural conversion over CoNi@NC still reached 95.2%, with a furfuryl alcohol selectivity of 94.8%. ICP-OES showed that the concentrations of Co and Ni in the filtrate after the reaction were both below 0.5 ppm, indicating minimal metal leaching. TEM observation of the catalyst after cycling showed that the particles slightly increased in size (average 5.1 nm) but still maintained high dispersion.

4 Discussion

The excellent catalytic performance of CoNi@NC can be attributed to the following factors: First, the electron transfer between Co and Ni in the CoNi alloy regulates the d-band center, optimizing the adsorption and activation of the C=O bond in furfural molecules. XPS results confirm the coexistence of metallic and oxidized states, and Coδ⁺-Niδ⁻ synergistic sites may exist at the interface, promoting the dehydrogenation of isopropanol to generate active hydrogen species. Second, the strong coordination between pyridinic nitrogen in the nitrogen-doped carbon matrix and metals effectively anchors the alloy particles, inhibiting their migration and agglomeration while improving electronic conductivity. Third, the high specific surface area and mesoporous structure facilitate reactant diffusion and exposure of active sites. Compared with the CoNi/AC (conversion 85%) and Ni@C (72%) reported in the literature, this catalyst exhibits superior performance. In addition, isopropanol as a hydrogen donor undergoes dehydrogenation on the catalyst surface to generate acetone and active hydrogen, which is directly transferred to the C=O bond of furfural, achieving selective hydrogenation. This pathway avoids high-pressure hydrogen and conforms to the principles of green chemistry.

5 Conclusion

In this study, a highly dispersed CoNi alloy embedded in nitrogen-doped graphitic carbon catalyst was successfully prepared and applied to the catalytic transfer hydrogenation of furfural. CoNi@NC achieved 98.6% furfural conversion and 96.3% furfuryl alcohol selectivity under conditions of 160 °C and 4 h, with excellent cycling stability. The electronic synergistic effect between the CoNi alloy and nitrogen-doped carbon, as well as the strong metal-support interaction, are key to the performance enhancement. The catalyst preparation method is simple and low-cost, providing a new strategy for the efficient conversion of biomass-based platform molecules with potential industrial application prospects.

title: Effects of Elevated CO2 on Nutritional Quality of Vegetables: A Review
text:
Effects of Elevated CO2 on Nutritional Quality of Vegetables: A Review

Abstract: The increase in atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration has a significant impact on the nutritional quality of vegetable crops. This paper reviews recent research progress on the effects of elevated CO2 on nutritional components in vegetables, including carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins, minerals, and secondary metabolites. Overall, elevated CO2 can promote photosynthesis in vegetables and increase carbohydrate accumulation, but often leads to decreased contents of proteins, some vitamins, and minerals. This paper analyzes the key factors affecting nutritional quality and discusses future research directions, aiming to provide a reference for facility vegetable production to adapt to climate change.

Keywords: elevated CO2; vegetables; nutritional quality; carbohydrates; minerals

1 Introduction

Since the Industrial Revolution, atmospheric carbon dioxide concentration has risen from approximately 280 μmol·mol⁻¹ to currently over 410 μmol·mol⁻¹, and is projected to reach 550–700 μmol·mol⁻¹ by the end of this century. As an important source of vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber in the human diet, the nutritional quality of vegetables is directly related to population health. As a substrate for photosynthesis, changes in CO2 concentration inevitably affect carbon-nitrogen metabolism and nutrient accumulation in vegetables. However, the effects of elevated CO2 on vegetable nutritional quality are not unidirectional; there are both positive effects of promoting carbohydrate accumulation and negative effects of reducing protein, mineral, and some vitamin contents. Based on relevant domestic and international studies, this paper systematically reviews the patterns and key regulatory factors of elevated CO2 effects on vegetable nutritional quality, aiming to provide a theoretical basis for high-quality facility vegetable production.

2 Key Technical Analysis

2.1 Effects of Elevated CO2 on Carbohydrate Content

Numerous studies have shown that elevated CO2 significantly promotes the accumulation of soluble sugars and starch in vegetables. For example, under 600–800 μmol·mol⁻¹ CO2 conditions, fructose and glucose contents in tomato fruit can increase by 15%–30%, and soluble sugar content in lettuce leaves increases by more than 20%. The mechanism lies in: elevated CO2 enhances the carboxylation efficiency of ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (Rubisco), inhibits photorespiration, and enables more photosynthetic products to be converted into carbohydrates. However, the magnitude of carbohydrate accumulation varies with vegetable species, cultivar, and growth stage. Leafy vegetables generally respond more strongly than fruit vegetables, and C3 vegetables respond more strongly than C4 vegetables. In addition, long-term elevated CO2 treatment may lead to excessive starch accumulation in leaves, which in turn feedback-inhibits photosynthesis and needs to be alleviated by adjusting nitrogen supply.

2.2 Effects of Elevated CO2 on Protein and Amino Acid Contents

In contrast to carbohydrates, elevated CO2 typically leads to decreased protein content in vegetables. Studies on cereals such as wheat and rice, as well as leafy vegetables such as spinach and lettuce, have found that elevated CO2 reduces total nitrogen concentration in plants by 10%–20%, with soluble protein content decreasing correspondingly. The main reasons include: first, the carbohydrate dilution effect, where non-structural carbohydrate accumulation leads to reduced nitrogen concentration per unit dry weight; second, elevated CO2 inhibits nitrate reductase activity, reducing nitrogen assimilation capacity; third, decreased stomatal conductance leads to reduced transpiration flow, affecting root uptake of nitrate nitrogen. Amino acid composition also changes, with the proportion of non-essential amino acids such as glutamate and aspartate increasing, while the proportion of essential amino acids such as lysine and methionine decreasing, potentially reducing the nutritional value of vegetable proteins.

2.3 Effects of Elevated CO2 on Vitamin and Mineral Contents

Regarding vitamins, the effect of elevated CO2 on vitamin C varies with vegetable species. Most studies show that vitamin C content in fruit vegetables such as tomato and pepper decreases by 10%–20%, while changes in leafy vegetables such as spinach and lettuce are not significant or slightly increase. Vitamin E and carotenoid contents generally show no significant changes or slight increases. Regarding minerals, elevated CO2 generally reduces the concentrations of calcium, magnesium, zinc, iron, and other elements in vegetables, with reductions of up to 5%–15%. This is mainly related to reduced transpiration flow, decreased root absorption capacity, and biomass dilution effects. For example, calcium content in lettuce decreases by approximately 12% and zinc content by approximately 9% under 800 μmol·mol⁻¹ CO2. Notably, potassium content is less affected, possibly related to its high mobility within plants.

2.4 Effects of Elevated CO2 on Secondary Metabolites

Regarding secondary metabolites, the effects of elevated CO2 on antioxidant substances such as phenolics and flavonoids are relatively complex. Most studies indicate that elevated CO2 can induce the activity of key enzymes in the phenylpropanoid metabolic pathway (such as phenylalanine ammonia-lyase), promoting phenolic substance accumulation. For example, total phenolic content in tomato fruit increases by 15%–25% under 700 μmol·mol⁻¹ CO2. However, some studies have reported that elevated CO2 reduces anthocyanin content. This discrepancy may be related to vegetable species, CO2 concentration levels, and nitrogen supply conditions. Overall, the effects of elevated CO2 on secondary metabolites still require more systematic research.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

Based on existing research, the effects of elevated CO2 on vegetable nutritional quality can be summarized as "one increase and three decreases": carbohydrates increase, while proteins, minerals, and some vitamins decrease. From a production benefit perspective, elevated CO2 can increase vegetable biomass and yield by 10%–30%, but the decline in nutritional quality may weaken their market value. Taking facility tomatoes as an example, under 800 μmol·mol⁻¹ CO2, single fruit weight increases by approximately 18%, but fruit calcium content decreases by 12% and soluble protein decreases by 15%, resulting in reduced fruit firmness and shortened shelf life. If nitrogen management is optimized (such as increasing the proportion of nitrate nitrogen) and calcium, zinc, and other trace elements are supplemented, the quality decline can be alleviated to some extent. In addition, selecting cultivars that are insensitive to elevated CO2, or adopting intermittent CO2 enrichment strategies, can also help balance yield and quality. From the consumer's perspective, increased carbohydrate content in vegetables may increase energy intake, but decreased proteins and minerals may exacerbate the risk of "hidden hunger," especially for populations that rely on vegetables as a primary dietary source.

4 Conclusions

The effects of elevated CO2 on vegetable nutritional quality are diverse and complex, generally manifested as increased carbohydrate accumulation, while protein, mineral, and some vitamin contents decrease. The mechanisms involve carbon-nitrogen metabolic imbalance, reduced transpiration flow, and dilution effects. Future research should focus on: first, the differences in responses of different vegetable species and cultivars to elevated CO2 and their molecular mechanisms; second, the interactions between CO2 and other environmental factors (such as temperature, nitrogen, and water); third, mitigating negative effects through agronomic measures (such as nitrogen regulation and foliar spraying of trace elements) and breeding approaches. Facility vegetable production should establish precise regulation strategies based on CO2 concentration monitoring to ensure nutritional quality while increasing yield, in order to adapt to future climate change.

title: Phoenixin participated in regulation of food intake and growth in spotted scat, Scatophagus argus
text:
Phoenixin Participates in the Regulation of Feeding and Growth in the Spotted Scat (*Scatophagus argus*)

 Abstract

Phoenixin (PNX) is a neuropeptide newly discovered in recent years, and has been confirmed to participate in feeding regulation and reproductive regulation in mammals; however, research on its function in teleost fish remains lacking. In this study, the spotted scat (*Scatophagus argus*), an important mariculture fish species in southern China, was used as the research subject. The coding sequence of its *pnx* gene was cloned, its tissue expression characteristics were analyzed, and the effects of intraperitoneal injection of different doses of synthetic PNX peptide (0, 10, 100 ng/g body weight) on the feeding behavior and growth performance of the spotted scat were investigated. The results showed that the open reading frame of the spotted scat *pnx* gene is 240 bp in length, encoding a 79-amino-acid precursor protein; tissue expression analysis revealed that *pnx* mRNA expression was highest in the hypothalamus and pituitary, followed by the intestine and liver. Intraperitoneal injection of PNX significantly inhibited short-term (0–2 h) food intake in a dose-dependent manner; after 14 d of continuous injection, the weight gain rate, specific growth rate, and feed conversion efficiency of fish in the high-dose group were all significantly reduced (*P*<0.05), accompanied by downregulated hypothalamic *npy* mRNA expression and upregulated *pomc* mRNA expression. This study is the first to confirm that PNX has feeding-suppressing and growth-regulating functions in the spotted scat, providing a new theoretical basis for a deeper understanding of the feeding regulatory network in fish.

Keywords: Phoenixin; spotted scat; feeding regulation; growth; neuropeptide

 1 Introduction

Feeding regulation is one of the core issues in aquaculture, directly related to feed costs, farming efficiency, and environmental loading of water bodies. The feeding behavior of fish is jointly regulated by multiple neuropeptides and hormones secreted by the central nervous system and peripheral tissues, forming a complex appetite regulation network. The hypothalamus, as the center of feeding regulation, integrates peripheral signals by expressing orexigenic factors (such as neuropeptide Y, NPY) and anorexigenic factors (such as proopiomelanocortin, POMC) to maintain energy homeostasis.

Phoenixin (PNX) is an endogenous neuropeptide first discovered in the mouse hypothalamus by Yosten et al. in 2013, produced by enzymatic cleavage of a precursor protein encoded by the *smpd3* gene. Studies have shown that PNX has multiple biological functions in mammals: central injection of PNX can dose-dependently inhibit food intake while promoting the secretion of gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH), participating in reproductive regulation. In addition, PNX is also involved in processes such as pain perception, anxiety behavior, and cardiovascular regulation. However, research on PNX in teleost fish is currently extremely limited, and whether it participates in feeding regulation in fish has not been reported.

The spotted scat (*Scatophagus argus*) belongs to the order Perciformes, family Scatophagidae, and is widely distributed in the Indo-Pacific Ocean. It is an important economic aquaculture fish species along the southeastern coast of China. This fish has advantages such as euryhalinity, fast growth, and delicious flesh, and its farming scale has been continuously expanding in recent years. However, research on the molecular mechanisms of feeding regulation in the spotted scat remains relatively weak, limiting the development of precision nutritional regulation technologies. This study aims to clone the *pnx* gene of the spotted scat, analyze its tissue expression pattern, and investigate the regulatory effects of PNX on feeding and growth through in vivo injection experiments, in order to provide new insights into the theory of feeding regulation in fish and provide a scientific basis for precision feeding strategies in spotted scat aquaculture.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Experimental Animals

Experimental spotted scat were purchased from an aquaculture farm in Zhanjiang City, Guangdong Province, with an average body weight of (45.6±3.2) g. Before the experiment, the fish were acclimated for 2 weeks in an indoor recirculating aquaculture system at a water temperature of (26±1)°C, salinity of 25±1, and a photoperiod of 12L:12D, and were fed to satiation twice daily (8:00 and 16:00) with commercial compound feed.

 2.2 Total RNA Extraction and Gene Cloning

Hypothalamus tissue of the spotted scat was collected, and total RNA was extracted using Trizol reagent (Invitrogen). After DNase I treatment, cDNA was synthesized by reverse transcription. Degenerate primers were designed based on the *pnx* sequences of closely related species in the NCBI database, and the full-length cDNA sequence of spotted scat *pnx* was obtained through RT-PCR and RACE techniques. DNAMAN software was used for sequence assembly and amino acid translation.

 2.3 Tissue Expression Analysis

A total of 12 tissues were collected from the spotted scat, including the hypothalamus, pituitary, telencephalon, cerebellum, medulla oblongata, heart, liver, spleen, kidney, intestine, muscle, and gonad. Total RNA was extracted and reverse transcribed. Real-time quantitative PCR (qRT-PCR) was used to detect the tissue expression distribution of *pnx* mRNA, with *β-actin* as the internal reference gene. The PCR reaction conditions were: 95°C pre-denaturation for 30 s; 95°C for 5 s, 60°C for 30 s, for a total of 40 cycles. The 2^−ΔΔCt method was used to calculate relative expression levels.

 2.4 In Vivo Injection Experiment

A total of 120 spotted scat were randomly divided into 4 groups (30 fish per group, 3 replicates), namely the control group (injected with 0.9% saline), low-dose group (10 ng/g body weight PNX), medium-dose group (50 ng/g body weight PNX), and high-dose group (100 ng/g body weight PNX). The PNX synthetic peptide was synthesized by Shanghai Sangon Biotech Co., Ltd., with a purity of >95%. Intraperitoneal injection was performed once daily for 14 consecutive days. During the experimental period, food intake was recorded daily, and body weight was measured at the beginning and end of the experiment.

 2.5 Detection of Feeding-Related Gene Expression
