Methods A total of 120 patients who underwent gynecological abdominal surgery in our hospital from January 2023 to June 2024 were selected and divided into an observation group and a control group according to the random number table method, with 60 cases in each group. The control group received a conventional postoperative analgesia regimen (patient-controlled intravenous analgesia pump), while the observation group received electroacupuncture combined with auricular acupuncture in addition to conventional analgesia. The electroacupuncture points were bilateral Zusanli (ST36), Sanyinjiao (SP6), and Hegu (LI4), and the auricular acupuncture points were Shenmen, Sympathetic, Subcortex, and Uterus. The visual analogue scale (VAS) scores at 6 h, 12 h, 24 h, and 48 h after surgery, the number of effective analgesic pump presses, serum interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) levels, gastrointestinal function recovery time, and the incidence of adverse reactions were compared between the two groups. Results The VAS scores of the observation group at 12 h, 24 h, and 48 h after surgery were significantly lower than those of the control group (P<0.05); the number of effective analgesic pump presses in the observation group was significantly less than that in the control group (P<0.01); the serum IL-6 and TNF-α levels at 24 h after surgery in the observation group were significantly lower than those in the control group (P<0.05); the recovery time of bowel sounds, time to first flatus, and time to first defecation in the observation group were all significantly shorter than those in the control group (P<0.05); there was no statistically significant difference in the incidence of adverse reactions between the two groups (P>0.05). Conclusion Electroacupuncture combined with auricular acupuncture can effectively alleviate pain after gynecological abdominal surgery, inhibit inflammatory responses, and promote gastrointestinal function recovery, with good safety. It can serve as an effective supplementary method for postoperative multimodal analgesia.

Keywords: electroacupuncture; auricular acupuncture; gynecological abdominal surgery; postoperative pain; randomized controlled trial; multimodal analgesia

1 Introduction

Gynecological abdominal surgery (such as hysterectomy, ovarian cystectomy, myomectomy, etc.) is a common clinical procedure, and the incidence of postoperative pain is as high as 70%–90%. Postoperative pain not only increases patient suffering, but can also activate the sympathetic nervous system, inhibit gastrointestinal peristalsis, prolong hospital stay, and increase medical burden. At present, postoperative analgesia is mainly based on opioid patient-controlled analgesia, but it has adverse reactions such as nausea and vomiting, respiratory depression, and intestinal paralysis, and the analgesic effect is unsatisfactory in some patients. Therefore, exploring safe and effective auxiliary analgesic methods has important clinical significance.

Acupuncture therapy, as an external treatment characteristic of traditional Chinese medicine, is increasingly widely used in the field of postoperative analgesia. Electroacupuncture enhances the acupuncture effect through electrical stimulation at different frequencies, can promote the release of endogenous opioid peptides, and inhibit pain transmission. Auricular acupuncture regulates autonomic nervous function and the endocrine-immune network by stimulating specific auricular points. Previous studies have mostly applied electroacupuncture or auricular acupuncture alone, and research on the combination of the two for postoperative analgesia after gynecological abdominal surgery is still insufficient. This study intends to systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of electroacupuncture combined with auricular acupuncture in pain management after gynecological abdominal surgery through a randomized controlled trial, so as to provide evidence-based basis for clinical promotion.

2 Materials and Methods

2.1 General information A total of 120 patients who underwent abdominal surgery in the gynecology department of our hospital from January 2023 to June 2024 were selected. Inclusion criteria: age 18–65 years; undergoing elective gynecological abdominal surgery; American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) grade I–II; informed consent and signed consent form. Exclusion criteria: long-term use of analgesics before surgery; skin infection at the acupuncture site; coagulation dysfunction; severe cardiac, hepatic, or renal insufficiency; pregnancy or lactation. They were divided into an observation group and a control group according to the random number table method, with 60 cases in each group. There were no statistically significant differences in age, body mass index, type of surgery, operative time, or intraoperative blood loss between the two groups (P>0.05), indicating comparability.

2.2 Intervention methods Both groups received general anesthesia and used a patient-controlled intravenous analgesia pump after surgery (sufentanil 100 μg + flurbiprofen axetil 100 mg + normal saline to 100 mL, background dose 2 mL/h, single press 0.5 mL, lockout time 15 min). The control group received only the analgesia pump. The observation group received electroacupuncture combined with auricular acupuncture on the basis of the control group: electroacupuncture was performed at bilateral Zusanli (ST36), Sanyinjiao (SP6), and Hegu (LI4), using Huatuo brand disposable acupuncture needles (0.30 mm × 40 mm); after perpendicular insertion and obtaining deqi, an electroacupuncture apparatus (SDZ-II type) was connected, with dilatational wave selected, frequency 2/100 Hz, and current intensity based on patient tolerance, for 30 min each time, starting at 6 h after surgery, once daily for 3 consecutive days. Auricular acupuncture was performed at Shenmen, Sympathetic, Subcortex, and Uterus, using Vaccaria seed pressure, pressed 3–5 times daily, 1 min per point each time, retained for 3 days.

2.3 Observation indicators ① Pain score: VAS score (0–10 points) was used to evaluate the degree of pain at 6 h, 12 h, 24 h, and 48 h after surgery. ② Number of effective analgesic pump presses. ③ Inflammatory indicators: venous blood was collected at 24 h after surgery, and serum IL-6 and TNF-α levels were detected by ELISA. ④ Gastrointestinal function recovery indicators: recovery time of bowel sounds, time to first flatus, and time to first defecation. ⑤ Adverse reactions: nausea and vomiting, dizziness, drowsiness, and acupuncture-related adverse events.

2.4 Statistical methods SPSS 26.0 software was used. Measurement data were expressed as mean ± standard deviation, independent samples t-test was used for comparison between groups, and repeated measures analysis of variance was used for repeated measurement data; count data were expressed as rates, and the χ² test was used. P<0.05 was considered statistically significant.

3 Results and Analysis

3.1 Comparison of VAS scores between the two groups The VAS scores of the observation group at 12 h, 24 h, and 48 h after surgery were (3.12±0.84), (2.35±0.71), and (1.48±0.52) points, respectively, while those of the control group were (3.86±0.92), (3.02±0.78), and (2.13±0.64) points, respectively. The observation group was significantly lower than the control group (t=4.621, 4.913, 6.127, P<0.05). There was no statistically significant difference in VAS scores between the two groups at 6 h after surgery (P>0.05).

3.2 Comparison of the number of analgesic pump presses between the two groups The number of effective analgesic pump presses within 48 h after surgery in the observation group was (5.2±2.1) times, significantly less than (9.8±3.4) times in the control group (t=8.874, P<0.01).

3.3 Comparison of inflammatory indicators between the two groups At 24 h after surgery, serum IL-6 in the observation group was (45.32±12.17) pg/mL and TNF-α was (18.64±5.23) pg/mL; those in the control group were (62.85±15.42) pg/mL and (26.37±6.81) pg/mL, respectively. The observation group was significantly lower than the control group (t=6.832, 6.945, P<0.05).

3.4 Comparison of gastrointestinal function recovery between the two groups The recovery time of bowel sounds, time to first flatus, and time to first defecation in the observation group were (18.35±4.62) h, (26.48±5.73) h, and (52.16±8.94) h, respectively, while those in the control group were (24.72±5.81) h, (34.15±6.92) h, and (63.82±10.27) h, respectively. The observation group was significantly shorter than the control group (t=6.541, 6.618, 6.782, P<0.05).

3.5 Comparison of adverse reactions between the two groups In the observation group, there were 3 cases of nausea and vomiting and 2 cases of dizziness, with an incidence of adverse reactions of 8.33%; in the control group, there were 5 cases of nausea and vomiting, 3 cases of dizziness, and 2 cases of drowsiness, with an incidence of 16.67%. There was no statistically significant difference between the two groups (χ²=1.926, P>0.05). No serious acupuncture-related adverse events were observed in the observation group.

4 Discussion

Postoperative pain is a major clinical problem faced by patients undergoing gynecological abdominal surgery, and its mechanism involves the release of inflammatory mediators after tissue injury, peripheral sensitization, and central sensitization. Although opioids have definite analgesic effects, their related adverse reactions limit their application. The concept of multimodal analgesia advocates combining analgesic methods with different mechanisms to reduce opioid dosage and adverse reactions.

The results of this study showed that electroacupuncture combined with auricular acupuncture can significantly reduce VAS scores at 12–48 h after gynecological abdominal surgery and reduce the number of analgesic pump presses, suggesting that it has a clear auxiliary analgesic effect. Its mechanism may be related to electroacupuncture promoting the release of β-endorphin and enkephalin and activating the descending inhibitory system; auricular acupuncture stimulation at Shenmen, Sympathetic, and other points can regulate autonomic nervous function, inhibit sympathetic excitation, and enhance the analgesic effect. In addition, the levels of IL-6 and TNF-α at 24 h after surgery in the observation group were significantly reduced, suggesting that electroacupuncture combined with auricular acupuncture can inhibit excessive postoperative inflammatory response and reduce pain sensitization. In terms of gastrointestinal function, the recovery of bowel sounds and the time to flatus and defecation in the observation group were significantly shortened, which may be related to acupuncture at Zusanli (ST36) and Sanyinjiao (SP6) regulating gastrointestinal hormone secretion and promoting vagus nerve excitation. In terms of safety, there was no significant difference in the incidence of adverse reactions between the two groups, suggesting that the combined regimen is safe and feasible.

This study has certain limitations: the sample size was small, it was a single-center design, the follow-up time was short, and blinded assessment was not used. Future multicenter, large-sample, double-blind randomized controlled trials are needed for further verification.

5 Conclusion

Electroacupuncture combined with auricular acupuncture can effectively alleviate pain after gynecological abdominal surgery, reduce the demand for analgesics, inhibit inflammatory responses, and promote gastrointestinal function recovery, without increasing adverse reactions. It can serve as an effective auxiliary method for postoperative multimodal analgesia and is worthy of clinical promotion and application.

title: Optimization of Nitrogen Fertilizer Application Enhances Biocontrol Function and Net Income
text:
Optimizing Nitrogen Fertilizer Application Enhances Biological Control Function and Net Income

Abstract: To clarify the synergistic effects of nitrogen fertilizer application levels on farmland biological control function and economic benefits, this study took the winter wheat–summer maize rotation system in the North China Plain as the object, set four treatments of conventional nitrogen application, 20% nitrogen reduction, 40% nitrogen reduction, and no nitrogen application, and monitored natural enemy insect population density, aphid occurrence, crop yield, and net income for two consecutive years. The results showed that under the 20% nitrogen reduction treatment, the numbers of natural enemies such as ladybeetles, lacewings, and spiders increased by 32.6%, 28.4%, and 21.7%, respectively, compared with conventional nitrogen application; the aphid population density at the peak period decreased by 41.2%, and the biological control function was significantly enhanced. At the same time, nitrogen fertilizer input was reduced, yield did not show a significant decline, and net income increased by 18.5%. Although the 40% nitrogen reduction treatment further increased the number of natural enemies, yield decreased significantly, and net income was instead lower than that of the conventional treatment. Comprehensive analysis indicated that reducing nitrogen fertilizer by 20% on the basis of conventional nitrogen application (i.e., reducing the pure nitrogen rate from 240 kg/hm² to 192 kg/hm²) can achieve synergistic improvement of biological control function and economic benefits, and is a green production technology model worthy of promotion.

Keywords: nitrogen fertilizer optimization; biological control; natural enemy insects; net income; green production

1 Introduction

Excessive application of chemical nitrogen fertilizer is a prominent problem in China's current grain production. In pursuit of high yield, nitrogen fertilizer rates in many regions far exceed crop demand, leading to soil acidification, water eutrophication, and increased greenhouse gas emissions. At the same time, excessive nitrogen fertilizer increases leaf nitrogen content in crops, providing high-quality food sources for piercing-sucking pests such as aphids, which instead exacerbates pest occurrence and forms a vicious cycle of "the more fertilizer applied, the more pesticide sprayed." Against this background, how to optimize nitrogen fertilizer management to both ensure crop yield and enhance the natural biological control function of farmland ecosystems has become a key issue in the green transformation of agriculture.

Biological control function refers to the ability of natural enemy insects in farmland ecosystems to regulate pest populations. The abundance and diversity of natural enemies such as ladybeetles, lacewings, spiders, and parasitic wasps directly determine whether pests outbreak. Studies have shown that nitrogen fertilizer application indirectly affects the interaction between natural enemies and pests by changing crop nutritional quality and field microclimate. Moderate nitrogen reduction can lower aphid reproduction rates while avoiding adverse effects on natural enemies, thereby improving biological control efficiency. However, the quantitative relationship among nitrogen reduction magnitude, biological control function, yield, and net income still lacks systematic research. Through a two-year field experiment, this study explored the effects of different nitrogen fertilizer levels on natural enemy populations, aphid occurrence, and economic benefits, aiming to provide technical basis for the coordinated promotion of nitrogen fertilizer reduction and biological control.

2 Analysis of Key Technologies

2.1 Gradient Design of Nitrogen Fertilizer Application Levels

Four nitrogen application treatments were set in the experiment: conventional nitrogen application (N240, pure nitrogen 240 kg/hm², with base fertilizer and topdressing each accounting for 50%), 20% nitrogen reduction (N192, pure nitrogen 192 kg/hm²), 40% nitrogen reduction (N144, pure nitrogen 144 kg/hm²), and no nitrogen application (N0). The amounts of phosphorus and potassium fertilizers were the same among all treatments, and management measures such as irrigation and weed control were identical. In the winter wheat season, nitrogen fertilizer was applied twice, as base fertilizer and topdressing at the jointing stage; in the summer maize season, it was applied twice, as base fertilizer and topdressing at the large trumpet stage. A randomized block design was adopted, with three replicates and a plot area of 60 m². The experiment was conducted for two consecutive years (2022–2023 and 2023–2024) in a typical fluvo-aquic soil area of the North China Plain.

2.2 Monitoring Methods for Natural Enemy Insects and Aphid Populations

Natural enemy insects were surveyed using the five-point sampling method, with 10 plants taken per point in each plot and surveys conducted every 7 days. The numbers of ladybeetles (adults and larvae), lacewings (larvae), spiders, and parasitic wasp mummies were recorded. Aphids were surveyed using the same sampling method, and the number of aphids per 100 plants was recorded. To evaluate biological control function, the population ratio of natural enemies to aphids (natural enemy units/aphids per 100 plants) was calculated; the higher the ratio, the stronger the natural regulation ability. At the same time, aphid parasitism rate and predation rate were counted at the aphid peak period. Parasitism rate was estimated by the proportion of mummies, and predation rate was determined by the field cage exclusion method.

2.3 Calculation Methods for Yield and Net Income

After winter wheat and summer maize matured, each plot was harvested for yield measurement and converted to yield per hectare. Net income was calculated as: crop output value (yield × local average purchase price in the current year) minus nitrogen fertilizer cost, other agricultural input costs, and labor and machinery costs. The nitrogen fertilizer price was calculated at 5.0 yuan/kg of pure nitrogen, the wheat purchase price was 2.6 yuan/kg, and the maize purchase price was 2.4 yuan/kg. At the same time, nitrogen fertilizer partial factor productivity (yield/nitrogen application rate) was calculated to reflect nitrogen fertilizer use efficiency. All economic data were expressed as two-year averages, and a 5% discount rate was considered to eliminate the influence of interannual fluctuations.

2.4 Data Statistics and Analysis Methods

SPSS 26.0 was used for one-way analysis of variance, and differences among treatments were tested by Duncan's new multiple range method (P<0.05). Linear regression analysis was used for the relationships between natural enemy numbers and aphid numbers, and between the natural enemy ratio and aphid population density at the peak period. The relationship between net income and nitrogen application rate was fitted with a quadratic curve to obtain the nitrogen application rate corresponding to maximum net income. All figures were drawn using Origin 2021.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

3.1 Effects of Different Nitrogen Application Levels on Natural Enemy Insect Populations

The two-year survey results showed that the natural enemy insect population density was highest under the 20% nitrogen reduction treatment. Under the 20% nitrogen reduction treatment, ladybeetle numbers increased by 32.6%, lacewings by 28.4%, spiders by 21.7%, and parasitic wasp mummy numbers by 35.2% compared with conventional nitrogen application. Under the 40% nitrogen reduction treatment, natural enemy numbers further increased, but the increase slowed; ladybeetles and lacewings increased by 41.3% and 36.8%, respectively, compared with conventional nitrogen application. Natural enemy numbers under the no-nitrogen treatment were similar to those under the 40% nitrogen reduction treatment, but field vegetation coverage was low, the habitat environment for natural enemies deteriorated, and population stability was poor. From the perspective of temporal dynamics, the 20% nitrogen reduction treatment maintained a relatively high natural enemy population at the early stage of aphid occurrence, with an obvious numerical response of natural enemies, whereas the natural enemy peak under the conventional nitrogen application treatment lagged by about 7–10 days, resulting in rapid aphid accumulation in the early stage.

3.2 Effects of Different Nitrogen Application Levels on Aphid Occurrence and Biological Control Function

The number of aphids per 100 plants at the peak period was highest under the conventional nitrogen application treatment, reaching 12,600; it was 7,420 under the 20% nitrogen reduction treatment, a decrease of 41.2%; 5,800 under the 40% nitrogen reduction treatment, a decrease of 54.0%; and 5,100 under the no-nitrogen treatment, a decrease of 59.5%. The ratio of natural enemies to aphids was highest under the 20% nitrogen reduction treatment, at 0.86, significantly higher than 0.42 under conventional nitrogen application. The parasitism rate was 18.7% under the 20% nitrogen reduction treatment and 9.2% under conventional nitrogen application; the predation rates were 24.3% and 13.5%, respectively. Regression analysis showed that the natural enemy ratio was significantly negatively correlated with aphid population density at the peak period (r=-0.83, P<0.01), indicating that the increase in natural enemy population was the main reason for aphid suppression. The 20% nitrogen reduction treatment not only avoided aphid outbreaks caused by excessive nitrogen fertilizer, but also maintained good crop growth, providing suitable habitat for natural enemies, and had the strongest biological control function.

3.3 Effects of Different Nitrogen Application Levels on Yield and Net Income

The yield results showed that under the 20% nitrogen reduction treatment, winter wheat yield was 8,250 kg/hm², only 2.0% lower than 8,420 kg/hm² under conventional nitrogen application, and the difference was not significant; summer maize yield was 9,450 kg/hm², 1.6% lower than 9,600 kg/hm² under conventional nitrogen application, and the difference was also not significant. Under the 40% nitrogen reduction treatment, wheat and maize yields decreased by 8.7% and 7.9%, respectively, reaching a significant level. The no-nitrogen treatment had the lowest yield, with wheat and maize decreasing by 25.3% and 22.6%, respectively, compared with conventional nitrogen application. In terms of net income, the two-year average net income under the 20% nitrogen reduction treatment was 28,650 yuan/hm², 18.5% higher than 24,180 yuan/hm² under conventional nitrogen application. The net income under the 40% nitrogen reduction treatment was 22,800 yuan/hm², lower than that under conventional nitrogen application. The no-nitrogen treatment had the lowest net income, at 16,200 yuan/hm². Nitrogen fertilizer partial factor productivity increased as the nitrogen application rate decreased; it was 42.9 kg/kg under the 20% nitrogen reduction treatment, 22.2% higher than 35.1 kg/kg under conventional nitrogen application.

3.4 Synergistic Enhancement Mechanism of Biological Control Function and Net Income

The 20% nitrogen reduction treatment achieved synergistic enhancement of biological control function and net income, and its mechanism can be summarized in three points: First, a moderate reduction in nitrogen fertilizer decreased the free amino acid content in crop leaves, inhibited aphid reproduction rate, and reduced pest pressure from the source; second, the field microclimate improved, and canopy ventilation and light transmission were enhanced, which was conducive to the activity and predation of natural enemies such as ladybeetles and spiders; third, nitrogen fertilizer cost decreased. Although yield declined slightly, the decline was far smaller than the benefits brought by fertilizer savings and pesticide reduction. At the same time, natural enemy control of aphids reduced the number of insecticide applications (an average reduction of 2.3 times over two years), further lowering costs and the risk of pesticide residues. Overall, the 20% nitrogen reduction treatment achieved the best balance between ecological benefits and economic benefits.

4 Conclusion

Through a two-year field experiment, this study clarified the synergistic enhancement effect of optimized nitrogen fertilizer application on farmland biological control function and net income. The main conclusions are as follows: (1) On the basis of conventional nitrogen application of 240 kg/hm², reducing application by 20% (i.e., 192 kg/hm²) significantly increased natural enemy insect population density, reduced aphid population density at the peak period by 41.2%, and enhanced biological control function; (2) the 20% nitrogen reduction treatment did not significantly reduce yield, increased net income by 18.5%, and increased nitrogen fertilizer partial factor productivity by 22.2%; (3) although 40% nitrogen reduction further increased the number of natural enemies, yield decreased significantly, and net income was lower than that of the conventional treatment, so it is not suitable for promotion; (4) the 20% nitrogen reduction treatment achieved a win-win situation for ecological and economic benefits by reducing the food source quality of aphids, improving natural enemy habitat, and reducing pesticide input. It is recommended that in the winter wheat–summer maize rotation area of the North China Plain, the pure nitrogen rate be controlled at about 192 kg/hm², combined with organic fertilizer substitution and natural enemy protection measures, so as to fully leverage the natural biological control function of farmland and promote green and low-carbon agricultural development.

title: Zimbabwean PreClinical Medical Students Use of Deep and Strategic Study Approaches to Learn Anatomy at Two New Medical Schools
text:
Abstract: Objective: To investigate the current status of deep learning and strategic learning approaches among preclinical medical students in anatomy learning at two newly established medical schools in Zimbabwe and their influencing factors. Methods: A cross-sectional survey design was adopted. From March to June 2023, a total of 248 preclinical medical students from two newly established medical schools in Zimbabwe were selected. The revised R-SPQ-2F scale and a self-designed learning behavior questionnaire were used for the survey. Results: The mean score for the deep learning approach was (3.21±0.54), and the mean score for the strategic learning approach was (3.45±0.61). The strategic learning score was significantly higher than the deep learning score (t=5.872, P<0.001). Female students scored higher than male students on the deep learning dimension (P<0.05); students with support from anatomy-related learning resources scored higher on both approaches (P<0.05). Multiple regression analysis showed that accessibility of learning resources, weekly anatomy study time, and interest in the anatomy course were independent influencing factors of the deep learning approach (P<0.05). Conclusion: Preclinical medical students at newly established medical schools in Zimbabwe are more inclined to adopt the strategic learning approach, and the level of deep learning needs to be improved. It is recommended to optimize the allocation of anatomy teaching resources, introduce clinical cases and problem-based teaching, and promote students' deep learning.

Keywords: anatomy; deep learning; strategic learning; preclinical medical students; Zimbabwe; medical education

1 Introduction

Anatomy is a foundational core course in medical education. Its knowledge system is vast and complex, with a heavy memorization load, placing high demands on the learning approaches of preclinical medical students. Learning approaches are generally divided into two categories: deep learning and strategic learning. Deep learning emphasizes understanding, integration, and critical thinking about knowledge, while strategic learning focuses on obtaining high scores through time management, examination techniques, and selective memorization. Previous studies have shown that if medical students rely excessively on strategic learning in anatomy learning, although they may achieve short-term examination scores, it is not conducive to long-term knowledge retention and the development of clinical transferability.

In recent years, Zimbabwe has established multiple new medical schools to alleviate the shortage of doctors. However, these new institutions generally face challenges such as insufficient anatomy teaching resources, faculty shortages, and immature curriculum systems. Against this background, there is a lack of systematic research on how preclinical medical students learn anatomy and what factors influence their choice of learning approaches. This study takes two newly established medical schools in Zimbabwe as examples to investigate the current status of deep learning and strategic learning use among preclinical medical students in anatomy learning and to analyze their influencing factors, with the aim of providing reference for anatomy teaching reform in new medical schools.

2 Materials and Methods

2.1 Study Subjects

Using cluster sampling, preclinical medical students from two newly established medical schools in Zimbabwe (located in Harare and Bulawayo, respectively) were selected as study subjects from March to June 2023. Inclusion criteria: having completed at least one semester of anatomy coursework; voluntary participation. A total of 260 questionnaires were distributed, and 248 valid questionnaires were returned, with a valid response rate of 95.4%. Among them, 132 were male (53.2%) and 116 were female (46.8%); the mean age was (20.4±1.8) years.

2.2 Research Instruments

The revised two-factor Study Process Questionnaire (R-SPQ-2F) was used to measure deep learning and strategic learning tendencies, each containing 10 items, scored on a 5-point Likert scale. The Cronbach's α for the deep learning dimension was 0.81, and for the strategic learning dimension was 0.78. A self-designed questionnaire collected general demographic information, accessibility of anatomy learning resources, weekly study time, and course interest.

2.3 Data Collection and Statistical Analysis

Trained investigators distributed and collected questionnaires on site. SPSS 26.0 was used for statistical analysis, including descriptive statistics, independent samples t-tests, one-way ANOVA, and multiple linear regression analysis, with a significance level of α=0.05.

3 Results and Analysis

3.1 Overall Scores of Learning Approaches

The mean score for the deep learning dimension was (3.21±0.54), and the mean score for the strategic learning dimension was (3.45±0.61). The strategic learning score was significantly higher than the deep learning score (t=5.872, P<0.001). In the deep learning dimension, the item "trying to relate new knowledge to existing knowledge" had the highest score (3.68±0.72); in the strategic learning dimension, the item "selectively studying based on examination key points" had the highest score (3.92±0.65).

3.2 Comparison of Scores Among Students with Different Characteristics

Female students' deep learning scores (3.32±0.51) were higher than those of male students (3.12±0.56), and the difference was statistically significant (t=2.914, P=0.004); there was no statistically significant gender difference in strategic learning scores (P>0.05). Students with adequate anatomy learning resources (such as models, digital atlases, and cadaver dissection opportunities) scored significantly higher on both deep learning and strategic learning than those with insufficient resources (P<0.05). Those with higher interest in the anatomy course had significantly higher deep learning scores (F=6.231, P=0.002).

3.3 Multiple Linear Regression Analysis

With deep learning scores as the dependent variable, independent variables including gender, accessibility of learning resources, weekly anatomy study time, and course interest were included. The results showed that accessibility of learning resources (β=0.312, P<0.001), weekly study time (β=0.198, P=0.012), and course interest (β=0.276, P<0.001) were independent influencing factors of the deep learning approach.

4 Discussion

This study found that preclinical medical students at two newly established medical schools in Zimbabwe are more inclined to adopt the strategic learning approach in anatomy learning, and the level of deep learning is relatively insufficient. This result is consistent with some medical education studies in African countries and may be related to the examination-oriented anatomy curriculum, limited teaching resources, and predominance of large-class lectures at new institutions. Although strategic learning helps cope with short-term examinations, it is not conducive to the long-term retention and clinical application of anatomy knowledge.

Female students scored higher in deep learning than male students, which may be related to female students being more inclined to adopt elaborative learning strategies. Accessibility of learning resources is an important predictor of deep learning, suggesting that new medical schools should strengthen the construction of anatomy laboratories, introduce digital anatomy platforms, and increase cadaver dissection opportunities. Course interest also has a significant positive effect on deep learning. It is recommended to stimulate students' intrinsic learning motivation through the introduction of clinical cases, problem-based learning, and early clinical exposure.

The limitations of this study are as follows: the sample was drawn from only two institutions, so generalization of the results should be made with caution; the cross-sectional design cannot infer causality; and self-reported data may be subject to social desirability bias. Future research could combine longitudinal tracking with qualitative interviews to further explore the dynamic changes in learning approaches and their relationship with academic performance.

5 Conclusion

Preclinical medical students at newly established medical schools in Zimbabwe show a stronger tendency toward strategic learning than deep learning in anatomy learning. Accessibility of learning resources, weekly study time, and course interest are important influencing factors of deep learning. It is recommended that new medical schools optimize the allocation of anatomy teaching resources, promote deep learning teaching strategies centered on understanding and integration, and enhance the quality of anatomy learning and clinical transferability of preclinical medical students.

title: Oral Immunization of Chickens with Lactococcus lactis Expressing cjaA Temporarily Reduces Campylobacter jejuni Colonization
text:
Short-term inhibitory effect of orally administered Lactococcus lactis expressing cjaA on Campylobacter jejuni colonization in chickens

Abstract: Campylobacter jejuni is one of the important pathogenic bacteria causing human bacterial gastroenteritis, and chickens are its important reservoir host. Reducing Campylobacter jejuni colonization in the chicken intestine is a key step in lowering the risk of human infection. In this study, food-grade Lactococcus lactis was used as a delivery vector to construct a recombinant strain surface-expressing the Campylobacter jejuni cjaA protein, and its effect on Campylobacter jejuni colonization in chickens was evaluated through oral immunization. The results showed that oral immunization with the recombinant Lactococcus lactis induced a local intestinal immune response in chickens and significantly reduced Campylobacter jejuni colonization in the cecum in the short term after immunization, but the inhibitory effect weakened over time. The results indicate that this strategy has potential as a short-term intervention approach, but further optimization of the immunization regimen is still needed to extend the protection period.

Introduction: Campylobacter jejuni is widely present in the intestinal tract of poultry and can be transmitted to humans through contaminated poultry meat and poultry products, causing symptoms such as diarrhea, abdominal pain, and fever. Due to restrictions on antibiotic use and the increasingly prominent problem of drug resistance, the development of safe and effective immune intervention measures has attracted attention. Lactococcus lactis is a recognized food-grade microorganism with advantages such as tolerance to the gastrointestinal environment and the ability to deliver antigens orally, and it has been used in research on various mucosal vaccines. cjaA is a conserved surface protein of Campylobacter jejuni that participates in amino acid transport and has good immunogenicity. This study aimed to construct a recombinant Lactococcus lactis expressing cjaA and evaluate the short-term inhibitory effect of its oral immunization on Campylobacter jejuni colonization in chickens, so as to provide a technical reference for subsequent vaccine development.

Analysis of key technologies:

1. Construction of recombinant Lactococcus lactis and cjaA expression
The study used Lactococcus lactis NZ9000 as the host, cloned the Campylobacter jejuni cjaA gene into an expression vector containing the nisA promoter, and obtained the recombinant strain by electroporation. After induction with nisin, Western blot was used to detect target protein expression. The results showed that the cjaA protein could be effectively expressed on the surface of Lactococcus lactis, and the expression level increased with prolonged induction time. This expression system has advantages such as mild induction conditions and clear protein localization, laying the foundation for subsequent oral immunization.

2. Oral immunization regimen and animal grouping
One-day-old healthy broiler chickens were selected and randomly divided into an immunization group and a control group. The immunization group was orally administered the recombinant Lactococcus lactis daily for 5 consecutive days, while the control group received the empty vector strain. After immunization was completed, all chickens were orally challenged with a standard strain of Campylobacter jejuni. Cecal contents were collected on days 3, 7, and 14 after challenge to determine the Campylobacter colonization load. This regimen simulates the natural route of infection and can better reflect the actual effect of local intestinal immunity.

3. Detection of intestinal colonization load and analysis of immune indicators
Selective medium was used to count the number of Campylobacter jejuni in cecal contents, and real-time fluorescence quantitative PCR was used for verification. At the same time, intestinal lavage fluid was collected to detect secretory IgA levels. The results showed that on days 3 and 7 after challenge, the Campylobacter colonization load in the cecum of the immunization group was significantly lower than that of the control group, while the difference was not significant on day 14. The intestinal sIgA level in the immunization group was significantly increased on day 7 after immunization, suggesting that local mucosal immunity was activated. These results indicate that the recombinant strain can induce a certain degree of immune protection, but the duration is limited.

4. Safety and feasibility evaluation
The recombinant Lactococcus lactis is a food-grade vector and does not introduce antibiotic resistance genes. After oral administration, no abnormalities in chicken growth performance or significant disturbance of the intestinal microbiota were observed. Compared with injected vaccines, oral immunization is simple to perform and causes little stress, making it suitable for use in large-scale farms. However, this study also found that the immune protection period was relatively short, which may be related to antigen expression level, number of immunizations, and the developmental stage of the chicken intestine. In the future, the effect can be improved by optimizing induction conditions, adding immune enhancers, or adopting a multivalent antigen strategy.

Results and benefit analysis: This study showed that orally administered Lactococcus lactis expressing cjaA can reduce Campylobacter jejuni colonization in chickens in the short term and reduce environmental shedding, thereby lowering the risk of poultry meat contamination. This strategy has advantages such as low cost, high safety, and ease of promotion, and is suitable as a short-term intervention measure on farms, especially during the critical stage before slaughter. Although the protection period is limited, it can still play a certain role when combined with biosecurity measures and husbandry management. From an economic perspective, reducing Campylobacter colonization helps lower food recall and medical burdens and has potential public health value.

Conclusion: This study successfully constructed recombinant Lactococcus lactis expressing cjaA and confirmed that its oral immunization can reduce Campylobacter jejuni colonization in chickens in the short term. This strategy provides a new idea for the control of Campylobacter in poultry, but the problem of the relatively short protection period still needs to be addressed by optimizing the immunization regimen, improving the antigen delivery system, or combining other intervention measures. Future field trials should be further carried out to evaluate its effect and stability under actual farming conditions.

title: The barriers to evidence-based nursing implementation in mainland China: A qualitative content analysis
text:
Barriers to the Implementation of Evidence-Based Nursing in Mainland China: A Qualitative Content Analysis

 Abstract

Objective: To explore the main barriers faced in the implementation of evidence-based nursing in mainland China, and to provide a reference for promoting the localized practice of evidence-based nursing. Methods: Using purposive sampling, 28 clinical nurses and nursing managers from 12 provinces (autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government) in mainland China were selected from March to August 2023 for semi-structured in-depth interviews. Qualitative content analysis was used to organize and analyze the interview data. Results: Four themes and 11 subthemes were extracted. The four themes were: insufficient capacity for evidence acquisition and appraisal, weak organizational support systems, constraints of cultural concepts and professional identity, and barriers to patient and family participation. Conclusion: The implementation of evidence-based nursing in mainland China is influenced by the interweaving of multiple factors, including individual capacity, organizational environment, cultural concepts, and patient participation. Coordinated advancement is needed in areas such as education and training, organizational management, cultural development, and patient empowerment.

Keywords: evidence-based nursing; implementation barriers; qualitative research; content analysis; mainland China

 1 Introduction

Evidence-based nursing (EBN) refers to the process in which nurses combine the best research evidence, clinical experience, and patient preferences when making nursing decisions. Since its introduction to China in the 1990s, evidence-based nursing has made remarkable progress in the dissemination of concepts, translation of guidelines, and talent cultivation. However, multiple surveys have shown that the translation rate of research evidence in clinical nursing practice in mainland China remains low, and the "knowing-doing" gap from evidence generation to clinical application remains prominent.

Existing studies have mostly analyzed the barriers to evidence-based nursing implementation from a quantitative perspective, such as knowledge levels, attitude scores, and organizational culture scales, but they have difficulty in deeply revealing the internal logic and contextual pathways through which barriers are formed. Qualitative research helps to understand nurses' real experiences and meaning construction in their specific workplace settings. This study adopted qualitative content analysis to systematically explore the barriers to the implementation of evidence-based nursing in mainland China, with the aim of providing a basis for formulating localized promotion strategies.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Study Participants

Using purposive sampling, while taking into account regional distribution, hospital level, and differences in positions, 28 study participants from 12 provinces (autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government) in mainland China were selected from March to August 2023. Inclusion criteria: (1) holding a nurse practice qualification certificate; (2) having ≥3 years of clinical nursing work experience; (3) being familiar with or having participated in evidence-based nursing-related practice; (4) providing informed consent and participating voluntarily. Among the study participants, there were 16 clinical nurses, 6 nursing team leaders, and 6 nursing managers; 19 were from tertiary hospitals and 9 from secondary hospitals; their ages ranged from 28 to 52 years, with a mean of (37.6±6.8) years.

 2.2 Data Collection

A semi-structured in-depth interview method was used. The interview outline was determined after literature review and expert consultation, and its main contents included: (1) How do you understand evidence-based nursing? (2) What difficulties have you encountered when applying research evidence in clinical work? (3) What support has your department and hospital provided? (4) How do patients and family members respond to evidence-based nursing practice? (5) What do you think most needs to be changed to promote the implementation of evidence-based nursing? The interviews were conducted face-to-face or by video, each lasting 40 to 70 minutes, and were audio-recorded with the participants' consent. Recruitment stopped when the data reached saturation and no new themes emerged.

 2.3 Data Analysis

Within 24 hours after the interviews, the recordings were transcribed verbatim and returned to the participants for verification. Graneheim and Lundman's qualitative content analysis method was used, and the analysis was carried out according to the steps of "reading the full text—extracting meaning units—coding—categorizing—refining themes." Two researchers independently coded the data, and disagreements were resolved through discussion or third-party arbitration. Methods such as triangulation, member checking, and audit trails were used to ensure the credibility of the study.

 3 Results and Analysis

After analysis, a total of 4 themes and 11 subthemes were extracted.

 3.1 Theme One: Insufficient Capacity for Evidence Acquisition and Appraisal

3.1.1 Difficulties in literature retrieval and foreign-language reading. Most participants stated that they were busy with daily work, lacked systematic literature retrieval training, and were unfamiliar with English databases and evidence-based resources. One participant said, "I know I should read the literature, but I don't know where to find it, and reading English is also laborious."

3.1.2 Insufficient confidence in evidence appraisal. Although some nursing staff could obtain literature, they lacked the ability to judge study design, levels of evidence, and strength of recommendations, making it difficult to translate research conclusions into actionable nursing measures.

3.1.3 Doubts about the local applicability of evidence. Participants generally reported that many guidelines and evidence came from abroad and differed from Chinese patients' disease spectrum, economic conditions, and medical environment, leading to considerable concerns when applying them directly.

 3.2 Theme Two: Weak Organizational Support Systems

3.2.1 Tight human resources. The clinical nursing workload was heavy and shift work was frequent, making it difficult for nursing staff to find time to consult the literature, discuss evidence, and revise procedures.

3.2.2 Insufficient training and resources. Although some hospitals carried out evidence-based nursing training, most of it consisted of one-off lectures and lacked continuous guidance and practical support; library database access was limited, and the accessibility of evidence-based tools was not high.

3.2.3 Absence of management and incentive mechanisms. Evidence-based nursing practice was not included in performance assessment and the professional title promotion system, resulting in a lack of motivation among nursing staff for sustained participation. One manager admitted, "Without institutional support, evidence-based nursing can easily become a passing fad."

 3.3 Theme Three: Constraints of Cultural Concepts and Professional Identity

3.3.1 Deep-rooted tradition of empiricism. Some senior nursing staff were accustomed to carrying out work based on experience and routine, and held a cautious or even resistant attitude toward changing existing procedures.

3.3.2 Hierarchical decision-making model limiting autonomy. In some departments, adjustments to nursing measures required approval at multiple levels, and frontline nurses lacked space to participate in decision-making, making it difficult to translate evidence into practice.

3.3.3 Low sense of professional identity in nursing. Some participants believed that nursing work had low social status and that evidence-based practice was regarded as an "extra burden" rather than an intrinsic requirement of professional development.

 3.4 Theme Four: Barriers to Patient and Family Participation

3.4.1 Differences in health literacy and information access. Some patients and family members did not understand the concept of evidence-based nursing and were more inclined to rely on doctors' opinions or traditional experience.

3.4.2 Constraints of economic and regional factors. In less developed areas, patients' ability to pay and medical resources were limited, and some evidence-based nursing measures were difficult to implement because of cost or accessibility issues.

 4 Discussion

This study found that the barriers to the implementation of evidence-based nursing in mainland China are not caused by a single factor, but are the result of interactions among individual capacity, organizational environment, cultural concepts, and patient factors. First, insufficient capacity for evidence acquisition and appraisal reflects that evidence-based nursing education is still not sufficiently embedded in undergraduate and continuing education. Compared with developed countries, training in evidence-based methodology in nursing education in mainland China started relatively late, and the clinical practice component lacks mentorship support. Therefore, an evidence-based competency training system should be constructed that connects "school education—standardized training—continuing education."

Second, weak organizational support systems are the key constraint on evidence translation. Tight human resources and the absence of management incentives make it difficult to institutionalize evidence-based nursing. Hospitals should incorporate evidence-based nursing into nursing quality management and performance assessment, establish evidence-based nursing groups or clinical nursing research positions, and provide guarantees in terms of databases, time, and funding.

Third, the issues of cultural concepts and professional identity suggest that promoting evidence-based nursing is not only a technical issue but also a matter of organizational cultural change. Through leadership support, team learning, and case demonstration, a nursing culture based on evidence and centered on patients should gradually be formed. At the same time, the social recognition and professional autonomy of the nursing profession should be enhanced.

Finally, the barriers to patient and family participation indicate that evidence-based nursing must respond to economic and regional differences in China's medical context. In resource-limited areas, low-cost, high-benefit evidence-based measures can be prioritized, and patients' capacity for participation can be improved through health education.

The limitations of this study are as follows: although the sample covered multiple provinces, it was mainly composed of nursing staff from tertiary hospitals, with less involvement of primary healthcare institutions and patient perspectives; the data were mainly self-reported, and future studies could further verify the findings by combining observation methods and case studies.

 5 Conclusion

The implementation of evidence-based nursing in mainland China faces multiple challenges, including insufficient evidence capacity, weak organizational support, constraints of cultural concepts, and barriers to patient participation. To promote the implementation of evidence-based nursing, educational institutions, medical institutions, managers, and nursing staff need to make coordinated efforts and adopt comprehensive measures in capacity building, institutional safeguards, cultural cultivation, and patient empowerment. Only by embedding evidence-based nursing into daily practice and organizational operations can a substantive transformation from "knowing evidence" to "using evidence" be achieved.

title: Thermosonication as a potential quality enhancement technique of apple juice
text:
Abstract: To address the issues of flavor deterioration and nutrient loss caused by traditional thermal sterilization in apple juice processing, this paper explores the feasibility of thermosonication technology as a means of improving apple juice quality. By analyzing the effects of key process parameters of thermosonication (temperature, ultrasonic power density, treatment time) on microbial inactivation, enzyme inactivation, and major quality indicators (color, turbidity, vitamin C, phenolic compounds, aroma components) in apple juice, and drawing on recent domestic and international research data, it is demonstrated that thermosonication can achieve equivalent sterilization at lower temperatures while better preserving the natural flavor and nutritional components of apple juice. This paper also discusses the engineering issues that need to be resolved for the scaled application of this technology, providing a reference for its promotion in the juice processing industry.

Keywords: thermosonication; apple juice; non-thermal processing; quality improvement; enzyme inactivation

 1 Introduction

Apple juice is one of the juice categories with relatively large production and consumption volumes in China. Although traditional thermal sterilization (e.g., short-time treatment above 90°C) can effectively inactivate microorganisms and enzymes, it easily triggers Maillard reactions, vitamin C degradation, loss of volatile aroma components, and color browning, leading to product quality deterioration. The growing consumer demand for "fresh, natural, minimally processed" juices has drawn attention to non-thermal processing technologies. Thermosonication is a non-thermal processing technology that combines ultrasound (typically 20–40 kHz) with moderate heating (40–60°C). The localized high temperature and pressure, microjets, and free radical effects generated by ultrasonic cavitation can synergize with thermal effects to accelerate microbial inactivation and enzyme inactivation, thereby achieving sterilization and enzyme inactivation at lower temperatures and reducing thermal damage. This paper analyzes the key technologies, quality impacts, and benefits of thermosonication treatment of apple juice, aiming to provide a basis for the industrial application of this technology.

 2 Key Technology Analysis

 2.1 Thermosonication Treatment System and Process Parameters

A typical thermosonication treatment system consists of an ultrasonic generator, transducer, stainless steel treatment chamber, and constant-temperature water bath circulation device. Apple juice is pumped through the treatment chamber and subjected to ultrasonic irradiation at a set temperature. Key parameters include: ultrasonic frequency (20–40 kHz), power density (typically 20–100 W/L), treatment temperature (40–60°C), treatment time (5–30 min), and juice flow rate. Studies have shown that excessively high power density can lead to cavitation shielding and excessive heating, which instead exacerbates quality deterioration; while excessively low temperature results in insufficient sterilization efficacy. Therefore, optimized combinations are needed, for example, using 40 kHz, 50 W/L, and 50°C for 10 min, which can maximize quality retention while ensuring microbial safety.

 2.2 Microbial Inactivation Efficacy

Thermosonication has demonstrated good inactivation efficacy against common spoilage bacteria and pathogenic bacteria in apple juice (such as Escherichia coli O157:H7, Salmonella, and Saccharomyces cerevisiae). The shear forces and reactive oxygen species (·OH, H₂O₂) generated by cavitation bubble collapse can disrupt cell wall and membrane structures, while moderate heating enhances cell membrane fluidity, making cells more susceptible to damage. Literature reports indicate that thermosonication treatment at 50°C for 10 min can reduce E. coli counts by more than 5 log cycles, comparable to thermal pasteurization at 72°C for 15 s. Moreover, thermosonication can more effectively penetrate the interstitial spaces of fruit pulp particles, and its sterilization uniformity for high-turbidity apple juice is superior to that of thermal sterilization alone.

 2.3 Enzyme Inactivation and Stability

Polyphenol oxidase (PPO) and pectin methylesterase (PME) in apple juice are the main enzymes causing browning and turbidity. Traditional thermal sterilization requires temperatures above 80°C to effectively inactivate PPO, whereas thermosonication can reduce PPO activity by 80%–95% and PME by 70%–90% at 50–60°C. The mechanism is that the shear forces generated by ultrasonic cavitation disrupt the secondary structure of enzyme proteins, while the thermal effect synergistically denatures the enzyme active center. Appropriate thermosonication treatment can significantly delay enzymatic browning and stratification phenomena in apple juice during storage, while avoiding non-enzymatic browning caused by high temperatures.

 2.4 Effects on Major Quality Indicators

Compared with thermal sterilization (90°C, 30 s), thermosonication (50°C, 10 min) treatment of apple juice increases the vitamin C retention rate by approximately 25%–35% and the total phenolic content retention rate by 15%–20%. In terms of color, the L* value (brightness) and a* value (red-greenness) of thermosonication-treated samples are closer to those of fresh-pressed juice, with the browning index (BI) reduced by approximately 30%. Regarding turbidity stability, thermosonication can moderately reduce pectin methylesterase activity without completely destroying the pectin structure, thereby maintaining a uniform turbid state. Among aroma components, the retention rates of typical apple aroma compounds such as esters and aldehydes are more than 40% higher than those of thermal sterilization, and no obvious cooked flavor is produced. In addition, thermosonication can promote the release of some bound phenolic compounds, slightly enhancing antioxidant activity.

 2.5 Synergy with Other Technologies

Thermosonication can be combined with mild heat treatment, natural antimicrobial agents (such as citric acid and nisin), or high-pressure carbon dioxide to further reduce treatment temperature and time. For example, thermosonication (45°C, 5 min) combined with 0.1% citric acid can achieve a sterilization effect equivalent to that of thermosonication alone for 10 min, while better preserving heat-sensitive components. This synergistic strategy helps reduce ultrasonic energy consumption and improve economic viability.

 3 Results and Benefit Analysis

From a technical benefit perspective, thermosonication treatment of apple juice can achieve: ① sterilization efficacy equivalent to traditional pasteurization, meeting food safety standards; ② sufficient enzyme inactivation, with no obvious browning or stratification in products stored at 4°C for 21 days; ③ significantly improved retention rates of vitamin C, phenolic compounds, and aroma components, with sensory quality closer to fresh-pressed juice. From an economic benefit perspective, the investment in thermosonication equipment is approximately 60%–70% of that of traditional ultra-high temperature sterilization systems, and operating energy consumption is reduced by approximately 20%–30% due to lower treatment temperatures. Although ultrasonic transducers require regular maintenance, the overall cost remains competitive. From a market benefit perspective, this technology can support high-end juice positioning such as "cold sterilization" and "fresh-pressed flavor," enhancing product added value. In terms of environmental benefits, low-temperature short-time treatment reduces cooling water usage and carbon emissions, aligning with green processing trends.

It should be noted that the scaled application of thermosonication treatment of apple juice still faces challenges: the uniformity of the ultrasonic field in continuous-flow treatment chambers needs optimization; high-power ultrasound may cause excessive fragmentation of suspended particles in juice, affecting mouthfeel; and transducer heating and corrosion issues during long-term operation need to be resolved. It is recommended that the next step involve pilot-scale continuous treatment trials combined with computational fluid dynamics simulation to optimize chamber design.

 4 Conclusion

Thermosonication, as a mild non-thermal processing technology, has demonstrated good potential in improving apple juice quality. Through rational regulation of temperature, ultrasonic power density, and treatment time, equivalent sterilization and enzyme inactivation can be achieved at 50–60°C, while significantly reducing vitamin C degradation, browning, and aroma loss. This technology meets consumer demand for high-quality, minimally processed juices and possesses favorable economic and environmental benefits. Future research should focus on process scale-up of continuous-flow systems, synergistic optimization with other hurdle technologies, and long-term storage stability verification to promote its practical application in the juice industry.

title: Effectiveness of electroacupuncture for pain after osteosarcoma post surgery: A study protocol of systematic review of randomized controlled trial
text:
Effectiveness of Electroacupuncture for Postoperative Pain in Osteosarcoma: A Study Protocol for a Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials

 Abstract

Background: Osteosarcoma is the most common primary malignant bone tumor in children and adolescents, and surgical resection is its main treatment modality. Postoperative pain management directly affects the quality of patient recovery and quality of life. Electroacupuncture, as a non-pharmacological analgesic approach, has shown potential efficacy in various types of postoperative pain, but its effectiveness in postoperative pain after osteosarcoma surgery still lacks a systematic review. Objective: This study aims to develop a systematic review protocol to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of electroacupuncture for postoperative pain in osteosarcoma. Methods: Chinese and English databases including CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library will be systematically searched from database inception to December 2025. Randomized controlled trials of electroacupuncture for postoperative pain in osteosarcoma will be included. Two researchers will independently conduct literature screening, data extraction, and quality assessment. The Cochrane risk of bias assessment tool will be used, and RevMan 5.4 will be used for meta-analysis. Expected results: Comprehensive evidence on the analgesic effectiveness of electroacupuncture is expected to be generated, providing a reference for clinical decision-making. Conclusion: This protocol will provide evidence-based medical evidence for the application of electroacupuncture in postoperative pain management of osteosarcoma.

Keywords: electroacupuncture; osteosarcoma; postoperative pain; systematic review; randomized controlled trial; study protocol

 1 Introduction

Osteosarcoma is a highly malignant tumor originating from mesenchymal tissue, predominantly affecting children and adolescents, with an annual incidence of approximately 3 to 5 per million[1]. With the application of neoadjuvant chemotherapy combined with wide resection, the five-year survival rate of osteosarcoma patients has increased from approximately 20% in the 1970s to the current 60%–70%[2]. However, surgical trauma is substantial, and postoperative pain is severe, seriously affecting patients' early functional exercise, sleep quality, and psychological state, and may even progress to chronic postsurgical pain[3].

Currently, postoperative analgesia mainly relies on opioids. Although they can effectively relieve pain, they are often accompanied by nausea and vomiting, respiratory depression, constipation, and tolerance[4]. Multimodal analgesia strategies have therefore received widespread attention, among which acupuncture therapy, as a non-pharmacological intervention, has been gradually incorporated into perioperative pain management due to its high safety and few side effects[5]. Electroacupuncture (EA) involves superimposing pulsed electrical stimulation on the basis of traditional acupuncture, which can enhance the deqi sensation and regulate the release of endogenous opioid peptides. Preliminary reports on its application in orthopedic postoperative pain exist[6].

However, the number of clinical studies on electroacupuncture for postoperative pain in osteosarcoma is currently limited, with small sample sizes and inconsistent conclusions, and no systematic review has synthesized the evidence. Therefore, this study intends to develop a systematic review protocol aimed at evaluating the effectiveness and safety of electroacupuncture in relieving postoperative pain in osteosarcoma, providing evidence-based support for clinical practice and future research.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Study Design

This study is a systematic review protocol, developed in accordance with the PRISMA-P (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Protocols) guidelines[7], and has been registered on the PROSPERO international prospective register of systematic reviews (Registration number: CRD42025XXXXXX).

 2.2 Inclusion and Exclusion Criteria

Inclusion criteria: (1) Study type: randomized controlled trials (RCTs), regardless of blinding; (2) Participants: patients pathologically diagnosed with osteosarcoma who underwent surgical resection, with no restrictions on age, sex, or nationality; (3) Intervention: the experimental group received electroacupuncture (which may be combined with conventional analgesia), while the control group received sham electroacupuncture, conventional analgesia, or blank control; (4) Outcome measures: the primary outcome was postoperative pain score (VAS or NRS), and secondary outcomes included opioid consumption, analgesic satisfaction, incidence of adverse reactions, and quality of life scores.

Exclusion criteria: (1) Non-RCT studies, such as case reports, reviews, and animal experiments; (2) duplicate publications; (3) incomplete data with unavailable full text; (4) interventions containing other types of acupuncture (such as manual acupuncture alone or auricular acupuncture) where the effect of electroacupuncture cannot be distinguished.

 2.3 Search Strategy

Computerized searches will be conducted in the China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Database, VIP Chinese Journal Database, China Biomedical Literature Database (CBM), PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science, from database inception to December 2025. Chinese search terms include "电针" "骨肉瘤" "术后疼痛" "随机对照", etc.; English search terms include "electroacupuncture" "osteosarcoma" "postoperative pain" "randomized controlled trial", etc. A combination of subject headings and free-text terms will be used, and references of included studies will be traced for supplementary searching.

 2.4 Literature Screening and Data Extraction

Two trained researchers will independently conduct literature screening. First, titles and abstracts will be read to exclude obviously irrelevant literature, and then full texts will be read to determine the final included studies. Disagreements will be resolved through discussion or third-party arbitration. Data extraction content includes: general information (authors, year, country), study design, sample size, patient characteristics, intervention details (acupoint selection, electroacupuncture parameters, treatment course), control measures, outcome measures, and follow-up duration.

 2.5 Quality Assessment

The Cochrane risk of bias assessment tool (RoB 2.0) will be used to assess the quality of included studies, including random sequence generation, allocation concealment, blinding implementation, completeness of outcome data, selective reporting, and other sources of bias[8]. Assessment results will be classified into three levels: "low risk," "some concerns," and "high risk."

 2.6 Statistical Analysis

RevMan 5.4 software will be used for meta-analysis. Continuous variables will be expressed as mean difference (MD) or standardized mean difference (SMD) with 95% confidence interval (CI); binary variables will be expressed as risk ratio (RR) with 95% CI. The I² statistic will be used to assess heterogeneity. If I²≤50%, a fixed-effect model will be used; if I²>50%, a random-effects model will be used and sources of heterogeneity will be analyzed. If the number of included studies is ≥10, a funnel plot will be used to assess publication bias. Sensitivity analysis will be performed by sequentially excluding individual studies.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Expected Literature Screening Results

Based on preliminary pre-search, it is estimated that approximately 320 relevant articles can be retrieved. After deduplication, approximately 210 articles will remain. After reading titles and abstracts, approximately 180 articles will be excluded. Finally, approximately 30 articles will be included for full-text assessment, and it is expected that approximately 8–12 RCTs will be ultimately included, with a cumulative sample size of approximately 600–900 cases.

 3.2 Expected Primary Outcomes

The expected meta-analysis results show that the electroacupuncture group will have lower VAS scores at 24 hours postoperatively compared with the control group, with an expected MD of -1.20 (95% CI: -1.65 to -0.75), and the difference will be statistically significant. VAS scores at 48 hours and 72 hours postoperatively will also show similar trends, suggesting that electroacupuncture has a sustained analgesic effect.

 3.3 Expected Secondary Outcomes

The cumulative postoperative opioid consumption in the electroacupuncture group is expected to be lower than that in the control group, with an SMD of approximately -0.65 (95% CI: -0.98 to -0.32). Analgesic satisfaction scores are expected to be higher than those in the control group, with an RR of approximately 1.35 (95% CI: 1.10 to 1.65). Regarding adverse reactions, the incidence of nausea and vomiting and dizziness in the electroacupuncture group is expected to be lower than that in the control group, suggesting that electroacupuncture can reduce opioid-related adverse reactions.

 3.4 Heterogeneity Analysis

Moderate heterogeneity is expected among studies (I² approximately 40%–60%). The main sources may include differences in electroacupuncture parameters (frequency 2/100 Hz vs 2 Hz), acupoint selection (Zusanli, Hegu, Neiguan, etc.), and differences in treatment course. Subgroup analysis will be stratified by electroacupuncture frequency and treatment course.

 4 Discussion

This systematic review protocol aims to comprehensively evaluate the effectiveness and safety of electroacupuncture for postoperative pain in osteosarcoma. The mechanism of postoperative pain in osteosarcoma is complex, involving multiple factors such as nociceptive pain, neuropathic pain, and inflammatory responses[9]. Electroacupuncture may exert analgesic effects by activating the descending inhibitory system, promoting the release of β-endorphin and enkephalin, and inhibiting phosphorylation of NMDA receptors in the spinal dorsal horn[10].

Compared with previous systematic reviews on orthopedic postoperative pain, this study focuses on the specific population of osteosarcoma, providing stronger clinical relevance. Most osteosarcoma patients are adolescents, who are more sensitive to opioid-related adverse reactions, and the clinical demand for non-pharmacological analgesic approaches is more urgent[11]. In addition, this study will use the RoB 2.0 tool for quality assessment, which is more rigorous than the traditional Cochrane tool and helps improve the reliability of evidence.

This protocol also has certain limitations. First, electroacupuncture interventions are difficult to double-blind, which may introduce performance bias; second, differences in electroacupuncture parameters among studies may affect result pooling; third, some studies may have small sample sizes and short follow-up durations, affecting the generalizability of conclusions. Therefore, subgroup analysis and sensitivity analysis are particularly necessary.

Future research should focus on the following directions: first, conducting multicenter, large-sample RCTs with standardized electroacupuncture parameters; second, extending follow-up duration to evaluate the preventive effect of electroacupuncture on chronic postsurgical pain; third, exploring the analgesic mechanisms of electroacupuncture in combination with objective pain biomarkers (such as cortisol and substance P).

 5 Conclusion

This systematic review protocol has developed a scientific and systematic research process for evaluating the effectiveness and safety of electroacupuncture for postoperative pain in osteosarcoma. The expected results will provide evidence-based medical evidence for the application of electroacupuncture in perioperative pain management of osteosarcoma and provide a reference for the design of subsequent high-quality clinical studies. If the results confirm that electroacupuncture is effective, it will help promote its inclusion in multimodal postoperative analgesia regimens for osteosarcoma and improve the quality of patient recovery.

 References

[1] Wang Zhongcheng, Zhang Wei. Advances in diagnosis and treatment of osteosarcoma[J]. Chinese Journal of Orthopaedics, 2023, 43(5): 289-295.

[2] Isakoff MS, Bielack SS, Meltzer P, et al. Osteosarcoma: current treatment and a collaborative pathway to success[J]. J Clin Oncol, 2015, 33(27): 3029-3035.

[3] Li Na, Chen Jing. Analysis of risk factors for chronic postsurgical pain in orthopedics[J]. Chinese Journal of Pain Medicine, 2022, 28(3): 201-206.

[4] Chou R, Gordon DB, de Leon-Casasola OA, et al. Management of postoperative pain: a clinical practice guideline[J]. J Pain, 2016, 17(2): 131-157.

[5] Liu Yang, Zhao Ming. Advances in the application of acupuncture in perioperative analgesia[J]. Chinese Acupuncture & Moxibustion, 2021, 41(8): 923-928.

[6] Wu MS, Chen KH, Chen IF, et al. The efficacy of acupuncture in post-operative pain management: a systematic review and meta-analysis[J]. PLoS One, 2016, 11(3): e0150367.

[7] Shamseer L, Moher D, Clarke M, et al. Preferred reporting items for systematic review and meta-analysis protocols (PRISMA-P) 2015: elaboration and explanation[J]. BMJ, 2015, 350: g7647.

[8] Sterne JAC, Savović J, Page MJ, et al. RoB 2: a revised tool for assessing risk of bias in randomised trials[J]. BMJ, 2019, 366: l4898.

[9] Zhang Lei, Wang Fang. Research advances in mechanisms of postoperative pain in osteosarcoma[J]. Chinese Journal of Clinical Oncology, 2022, 49(12): 635-640.

[10] Zhao ZQ. Neural mechanism underlying acupuncture analgesia[J]. Prog Neurobiol, 2008, 85(4): 355-375.

[11] Chen Xiao, Liu Min. Optimization of postoperative analgesia strategies for adolescent cancer patients[J]. National Medical Journal of China, 2023, 103(18): 1421-1426.

title: The psychological experiences of nurses after inpatient suicide: A meta-synthesis of qualitative research studies
text:
Psychological Experiences of Nurses After Inpatient Suicide: A Meta-Synthesis of Qualitative Research

Abstract

Objective To systematically synthesize the psychological experiences of nurses after inpatient suicide, and to provide evidence for clinical nursing management and psychological support. Methods A computer-based search was conducted in databases including CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, PubMed, Web of Science, and CINAHL for qualitative studies on nurses' psychological experiences after inpatient suicide, with the search period from database inception to December 2024. The quality of included literature was evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Critical Appraisal Checklist for Qualitative Research. The Meta-synthesis method was used to summarize the results. Results A total of 12 qualitative studies were included, from which 35 explicit findings were extracted and categorized into 8 categories, ultimately forming 3 synthesized themes: emotional impact and trauma reactions, professional identity and self-doubt, and support needs and post-traumatic growth. Conclusion Nurses experience complex and enduring psychological experiences after inpatient suicide. Managers should establish a systematic psychological support system, attend to nurses' emotional needs, and promote their post-traumatic growth.

Keywords inpatient suicide; nurses; psychological experience; qualitative research; Meta-synthesis


1 Introduction

Inpatient suicide is a relatively serious negative event in psychiatric and general hospital clinical nursing. When a patient ends their life in the hospital environment, it not only brings tremendous grief to family members but also causes profound psychological effects on nurses directly involved in care. Nurses are often the first to discover the suicide event or the first responders at the scene, and they must complete multiple tasks within a short time, including coordinating rescue efforts, securing the scene, and communicating with family members, while simultaneously enduring multiple pressures from themselves, colleagues, managers, and society.

Previous studies have mostly focused on suicide prevention strategies and patient risk assessment, with insufficient attention to nurses' psychological experiences after the event. In recent years, qualitative studies at home and abroad have gradually increased, revealing themes such as nurses' guilt, fear, anger, and helplessness after patient suicide, as well as shaken professional identity and strong support needs. However, individual qualitative studies have small sample sizes and large contextual differences, making it difficult to form a systematic understanding. This study adopted the Meta-synthesis method to systematically review existing qualitative studies, aiming to comprehensively present nurses' psychological experiences after inpatient suicide and provide a reference for clinical intervention.

2 Key Technical Analysis

2.1 Literature Search and Screening Strategy
