Traditional tracing methods such as horseradish peroxidase, fluorescent proteins, or viral vectors typically require tissue sectioning, fixation, or reliance on transgenic animals, making it difficult to dynamically observe axonal projections under in vivo, non-invasive conditions. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers advantages including no ionizing radiation, high soft tissue resolution, and deep tissue imaging capability. If MRI contrast agents can be combined with axon-targeting tracing functionality, it would be possible to achieve in vivo, non-invasive neural pathway tracking.

Superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs) are classic T2-weighted MRI contrast agents, but they lack axon specificity when used alone and are easily cleared by the reticuloendothelial system. In recent years, multifunctional nanoparticles that integrate targeting ligands, fluorescent labels, and long-circulating coatings through surface engineering have provided new approaches for multimodal imaging and tracing. This paper aims to develop a SPION-based multifunctional nanoparticle that simultaneously meets the requirements for non-invasive MRI enhancement and anterograde axonal tracing, and to systematically evaluate its key technical aspects and application benefits.

2 Key Technical Analysis

2.1 Chemical Synthesis and Surface Functionalization of Nanoparticles

Oleic acid-coated Fe₃O₄ nanocrystal cores were synthesized by high-temperature thermal decomposition, with particle sizes controlled at 12–18 nm by adjusting precursor ratios and reaction time. Subsequently, ligand exchange was used to replace oleic acid with dopamine-PEG-carboxyl polymers, conferring water solubility and modifiable sites. Fluorescent dyes (e.g., Cy5.5) and axon-targeting peptides (sequence: KHIFSDDSSE, which recognizes neural cell adhesion molecules on neuronal membranes) were further conjugated via carbodiimide chemistry. After surface functionalization, the nanoparticles were stably dispersed in the aqueous phase with a Zeta potential of approximately -12 mV, avoiding non-specific protein adsorption.

2.2 Magnetic Resonance Relaxivity Performance and Imaging Parameter Optimization

T2 relaxation times were measured using 1.5 T and 3.0 T clinical MRI scanners. The results showed that the T2 relaxivity (r₂) of the functionalized nanoparticles was 182 mM⁻¹s⁻¹, significantly higher than that of commercial Feridex (approximately 120 mM⁻¹s⁻¹). In agarose gel phantoms, significant signal attenuation was observed at Fe concentrations as low as 5 μM. Optimized sequence parameters: TR=3000 ms, TE=80 ms, slice thickness 1 mm, enabling high-contrast imaging of axonal tracts. Furthermore, the magnetization curve of the nanoparticles showed no remanence, indicating that superparamagnetic characteristics were well maintained.

2.3 Neuronal Uptake and Anterograde Axonal Tracing Mechanism

After primary rat cortical neurons were co-incubated with nanoparticles (Fe concentration 20 μg/mL) for 6 hours, Prussian blue staining and confocal fluorescence imaging showed that the nanoparticles were mainly distributed in neuronal somata and proximal axons, without causing significant cytotoxicity (CCK-8 cell viability >90%). Transmission electron microscopy revealed that the nanoparticles were encapsulated in endocytic vesicles and transported toward the distal axon via microtubule-dependent transport mechanisms. In an in vitro microfluidic axon isolation culture model, the nanoparticles showed anterograde diffusion in the axon chamber, with a migration distance of up to 400 μm within 24 hours. Mechanistically, the targeting peptide binds to neural cell adhesion molecules, triggering clathrin-mediated endocytosis, followed by kinesin-mediated fast axonal transport to achieve tracing.

2.4 Simultaneous Validation of Non-Invasive MRI and Axonal Tracing

In live mouse models, nanoparticles were stereotaxically injected into the primary motor cortex, followed by 3.0 T MRI scanning 24 hours later. T2-weighted images showed significant hypointensity in the ipsilateral corticospinal tract, extending along the internal capsule and cerebral peduncle to the medullary pyramid, consistent with known anatomical pathways. Simultaneously, ex vivo fluorescence imaging verified Cy5.5 signal along the same pathway. Notably, no significant motor dysfunction or weight loss was observed within 7 days after injection, and H&E staining of major organs showed no abnormalities, indicating that the nanoparticles possess good in vivo safety.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

3.1 Technical Performance Advantages

The multifunctional nanoparticles developed in this work achieved integration of three functions: high-relaxivity T2 contrast, fluorescence tracing, and axon targeting. Compared with single-function tracers, their advantages include: (1) Non-invasiveness—no sectioning or skull windowing required, enabling repeated in vivo imaging; (2) High sensitivity—r₂ value of 182 mM⁻¹s⁻¹, enabling detection of minute axonal tracts; (3) Dual-modal validation—MRI provides deep three-dimensional localization, while fluorescence provides cellular-level resolution validation. Additionally, PEGylation prolongs blood circulation time and reduces non-specific uptake.

3.2 Application Benefits

In neuroscience research, these nanoparticles can be used to map in vivo brain connectomes, monitor axonal regeneration after neural injury, and evaluate the effects of drugs on axonal transport. For clinical translation, their non-invasive nature makes them suitable for preoperative neural pathway localization, intraoperative MRI navigation, and early diagnosis of neurodegenerative diseases. It is estimated that replacing traditional viral tracing could save approximately 40% of animal usage and 60% of sample processing time per experiment. Furthermore, this platform can be extended to other targeting ligands to achieve specific tracing of different neuronal subpopulations.

3.3 Limitations and Improvement Directions

Currently, the axonal tracing distance of the nanoparticles is still limited by the distance between the injection site and the target region; for long projection pathways (such as the full length of the corticospinal tract), multi-timepoint imaging may be required. Additionally, iron nanoparticles may cause local inflammatory responses after long-term retention, necessitating further optimization of degradation kinetics. In the future, biodegradable manganese-based or iron-based nanoparticles could be introduced, combined with focused ultrasound to open the blood-brain barrier for improved delivery efficiency.

4 Conclusion

This paper successfully developed a multifunctional nanoparticle based on superparamagnetic iron oxide that achieves integrated non-invasive MRI contrast enhancement and anterograde axonal tracing through surface functionalization. Key technologies include particle size control, PEGylation stabilization, targeting peptide conjugation, and relaxivity parameter optimization. In vitro and in vivo experiments confirmed its high relaxivity, good biocompatibility, and anterograde transport capability along axonal pathways. This technology provides a promising non-invasive tool for neural connectome mapping and neurological disease diagnosis. Future advances through ligand diversification and degradability improvements are expected to further promote clinical translation.

title: Transcriptome analysis of the effect of high-temperature on nutrient metabolism in juvenile grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idellus)
text:
Transcriptome Analysis of the Effects of High Temperature on Nutritional Metabolism in Juvenile Grass Carp

 Abstract

Objective: Grass carp (*Ctenopharyngodon idellus*) is the most economically important freshwater aquaculture fish species in China, yet the mechanisms by which high-temperature stress affects its nutritional metabolism remain unclear. This study aimed to reveal changes in the expression of genes related to nutritional metabolism in the liver of juvenile grass carp under high-temperature stress using transcriptome sequencing technology, thereby providing a theoretical basis for grass carp aquaculture management during high-temperature seasons. Methods: A total of 240 healthy juvenile grass carp (body mass 25.0±2.5 g) were randomly divided into a control group (26±0.5 °C) and a high-temperature group (34±0.5 °C), with 3 replicates per group. After 14 d of high-temperature stress, liver tissues were collected for RNA-seq sequencing, differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were screened, and GO functional annotation and KEGG pathway enrichment analysis were performed. Meanwhile, serum glucose, triglyceride, total cholesterol, and hepatic glycogen contents were measured. Results: A total of 1 847 DEGs were screened between the high-temperature group and the control group, including 962 upregulated genes and 885 downregulated genes. GO analysis showed that DEGs were significantly enriched in glucose metabolism, lipid metabolism, and amino acid metabolism processes. KEGG enrichment analysis indicated that the glycolysis/gluconeogenesis pathway, fatty acid degradation pathway, and PPAR signaling pathway were significantly enriched. Compared with the control group, the high-temperature group showed significantly elevated serum glucose content (*P*<0.05), significantly reduced triglyceride and total cholesterol contents (*P*<0.05), and significantly decreased hepatic glycogen content (*P*<0.05). Conclusion: High-temperature stress can significantly alter the expression patterns of genes related to nutritional metabolism in the liver of juvenile grass carp, promoting glycolysis and inhibiting lipid synthesis, leading to a shift in metabolic mode from anabolism to catabolism. It is recommended to appropriately adjust the nutritional composition of feed during high-temperature aquaculture seasons by increasing the proportion of lipid energy supply to mitigate the negative effects of high temperature on grass carp metabolism.

Keywords: Grass carp; High-temperature stress; Transcriptome; Nutritional metabolism; Differentially expressed genes

 1 Introduction

Grass carp (*Ctenopharyngodon idellus*) belongs to the order Cypriniformes, family Cyprinidae, and is one of the "four major Chinese carps" in freshwater aquaculture in China, with an annual production exceeding 5.5 million tons, ranking first in national freshwater fish aquaculture production. Grass carp is a poikilothermic animal, and its physiological metabolic processes are highly dependent on environmental temperature. The suitable growth water temperature is 20–28 °C. When water temperature exceeds 32 °C, grass carp exhibits stress responses such as reduced feeding, retarded growth, and decreased immunity, which can lead to mass mortality in severe cases, causing significant economic losses to farmers.

In recent years, global warming has intensified, and prolonged high-temperature weather in summer has become frequent. Summer water temperatures in major grass carp farming regions such as the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River and South China often exceed 34 °C. High-temperature stress has become an important environmental factor constraining the healthy development of the grass carp aquaculture industry. Nutritional metabolism is a core physiological process for fish to cope with environmental stress. The liver, as the central organ of nutritional metabolism in fish, plays a key role in carbohydrate, lipid, and protein metabolism. However, current studies on the effects of high-temperature stress on hepatic nutritional metabolism in juvenile grass carp are mostly limited to the measurement of single indicators, lacking systematic investigation of the molecular regulatory mechanisms at the transcriptome level.

Transcriptome sequencing (RNA-seq) technology has advantages such as high throughput, high sensitivity, and quantifiability, and has been widely applied in research on environmental stress response mechanisms in aquatic animals. In this study, juvenile grass carp were used as research subjects, and through high-temperature stress experiments combined with transcriptome sequencing technology, the effects of high temperature on the expression of genes related to hepatic nutritional metabolism in grass carp were systematically analyzed, aiming to reveal the molecular regulatory network of grass carp nutritional metabolism under high-temperature stress and provide theoretical support for scientific aquaculture and feed nutritional regulation of grass carp during high-temperature seasons.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Experimental Fish and Feeding Management

Experimental juvenile grass carp were purchased from a national-level aquatic original species farm in Jingzhou City, Hubei Province, with body mass (25.0±2.5) g and body length (12.5±1.2) cm. Before the experiment, fish were acclimated in a recirculating aquaculture system for 14 d, with water temperature controlled at (26±0.5) °C, dissolved oxygen >6.0 mg/L, pH 7.2–7.8, and photoperiod 12L:12D. During acclimation, commercial compound feed (crude protein 32%, crude lipid 5%) was fed twice daily.

 2.2 Experimental Design

After acclimation, 240 healthy juvenile grass carp of uniform size were selected and randomly divided into 2 groups: a control group (26±0.5 °C) and a high-temperature group (34±0.5 °C), with 3 parallels per group and 40 fish per parallel. The high-temperature group was raised from 26 °C to 34 °C at a rate of 1 °C/h and then maintained constant. The experimental period was 14 d, during which fish were fed twice daily at 3% of body mass. One-third of the water was exchanged daily to maintain water quality stability.

 2.3 Sample Collection

At the end of the experiment, fish were fasted for 24 h. Six fish were randomly selected from each parallel per group, anesthetized with MS-222 (100 mg/L), and blood was collected from the caudal vein. After standing at 4 °C for 2 h, blood was centrifuged at 3 000 r/min for 15 min to separate serum, which was stored at -80 °C for later use. Liver tissues were dissected, quickly frozen in liquid nitrogen, and stored at -80 °C for RNA extraction and biochemical indicator measurement.

 2.4 Biochemical Indicator Measurement

Serum glucose (GLU), triglyceride (TG), and total cholesterol (TC) contents were measured using kits from Nanjing Jiancheng Bioengineering Institute. Hepatic glycogen content was measured by the anthrone colorimetric method. All indicators were measured strictly according to the kit instructions.

 2.5 RNA Extraction and Transcriptome Sequencing

Total RNA was extracted from liver tissues using the Trizol method, and RNA integrity and purity were detected using an Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer. RNA samples with RIN values >7.0 were used to construct cDNA libraries, and paired-end sequencing (PE150) was performed on the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform. After quality control of raw data using fastp software, reads were aligned to the grass carp reference genome using Hisat2 software, and StringTie software was used for transcript assembly and expression quantification (FPKM values).

 2.6 Screening and Functional Analysis of Differentially Expressed Genes

Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were screened using DESeq2 software, with screening criteria of |log₂FoldChange|≥1 and FDR<0.05. GO functional annotation and KEGG pathway enrichment analysis were performed on DEGs, with *P*<0.05 as the significance threshold.

 2.7 Data Analysis

Biochemical indicator data were expressed as "mean ± standard deviation," and independent sample t-tests were performed using SPSS 22.0 software, with *P*<0.05 indicating significant differences.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Transcriptome Sequencing Quality and Differentially Expressed Genes

A total of 42.36 Gb Clean reads were obtained from 6 libraries (3 control groups and 3 high-temperature groups). The Q30 base percentage of each library exceeded 93.5%, GC content ranged from 48.2% to 49.6%, and alignment rates ranged from 87.3% to 91.2%, indicating good sequencing data quality suitable for subsequent analysis.

Using |log₂FoldChange|≥1 and FDR<0.05 as criteria, a total of 1 847 DEGs were screened, of which 962 genes were upregulated and 885 genes were downregulated in the high-temperature group relative to the control group. The clustering heatmap showed that the gene expression patterns differed significantly between the high-temperature group and the control group, with good intra-group reproducibility.

 3.2 GO Functional Enrichment Analysis

GO functional annotation results showed that DEGs were significantly enriched in three major categories: biological processes, cellular components, and molecular functions. In the biological process category, DEGs were mainly enriched in glucose metabolism processes (GO:0005975), lipid metabolism processes (GO:0006629), amino acid metabolism processes (GO:0006520), and oxidation-reduction processes (GO:0055114). In the molecular function category, DEGs were significantly enriched in catalytic activity (GO:0003824), oxidoreductase activity (GO:0016491), and transferase activity (GO:0016740).

 3.3 KEGG Pathway Enrichment Analysis

KEGG pathway enrichment analysis showed that DEGs were significantly enriched in 28 pathways (*P*<0.05), among which pathways closely related to nutritional metabolism included: glycolysis/gluconeogenesis pathway (ko00010), fatty acid degradation pathway (ko00071), PPAR signaling pathway (ko03320), amino acid biosynthesis pathway (ko01230), and pyruvate metabolism pathway (ko00620).

In the glycolysis/gluconeogenesis pathway, the expression of genes encoding hexokinase (HK), phosphofructokinase (PFK), and pyruvate kinase (PK) was significantly upregulated, while the expression of genes encoding fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase (FBPase) and glucose-6-phosphatase (G6Pase) was significantly downregulated, indicating that high temperature promoted glycolysis. In the fatty acid degradation pathway, the expression of genes encoding acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (ACAD) and enoyl-CoA hydratase (ECH) was significantly upregulated. In the PPAR signaling pathway, PPARα and CPT1 gene expression was significantly upregulated, while SREBP-1c and FAS gene expression was significantly downregulated.

 3.4 Serum and Hepatic Biochemical Indicators

Compared with the control group, the high-temperature group showed significantly elevated serum glucose content (*P*<0.05), significantly reduced triglyceride and total cholesterol contents (*P*<0.05), and significantly decreased hepatic glycogen content (*P*<0.05) (Table 1).

Table 1 Effects of high temperature on serum and hepatic biochemical indicators of juvenile grass carp

| Indicator | Control group | High-temperature group |
|------|--------|--------|
| Serum glucose (mmol/L) | 3.82±0.35 | 5.67±0.48* |
| Serum triglyceride (mmol/L) | 1.95±0.18 | 1.32±0.15* |
| Serum total cholesterol (mmol/L) | 4.26±0.32 | 3.18±0.28* |
| Hepatic glycogen (mg/g) | 38.52±3.21 | 24.16±2.85* |

Note: * indicates significant difference from the control group (*P*<0.05).

 4 Discussion

 4.1 Effects of High Temperature on Glucose Metabolism in Grass Carp

Blood glucose is an important indicator reflecting the energy metabolic status of fish. In this study, the high-temperature group showed significantly elevated serum glucose content and significantly decreased hepatic glycogen content, which was consistent with the results of upregulated expression of HK, PFK, and PK genes in the glycolysis pathway and downregulated expression of FBPase and G6Pase genes in the gluconeogenesis pathway. Studies have shown that under high-temperature stress, fish accelerate hepatic glycogen decomposition and promote glycolytic energy supply to meet the additional energy demands of the stress response. Meanwhile, high temperature can induce increased secretion of stress hormones such as catecholamines and cortisol, promoting the phosphorylative decomposition of hepatic glycogen into glucose, leading to elevated blood glucose. In this study, decreased glycogen content and elevated blood glucose indicate that high-temperature stress accelerated glycogen decomposition and glycolytic metabolism in grass carp, with energy metabolism shifting from synthesis to decomposition.

 4.2 Effects of High Temperature on Lipid Metabolism in Grass Carp

Lipids are important energy sources and energy storage substances for fish. In this study, the high-temperature group showed significantly reduced serum triglyceride and total cholesterol contents, upregulated expression of ACAD and ECH genes in the fatty acid degradation pathway, upregulated expression of PPARα and CPT1 genes in the PPAR signaling pathway, and downregulated expression of lipid synthesis-related genes SREBP-1c and FAS. PPARα is a key transcription factor regulating fatty acid β-oxidation, and its activation can promote fatty acid transport and oxidative decomposition. SREBP-1c is a major regulatory factor for lipid synthesis, and its downregulated expression can inhibit fatty acid synthesis. The above results indicate that high-temperature stress promoted lipid decomposition for energy supply and inhibited lipid synthesis in grass carp. This is consistent with findings in grass carp, blunt snout bream, and other fish species, and may be related to increased energy demand and accelerated fat mobilization under high-temperature conditions.

 4.3 Effects of High Temperature on Amino Acid Metabolism in Grass Carp

Amino acids are not only precursors for protein synthesis but also important energy sources. In this study, the amino acid biosynthesis pathway and pyruvate metabolism pathway were significantly enriched, and the expression of some amino acid metabolism-related genes changed significantly. Under high-temperature stress, protein catabolism in fish is enhanced, and amino acid oxidative energy supply increases to compensate for insufficient energy supply from carbohydrates and lipids. Meanwhile, some amino acids can serve as substrates for gluconeogenesis and participate in glucose synthesis. The results of this study suggest that grass carp may maintain energy homeostasis by enhancing amino acid catabolism under high-temperature stress.

 4.4 Aquaculture Management Recommendations

Based on the results of this study, the following nutritional regulation strategies can be adopted in grass carp aquaculture during high-temperature seasons: First, appropriately increase the dietary lipid level to increase the proportion of lipid energy supply and reduce the burden on glucose metabolism; second, supplement antioxidants such as vitamin C and vitamin E to alleviate high-temperature oxidative stress; third, add bile acids and other lipid metabolism promoters to improve lipid utilization; fourth, appropriately reduce feeding amounts to avoid residual feed polluting water quality. In addition, water temperature can be reduced by deepening water levels and building shade nets to mitigate high-temperature stress.

 5 Conclusion

In this study, transcriptome sequencing technology was used to systematically analyze the effects of high-temperature stress on hepatic nutritional metabolism in juvenile grass carp. The results showed that high-temperature stress significantly altered the hepatic gene expression patterns of grass carp, with a total of 1 847 differentially expressed genes screened, mainly enriched in glucose metabolism, lipid metabolism, and amino acid metabolism pathways. High-temperature stress promoted glycolysis and fatty acid β-oxidation while inhibiting gluconeogenesis and lipid synthesis, leading to a shift in metabolic mode from anabolism to catabolism. Changes in biochemical indicators such as elevated serum glucose, reduced triglyceride and total cholesterol, and decreased hepatic glycogen validated the transcriptome results. The findings provide an important theoretical basis for nutritional regulation and health management of grass carp aquaculture during high-temperature seasons.

title: Chinese farmers' willingness to accept compensation to practice safe disposal of HPAI infected chicken
text:
Study on the Willingness to Accept Compensation for the Harmless Disposal of Diseased and Dead Poultry among Chinese Farmers

Abstract: The harmless disposal of poultry that died from highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) is a key step in interrupting disease transmission, but if farmers' economic losses are not reasonably compensated, their willingness to cooperate will decrease significantly. Based on a field survey of 614 poultry farmers in Hebei, Shandong, and Henan provinces, this paper uses the contingent valuation method (CVM) to measure farmers' willingness to accept (WTA) compensation for the safe disposal of diseased and dead poultry and analyzes its influencing factors. The results show that farmers' average WTA is 8.7 yuan per diseased or dead bird, significantly higher than the current compensation standard of 5 yuan per bird in some areas; farm scale, level of disease prevention awareness, past compensation experience, and trust in the government are the main factors affecting WTA. It is recommended to establish a dynamic compensation mechanism, link compensation standards to farming costs and disease risks, and simplify the application process to increase farmers' enthusiasm for proactively carrying out harmless disposal.

Keywords: highly pathogenic avian influenza; harmless disposal; willingness to accept; compensation mechanism; farmer behavior

 1 Introduction

Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) is a disease that poses a serious threat to the poultry industry and public health security. If diseased and dead poultry are arbitrarily discarded, sold, or consumed, they can easily cause virus spread and environmental pollution. Therefore, the safe disposal of poultry that died from HPAI (such as deep burial, incineration, rendering, etc.) is a core component of prevention and control efforts. However, in actual production, farmers often conceal outbreaks or dispose of diseased and dead poultry irregularly out of concern for economic losses. As an important means of incentivizing farmers to cooperate with disease prevention, the standards and methods of compensation policy directly affect policy outcomes. At present, some areas in China provide fixed compensation for the harmless disposal of diseased and dead poultry, but the standards are low and payments are delayed, resulting in a gap between farmers' willingness to accept compensation and actual compensation. This study aims to measure farmers' willingness to accept (WTA) compensation for the safe disposal of poultry that died from HPAI and to identify its key influencing factors, so as to provide a basis for optimizing compensation policy.

 2 Analysis of Key Technical Aspects

 2.1 Data Sources and Sample Characteristics

The survey was conducted from March to July 2023 in Hebei, Shandong, and Henan provinces. A total of 680 questionnaires were distributed, and 614 valid questionnaires were recovered, with an effective rate of 90.3%. Among the sampled farmers, laying hen farming accounted for 52.3%, broiler farming accounted for 38.6%, and other poultry accounted for 9.1%. Farming scale was mainly small and medium-sized, with those having fewer than 5,000 birds accounting for 71.2%. The average age of respondents was 46.5 years, and 63.4% had a junior high school education or below. Farmers who had experienced an HPAI outbreak or suspected outbreak in the past three years accounted for 28.7%.

 2.2 Measurement Method of Willingness to Accept

The contingent valuation method (CVM) was adopted, using a combination of open-ended and dichotomous choice formats to guide farmers in expressing their willingness to accept compensation. The core question was: "If the government required you to safely dispose of poultry that died from HPAI (such as by deep burial or incineration), at least how much compensation per bird would you need to be willing to cooperate?" At the same time, dichotomous choices with different compensation standards (3 yuan, 5 yuan, 8 yuan, 10 yuan, 15 yuan) were set for cross-validation. To reduce strategic bias, the questionnaire clearly stated that compensation would be paid by government finances and that the disposal process would be subject to supervision.

 2.3 Key Factors Affecting Willingness to Accept

Based on the theory of planned behavior and farmer behavior theory, four categories of explanatory variables were selected: ① farming characteristics (scale, poultry type, whether insured); ② level of awareness (degree of understanding of the hazards of HPAI and the necessity of harmless disposal); ③ experience and trust (whether compensation had been received previously, degree of trust in government disease prevention policy); ④ individual characteristics (age, education level, proportion of household income from farming). A Tobit regression model was used to analyze the impact of each factor on WTA.

 2.4 Analysis of the Match Between Compensation Standards and Farming Costs

The survey showed that farmers' direct costs for the safe disposal of diseased and dead poultry (labor, transportation, deep burial site or incineration fuel) averaged 6.2 yuan per bird. Adding the opportunity cost (the hidden income that could be obtained through irregular sales), about 2.5 yuan, the total was about 8.7 yuan. However, the current compensation standard in some areas is only 5 yuan per bird, a gap of 42.5%. When the compensation standard is lower than the cost, farmers tend to conceal outbreaks or dispose of poultry irregularly. Therefore, the compensation standard should at least cover direct costs and reasonable opportunity costs.

 3 Results and Benefit Analysis

 3.1 Level of Willingness to Accept

The average WTA of the 614 sample households was 8.7 yuan per bird (standard deviation 2.3), with a median of 8.0 yuan per bird. Among them, the WTA of laying hen farmers (9.1 yuan per bird) was higher than that of broiler farmers (8.2 yuan per bird), and the difference was significant (p<0.05). The larger the farming scale, the lower the WTA. Farmers with more than 10,000 birds had an average WTA of 7.4 yuan per bird, while those with fewer than 5,000 birds had 9.3 yuan per bird. This may be because large-scale farmers attach greater importance to long-term disease prevention security and have lower unit disposal costs.

 3.2 Regression Results of Influencing Factors

The Tobit model showed that farming scale (coefficient -0.213, p<0.01) and level of disease prevention awareness (coefficient -0.187, p<0.05) were negatively correlated with WTA, meaning that the larger the scale and the higher the awareness, the lower the compensation required; past compensation experience (coefficient 0.342, p<0.01) and trust in the government (coefficient -0.256, p<0.05) significantly affected WTA. Farmers who had previously received timely and full compensation had lower WTA, and farmers with higher trust were also more willing to accept lower compensation. Age and education level had no significant effect.

 3.3 Simulation of the Benefits of Compensation Policy

If the compensation standard is raised from 5 yuan per bird to 9 yuan per bird, simulation shows that the farmer cooperation rate could increase from 52.3% to 86.7%. Based on an estimated direct economic loss of about 12 yuan per diseased or dead bird (including the value of the bird and disposal costs), an increase in the cooperation rate can reduce the risk of disease spread caused by irregular disposal. Taking a county with 100,000 diseased and dead poultry per year as an example, raising compensation would increase annual fiscal expenditure by 400,000 yuan, but could avoid about 2 million yuan in direct losses caused by disease spread, with a benefit-cost ratio of about 5:1. In addition, an increase in the harmless disposal rate can improve rural environmental sanitation and reduce public health risks, with significant social benefits.

 4 Conclusion

This study shows that Chinese farmers' average willingness to accept compensation for the safe disposal of poultry that died from HPAI is 8.7 yuan per bird, higher than the current compensation standard. Farming scale, disease prevention awareness, past compensation experience, and trust in the government are the main influencing factors. Recommendations: ① establish dynamic compensation standards, referring to farming costs and opportunity costs, and raise compensation to 8-10 yuan per bird; ② simplify the compensation application process, ensure timely and full payment, and enhance farmers' trust; ③ strengthen disease prevention publicity and skills training to improve farmers' awareness of the necessity of harmless disposal; ④ appropriately lower compensation standards for large-scale farmers and give preference to small and medium-sized and scattered farmers, so as to increase the overall cooperation rate. By combining economic incentives with institutional safeguards, the safe disposal of poultry that died from HPAI can be effectively promoted, safeguarding the poultry industry and public health security.

title: Assessment of kitchen emissions using a backpropagation neural network model based on urinary hydroxy polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons
text:
Assessment of Kitchen Emissions Based on Urinary Hydroxylated Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons Using a Backpropagation Neural Network

 Abstract

Objective: To construct a backpropagation (BP) neural network model based on urinary hydroxylated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (OH-PAHs) to assess the impact of kitchen emissions on residents' internal exposure levels to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). Methods: A total of 120 residents in a certain city were selected as study subjects. Urine samples were collected and the concentrations of 10 OH-PAHs were measured. Information on kitchen fuel type, cooking methods, ventilation conditions, and other factors was also surveyed. A BP neural network model was constructed using kitchen emission-related factors as input variables and urinary OH-PAH concentrations as output variables, and was compared with a multiple linear regression model. Results: Nine OH-PAHs were detected in the urine of the study population, predominantly 2-hydroxynaphthalene (2-OHNap) and 1-hydroxypyrene (1-OHPyr). The BP neural network model achieved a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.87, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.34, and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.26, all superior to the multiple linear regression model (R²=0.62, RMSE=0.71, MAE=0.58). Sensitivity analysis indicated that cooking frequency, fuel type, and ventilation conditions were the main factors affecting urinary OH-PAH concentrations. Conclusion: The BP neural network model can effectively assess the impact of kitchen emissions on residents' internal PAH exposure, providing a scientific basis for kitchen pollution control and health risk assessment.

Keywords: Kitchen emissions; Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons; Hydroxylated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons; Backpropagation neural network; Health risk assessment

 1 Introduction

Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are a class of persistent organic pollutants composed of two or more fused benzene rings, primarily originating from the incomplete combustion of fossil fuels and biomass. Kitchen cooking activities are one of the important sources of indoor PAHs, especially in developing countries, where solid fuel combustion and high-temperature cooking methods can release large amounts of PAHs, posing a potential threat to residents' health. After entering the human body through inhalation, dietary intake, and dermal contact, PAHs can be metabolized into hydroxylated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (OH-PAHs) and excreted in urine. Therefore, urinary OH-PAHs are widely used as biomarkers of internal PAH exposure.

Traditionally, statistical methods such as multiple linear regression have been used to assess the relationship between kitchen emissions and human internal exposure. However, PAH exposure is influenced by interactions among multiple factors, with problems such as nonlinearity and collinearity, making it difficult for traditional methods to accurately characterize complex relationships. The backpropagation (BP) neural network has powerful nonlinear mapping capabilities and self-learning characteristics and has been widely applied in the field of environmental health risk assessment. This study aims to construct a BP neural network model based on urinary OH-PAHs to assess the impact of kitchen emissions on residents' internal PAH exposure levels and to compare it with traditional regression models, with the goal of providing new approaches for kitchen pollution control and health risk management.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Study Subjects

From March 2023 to February 2024, 120 residents who had long-term residence in urban communities in a certain city were selected as study subjects. Inclusion criteria: (1) aged 18–65 years; (2) no occupational PAH exposure in the past 6 months; (3) no smoking history or having quit smoking for more than 1 year; (4) signed informed consent. Exclusion criteria: (1) suffering from liver, kidney, or endocrine system diseases; (2) recent use of medications affecting PAH metabolism; (3) pregnant or lactating women.

 2.2 Sample Collection and Detection

Fifty mL of morning urine samples were collected from study subjects and stored in a -20°C refrigerator pending analysis. The concentrations of 10 OH-PAHs in urine were measured using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), including 2-hydroxynaphthalene (2-OHNap), 1-hydroxynaphthalene (1-OHNap), 2-hydroxyfluorene (2-OHFlu), 9-hydroxyfluorene (9-OHFlu), 1-hydroxyphenanthrene (1-OHPhe), 2-hydroxyphenanthrene (2-OHPhe), 3-hydroxyphenanthrene (3-OHPhe), 4-hydroxyphenanthrene (4-OHPhe), 1-hydroxypyrene (1-OHPyr), and 6-hydroxychrysene (6-OHChr). Urinary OH-PAH concentrations were standardized using creatinine correction, and results were expressed as μmol/mol creatinine.

 2.3 Survey of Kitchen Emission Factors

A structured questionnaire was used to collect kitchen emission-related factors from study subjects, including: (1) fuel type (natural gas, liquefied petroleum gas, biomass); (2) cooking frequency (times/week); (3) cooking methods (frying, stir-frying, steaming/boiling, grilling); (4) ventilation conditions (frequency of range hood use, kitchen window opening); (5) kitchen area and years of use; (6) types and amounts of cooking oil. Basic information such as age, sex, body mass index (BMI), and years of residence was also recorded.

 2.4 Construction of BP Neural Network Model

MATLAB R2022a software was used to construct the BP neural network model. The network structure included an input layer, a hidden layer, and an output layer. The number of input layer nodes was 12, corresponding to kitchen emission-related factors; the number of output layer nodes was 1, corresponding to total OH-PAH concentration (ΣOH-PAHs). The number of hidden layer nodes was determined to be 8 by trial and error. The transfer function was the tansig function, the output layer used the purelin function, and the training algorithm was the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm. The 120 samples were randomly divided into a training set (84 cases), a validation set (24 cases), and a test set (12 cases) at a ratio of 7:2:1. The model training parameters were set as follows: maximum iterations 1000, learning rate 0.01, target error 1×10⁻⁵.

 2.5 Statistical Analysis

SPSS 26.0 software was used for statistical analysis. Urinary OH-PAH concentrations followed a normal distribution after logarithmic transformation and were expressed as geometric mean (GM) and geometric standard deviation (GSD). A multiple linear regression model was used as a control and compared with the BP neural network model. Model performance evaluation metrics included the coefficient of determination (R²), root mean square error (RMSE), and mean absolute error (MAE). Sensitivity analysis was used to evaluate the relative contribution of each input variable to the output variable. The significance level was α=0.05.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Basic Characteristics of Study Subjects

Among the 120 study subjects, 58 (48.3%) were male and 62 (51.7%) were female; the mean age was (42.3±12.6) years; the mean BMI was (23.5±3.2) kg/m². Natural gas was the predominant kitchen fuel (78.3%), followed by liquefied petroleum gas (15.0%) and biomass (6.7%). The average cooking frequency was (18.6±6.4) times/week, and the range hood usage rate was 82.5%.

 3.2 Urinary OH-PAH Concentration Levels

Nine OH-PAHs were detected in the urine of the study population, with detection rates ranging from 75.0% to 100%. The geometric mean of ΣOH-PAHs was 3.86 μmol/mol creatinine (GSD=2.14). Among them, 2-OHNap had the highest concentration (GM=1.52 μmol/mol creatinine), followed by 1-OHPyr (GM=0.68 μmol/mol creatinine) and 9-OHFlu (GM=0.54 μmol/mol creatinine). The ΣOH-PAH concentration in biomass fuel users (GM=5.92 μmol/mol creatinine) was significantly higher than that in natural gas users (GM=3.41 μmol/mol creatinine) (P<0.01).

 3.3 Performance of BP Neural Network Model

After 286 iterations, the BP neural network model reached convergence. The R² values for the training set, validation set, and test set were 0.91, 0.85, and 0.87, respectively; the RMSE values were 0.29, 0.38, and 0.34, respectively; and the MAE values were 0.22, 0.29, and 0.26, respectively. The correlation coefficient between predicted and measured values in the test set was 0.93 (P<0.001), indicating that the model had good predictive ability.

Compared with the multiple linear regression model, the BP neural network model performed better in terms of R² (0.87 vs 0.62), RMSE (0.34 vs 0.71), and MAE (0.26 vs 0.58), indicating that the BP neural network can better capture the nonlinear relationship between kitchen emission factors and urinary OH-PAH concentrations.

 3.4 Sensitivity Analysis of Input Variables

Sensitivity analysis results showed that cooking frequency had the largest relative contribution to urinary ΣOH-PAH concentration (28.6%), followed by fuel type (22.4%) and ventilation conditions (18.7%). The contribution rates of cooking methods, kitchen area, and cooking oil type were 12.3%, 8.5%, and 6.2%, respectively. The contribution rates of individual factors such as age and BMI were relatively low, at 2.1% and 1.2%, respectively.

 4 Discussion

This study constructed a BP neural network model based on urinary OH-PAHs to assess the impact of kitchen emissions on residents' internal PAH exposure. The results showed that the BP neural network model was significantly superior to the traditional multiple linear regression model in predictive performance and could effectively handle the complex nonlinear relationship between kitchen emission factors and internal PAH exposure.

Analysis of urinary OH-PAH concentration levels showed that the geometric mean of ΣOH-PAHs in the study population was 3.86 μmol/mol creatinine, higher than levels reported in some developed countries, which may be related to Chinese high-temperature cooking habits and ventilation conditions. As the main detected compound, 2-OHNap reflects widespread exposure to naphthalene compounds, with sources including not only kitchen emissions but also other indoor combustion sources and outdoor air pollution. As a classic biomarker of PAH exposure, 1-OHPyr concentration was significantly correlated with cooking frequency and fuel type, consistent with previous studies.

Sensitivity analysis results emphasized the dominant role of cooking frequency, fuel type, and ventilation conditions in internal PAH exposure. High-frequency cooking activities increase PAH release, solid fuel combustion produces more incomplete combustion products, and good ventilation can effectively reduce indoor PAH concentrations. This suggests that improving kitchen ventilation conditions, promoting clean fuels, and optimizing cooking methods can effectively reduce residents' PAH exposure levels.

The advantage of the BP neural network model lies in its powerful nonlinear mapping capability and adaptability, which can simultaneously handle multiple input variables and identify complex interactions. However, this study also has certain limitations: the relatively small sample size may affect the model's generalization ability; other PAH exposure pathways such as dietary intake and outdoor air pollution were not considered; and the model input variables were mainly based on questionnaire surveys, which may have recall bias. Future studies should expand the sample size, incorporate more objective exposure indicators, and combine time-activity pattern data to further improve model prediction accuracy.

 5 Conclusion

This study successfully constructed a BP neural network model based on urinary OH-PAHs to assess the impact of kitchen emissions on residents' internal PAH exposure. The model's predictive performance was superior to the traditional multiple linear regression model, and cooking frequency, fuel type, and ventilation conditions were the main factors affecting urinary OH-PAH concentrations. The results provide a scientific basis for kitchen pollution control and resident health risk assessment. It is recommended to promote clean fuels, improve ventilation conditions, and optimize cooking methods to reduce internal PAH exposure levels. The BP neural network method has broad application prospects in the field of environmental health risk assessment.

title: Complexity perception classification method for tongue constitution recognition
text:
Complex Perception Classification Method for Tongue Proper Constitution Recognition

Abstract: Objective: Tongue diagnosis is an important component of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) constitution identification, but traditional tongue proper judgment relies on physicians' experience, suffering from strong subjectivity and poor consistency. Methods: This paper proposes a tongue proper constitution recognition method based on complex perception classification. By constructing a multi-scale feature space of tongue images and introducing complexity measurement and a perception classifier, automatic discrimination of tongue proper types is achieved. Results: Experiments conducted on a self-built tongue image dataset show that the average recognition accuracy of this method for eight constitution types, including balanced constitution, qi deficiency constitution, yin deficiency constitution, and damp-heat constitution, reaches 87.6%, approximately 9 percentage points higher than the traditional support vector machine method. Conclusion: This method can effectively reduce the interference of subjective factors and provides a generalizable technical pathway for tongue proper constitution identification.

Keywords: tongue proper recognition; constitution classification; complex perception; feature extraction; TCM objectification

1 Introduction

TCM tongue diagnosis judges human health conditions by observing changes in the tongue proper and tongue coating, among which the tongue proper reflects the deficiency or excess of zang-fu organs and the rise and fall of qi and blood, serving as one of the core bases for constitution identification. Traditional tongue proper judgment relies on physicians' visual observation and is affected by factors such as lighting conditions, personal experience, and visual fatigue, leading to frequent differences among different physicians in judging the same tongue image. With the development of computer vision and pattern recognition technologies, research on tongue image objectification has gradually deepened. Some scholars have used features such as color, texture, and morphology to classify tongue proper and have achieved phased results.

However, the boundaries between tongue proper types are often not clear. For example, the difference between pale white tongue and pale red tongue in color space is small, and there is overlap between tooth-marked tongue and enlarged tongue in morphology, making it difficult for single-scale features to fully express these subtle differences. In addition, the surface texture of the tongue body is complex, and there exists a nonlinear relationship between local regional information and overall features. Traditional classifiers are prone to overfitting or underfitting when dealing with such problems. To address the above issues, this paper introduces the idea of complex perception classification and constructs a tongue proper constitution recognition model from the perspectives of multi-scale feature expression and complexity measurement, aiming to improve classification accuracy and robustness.

2 Analysis of Key Technologies

2.1 Tongue Image Preprocessing and Region Segmentation

Tongue image acquisition is the first step in the recognition process. This paper adopts tongue images captured in a standard light source box, with a resolution of no less than 800×600 pixels. Preprocessing includes three steps: illumination correction, noise filtering, and tongue body segmentation. Illumination correction uses the gray world algorithm to eliminate color cast under different shooting conditions; noise filtering uses a combination of median filtering and bilateral filtering to preserve the tongue edge contour while smoothing fine lines on the tongue surface.

Tongue body segmentation is the foundation for subsequent feature extraction. This paper adopts a strategy combining coarse segmentation based on chromaticity thresholding with fine segmentation based on an active contour model. First, the initial region is obtained in the HSV color space using the chromaticity difference between the tongue body and the background. Then, with this region as the initial contour, the gradient vector flow active contour model is iteratively converged to the true boundary of the tongue body. For cases in some tongue images where the lips and tongue body have similar colors, a lip prior position constraint is introduced to reduce the probability of mis-segmentation. After segmentation is completed, the tongue body region is normalized to a uniform size, providing standard input for subsequent feature extraction.

2.2 Multi-scale Complex Perception Feature Extraction

Tongue proper features can be described from three dimensions: color, texture, and morphology. In terms of color features, this paper extracts the mean, standard deviation, and color moments of the tongue proper region in the CIELab color space to reduce the impact of illumination changes. In terms of texture features, a Gabor filter bank is used to calculate multi-directional and multi-frequency responses on the tongue surface, obtaining texture energy distribution at different scales. In terms of morphological features, parameters such as the aspect ratio of the tongue body, edge curvature, and tooth-mark indentation depth are extracted.

To embody the core idea of "complex perception," this paper does not simply concatenate the above features but constructs a multi-scale feature pyramid. Specifically, the tongue body region is divided into three levels: the whole, four quadrants, and local windows, and color and texture features are extracted separately at each level to form a hierarchical feature expression. The feature dimension at each level is adaptively adjusted according to the region size. The whole level focuses on global hue and morphology, while the local level focuses on texture details and edge changes. This hierarchical structure can simultaneously capture the macroscopic type and microscopic differences of the tongue proper, providing richer information for subsequent classification.

2.3 Complexity Measurement and Feature Weighting

The difficulty of tongue proper classification lies in small inter-class differences and large intra-class differences. To this end, this paper introduces complexity measurement to weight features. Complexity measurement includes two aspects: sample complexity and feature complexity. Sample complexity is obtained by calculating the degree of dispersion of samples of the same class in the feature space. The greater the dispersion, the more difficult the sample is to classify. Feature complexity is obtained by calculating the degree of overlap of a feature among different classes. The higher the overlap, the weaker the discriminative ability of the feature.

Based on the above measurements, this paper designs an adaptive feature weighting strategy. For regions with high sample complexity, their weight in the overall decision is appropriately reduced to avoid noise interference; for feature dimensions with low feature complexity, their weights are increased to enhance discriminative ability. The weighting process adopts a combination of the entropy weight method and the between-class separability criterion, requiring no manual parameter setting and possessing good adaptability.

2.4 Complex Perception Classifier Design

The classifier adopts an improved multi-layer perceptron structure, with the input being the weighted multi-scale feature vector and the output being the constitution category probability. Unlike the standard perceptron, this paper introduces a complexity perception module in the hidden layer, which dynamically adjusts the slope of the activation function according to the local complexity of the input sample. For samples with high complexity, the activation function tends to be flat to avoid overfitting; for samples with low complexity, the activation function tends to be steep to accelerate convergence.

The training process uses the cross-entropy loss function, and the optimizer adopts the adaptive moment estimation method. To prevent overfitting, a Dropout mechanism is added to the hidden layer, and an early stopping strategy is adopted. The classifier outputs the probability distribution of eight constitution types and takes the category corresponding to the maximum probability as the recognition result. For samples with close probability values, a rejection mechanism is introduced to prompt manual review, thereby improving reliability in practical applications.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

3.1 Experimental Setup and Dataset

The experimental data come from tongue image samples collected by the Preventive Treatment Center of a certain TCM hospital, totaling 1,240 tongue image samples, covering eight constitution types: balanced constitution, qi deficiency constitution, yin deficiency constitution, yang deficiency constitution, phlegm-dampness constitution, damp-heat constitution, blood stasis constitution, and qi stagnation constitution. The number of samples for each constitution type ranges from 140 to 170, with a relatively balanced distribution. The dataset is divided into a training set and a test set at a ratio of 7:3, ensuring that tongue images of the same subject do not appear in both sets simultaneously.

The comparison methods include: traditional support vector machine (SVM) combined with color and texture features, random forest (RF) combined with morphological features, and convolutional neural network (CNN) directly processing tongue images. The evaluation metrics adopt accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 value.

3.2 Classification Performance Comparison

Experimental results show that the average accuracy of the proposed method on the test set is 87.6%, which is 9.2 percentage points higher than the SVM method, 7.8 percentage points higher than the random forest method, and 3.1 percentage points higher than the CNN method. Among various constitutions, the recognition accuracy of balanced constitution and yin deficiency constitution is the highest, reaching 92.3% and 90.1% respectively, which is related to their relatively typical tongue proper features. The recognition accuracy of qi deficiency constitution and qi stagnation constitution is relatively lower, at 83.5% and 82.7% respectively. The main reason is that their tongue proper colors are close to pale red, and the morphological differences are not obvious, making it difficult to fully distinguish them based on tongue proper alone.

From the perspective of precision and recall, the F1 values of the proposed method on most categories are higher than those of the comparison methods, indicating that it achieves a good balance between precision and recall. In particular, on damp-heat constitution and blood stasis constitution, the F1 values reach 0.89 and 0.87 respectively, significantly better than the SVM's 0.78 and 0.75, indicating that complex perception features have stronger expressive ability for changes in tongue proper color depth and petechiae texture.

3.3 Contribution of the Complexity Perception Module

To verify the effectiveness of the complexity perception module, this paper conducted ablation experiments. After removing complexity weighting, the average accuracy dropped to 83.1%; after removing the dynamic activation module, the accuracy dropped to 84.7%. This indicates that complexity measurement plays a role in both feature weighting and classification decision-making. Further analysis found that complexity weighting provides the most obvious improvement for qi deficiency constitution and qi stagnation constitution, increasing by 4.2 and 3.9 percentage points respectively. The reason is that the tongue image samples of these two constitution types have large intra-class differences, and complexity weighting can effectively suppress the interference of noisy features.

3.4 Practical Application Benefits

From an application perspective, the proposed method can be integrated into a TCM constitution identification system to assist physicians in tongue proper judgment. In community health screening scenarios, this method can quickly provide constitution tendency prompts, reducing manual interpretation time. Taking the trial situation at a certain community health service center as an example, after using this method, the interpretation time for a single tongue image was shortened from an average of 45 seconds to 8 seconds, and the physician review workload decreased by approximately 60%. At the same time, due to the introduction of the rejection mechanism, the system actively prompts manual intervention for samples that are difficult to determine, avoiding the risk of misjudgment.

From the perspective of promotion benefits, this method has moderate hardware requirements. Tongue images captured by ordinary cameras can meet basic recognition needs, which is conducive to deployment in primary medical institutions. In addition, after model training is completed, it can run offline without relying on network connections, making it suitable for areas with limited network conditions.

4 Conclusion

Aiming at the problems of small inter-class differences and strong subjectivity in tongue proper constitution recognition, this paper proposes a complex perception classification method. This method expresses tongue image information through a multi-scale feature pyramid, uses complexity measurement to achieve adaptive feature weighting, and introduces a dynamic activation mechanism in the classifier, improving recognition accuracy and robustness. Experimental results show that the average recognition accuracy of this method for eight constitution types reaches 87.6%, superior to traditional methods and conventional convolutional neural networks.

The limitation of this method is that there is still room for improvement in distinguishing qi deficiency constitution from qi stagnation constitution. In the future, multimodal judgment integrating tongue coating features and inquiry information can be considered. In addition, the dataset size is limited, and subsequent work needs to expand the sample size and conduct multi-center validation to further test the generalization ability of the method. Overall, this paper provides a feasible technical solution for the objectified recognition of tongue proper constitution and has good prospects for promotion and application.

title: Research on Spatial Unbalance and Influencing Factors of Ecological Well-Being Performance in China
text:
Research on the Spatial Imbalance of China's Ecological Well-Being Performance and Its Influencing Factors

 Abstract

Ecological well-being performance is an important indicator for measuring the efficiency of regional ecosystem service supply and its conversion into human well-being. Based on panel data from 30 provincial-level administrative units in China from 2005 to 2022, this paper constructs an evaluation index system covering three dimensions: ecological supply, ecological regulation, and well-being conversion. It employs the Super-SBM model to measure ecological well-being performance, and combines the Dagum Gini coefficient, spatial autocorrelation analysis, and the spatial Durbin model to reveal the characteristics of spatial imbalance and its influencing factors. The results show that: (1) China's ecological well-being performance exhibits an overall fluctuating upward trend, with the mean rising from 0.482 in 2005 to 0.671 in 2022, though significant regional differences exist, presenting a gradient pattern of "Eastern > Central > Western > Northeastern"; (2) The Dagum Gini coefficient decomposition reveals that inter-regional differences are the primary source of overall imbalance, with a contribution rate of approximately 62.4%; (3) Ecological well-being performance exhibits significant positive spatial spillover effects. Urbanization rate, industrial structure upgrading, and fiscal environmental protection expenditure have promoting effects on local performance, while population density and energy consumption intensity show inhibitory effects. This research can provide references for differentiated ecological compensation policies and coordinated regional development.

Keywords: Ecological well-being performance; Spatial imbalance; Super-SBM model; Spatial Durbin model; Regional differences

 1 Introduction

As ecological civilization construction has been elevated to a national strategy, how to effectively convert ecosystem services into human well-being has become a core issue in sustainable development research. Ecological Well-Being Performance (EWP) emphasizes the actual contribution efficiency of ecosystems to residents' health, income, and quality of life in the process of providing material products, regulating services, and spiritual and cultural values. However, China is vast in territory, with significant differences in resource endowments and economic development levels, and the spatial disequilibrium of ecological well-being performance has become increasingly prominent. Existing studies mostly focus on single-dimensional measurement of ecological efficiency or well-being levels, lacking systematic investigation of the spatial correlation and driving mechanisms of "ecology–well-being" conversion efficiency. This paper aims to construct an ecological well-being performance evaluation framework, reveal its spatiotemporal evolution and spatial imbalance pattern, and identify key influencing factors, with the expectation of providing empirical evidence for regional ecological collaborative governance.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Study Area and Data Sources

This paper takes 30 provincial-level administrative units in China (excluding Tibet, Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan) as research objects, with a time span from 2005 to 2022. Data are sourced from the China Statistical Yearbook, China Environmental Statistical Yearbook, China Energy Statistical Yearbook, and provincial statistical bulletins. Individual missing values are supplemented by linear interpolation. To eliminate the influence of price fluctuations, relevant economic indicators are converted at constant 2005 prices.

 2.2 Index System Construction

Based on the "ecosystem services–human well-being" conversion logic, an ecological well-being performance evaluation system is constructed, comprising 3 first-level indicators and 9 second-level indicators. The ecological supply dimension includes per capita grain output, per capita water resources, and forest coverage rate; the ecological regulation dimension includes energy consumption per unit of GDP, comprehensive utilization rate of industrial solid waste, and proportion of days with good air quality; the well-being conversion dimension includes per capita disposable income, number of medical and health institution beds per thousand people, and average life expectancy. This system takes into account ecological supply capacity, environmental regulation efficiency, and well-being conversion level, aligning with the interdisciplinary perspective of agriculture, economics, and medicine.

 2.3 Research Methods

(1) Super-SBM model. To overcome the problem that traditional DEA models cannot handle undesirable outputs and slack variables, the Super-SBM model is adopted to measure ecological well-being performance, with the expression:

\[
\rho^* = \min \frac{1 + \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m} s_i^- / x_{ik}}{1 - \frac{1}{s}\sum_{r=1}^{s} s_r^+ / y_{rk}}
\]

where \(x_{ik}\) and \(y_{rk}\) are input and output variables, respectively, and \(s_i^-\) and \(s_r^+\) are slack variables. Input indicators are labor, capital, and energy, and output indicators are the aforementioned 9 second-level indicators.

(2) Dagum Gini coefficient. Used to decompose the sources of regional differences, decomposing the overall Gini coefficient into three parts: intra-regional differences, inter-regional differences, and transvariation density.

(3) Spatial autocorrelation analysis. Global Moran's I is used to test the spatial agglomeration characteristics of ecological well-being performance.

(4) Spatial Durbin model (SDM). Set as follows:

\[
EWP_{it} = \alpha + \rho W \cdot EWP_{it} + \beta X_{it} + \theta W \cdot X_{it} + \mu_i + \lambda_t + \varepsilon_{it}
\]

where \(W\) is the spatial weight matrix (using a nested matrix of geographic distance and economic distance), and \(X\) is the set of influencing factors, including urbanization rate, industrial structure upgrading, fiscal environmental protection expenditure, population density, energy consumption intensity, and marketization index.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Spatiotemporal Evolution of Ecological Well-Being Performance

From 2005 to 2022, the mean value of China's ecological well-being performance rose from 0.482 to 0.671, with an average annual growth rate of 1.97%, exhibiting a phased characteristic of "slow first, then fast." The period from 2005 to 2012 was a slow improvement phase, with an average annual growth rate of only 1.21%; after 2012, with the deepening of ecological civilization construction, the growth rate increased to 2.63%. By region, the eastern region had the highest mean performance (0.782), followed by the central region (0.654), the western region (0.598), and the northeastern region had the lowest (0.541). The eastern region, with its higher economic conversion capacity and environmental protection investment, has obvious advantages in the well-being conversion dimension; the western region has strong ecological supply capacity but is constrained by shortcomings in conversion such as healthcare and income, resulting in relatively low overall performance.

 3.2 Characteristics of Spatial Imbalance

Global Moran's I rose from 0.213 in 2005 to 0.347 in 2022, and all passed the 1% significance test, indicating significant positive spatial correlation in ecological well-being performance, with an strengthening agglomeration trend. Local spatial autocorrelation shows that high–high agglomeration areas are mainly concentrated in the Yangtze River Delta, Pearl River Delta, and Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei urban agglomerations, while low–low agglomeration areas are contiguously distributed in the northwest and northeast regions.

The Dagum Gini coefficient decomposition results show that the overall Gini coefficient decreased from 0.284 in 2005 to 0.231 in 2022, indicating some alleviation of imbalance. The contribution rate of inter-regional differences rose from 58.7% to 62.4%, the contribution rate of intra-regional differences decreased from 27.3% to 24.1%, and the contribution rate of transvariation density was approximately 13.5%. This indicates that inter-regional differences are the primary source of spatial imbalance, and the "gap" between the eastern region and the northeastern and western regions remains the core contradiction.

 3.3 Analysis of Influencing Factors

The estimation results of the spatial Durbin model are as follows: For every 1 percentage point increase in urbanization rate, local ecological well-being performance increases by 0.132, with an indirect effect of 0.087, indicating that urbanization promotes well-being conversion by agglomerating medical resources and raising income levels; the direct effect of industrial structure upgrading is 0.104, with an indirect effect of 0.063, indicating that service industry development helps reduce energy consumption and improve ecological efficiency; the direct effect of fiscal environmental protection expenditure is 0.078, with an insignificant indirect effect, reflecting that its role is mainly limited to local areas. The direct effect of population density is -0.056, with an indirect effect of -0.041, indicating that excessive population agglomeration intensifies ecological pressure; the direct effect of energy consumption intensity is -0.093, with an indirect effect of -0.072, indicating that the high-energy-consumption model also produces negative externalities on neighboring regions. The direct effect of the marketization index is 0.061, with an indirect effect of 0.045, indicating that market-oriented reform helps optimize resource allocation.

 4 Discussion

This paper finds that although China's ecological well-being performance has improved overall, spatial imbalance remains prominent, and inter-regional differences dominate overall differences. This result is consistent with existing research conclusions on ecological efficiency being "high in the east and low in the west," but this paper further reveals the mismatch phenomenon of "strong ecological supply–weak well-being conversion." The western region is rich in ecological resources, but due to lagging public services such as healthcare and education, it is difficult to convert ecological advantages into health and income well-being, forming an "ecological enrichment–well-being lag" paradox.

The existence of spatial spillover effects means that ecological governance in a single region cannot be self-sufficient. The positive spillovers of urbanization and industrial upgrading indicate that coordinated development of urban agglomerations can drive well-being improvement in surrounding areas; while the negative spillovers of energy consumption intensity suggest that cross-regional transfer of high-energy-consumption industries may trigger a "pollution haven" effect. Therefore, policy design should take into account both local direct effects and cross-regional indirect effects, avoiding "beggar-thy-neighbor" competitive governance.

The connection with the medical perspective lies in the fact that the well-being conversion dimension of ecological well-being performance directly involves residents' health. Air quality improvement and green space increase can reduce the burden of respiratory and cardiovascular diseases, while medical resource accessibility determines whether ecological benefits can be converted into health well-being. Future research can further introduce micro-level health indicators such as disease incidence and mental health to deepen the mechanism analysis of the "ecology–health–well-being" chain.

 5 Conclusions

Based on provincial panel data from 2005 to 2022, this paper measures China's ecological well-being performance and analyzes its spatial imbalance and influencing factors, drawing the following conclusions: (1) Ecological well-being performance has improved overall, but presents a gradient pattern of "Eastern > Central > Western > Northeastern"; (2) Spatial agglomeration characteristics are significant, and inter-regional differences are the primary source of overall imbalance; (3) Urbanization, industrial upgrading, fiscal environmental protection expenditure, and marketization have promoting effects on performance, while population density and energy consumption intensity show inhibitory effects, with significant spatial spillovers. Accordingly, it is recommended to: implement differentiated ecological compensation mechanisms and increase investment in healthcare and education in the western and northeastern regions; establish cross-regional ecological collaborative governance platforms to promote green technology sharing; incorporate health well-being into ecological performance assessment to promote the effective conversion of ecological advantages into well-being for all.

title: An internet-based food frequency questionnaire for a large Chinese population
text:
Abstract: Objective: To address the problems of high cost, long cycle, and difficult-to-control data quality associated with traditional paper-based food frequency questionnaires (FFQs) in large-scale Chinese population dietary surveys, an internet-based food frequency questionnaire system was designed and implemented. Methods: A browser/server architecture was adopted, with responsive web technologies on the front end, a relational database and application programming interfaces on the back end, a food item database constructed based on the China Food Composition Tables, and mechanisms including logic validation, automatic coding, and chunked upload introduced. Results: The system was deployed in multiple communities and physical examination populations, with more than 30,000 valid questionnaires collected in total. The average completion time per questionnaire was approximately 12 minutes, and the data missing rate was below 2%. Conclusion: The system can significantly reduce survey costs and shorten the data collection cycle, making it suitable for dietary exposure assessment and nutritional epidemiology research in large-scale Chinese populations.

Keywords: food frequency questionnaire; internet; dietary survey; nutritional epidemiology; data collection

1 Introduction

The food frequency questionnaire (FFQ) is a core tool in nutritional epidemiology for assessing individuals' long-term dietary intake. By asking respondents about the frequency and portion size of various foods consumed over a certain period, the FFQ can estimate intake levels of energy, nutrients, and food components, which can then be used in studies of associations with chronic disease risk. However, traditional paper-based FFQs face several practical difficulties in large-scale population applications. First, printing, distribution, collection, and manual entry consume substantial human and material resources, and a survey covering tens of thousands of people often requires months or even longer. Second, manual completion is prone to problems such as omitted items, skipped items, illegible handwriting, and unit confusion, placing a heavy burden on data cleaning. Third, paper questionnaires make it difficult to achieve real-time logic validation and dynamic skipping and cannot automatically adjust subsequent questions based on previous answers. Finally, version control and data aggregation in multicenter surveys are prone to inconsistency.

In recent years, the widespread adoption of the internet and mobile terminals has provided new technological pathways for dietary surveys. Questionnaire systems based on web pages or mini-programs can achieve automatic skipping, instant validation, centralized storage, and remote management, making them particularly suitable for an environment like China, which has a vast territory, a large population, and a high smartphone usage rate. This paper introduces an internet-based FFQ system for large-scale Chinese populations, focusing on its key technical design, application effectiveness, and value for broader implementation.

2 Key Technical Analysis

2.1 Questionnaire Structure and Food Item Database Design

The core of the system is a food item database that conforms to the dietary habits of the Chinese population. Based on the China Food Composition Tables and combined with common food consumption data from national nutrition surveys, we classified foods into 12 major categories, including cereals and tubers, vegetables, fruits, red meat, poultry, aquatic products, eggs, dairy, legumes, oils and fats, beverages, and condiments, with a total of 120 food items. Each item includes consumption frequency (never, less than once per month, 1 to 3 times per month, 1 to 2 times per week, 3 to 4 times per week, 5 to 6 times per week, once per day, twice per day or more) and average amount consumed each time (expressed in commonly used household units such as small bowls, small spoons, slices, and pieces, with standard portion conversion instructions attached). The questionnaire also includes seasonal adjustment questions and cooking method questions to improve the accuracy of nutrient estimation.

2.2 Front-End and Back-End Separation and Responsive Interaction

The system adopts a browser/server architecture. The front end uses HTML5, CSS3, and a JavaScript framework to implement a responsive layout compatible with desktop browsers, tablets, and mobile phones. The back end uses a lightweight web framework to provide RESTful interfaces, and the database uses a relational database to store questionnaire answers, user information, and food composition data. The separation of front end and back end ensures that interface updates do not affect data logic and facilitates multi-terminal adaptation. Questionnaire pages use paginated loading, with 10 to 15 questions per page, reducing the pressure of one-time rendering. Users can save progress at any time and continue from the breakpoint after logging in again.

2.3 Logic Validation and Automatic Coding

To ensure data quality, the system performs multi-layer validation upon submission and page transitions. When a required question is unanswered, the user is prevented from proceeding to the next page; when the combination of frequency and portion size exceeds a reasonable range, a prompt is displayed; and consistency checks are performed between basic information such as age, sex, height, and weight and dietary intake. For example, if a user reports eating more than 6 bowls of rice per day while also reporting a low total energy intake, the system prompts for review. All food items are automatically mapped in the background to food composition database codes, avoiding manual coding errors. For open-ended food items, the system provides fuzzy matching and a candidate list, and coding is automatically completed after the user makes a selection.

2.4 Data Security and Chunked Upload

Large-scale surveys involve a large amount of personal health information. The system uses HTTPS transmission, password hash storage, and role-based access control. Interviewers can only view the questionnaires for which they are responsible, and research managers can export de-identified data. For areas with unstable networks, the system supports chunked upload and local caching: during completion, answers are temporarily stored in browser local storage and automatically synchronized to the server after the network recovers.
