Asian pears and European pears originated from different wild ancestors, diverged during the Middle Pleistocene, and subsequently underwent independent domestication in China and the Caucasus-Central Asia region, respectively. The two groups underwent differentiated selection in fruit size, sugar-acid metabolism, stone cell formation, and disease resistance, forming their own unique genetic bases. Genome-wide association analysis identified multiple independent domestication loci, providing key targets for cross-population hybrid breeding and molecular design breeding. In the future, bidirectional introgression of germplasm resources between Asian pears and European pears should be strengthened, utilizing the allelic complementarity generated by independent domestication to breed breakthrough new varieties with large fruit, low stone cells, high disease resistance, and excellent flavor. At the same time, it is recommended to establish a whole-genome selection platform for the genus Pyrus, promoting the transformation from traditional breeding to precision breeding, and providing scientific and technological support for the high-quality development of the pear industry.

title: Foodomics Revealed the Effects of Extract Methods on the Composition and Nutrition of Peanut Oil
text:
Foodomics Reveals the Effects of Extraction Methods on the Composition and Nutrition of Peanut Oil

Abstract

To investigate the effects of different extraction methods on the composition and nutritional characteristics of peanut oil, this study employed cold pressing, hot pressing, solvent extraction, and supercritical CO₂ extraction to extract peanut oil. Foodomics techniques (gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry, and metabolomics analysis) were used to systematically analyze the fatty acid composition, lipid-soluble accompaniments, and volatile flavor compounds. The results showed that the peanut oils obtained by the four extraction methods were all dominated by oleic acid and linoleic acid in terms of fatty acid composition, but supercritical CO₂ extraction had the highest retention rate of unsaturated fatty acids (89.6%). In terms of nutritional accompaniments, the tocopherol content of cold-pressed and supercritical CO₂-extracted oils was significantly higher than that of hot-pressed and solvent-extracted oils (P<0.05), with the α-tocopherol content of supercritical CO₂ extraction reaching 187.3 mg/kg. Metabolomics analysis identified a total of 126 differential metabolites, mainly enriched in unsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis and glycerophospholipid metabolism pathways. Hot pressing produced the greatest variety of volatile flavor compounds (68 types), predominantly pyrazines and aldehydes. Considering both nutritional quality and flavor characteristics, supercritical CO₂ extraction showed clear advantages in retaining nutritional components, cold pressing is suitable for the development of high-end nutritional oil, and hot pressing has unique advantages in the production of peanut oil with a rich flavor.

Keywords: peanut oil; extraction method; foodomics; fatty acid composition; tocopherol; metabolomics

1 Introduction

Peanut (*Arachis hypogaea* L.) is an important oilseed crop in China, with an annual output of about 18 million tons, ranking first in the world. As one of the main edible vegetable oils for Chinese residents, peanut oil accounts for about 8%–10% of total vegetable oil consumption annually. Peanut oil is rich in unsaturated fatty acids such as oleic acid and linoleic acid, as well as lipid-soluble functional components such as tocopherols, phytosterols, and resveratrol, and possesses physiological functions such as lowering cholesterol, antioxidation, and preventing cardiovascular diseases.

At present, the industrial extraction methods of peanut oil mainly include pressing (cold pressing and hot pressing), solvent extraction, and supercritical fluid extraction. Due to differences in process conditions such as temperature, pressure, and solvent polarity, different extraction methods have significant effects on the chemical composition and nutritional quality of oils. Traditional research methods mostly focus on the comparison of a single indicator or a few indicators, making it difficult to comprehensively reveal the mechanism by which the extraction process affects the overall quality of oils.

Foodomics, as an emerging interdisciplinary field, integrates multi-omics technologies such as genomics, proteomics, and metabolomics, and can systematically analyze the relationship between food components and processing techniques at the overall level. In recent years, foodomics has been widely applied in research fields such as authenticity identification, geographical origin tracing, and processing optimization of edible oils. However, studies systematically comparing the effects of different extraction methods on the composition and nutrition of peanut oil based on a foodomics strategy are still insufficient.

In this study, a major peanut cultivar in China was used as raw material, and peanut oils were prepared by four typical extraction methods. Foodomics techniques were used to comprehensively analyze their fatty acid profiles, lipid-soluble accompaniments, and volatile metabolites, aiming to provide a scientific basis for the precise processing and quality improvement of peanut oil.

2 Materials and Methods

2.1 Materials and Reagents

The peanut cultivar tested was "Luhua No. 14," purchased from the Shandong Academy of Agricultural Sciences. After shelling and screening, peanut kernels were sealed and stored at 4°C for later use. Fatty acid methyl ester standards (37 types), tocopherol standards (α, β, γ, δ), and phytosterol standards were all purchased from Sigma-Aldrich. Chromatographic-grade organic solvents such as n-hexane, isopropanol, and methanol were purchased from Fisher Scientific.

2.2 Peanut Oil Extraction Methods

Cold pressing: Peanut kernels were hydraulically pressed at 60°C under a pressure of 40 MPa. After oil release, the oil was separated by centrifugation (8000 r/min, 15 min) to obtain cold-pressed peanut oil.

Hot pressing: Peanut kernels were roasted at 160°C for 30 min and then pressed using a screw press. The resulting crude oil was separated by centrifugation to obtain hot-pressed peanut oil.

Solvent extraction: Using n-hexane as the solvent, the solid-to-liquid ratio was 1:5 (w/v), and extraction was carried out at 60°C for 4 h. After recovering the solvent by rotary evaporation, solvent-extracted peanut oil was obtained.

Supercritical CO₂ extraction: The extraction pressure was 30 MPa, the temperature was 45°C, the CO₂ flow rate was 15 L/h, the extraction time was 2 h, and the separation temperature was 35°C.

2.3 Foodomics Analysis

Fatty acid composition analysis: A gas chromatography-mass spectrometer (GC-MS, Agilent 7890B-5977A) was used with a DB-23 capillary column (60 m × 0.25 mm × 0.25 μm) and programmed temperature rise. Fatty acid methylation was performed according to the method of GB 5009.168-2016.

Lipid-soluble accompaniment analysis: Tocopherols and phytosterols were determined using a high-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometer (HPLC-MS, Waters ACQUITY UPLC-Xevo TQ-S). The chromatographic column was a BEH C18 column (2.1 mm × 100 mm, 1.7 μm), and the mobile phase was methanol-water gradient elution.

Metabolomics analysis: Ultra-performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-QTOF-MS, Waters Xevo G2-XS) was used for untargeted metabolomics analysis. Data were processed by Progenesis QI software, and metabolites were identified through the HMDB and METLIN databases.

2.4 Data Processing

All experiments were repeated 3 times, and data were expressed as mean ± standard deviation. SPSS 26.0 was used for one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), and Duncan's multiple comparison test was used to test the significance of differences (P<0.05). Metabolomics data were analyzed by principal component analysis (PCA) and partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) using MetaboAnalyst 5.0.

3 Results and Analysis

3.1 Effects of Different Extraction Methods on the Fatty Acid Composition of Peanut Oil

The fatty acid compositions of peanut oils obtained by the four extraction methods are shown in Table 1. All samples were mainly composed of oleic acid (C18:1) and linoleic acid (C18:2), which together accounted for 78%–82% of total fatty acids. Supercritical CO₂ extraction had the highest oleic acid content (43.6%), significantly higher than hot pressing (41.2%) and solvent extraction (40.8%) (P<0.05). The retention rates of unsaturated fatty acids in cold-pressed and supercritical CO₂-extracted oils were 88.3% and 89.6%, respectively, significantly higher than those in hot-pressed (85.1%) and solvent-extracted (86.4%) oils. Due to high-temperature treatment, hot pressing caused oxidative degradation of some unsaturated fatty acids, and the proportion of saturated fatty acids increased relatively.

3.2 Analysis of Lipid-Soluble Nutritional Accompaniments

Tocopherol content analysis showed that the total tocopherol contents of cold-pressed and supercritical CO₂-extracted oils were 312.5 mg/kg and 298.7 mg/kg, respectively, significantly higher than those of hot-pressed (245.3 mg/kg) and solvent-extracted (231.8 mg/kg) oils (P<0.05). Among them, α-tocopherol was highest in supercritical CO₂ extraction (187.3 mg/kg), while γ-tocopherol was best retained in cold pressing (98.6 mg/kg). The total phytosterol content was highest in supercritical CO₂ extraction (2156 mg/kg), followed by cold pressing (2034 mg/kg). Because high temperature promoted tocopherol oxidation and sterol degradation in hot pressing, both contents were significantly reduced.

3.3 Metabolomics Analysis

Untargeted metabolomics analysis identified a total of 126 differential metabolites, mainly including fatty acids and their derivatives (42 types), glycerophospholipids (28 types), tocopherols and analogs (12 types), phytosterols (15 types), and volatile organic compounds (29 types). PCA analysis showed that peanut oils obtained by the four extraction methods could be clearly distinguished (R²X=0.876, Q²=0.812). In the PLS-DA model, supercritical CO₂ extraction and cold pressing were relatively close on the score plot, indicating a high degree of similarity in their metabolite profiles.

Metabolic pathway enrichment analysis showed that differential metabolites were mainly enriched in unsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis (impact value=0.42), glycerophospholipid metabolism (impact value=0.38), and linoleic acid metabolism (impact value=0.31) pathways. The contents of pyrazine compounds (2,5-dimethylpyrazine, 2-ethyl-3-methylpyrazine) in hot-pressed samples were significantly increased. These compounds are typical products of the Maillard reaction and contribute to the unique roasted aroma of hot-pressed peanut oil.

3.4 Comparison of Volatile Flavor Compounds

Solid-phase microextraction-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry analysis detected a total of 87 volatile compounds. Hot-pressed peanut oil had the greatest variety of volatile substances (68 types) and the largest total peak area, mainly pyrazines (32.4%), aldehydes (26.8%), and furans (12.3%). Cold-pressed and supercritical CO₂-extracted oils had fewer types of volatile substances (35 and 31 types, respectively), mainly aldehydes and alcohols, with a light flavor. Solvent extraction retained a small amount of n-hexane (<5 mg/kg), but this met the national standard limit requirements.

4 Discussion

Based on a foodomics strategy, this study systematically revealed the effects of four extraction methods on the composition and nutrition of peanut oil. Fatty acid analysis showed that supercritical CO₂ extraction had clear advantages in retaining unsaturated fatty acids, which is closely related to its low-temperature, oxygen-free extraction environment. The tunable polarity of supercritical CO₂ gives it high selectivity for nonpolar fatty acids while avoiding high-temperature oxidation. Although cold pressing does not use organic solvents, mechanical shear force during pressing may cause partial destruction of cell structures, release endogenous lipases, and cause slight hydrolysis.

As important lipid-soluble functional components in peanut oil, tocopherols and phytosterols are significantly affected by extraction temperature. The high-temperature roasting of hot pressing (160°C) led to thermal degradation and oxidative polymerization of tocopherols, with a total tocopherol loss rate of 21.5%. Although solvent extraction uses a lower temperature (60°C), the polarity of n-hexane may affect the extraction efficiency of tocopherols. Supercritical CO₂ extraction can efficiently extract tocopherols at 45°C, and the inert environment of CO₂ effectively inhibits oxidation reactions, thus giving the highest retention rate of α-tocopherol.

Metabolomics analysis further revealed the effects of extraction methods on the overall metabolic profile of peanut oil. The enrichment of pyrazine compounds in hot-pressed samples was highly correlated with its unique flavor characteristics. These compounds are generated by the Maillard reaction of amino acids and reducing sugars in peanuts at high temperature. However, the Maillard reaction is also accompanied by the production of potentially harmful substances such as acrylamide, which need to be controlled in process optimization. The metabolite profiles of supercritical CO₂ extraction and cold pressing were similar, but the former had greater advantages in the retention of glycerophospholipids and phytosterols, which may be related to its higher extraction selectivity and efficiency.

From the perspective of nutritional economics, although supercritical CO₂ extraction requires higher equipment investment, it has a high oil yield (98.5%), no solvent residue, and good retention of nutrients, making it suitable for the development of high-end peanut oil products. Cold pressing has a simple process and low cost, making it suitable for small- and medium-scale production of organic cold-pressed peanut oil. Hot pressing has an irreplaceable position in the market for rich-flavored peanut oil, but the roasting temperature and time need to be optimized to balance flavor and nutrition. Solvent extraction has high efficiency and low cost, but solvent residues must be strictly controlled, making it suitable for large-scale peanut oil production.

The limitation of this study is that only a single peanut cultivar was used. In the future, it is necessary to expand cultivar coverage and combine multi-omics approaches such as genomics and proteomics to further analyze the molecular mechanisms of nutrient changes during extraction.

5 Conclusion

This study used foodomics techniques to systematically compare the effects of cold pressing, hot pressing, solvent extraction, and supercritical CO₂ extraction on the composition and nutrition of peanut oil. The main conclusions are as follows: (1) Supercritical CO₂ extraction had the highest retention rate of unsaturated fatty acids (89.6%), and its α-tocopherol content reached 187.3 mg/kg, giving it the best overall nutritional quality; (2) cold pressing performed well in retaining γ-tocopherol and phytosterols and is suitable for the development of high-end nutritional oil; (3) hot pressing produced abundant volatile flavor compounds such as pyrazines and aldehydes (68 types), imparting a unique roasted aroma to peanut oil; (4) metabolomics analysis identified 126 differential metabolites, mainly enriched in unsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis and glycerophospholipid metabolism pathways. The results provide a theoretical basis for the precise processing and quality regulation of peanut oil and also provide a methodological reference for the application of foodomics in the field of edible oil processing.

title: Machine learning models predict coagulopathy in spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage patients in ER
text:
Machine Learning Models for Predicting Coagulopathy in Emergency Patients with Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage

Abstract: Objective: To investigate the predictive value of machine learning models built upon routine clinical and laboratory indicators at emergency admission for coagulopathy in patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH). Methods: Clinical data of sICH patients admitted to the emergency department were retrospectively collected. With coagulopathy as the outcome variable, logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and support vector machine models were constructed, and five-fold cross-validation was used to evaluate model performance. Results: The random forest and XGBoost models demonstrated the best predictive performance, with AUCs of 0.87 and 0.85, respectively, significantly outperforming traditional logistic regression (AUC = 0.76). Key predictive variables included platelet count, international normalized ratio, Glasgow Coma Scale score, and hematoma volume. Conclusion: Machine learning models can effectively utilize routine emergency data to early identify patients at high risk of coagulopathy after sICH, providing support for clinical decision-making.

1 Introduction

Spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH) accounts for 10%–15% of all strokes, yet its mortality and disability rates rank first among all stroke types. Coagulopathy is an independent risk factor for hematoma expansion and poor prognosis in patients with sICH. As the first point of contact for sICH patients, the emergency department's ability to identify coagulation abnormalities within a short time directly affects treatment selection and transfer decisions. However, traditional coagulation function tests are time-consuming, and some patients show no obvious abnormalities in early indicators, making clinical judgment difficult.

In recent years, machine learning techniques have demonstrated promising predictive capabilities in emergency and critical care medicine. Their advantage lies in the ability to simultaneously handle multivariable, nonlinear relationships and to uncover latent patterns from routine data. This study aims to construct machine learning models based on routine clinical and laboratory indicators at emergency admission to predict coagulopathy in sICH patients, and to compare the performance of different models, providing a reference for early identification in the emergency setting.

2 Key Technical Analysis

2.1 Data Source and Variable Selection

The study included sICH patients admitted to the emergency department of a tertiary hospital. Inclusion criteria were: presentation within 24 hours of onset, confirmed by cranial CT, and age ≥18 years. Patients with traumatic hemorrhage, isolated intraventricular hemorrhage, and incomplete data were excluded. Based on the first coagulation function test after admission, coagulopathy was defined as international normalized ratio (INR) >1.4 or activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) >40 seconds or platelet count <100×10⁹/L.

Candidate predictive variables included: demographic characteristics (age, sex), medical history (hypertension, diabetes, liver disease, anticoagulant use), vital signs at admission, Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score, hematoma volume, and laboratory indicators (platelet count, white blood cell count, blood glucose, INR, APTT, etc.). Univariate analysis and LASSO regression were used for variable selection, and 12 predictors were ultimately retained.

2.2 Machine Learning Model Construction

Four models were constructed: logistic regression as the baseline model; random forest, which reduces overfitting by integrating multiple decision trees; XGBoost, which employs a gradient boosting framework to handle class imbalance; and support vector machine, which uses kernel functions to handle nonlinear relationships. Continuous variables were standardized, and categorical variables were one-hot encoded. To address the class imbalance caused by the low incidence of coagulopathy, SMOTE oversampling combined with class weight adjustment was employed.

2.3 Model Evaluation and Validation

Five-fold cross-validation was used to evaluate model stability. The primary evaluation metric was the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), along with sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, and Brier score. SHAP value analysis was used to explain the contribution of each variable to prediction results, enhancing model interpretability. All analyses were performed using Python 3.9 with the scikit-learn and XGBoost libraries.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

A total of 326 sICH patients were included, of whom 78 (23.9%) had coagulopathy. The random forest model performed best, with an AUC of 0.87 (95% CI: 0.82–0.91), sensitivity of 0.81, and specificity of 0.83; the XGBoost model had an AUC of 0.85, and logistic regression had an AUC of 0.76. SHAP analysis showed that platelet count, INR, GCS score, and hematoma volume were the most important predictive variables, with decreased platelet count and elevated INR contributing most to prediction results.

From a clinical benefit perspective, this model can complete risk assessment at the emergency triage stage using only routine laboratory data, without additional testing costs. Taking the random forest model as an example, if the prediction probability threshold is set at 0.35, approximately 80% of patients with coagulopathy can be identified while reducing unnecessary coagulation re-testing by approximately 30%. For high-risk patients, emergency physicians can initiate coagulation correction, adjust anticoagulation strategies, or prioritize ICU monitoring in advance, potentially reducing the risk of hematoma expansion.

Compared with existing clinical scores (such as the ICH score), machine learning models significantly improve predictive accuracy while maintaining interpretability. Furthermore, the model can be embedded into emergency information systems to enable automatic calculation and real-time alerts, demonstrating promising prospects for broader application.

4 Conclusion

Machine learning models constructed based on routine emergency data in this study can effectively predict coagulopathy in sICH patients, with the random forest model demonstrating the best performance. This approach does not increase additional testing burden and is suitable for promotion in the emergency setting. Future efforts should focus on multicenter external validation to further confirm model generalizability, and explore integration into emergency clinical decision support systems to assist early identification and intervention.

title: MiR319-targeted OsTCP21 and OsGAmyb regulate tillering and grain yield in rice
text:
Mechanistic Study of MiR319 Targeting OsTCP21 and OsGAmyb in Regulating Rice Tillering and Yield

 Abstract

【Objective】Tiller number is one of the core agronomic traits determining rice yield. The microRNA319 (miR319) family plays important regulatory roles in plant growth and development, but its downstream target genes and molecular mechanisms in rice tillering regulation remain incompletely understood. This study aims to elucidate the molecular mechanism by which miR319 regulates rice tillering and yield through targeting OsTCP21 and OsGAmyb. 【Methods】Using japonica rice variety Zhonghua 11 as the background, miR319 overexpression (OE-miR319), OsTCP21 knockout (ostcp21), and OsGAmyb knockout (osgamyb) transgenic lines were constructed. Field agronomic trait investigation, tissue section observation, qRT-PCR expression analysis, and dual-luciferase reporter system validation were combined to systematically dissect the function of the miR319-OsTCP21/OsGAmyb regulatory module. 【Results】The tiller number of OE-miR319 lines increased significantly by 42.6% compared with the wild type, and per-plant yield increased by 18.3%; both ostcp21 and osgamyb mutants exhibited increased tillering phenotypes, but the osgamyb mutant showed a significant decrease in grain number per panicle. Expression analysis indicated that both OsTCP21 and OsGAmyb were highly expressed in young tiller buds and were negatively regulated by miR319. The dual-luciferase reporter system confirmed that miR319 can directly cleave the mRNAs of OsTCP21 and OsGAmyb. Further investigation revealed that OsTCP21 negatively regulates tillering by inhibiting the expression of the strigolactone biosynthesis gene D10, while OsGAmyb regulates grain number per panicle by affecting the expression of the cytokinin oxidase gene OsCKX2. 【Conclusion】miR319 coordinately targets OsTCP21 and OsGAmyb to regulate rice tillering and grain number per panicle through the strigolactone and cytokinin pathways, respectively, ultimately affecting yield. This regulatory module provides important targets for molecular breeding of high-yield rice.

 Keywords

Rice; miR319; OsTCP21; OsGAmyb; Tillering; Yield; Strigolactone; Cytokinin

 1 Introduction

Rice (*Oryza sativa* L.) is one of the most important food crops worldwide, and its yield is directly related to food security. Tiller number is an important component factor of rice yield. A reasonable tiller number can optimize population structure, improve light use efficiency, and thereby increase yield per unit area. Therefore, dissecting the molecular regulatory network of rice tillering has important theoretical significance and application value.

MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are a class of endogenous non-coding small RNAs approximately 20–24 nt in length that play key regulatory roles in plant organ development, hormone signal transduction, and stress responses by cleaving or inhibiting the translation of target gene mRNAs. miR319 is a highly conserved miRNA family in plants, and previous studies have shown that it regulates leaf development and senescence by targeting TCP transcription factor family members. However, the function of miR319 in rice tillering regulation and its downstream target gene network remain unclear.

The TCP transcription factor family is a class of plant-specific transcriptional regulators involved in the regulation of cell proliferation and differentiation. OsTCP21 is a member of the rice TCP family, and preliminary transcriptome data showed that it is highly expressed in tiller buds, but its specific function in tillering regulation has not been reported. OsGAmyb is a member of the MYB transcription factor family and is known to participate in the gibberellin signaling pathway, but its relationship with tillering and yield traits remains unclear.

In this study, through a combination of genetics, molecular biology, and agronomy, the function of the miR319-OsTCP21/OsGAmyb regulatory module in rice tillering and yield formation was systematically investigated, aiming to reveal its molecular mechanism and provide a theoretical basis for high-yield rice breeding.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Plant Materials and Field Trials

The japonica rice variety Zhonghua 11 (ZH11) was used as the wild-type control. OE-miR319 overexpression lines were constructed via Agrobacterium-mediated transformation; ostcp21 and osgamyb knockout mutants were constructed using CRISPR/Cas9 technology. All materials were planted at the Experimental Farm of Nanjing Agricultural University using a randomized complete block design with 3 replications, 30 plants per plot, with a row spacing of 25 cm and a plant spacing of 20 cm, under conventional water and fertilizer management. Agronomic traits including tiller number, grain number per panicle, seed setting rate, and per-plant yield were investigated at maturity.

 2.2 Expression Analysis

Tiller buds at the seedling stage, young panicles, leaves, stems, and root tissues of wild-type rice were collected separately. Total RNA was extracted using the Trizol method and reverse-transcribed into cDNA. SYBR Green real-time quantitative PCR (qRT-PCR) was used to detect the tissue expression patterns of OsTCP21 and OsGAmyb. OsUBQ was used as the internal reference gene, and the 2^-ΔΔCt method was used to calculate relative expression levels. Small RNA expression detection used stem-loop reverse transcription primers.

 2.3 Dual-Luciferase Reporter System

The 3'UTR fragments of OsTCP21 and OsGAmyb were cloned into the psicheck2 vector to construct reporter plasmids. The miR319 precursor sequence was cloned into the pCAMBIA1300 vector as the effector plasmid. Tobacco leaf protoplasts were co-transformed and cultured in the dark for 24 h, after which the ratio of firefly luciferase to Renilla luciferase activity was measured.

 2.4 Tissue Sectioning and Hormone Content Determination

Tiller bud tissues at the seedling stage were collected, fixed in FAA, paraffin-sectioned, stained with toluidine blue, and observed under a light microscope for cell morphology. ELISA was used to determine the contents of strigolactone (SL) and cytokinin (CTK) in tiller buds.

 2.5 Statistical Analysis

Data are presented as mean ± standard deviation. One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) was performed using SPSS 22.0, and Duncan's multiple range test was used to test the significance of differences (P<0.05).

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 miR319 Overexpression Promotes Rice Tillering and Yield

Field trait investigation showed that the tiller number of OE-miR319 lines increased significantly by 42.6% compared with the wild type (P<0.01), and per-plant yield increased by 18.3% (P<0.05), while plant height, 1000-grain weight, and seed setting rate showed no significant differences (Table 1). At maturity, the number of effective panicles of OE-miR319 lines increased significantly, indicating that miR319 positively regulates rice tillering.

 3.2 OsTCP21 and OsGAmyb Are Direct Target Genes of miR319

Bioinformatics prediction indicated that the 3'UTRs of both OsTCP21 and OsGAmyb contain potential binding sites for miR319. Dual-luciferase reporter system results showed that after co-expression of miR319, the luciferase activity of reporter plasmids carrying the OsTCP21 or OsGAmyb 3'UTR decreased by 63.2% and 58.7%, respectively (P<0.01), while the activity was restored after mutation of the binding sites, confirming that miR319 can directly target and cleave the mRNAs of these two genes. qRT-PCR analysis showed that the expression levels of OsTCP21 and OsGAmyb in OE-miR319 lines decreased by 71.4% and 66.8%, respectively, compared with the wild type.

 3.3 Functional Validation of OsTCP21 and OsGAmyb in Regulating Tillering

The tiller number of ostcp21 mutants increased by 35.2% compared with the wild type (P<0.01), consistent with the OE-miR319 phenotype; the tiller number of osgamyb mutants increased by 28.7% (P<0.05), but grain number per panicle decreased significantly by 22.4% (P<0.01), resulting in no significant increase in per-plant yield. Tissue section observation showed that the actively dividing cell regions in tiller buds of ostcp21 and osgamyb mutants were expanded, with increased cell numbers.

 3.4 Hormone Pathway Analysis

ELISA results showed that the strigolactone content in tiller buds of ostcp21 mutants decreased by 46.3% compared with the wild type (P<0.01), while the expression level of the D10 gene (a key gene for SL biosynthesis) decreased by 58.9%. Yeast two-hybrid and gel shift assays confirmed that OsTCP21 can directly bind to the TCP binding element in the D10 promoter region. In osgamyb mutants, cytokinin content increased by 32.1% (P<0.05), and OsCKX2 expression decreased by 44.7%, indicating that OsGAmyb reduces CTK levels by activating OsCKX2 expression, thereby affecting grain number per panicle.

 3.5 Regulatory Model

Based on the above results, miR319 negatively regulates OsTCP21, relieving its inhibition of D10, promoting SL synthesis and thereby inhibiting tillering; meanwhile, miR319 targets OsGAmyb, reducing OsCKX2 expression, increasing CTK levels, and coordinately promoting tiller bud elongation. However, excessive inhibition of OsGAmyb reduces grain number per panicle, indicating that this module maintains a fine balance between tillering and grain number per panicle.

 4 Discussion

This study reveals for the first time the molecular mechanism by which miR319 regulates rice tillering and yield through coordinately targeting OsTCP21 and OsGAmyb. Consistent with previous studies in Arabidopsis, the miR319-TCP module has conserved functions in plant organ development. This study found that OsTCP21 negatively regulates tillering through the SL pathway, expanding the understanding of TCP transcription factor functions in hormone signal crosstalk.

It is noteworthy that although the osgamyb mutant showed increased tillering, the decrease in grain number per panicle resulted in no significant yield improvement, suggesting that fine regulation of OsGAmyb expression levels is needed in breeding applications. In contrast, the ostcp21 mutant and OE-miR319 lines increased tillering without sacrificing grain number per panicle, possessing higher breeding application value.

The dual-pathway regulatory model of "miR319-OsTCP21-D10-SL" and "miR319-OsGAmyb-OsCKX2-CTK" constructed in this study provides a new perspective for understanding the molecular regulatory network of rice tillering. In the future, precise editing of miR319 target sites or the use of tissue-specific promoters to regulate target gene expression could achieve coordinated optimization of tillering and grain number per panicle, providing new strategies for high-yield rice breeding.

 5 Conclusion

(1) miR319 overexpression significantly promotes rice tillering and increases per-plant yield by 18.3%. (2) OsTCP21 and OsGAmyb are direct target genes of miR319 and are negatively regulated by it. (3) OsTCP21 negatively regulates tillering by inhibiting D10 expression, and OsGAmyb affects grain number per panicle by activating OsCKX2. (4) The miR319-OsTCP21/OsGAmyb module coordinately regulates rice tillering and yield through the dual hormone pathways of SL and CTK, providing important targets for high-yield molecular breeding.

title: "Gut-skin"axis: understanding psoriasis from the gut
text:
"The Gut-Skin" Axis: Understanding Psoriasis from the Gut

Abstract: Psoriasis is a common chronic inflammatory skin disease, and traditional treatments mostly focus on the local skin. In recent years, studies have found that gut microbiota dysbiosis and impaired intestinal barrier function are closely related to the occurrence and development of psoriasis, thus giving rise to the concept of the "gut-skin" axis. This article reviews the key technical analyses of the "gut-skin" axis, including gut microbiota sequencing, metabolite detection, intestinal permeability assessment, and intervention approaches, and analyzes the therapeutic benefits based on this axis. The results indicate that regulating the gut microecology can significantly improve psoriasis symptoms, providing new ideas for clinical promotion.

Introduction: The global prevalence of psoriasis is approximately 2%-3%, manifesting as erythema, scaling, and systemic inflammation. It is traditionally believed to be triggered jointly by genetics, immunity, and environment, but increasing evidence shows that gut health status directly affects skin inflammation. For example, patients with psoriasis often have comorbid inflammatory bowel disease, and antibiotic treatment can induce or aggravate skin lesions. These phenomena suggest that a bidirectional communication network exists between the gut and the skin, namely the "gut-skin" axis. Understanding this axis helps develop safer and more economical therapies suitable for promotion.

Key Technical Analysis

1. Analysis of Gut Microbiota Composition
Through 16S rRNA high-throughput sequencing or metagenomic sequencing, the differences in fecal microbiota between patients with psoriasis and healthy populations can be compared. Studies have found that in the gut of patients, Prevotella and Akkermansia are reduced, while Enterobacteriaceae and Streptococcus are increased. Microbiota dysbiosis leads to insufficient production of short-chain fatty acids (such as butyrate), weakening regulatory T cell function, thereby exacerbating skin Th17 inflammation. The cost of this technology has dropped to the thousand-yuan level, making it suitable for grassroots promotion.

2. Detection of Intestinal Barrier Function
Serum zonulin, lipopolysaccharide (LPS), and intestinal fatty acid-binding protein (I-FABP) are used as markers, combined with the urine lactulose/mannitol ratio, to assess intestinal permeability. Patients with psoriasis often have a "leaky gut" phenomenon, in which endotoxins enter the blood, activate immune cells, and migrate to the skin. The detection methods are non-invasive and repeatable, facilitating dynamic monitoring of therapeutic efficacy.

3. Analysis of Metabolites and Immune Pathways
Targeted metabolomics can detect short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, and tryptophan metabolites. Butyrate downregulates the NF-κB pathway through histone deacetylase inhibition; indole derivatives activate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor and promote IL-22 secretion, which may instead aggravate skin lesions. Therefore, the metabolite profile needs to be balanced. This technology requires mass spectrometry equipment, but it can be standardized for promotion.

4. Intervention Approaches: Probiotics, Fecal Microbiota Transplantation, and Diet
Probiotics (such as Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus) can restore microbiota balance and reduce PASI scores. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) has shown complete resolution of skin lesions in individual cases, but donors need to be strictly screened. In terms of diet, a high-fiber, low-fat diet increases butyrate production, while alcohol and spicy foods damage the barrier. These interventions are low-cost and easy to promote.

5. Animal Models and Causal Verification
Using the imiquimod-induced mouse psoriasis model, combined with germ-free mice or antibiotic-treated mice, the causal relationship between gut microbiota and skin inflammation can be verified. For example, transplanting patient microbiota into germ-free mice can induce skin lesions. This technology provides support for mechanistic research, but promotion requires simplification.

Results and Benefit Analysis

Interventions based on the "gut-skin" axis have achieved positive results in multiple clinical studies. A randomized controlled trial showed that after 12 weeks of oral probiotics, the PASI50 response rate in patients with psoriasis reached 60%, significantly higher than 35% in the placebo group. Another FMT study reported that in 2 of 3 patients, skin lesions resolved by more than 75%, with no serious adverse reactions. In terms of benefits: first, it reduces the use of topical corticosteroids and immunosuppressants, lowering hepatorenal toxicity; second, through self-management with diet and probiotics, patient adherence is high; third, early regulation of the gut can prevent psoriasis comorbidities (such as metabolic syndrome). Economic analysis shows that the annual cost of probiotics combined with dietary guidance is about 1/20 that of biologics, making it suitable for grassroots promotion. However, it should be noted that individual microbiota differences are large, and rapid detection kits need to be developed to guide precise intervention.

Conclusion

The "gut-skin" axis provides a new perspective for psoriasis by starting from the gut. Through microbiota sequencing, barrier detection, metabolite analysis, and probiotic/FMT intervention, skin lesions can be safely and effectively improved. In the future, standardized protocols need to be established, multicenter validation carried out, and community screening promoted. Promoting this technology is expected to reduce the medical burden and achieve the inclusive goal of "treating the skin from the gut."

title: The effects of tea plants-soybean intercropping on the secondary metabolites of tea plants by metabolomics analysis
text:
Metabolomic Analysis of the Effects of Tea Tree–Soybean Intercropping on Tea Tree Secondary Metabolites

 Abstract

To investigate the effects of the tea tree–soybean intercropping model on tea tree secondary metabolites, this study used the Longjing 43 tea cultivar as material, set up two treatments of tea tree monoculture and tea tree–soybean intercropping, and employed ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography–quadrupole–electrostatic field orbitrap high-resolution mass spectrometry (UPLC-Q-Exactive Orbitrap MS) combined with an untargeted metabolomics approach to perform qualitative and quantitative analysis of metabolites in tea tree new shoots. The results showed that a total of 78 differential metabolites were screened out under the intercropping treatment, including 32 flavonoids, 14 phenolic acids, 8 alkaloids, 12 amino acids, 7 terpenoids, and 5 other compounds. Compared with monoculture, the contents of epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), epicatechin gallate (ECG), and gallic acid in tea tree new shoots under intercropping were significantly increased by 18.6%, 15.3%, and 22.4%, respectively (P<0.05), while caffeine content decreased by 9.2%. KEGG pathway enrichment analysis showed that the differential metabolites were mainly enriched in pathways such as flavonoid biosynthesis, phenylpropanoid metabolism, and amino acid biosynthesis. This study revealed that tea tree–soybean intercropping can promote the accumulation of flavonoid secondary metabolites in tea trees, providing a theoretical basis for the optimization of tea garden intercropping models and the improvement of tea quality.

Keywords: tea tree; soybean; intercropping; secondary metabolites; metabolomics; flavonoids

 1 Introduction

Tea tree (*Camellia sinensis* (L.) O. Kuntze) is an important economic crop in China, and the secondary metabolites in its fresh leaves, especially tea polyphenols, alkaloids, amino acids, and other components, directly determine the quality and health-promoting functions of tea. In recent years, with the continuous improvement of people's requirements for tea quality, how to regulate the accumulation of tea tree secondary metabolites through agronomic measures has become a research hotspot.

Intercropping is a traditional sustainable agricultural planting model. Through niche complementarity and efficient resource utilization among different crops, it can improve the field microenvironment, increase soil fertility, and affect crop metabolic processes. Soybean (*Glycine max* (L.) Merr.), as a leguminous plant, has biological nitrogen fixation capacity, can increase soil nitrogen content, and its root exudates may also exert allelopathic effects on neighboring plants. Previous studies have shown that intercropping tea trees with soybean can improve the ecological environment of tea gardens and increase tea yield and quality, but its systematic effects on tea tree secondary metabolites remain unclear.

Metabolomics technology can comprehensively and high-throughput detect small-molecule metabolites in organisms, providing a powerful tool for elucidating the effects of intercropping on the tea tree metabolic network. This study used an untargeted metabolomics approach to systematically analyze changes in metabolites in tea tree new shoots under the tea tree–soybean intercropping model, aiming to reveal the effects of intercropping on the accumulation of tea tree secondary metabolites and their metabolic regulatory mechanisms, and to provide theoretical support for the scientific application of tea garden intercropping models.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Experimental Site and Design

The experiment was conducted from March to October 2022 in a tea garden in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province. The tea cultivar tested was Longjing 43 (5 years old), and the soybean cultivar was Zhechun No. 3. Two treatments were set up: (1) tea tree monoculture (CK), with conventional management; (2) tea tree–soybean intercropping (TS), with soybean planted between tea rows at a row spacing of 40 cm and a plant spacing of 20 cm. Each treatment had 3 replicate plots, each with an area of 30 m², arranged in a randomized block design. Soybean was sown in late March, and after harvest in mid-July, the straw was returned to the field.

 2.2 Sample Collection and Processing

In mid-September 2022 (autumn tea season), one bud and two leaves of tea tree new shoots were collected. Five points were collected from each plot and mixed into one sample, quickly frozen in liquid nitrogen, and stored at -80°C for later use.

 2.3 Metabolite Extraction and Detection

A 100 mg portion of frozen ground tea sample was weighed, 1 mL of pre-cooled methanol/water (80:20, v/v) solution was added, ultrasonic extraction was performed for 30 min, and centrifugation was carried out (12000 rpm, 4°C) for 15 min. The supernatant was filtered through a 0.22 μm membrane and then analyzed. A UPLC-Q-Exactive Orbitrap MS system (Thermo Fisher Scientific, USA) was used, with an ACQUITY UPLC HSS T3 column (2.1×100 mm, 1.8 μm). Mobile phase A was 0.1% formic acid aqueous solution, and B was acetonitrile. The gradient elution program was: 0-2 min, 5% B; 2-10 min, 5%-95% B; 10-12 min, 95% B; 12-12.1 min, 95%-5% B; 12.1-15 min, 5% B. The flow rate was 0.3 mL/min, the column temperature was 40°C, and the injection volume was 2 μL. Mass spectrometry used positive and negative ion full-scan mode, with a scan range of m/z 100-1500.

 2.4 Data Processing and Statistical Analysis

Raw data were subjected to peak extraction, alignment, and annotation using Compound Discoverer 3.1 software. MetaboAnalyst 5.0 was used for principal component analysis (PCA) and orthogonal partial least squares discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA), and differential metabolites were screened based on VIP>1 and P<0.05. KEGG pathway enrichment analysis was performed using the hypergeometric test.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Quality Assessment of Metabolomics Data

QC samples clustered tightly in the PCA score plot, indicating good instrument stability. A total of 1246 metabolic features were detected, including 786 in positive ion mode and 460 in negative ion mode. The OPLS-DA model showed clear separation of metabolic profiles between the CK and TS groups (R²Y=0.976, Q²=0.912), indicating that intercropping significantly changed the metabolite composition of tea tree new shoots.

 3.2 Screening of Differential Metabolites

Using VIP>1 and P<0.05 as criteria, a total of 78 differential metabolites were screened out. Among them, after intercropping treatment, the contents of 42 metabolites were significantly upregulated and 36 were significantly downregulated. The differential metabolites mainly included 32 flavonoids (41.0%), 14 phenolic acids (17.9%), 12 amino acids (15.4%), 8 alkaloids (10.3%), 7 terpenoids (9.0%), and 5 others (6.4%).

 3.3 Changes in Key Secondary Metabolites

Among flavonoids, catechin components showed the most significant changes. Compared with monoculture, the contents of EGCG, ECG, and gallic acid in tea tree new shoots under intercropping increased by 18.6%, 15.3%, and 22.4%, respectively (P<0.05); the contents of epigallocatechin (EGC) and epicatechin (EC) increased by 12.7% and 9.8%, respectively. In addition, the contents of quercetin-3-O-glucoside and kaempferol-3-O-rutinoside increased by 25.3% and 19.7%, respectively.

Among phenolic acid compounds, the contents of chlorogenic acid and caffeic acid increased by 16.8% and 13.5%, respectively, while salicylic acid content decreased by 11.2%. Among alkaloids, caffeine content decreased by 9.2%, while theobromine content showed no significant change. Among amino acids, theanine content increased by 14.6%, and glutamic acid and aspartic acid contents increased by 11.3% and 8.9%, respectively.

 3.4 Enrichment Analysis of Metabolic Pathways

KEGG pathway enrichment analysis showed that the differential metabolites were significantly enriched in 8 metabolic pathways (P<0.05), mainly including flavonoid biosynthesis (ko00941), phenylpropanoid biosynthesis (ko00940), amino acid biosynthesis (ko01230), arginine and proline metabolism (ko00330), purine metabolism (ko00230), etc. Among them, the flavonoid biosynthesis pathway had the highest degree of enrichment (Rich factor=0.42), involving metabolite changes corresponding to key enzyme genes such as PAL, C4H, 4CL, CHS, CHI, F3H, DFR, LAR, and ANR.

 4 Discussion

Through metabolomics analysis, this study found that tea tree–soybean intercropping significantly promoted the accumulation of flavonoids in tea tree new shoots, especially ester-type catechins (EGCG, ECG) and gallic acid. This result is closely related to changes in light conditions and regulation of nitrogen nutrition in the intercropping system. After soybean straw was returned to the field, soil organic matter and nitrogen content increased. Moderate nitrogen supply can promote the activities of key enzymes such as PAL and C4H in the phenylpropanoid metabolic pathway, thereby promoting the synthesis of flavonoids. At the same time, shading of light by the soybean canopy changed the light quality and light intensity of the tea tree canopy, and moderate shading can induce the expression of flavonoid biosynthesis genes in tea trees.

It is worth noting that intercropping treatment reduced caffeine content. Caffeine and catechins share precursor substances in tea tree nitrogen metabolism (such as glycine, aspartic acid, etc.). Under intercropping conditions, the allocation of nitrogen metabolism to the polyphenol pathway increased, which may lead to a relative reduction in the supply of substrates for caffeine synthesis in the purine metabolic pathway. In addition, the increase in theanine content indicates that intercropping is beneficial to nitrogen assimilation in tea trees, which is related to the increase in soil available nitrogen content caused by biological nitrogen fixation by soybean.

Changes in phenolic acid compounds reflected adjustments in tea tree defense metabolism in the intercropping system. Increases in chlorogenic acid and caffeic acid contents may enhance the antioxidant capacity of tea trees, while the decrease in salicylic acid content suggests that the degree of biotic stress suffered by tea trees under intercropping conditions was somewhat reduced. These changes together constitute a systematic response of the secondary metabolic network of tea trees under intercropping.

From the perspective of production application, tea tree–soybean intercropping can not only improve land utilization in tea gardens, but also improve tea quality by regulating the composition of secondary metabolites. An increase in ester-type catechin content is beneficial for enhancing the taste intensity and antioxidant activity of tea infusion, while a moderate decrease in caffeine content can reduce the bitterness of tea infusion and make the taste more mellow.

 5 Conclusion

This study used an untargeted metabolomics approach to systematically reveal the effects of tea tree–soybean intercropping on secondary metabolites in tea tree new shoots. The main conclusions are as follows: (1) intercropping treatment significantly changed the metabolic profile of tea tree new shoots, and a total of 78 differential metabolites were identified; (2) intercropping promoted the accumulation of flavonoids (especially ester-type catechins) and some phenolic acids and amino acids, while reducing caffeine content; (3) differential metabolites were mainly enriched in flavonoid biosynthesis, phenylpropanoid metabolism, and amino acid biosynthesis pathways. The results provide scientific evidence at the metabolic level for the quality effects of tea garden intercropping models, and it is recommended to promote the application of tea tree–soybean intercropping in suitable tea regions to improve tea quality.

 References

[1] Wan Xiaochun. Tea Biochemistry [M]. Beijing: China Agriculture Press, 2003.

[2] Zhang Zhengzhu, Li Daxiang, Xia Tao. Research progress on the application of metabolomics in tea research [J]. Journal of Tea Science, 2018, 38(2): 111-120.

[3] Wang Mengxin, Han Shanjie, Pan Cheng, et al. Research progress on the effects of intercropping on tea tree growth and tea quality [J]. Chinese Journal of Applied Ecology, 2020, 31(6): 2103-2112.

[4] Liu Yang, Li Xin, Zhang Li, et al. Effects of soybean intercropping on soil nutrients and tea quality in tea gardens [J]. Chinese Journal of Eco-Agriculture, 2021, 29(8): 1385-1394.

[5] Daglia M, Di Lorenzo A, Nabavi SF, et al. Polyphenols: a nutraceutical approach to diabetes mellitus[J]. Trends in Food Science & Technology, 2017, 69: 224-234.

[6] Fang K, Xia Z, Li H, et al. Metabolomics reveals the response of tea plant to shading stress[J]. Food Chemistry, 2022, 373: 131456.

[7] Chen Lin, Zhang Yinggen, Chen Jian, et al. Effects of tea tree intercropping models on tea garden ecology and tea quality [J]. Fujian Journal of Agricultural Sciences, 2019, 34(10): 1176-1183.

title: The complete mitochondrial genome of the stick tea thrips Dendrothrips minowai (Thysanoptera: Thripidae)
text:
Complete Mitochondrial Genome Sequencing and Analysis of Dendrothrips minowai

Abstract: Dendrothrips minowai is one of the important pests damaging tea plants. In this study, high-throughput sequencing technology was used to determine the complete mitochondrial genome sequence of Dendrothrips minowai for the first time. The genome is 15,286 bp in length, containing 13 protein-coding genes, 22 tRNA genes, 2 rRNA genes, and one control region. The A+T content of the whole genome is 76.8%, showing an obvious AT bias. Phylogenetic analysis showed that Dendrothrips minowai clustered with other species of Thripidae, supporting its taxonomic status. This study provides basic data for molecular identification, population genetic structure analysis, and control strategy development of Dendrothrips minowai.

Introduction

Dendrothrips minowai (*Dendrothrips minowai*) belongs to Thysanoptera, Thripidae, and is a small pest commonly occurring in tea-growing areas of China. Its adults and nymphs mainly inhabit the underside of tender tea leaves, feeding on mesophyll sap through piercing-sucking mouthparts, causing silvery-white spots on leaves. In severe cases, leaves curl and scorch, affecting tea yield and quality. In recent years, with increased tea garden planting density and changing climatic conditions, the occurrence range of Dendrothrips minowai has continued to expand, causing varying degrees of damage in major tea-producing areas such as Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, and Yunnan.

Currently, the control of Dendrothrips minowai still relies mainly on chemical pesticides, but long-term use has led to problems such as increased resistance, damage to natural enemies, and excessive pesticide residues. Therefore, there is an urgent need to develop precise monitoring and green control methods based on molecular technology. The mitochondrial genome, due to its maternal inheritance, moderate evolutionary rate, and conserved structure, has been widely used in insect phylogenetics, population genetic diversity, and molecular diagnostics research. However, research on the mitochondrial genome of Dendrothrips minowai has not yet been reported. This study aims to determine and analyze the complete mitochondrial genome sequence of Dendrothrips minowai, providing a foundation for its molecular identification and phylogenetic research.

Key Technical Analysis

1. Sample Collection and DNA Extraction

Dendrothrips minowai samples were collected in July 2023 from a tea garden in Anxi County, Fujian Province. The collection method was as follows: adult thrips were gently swept from the underside of tender tea leaves using a soft brush and immediately preserved in 95% ethanol. After morphological identification as Dendrothrips minowai, 30 adults were mixed for genomic DNA extraction. Extraction was performed using a column-based insect DNA extraction kit according to the manufacturer's instructions. The final DNA was dissolved in 50 μL TE buffer and stored at -20°C for future use.

2. High-Throughput Sequencing and Assembly

Paired-end 150 bp sequencing was performed on the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform, with a 350 bp insert fragment library constructed. After quality control of raw data using FastQC, Trimmomatic was used to remove adapters and low-quality bases. Using the mitochondrial genome of a closely related thrips species as the reference sequence, clean reads were aligned to the reference sequence using BWA software, and the aligned reads were extracted for de novo assembly. Assembly was performed using SPAdes software with default parameters. The assembly results were verified by PCR amplification and Sanger sequencing to ensure sequence accuracy.

3. Gene Annotation and Sequence Analysis

The assembled mitochondrial genome was preliminarily annotated using the MITOS online tool to predict the positions and boundaries of protein-coding genes, tRNAs, and rRNA genes. The start and stop codons of protein-coding genes were confirmed using ORF Finder. The secondary structure of tRNA genes was predicted using tRNAscan-SE software. The control region was determined by aligning with closely related species sequences. Nucleotide composition analysis was performed using MEGA 11 software to calculate A, T, G, C content and AT bias. Codon usage frequency was analyzed using CodonW software.

4. Phylogenetic Analysis

Mitochondrial genome sequences of Thripidae and other Thysanoptera insects were downloaded from NCBI, with a total of 12 species selected as outgroups and ingroups. The 13 protein-coding genes were aligned using MAFFT software, and ambiguous sites outside conserved regions were removed. Phylogenetic trees were constructed using maximum likelihood (ML) and Bayesian inference (BI) methods. ML analysis was performed using RAxML software with 1000 bootstrap replicates; BI analysis was performed using MrBayes software, running 1×10⁶ generations, sampling every 1000 generations, and discarding the first 25% as burn-in. The final tree was visualized using FigTree.

Results and Benefit Analysis

1. Mitochondrial Genome Structure

The complete mitochondrial genome of Dendrothrips minowai is 15,286 bp in length, exhibiting a typical circular structure. The whole genome contains 37 genes, including 13 protein-coding genes (*cox1*, *cox2*, *cox3*, *atp6*, *atp8*, *nad1*, *nad2*, *nad3*, *nad4*, *nad4L*, *nad5*, *nad6*, *cob*), 22 tRNA genes, 2 rRNA genes (*rrnL* and *rrnS*), and a control region of 1,024 bp. The gene arrangement order is consistent with typical insect mitochondrial genomes such as Drosophila, and no gene rearrangement was found.

2. Base Composition and Codon Usage

The A+T content of the whole genome is 76.8%, showing an obvious AT bias. The A+T content of protein-coding genes is 75.4%, with the highest A+T content at the third codon position (84.2%). Codon usage analysis showed that Dendrothrips minowai prefers codons ending in A or T, such as UUU (phenylalanine), AUU (isoleucine), and UUA (leucine). This preference is related to the high AT content in the mitochondrial genome.

3. Phylogenetic Relationships

The phylogenetic tree constructed based on 13 protein-coding genes showed that Dendrothrips minowai clustered with other species of Thripidae (such as *Thrips palmi* and *Frankliniella occidentalis*), supporting its belonging to Thripidae. This result is consistent with morphological classification. Interspecific genetic distance analysis showed that the cox1 gene sequence divergence between Dendrothrips minowai and closely related species was 12.3%–15.6%, indicating that the mitochondrial genome can serve as an effective marker for molecular identification.

4. Application Benefits

The complete mitochondrial genome sequence of Dendrothrips minowai obtained in this study provides a foundation for developing specific molecular markers (such as cox1 barcodes). These markers can be used for:
(1) Rapid molecular identification of Dendrothrips minowai, especially for morphologically similar nymphs and eggs;
(2) Research on genetic diversity and genetic differentiation of thrips populations in tea gardens;
(3) Evolutionary analysis of genes related to pesticide resistance;
(4) Phylogenetic and biogeographic research based on mitochondrial genes.
From a promotion perspective, this achievement helps grassroots agricultural technicians use molecular tools for early monitoring, reduce blind pesticide application, lower control costs, and enhance the level of green control in tea gardens.

Conclusion

This study determined the complete mitochondrial genome sequence of Dendrothrips minowai for the first time, which has a conserved structure, high AT content, and typical gene arrangement. Phylogenetic analysis supports its taxonomic status and reveals genetic distances from closely related species. This genome data provides an important foundation for molecular identification, population genetics, and control technology development of Dendrothrips minowai. Subsequent research can develop simple PCR detection methods based on this to promote the practical application of molecular technology in tea garden pest management.

title: Comprehensive evaluation on water resource carrying capacity in karst areas using cloud model with combination weighting method: a case study of Guiyang, southwest China
text:
Comprehensive Evaluation of Water Resource Carrying Capacity in Karst Areas Based on a Combination Weighting Cloud Model: A Case Study of Guiyang City, Southwest China

Abstract: Water resource carrying capacity is an important factor constraining the sustainable socioeconomic development of karst areas. To scientifically assess the water resource carrying status in karst areas, this paper takes Guiyang City, a typical karst city in Southwest China, as a case study. An evaluation index system is constructed from three dimensions: water resource endowment, socioeconomic pressure, and ecological environment response. The analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and the entropy weight method are combined for weighting, and a cloud model is integrated to quantify the uncertainty of evaluation grades. The results show that from 2018 to 2023, the comprehensive cloud membership degree of water resource carrying capacity in Guiyang City gradually shifted from "critical overload" to "mild carrying," with the comprehensive score rising from 0.482 to 0.631. Among the dimensions, water resource endowment improved most significantly, with a contribution rate of 46.3%, while the socioeconomic pressure dimension remained in an "overload" state, with water consumption per 10,000 yuan of GDP and urbanization rate being the main limiting factors. This study can provide methodological references for refined water resource management and agricultural irrigation optimization in karst areas.

Keywords: water resource carrying capacity; karst; cloud model; combination weighting; Guiyang City; sustainable development

1 Introduction

Water resource carrying capacity refers to the maximum scale at which a regional water resource system can sustainably support the healthy development of population, economy, and ecosystems under a certain level of technological, economic, and social production conditions. In karst areas, surface water leakage is severe, aquifer structures are complex, and the spatiotemporal distribution of water resources is highly uneven, making carrying capacity evaluation more uncertain than in non-karst areas. Traditional evaluation methods such as fuzzy comprehensive evaluation and principal component analysis struggle to simultaneously address randomness and fuzziness, and their weight determination is highly subjective. The cloud model characterizes the transformation between qualitative concepts and quantitative data through three numerical features—expectation, entropy, and hyper-entropy—making it suitable for problems with fuzzy grade boundaries in carrying capacity. This paper takes Guiyang City as a case study and constructs a combination weighting–cloud model evaluation framework, aiming to provide a scientific basis for water resource regulation and agricultural water security in karst areas.

2 Materials and Methods

2.1 Overview of the Study Area

Guiyang City is located in the eastern part of the Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau, with karst landforms accounting for more than 85% of the city's total area. The average annual precipitation is approximately 1120 mm, but the surface runoff coefficient is only 0.28, with intense karst leakage. The city's permanent population is approximately 6.2 million, the total GDP is approximately 520 billion yuan, and agricultural water use accounts for 18.6% of total water consumption.

2.2 Construction of the Index System

Following the principles of scientific rigor, accessibility, and karst specificity, a three-tier index system is constructed: the target layer (water resource carrying capacity), the criterion layer (water resource endowment B1, socioeconomic pressure B2, ecological environment response B3), and the indicator layer with a total of 12 indicators. B1 includes per capita water resources, water production modulus, groundwater recharge modulus, and runoff coefficient; B2 includes water consumption per 10,000 yuan of GDP, urbanization rate, population density, and water consumption per mu of farmland irrigation; B3 includes ecological water use ratio, sewage treatment rate, rocky desertification control rate, and water quality compliance rate.

2.3 Combination Weighting Method

AHP is used to determine subjective weights by constructing a judgment matrix and passing the consistency test (CR<0.1); the entropy weight method is used to determine objective weights. The combination weight \( w_i \) is calculated as \( w_i = \alpha w_i' + (1-\alpha)w_i'' \), where \( \alpha=0.5 \), balancing expert experience and data dispersion.

2.4 Cloud Model Evaluation Steps

The evaluation grades are set as five levels: Grade I (severe overload), Grade II (overload), Grade III (critical overload), Grade IV (mild carrying), and Grade V (good carrying). Cloud parameters \( Ex \), \( En \), and \( He \) are calculated for each indicator; the combination weights and the cloud membership degrees of each indicator are synthesized into a comprehensive cloud, and a forward cloud generator is used to generate cloud droplets. The grade is determined by the maximum membership degree principle, and ranking is conducted using the comprehensive score \( S=\sum w_i \cdot \mu_i \).

3 Results and Analysis

3.1 Weight Results

After combination weighting, the weights of B1, B2, and B3 are 0.384, 0.342, and 0.274, respectively. At the indicator layer, per capita water resources (0.112), water consumption per 10,000 yuan of GDP (0.098), and rocky desertification control rate (0.086) rank in the top three, reflecting the key role of water resource endowment and ecological governance in karst areas.

3.2 Temporal Evolution of Carrying Capacity

In 2018, the peak comprehensive cloud membership degree was at Grade III (critical overload), with a comprehensive score of 0.482; in 2020, it rose to 0.534, still Grade III; in 2022, it entered Grade IV (mild carrying), with a score of 0.587; in 2023, the score was 0.631, with the peak membership degree stabilizing at Grade IV. This indicates that the water resource carrying capacity of Guiyang City is generally improving, but has not yet reached the good state of Grade V.

3.3 Characteristics of Dimensional Differentiation

The score of the water resource endowment dimension rose from 0.441 to 0.672, the largest improvement, mainly due to the enhancement of the groundwater recharge modulus and the optimization of the runoff coefficient. The score of the socioeconomic pressure dimension decreased from 0.396 to 0.372, remaining at Grade II overload. Although water consumption per 10,000 yuan of GDP decreased from 58 m³ to 41 m³, it is still higher than the national average. The ecological environment response dimension rose from 0.512 to 0.618, with significant contributions from the sewage treatment rate and rocky desertification control rate.

3.4 Spatial Differences

Taking 2023 as an example, the comprehensive scores of Yunyan District and Nanming District are 0.594 and 0.607, respectively, belonging to Grade IV; Huaxi District and Wudang District are 0.638 and 0.651, approaching Grade V; Xiuwen County and Kaiyang County are 0.548 and 0.561, respectively, still at Grade III. The central urban areas are constrained by population density and economic intensity, and their carrying capacity is lower than that of peripheral counties.

4 Discussion

The combination weighting cloud model in this paper effectively reduces the bias of single weighting, and the dispersion of cloud droplets reflects the uncertainty of evaluation in karst areas. The results show that the improvement of water resource carrying capacity in Guiyang City mainly depends on ecological governance and the improvement of water resource endowment, while socioeconomic pressure has not yet been fundamentally alleviated. Regarding agriculture, the weight of water consumption per mu of farmland irrigation is 0.071, and its value decreased from 412 m³/mu in 2018 to 368 m³/mu in 2023, but the canal leakage rate in karst areas still reaches 22%, indicating considerable water-saving potential. In the future, sprinkler and micro-irrigation technologies should be promoted, and the regulation and storage of karst underground reservoirs should be strengthened. In terms of medical/public health relevance, the water quality compliance rate increased to 96.2%, reducing the risk of waterborne infectious diseases. The limitation of this study is that it does not consider climate change scenarios and the impact of inter-regional water transfer. Future research can introduce system dynamics coupled with the cloud model for dynamic simulation.

5 Conclusions

(1) A combination weighting cloud model evaluation system suitable for water resource carrying capacity in karst areas was constructed, balancing subjective and objective information and grade fuzziness. (2) From 2018 to 2023, the water resource carrying capacity of Guiyang City shifted from critical overload to mild carrying, with the comprehensive score increasing by 31.0%, but the socioeconomic pressure dimension remained overloaded. (3) Per capita water resources, water consumption per 10,000 yuan of GDP, and rocky desertification control rate are the core driving factors; the carrying capacity of central urban areas is lower than that of peripheral counties. (4) It is recommended to strengthen agricultural water conservation and karst water regulation and storage, and promote the coordinated optimization of water resources, economy and society, and ecology.

title: Identifying the Biological Characteristics Associated with Oviposition Behavior of Tea Leafhopper Empoasca onukii Matsuda Using the Blue Light Detection Method
text:
Identification of Biological Characteristics Related to the Oviposition Behavior of the Tea Green Leafhopper Using a Blue-Light Detection Method

Abstract: The tea green leafhopper (*Empoasca onukii* Matsuda) is one of the most important pests in tea-growing regions of China. Its oviposition behavior is cryptic, making control difficult. This paper introduces a technique based on a blue-light detection method for identifying biological characteristics related to the oviposition behavior of the tea green leafhopper. This method utilizes the taxis of the tea green leafhopper toward the blue-light band, combined with the fluorescence color reaction of oviposition wounds, to rapidly locate oviposition sites and count the number of eggs laid. By analyzing the relationships between oviposition behavior and temperature, humidity, host tenderness, and photoperiod, key characteristics were identified, including the pest's preference for ovipositing beneath the epidermis of tender stems, an oviposition peak concentrated between 20:00 and 24:00, and an optimal oviposition temperature of 22–28°C. Compared with conventional dissection methods, the blue-light detection method improves efficiency by approximately threefold, causes minimal damage to the insect body and tea shoots, and is suitable for promotion in tea garden forecasting and control practices.

Keywords: tea green leafhopper; blue-light detection; oviposition behavior; biological characteristics; forecasting technology

1 Introduction

The tea green leafhopper (*Empoasca onukii* Matsuda) belongs to the family Cicadellidae in the order Hemiptera. It is a piercing-sucking pest that occurs commonly and causes severe damage in tea-growing regions throughout China. Both adults and nymphs pierce and suck the sap from tender shoots of tea plants, causing scorched margins and curling of buds and leaves. In severe cases, tea garden yields can be reduced by 20%–50%, with particularly prominent impacts on the quality of summer and autumn tea. For a long time, chemical pesticides have been the primary means of controlling this pest. However, due to severe generation overlap, strong adult migratory capacity, and the cryptic nature of oviposition sites, control effectiveness is often unsatisfactory. Clarifying its oviposition behavior and related biological characteristics is fundamental to achieving precise forecasting and green control.

However, observing the oviposition behavior of the tea green leafhopper has long presented technical difficulties. Female adults lay eggs beneath the cortex of tender tea stems or within petiole tissues. The eggs are minute and pale in color, making them difficult to detect with the naked eye. Conventional methods require bringing tea shoots back to the laboratory for segment-by-segment dissection, which is time-consuming and labor-intensive, destroys samples, and is difficult to apply on a large scale in the field. In recent years, optical biological detection technology has provided new approaches for insect behavior research. Studies have found that the tea green leafhopper exhibits a pronounced taxis toward the blue-light band (approximately 450–470 nm), and its oviposition wounds produce a specific fluorescence reaction under blue-light excitation, thereby making oviposition sites visible. Based on this, the present study established and optimized a blue-light detection method and used it to systematically identify biological characteristics related to the oviposition behavior of the tea green leafhopper, aiming to provide technical support for tea garden forecasting and green control.

2 Analysis of Key Technologies

2.1 Blue-Light Detection Device and Operating Methods

The blue-light detection device consists of a portable blue-light source, an optical filter, a magnifying lens, and an image acquisition module. The light source employs an LED array with a wavelength of 450–470 nm and a power of 3–5 W, equipped with a cutoff filter to block reflected blue light and allow only the yellow-green fluorescence emitted from oviposition wounds to pass through. During field operation, tender tea shoots are selected, and the light source is placed close to the shoot surface for illumination, with the stem and petiole areas observed through the magnifying lens. Under blue-light excitation, oviposition wounds appear as distinct yellow-green fluorescent spots, clearly contrasting with surrounding normal tissues. After each spot is confirmed, its position is marked with a marking pen, and the number is recorded. For indoor verification, tea shoots can be cut and placed in a dark box for observation, yielding even better results. A single detection with this method takes approximately 30–60 seconds, causes no mechanical damage to tea shoots, and allows eggs to continue normal incubation, facilitating subsequent tracking and observation.

2.2 Identification of Oviposition Sites and Egg Counts

Using the blue-light detection method, the oviposition sites of the tea green leafhopper can be clearly identified. Observation results indicate that female adults prefer to lay eggs beneath the cortex of tender tea stems, with the second and third internodes being the most concentrated, accounting for more than 65% of total oviposition; the base of petioles ranks second, accounting for approximately 20%; oviposition in the main veins of leaves and tender leaf tissues is relatively rare. Oviposition wounds are mostly single eggs laid separately, with a few occurring as clusters of 2–3 eggs. Each fluorescent spot corresponds to one egg, based on which the number of eggs laid can be accurately counted. Compared with conventional dissection methods, the blue-light detection method achieves an accuracy rate of over 92% in counting egg numbers, with errors mainly arising from a very small number of eggs that exhibit weak fluorescence or are obscured by tea hairs. By regularly detecting the same batch of tea shoots, the developmental progress and hatching time of eggs can also be tracked, providing a basis for predicting nymph occurrence periods.

2.3 Temporal Rhythm of Oviposition Behavior and Responses to Temperature and Humidity

With the blue-light detection method, the oviposition rhythm can be continuously observed without disturbing the insect body. Results indicate that oviposition by female adults of the tea green leafhopper exhibits a distinct circadian rhythm, with the oviposition peak concentrated between 20:00 and 24:00, accounting for approximately 60% of total oviposition; oviposition during the daytime is relatively low, with the lowest occurring between 12:00 and 16:00. Temperature significantly affects oviposition behavior: 22–28°C is the optimal oviposition temperature range, within which the daily oviposition per female can reach 3–5 eggs; below 15°C or above 32°C, oviposition decreases markedly or even ceases. Relative humidity of 75%–85% is optimal; excessively low humidity (<60%) causes egg dehydration and weakens the fluorescence reaction, affecting detection effectiveness. In addition, the photoperiod also affects the initiation time of oviposition; under short-day conditions (12L:12D), the oviposition peak advances by approximately one hour. These characteristics provide important parameters for predicting oviposition peaks and determining optimal control timing.

2.4 Relationship Between Host Tenderness and Oviposition Selection

The tea green leafhopper exhibits pronounced selectivity for host tenderness. Using the blue-light detection method to compare tea shoots of different tenderness levels, it was found that female adults prefer to oviposit on tender shoots at the one-bud-two-leaves to one-bud-three-leaves stage, with the highest oviposition occurring on tender stems whose epidermis has not yet lignified. As tea shoots age and the degree of stem lignification increases, oviposition wounds decrease significantly. Detection data show that the number of eggs laid on one-bud-two-leaves tender shoots is 2.8 times that on one-bud-four-leaves shoots, with virtually no oviposition on old leaf stems. This characteristic is closely related to the growth cycle of new tea shoots and also explains why tender shoots of summer and autumn tea suffer more severe damage. In tea garden forecasting, detection can focus on one-bud-two-leaves to one-bud-three-leaves tender shoots to improve detection efficiency.

2.5 Optimization of the Detection Method and Field Applicability

To improve field applicability, several optimizations were made to the blue-light detection method.
