Although the HRT 48 h group had higher vegetable biomass (172.3 g/plant), fish SGR decreased to 1.08%/d and FCR increased to 1.62, indicating that long-term hypoxic stress inhibited fish growth.

Table 2 Biological growth performance under different HRTs

| HRT (h) | Fish SGR (%/d) | FCR   | Vegetable fresh weight (g/plant) |
|---------|--------------|-------|----------------|
| 12      | 1.21±0.08b   | 1.52±0.06b | 141.7±8.2c |
| 24      | 1.42±0.06a   | 1.38±0.04c | 186.5±7.5a |
| 36      | 1.29±0.07b   | 1.47±0.05b | 178.2±9.1ab |
| 48      | 1.08±0.09c   | 1.62±0.07a | 172.3±8.8b |

 4 Discussion

HRT directly affects the nitrogen transformation pathways and oxygen supply-demand balance of AA systems by regulating water flow velocity and nutrient retention time. In this study, the HRT 24 h group exhibited the optimal TN removal rate and biological growth performance, and the mechanism can be attributed to the following three aspects:

First, HRT 24 h achieved synergistic optimization of nitrifying bacteria and algal growth. A shorter HRT (12 h) caused excessively rapid water flow, preventing the nitrifying bacteria biofilm from fully contacting ammonia nitrogen, resulting in incomplete nitrification and NO₂⁻-N accumulation; while an excessively long HRT (36–48 h) caused excessive accumulation of algal biomass, intensified oxygen consumption through nighttime respiration, inhibited nitrifying bacteria activity, and led to NO₂⁻-N accumulation and decreased TN removal rate. This is consistent with the "HRT threshold effect" found by Zhou et al. (2022) in algal-bacterial granular sludge systems.

Second, the spatiotemporal distribution of DO is a key factor limiting AA system performance. Algal photosynthetic oxygen production has significant diurnal fluctuations, with afternoon surface DO supersaturated (>12 mg/L), while nighttime bottom DO may drop below the suffocation threshold for fish. The HRT 24 h group transported oxygen-rich surface water to the bottom layer through moderate water renewal, alleviating nighttime hypoxia while avoiding algal loss caused by too short an HRT. This result indicates that HRT regulation is an effective strategy for balancing algal oxygen production and fish oxygen consumption.

Third, the coupled distribution of nitrogen and oxygen determines the nutrient utilization efficiency of the system. The NO₃⁻-N concentration in the HRT 24 h group matched the vegetable absorption rate, avoiding the toxicity risk of nitrate accumulation to fish. Although the HRT 48 h group had the highest algal biomass, nighttime hypoxia led to decreased fish SGR, indicating that the optimization of AA systems needs to consider both algal oxygen production potential and fish welfare.

This study has certain limitations: the interactive effects of environmental factors such as temperature and light intensity were not considered, and the experimental period was relatively short. Future research can combine mathematical models to quantify the coupling relationship between HRT and algal-bacterial metabolism, providing more comprehensive theoretical support for precise regulation of AA systems.

 5 Conclusions

(1) HRT significantly affected the nitrogen transformation efficiency of AA systems. At HRT 24 h, the TN removal rate was highest (68.3%) and NO₂⁻-N accumulation was lowest (0.18 mg/L). (2) DO distribution exhibited diurnal fluctuations and vertical stratification. The HRT 24 h group maintained nighttime bottom DO above 2.1 mg/L, meeting fish requirements; the HRT 48 h group had nighttime bottom DO dropping to 1.3 mg/L, causing hypoxic stress. (3) The HRT 24 h group had the optimal fish SGR (1.42%/d) and vegetable fresh weight (186.5 g/plant), indicating that moderate HRT can synergistically enhance nitrogen utilization and biological growth performance. Considering the distribution characteristics of nitrogen and oxygen comprehensively, it is recommended that algal-bacterial symbiotic aquaponics systems adopt a 24 h hydraulic retention time as the optimized operational parameter.

title: RaptorX-Property: a web server for protein structure property prediction
text:
Abstract: Prediction of protein structural properties is of great significance for understanding protein function, guiding drug design, and protein engineering. However, traditional experimental methods for determining these properties are costly and time-consuming. This paper introduces a web-based server, RaptorX-Property, which can efficiently and accurately predict key structural properties of proteins, including secondary structure, solvent accessibility, disordered regions, and disulfide bonds. The server integrates key technologies such as multiple sequence alignment, deep convolutional neural networks, and conditional random fields, and demonstrates superior performance compared with similar methods in multiple benchmark tests. This paper elaborates on the technical principles, system architecture, prediction workflow, and practical application benefits of RaptorX-Property in biomedical research, aiming to provide researchers in related fields with an easy-to-use and high-performance online analysis tool.

Keywords: protein structure prediction; secondary structure; solvent accessibility; disordered regions; web server; deep learning

 1 Introduction

Proteins are the executors of life activities, and their functions are closely related to their three-dimensional structures. Protein structural properties, such as secondary structure (helix, sheet, coil), solvent accessibility (the degree to which each residue is exposed to solvent), intrinsically disordered regions, and disulfide bonds, are important bridges connecting amino acid sequences to three-dimensional spatial structures. Accurately obtaining these properties facilitates protein function annotation, molecular docking, mutation effect analysis, and drug target identification.

Experimental methods such as X-ray crystallography and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy can accurately determine protein structures, but they have low throughput and high cost. With the development of high-throughput sequencing technologies, massive numbers of protein sequences have been obtained, while the number of experimentally resolved structures lags far behind. Therefore, computational methods for predicting protein structural properties have become indispensable complementary approaches. In recent years, deep learning technologies have significantly improved prediction accuracy. RaptorX-Property was developed against this background as an online web server, aiming to provide biologists without programming skills with convenient and high-precision structural property prediction services. This paper introduces the server from the aspects of key technologies, system implementation, and benefit analysis.

 2 Analysis of Key Technologies

 2.1 Multiple Sequence Alignment and Evolutionary Information Extraction

The evolutionary information contained in protein sequences is crucial for structure prediction. RaptorX-Property first uses tools such as HHblits or JackHMMER to construct a multiple sequence alignment (MSA) for the input sequence. Through the MSA, the server can calculate conservation scores, position-specific scoring matrices (PSSMs), and covariance information for each residue position. These features reflect the degree of conservation and interdependence of residues during evolution. Compared with single-sequence input, the evolutionary coupling signals provided by the MSA can significantly improve the accuracy of secondary structure and solvent accessibility prediction. To control computation time, the server filters MSA depth and diversity to ensure high-quality features are obtained within a reasonable time.

 2.2 Joint Model of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks and Conditional Random Fields

The core prediction engine of RaptorX-Property is based on a joint architecture of deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and conditional random fields (CRFs). The CNN part uses one-dimensional convolution kernels that slide along the sequence to automatically extract sequence patterns and evolutionary features within local windows. Multiple convolutional layers and pooling layers are stacked to form hierarchical feature representations capable of capturing short-range to medium-range residue interactions. Subsequently, fully connected layers map the features to the label space of each residue. Considering that protein structural properties exhibit sequence continuity—for example, secondary structures usually appear in segments—the model incorporates a CRF layer on top of the CNN output. The CRF can model dependencies between labels of adjacent residues, thereby outputting a globally optimal label sequence. This hybrid "CNN+CRF" model is optimized end-to-end through backpropagation during training, balancing local feature extraction and global label consistency.

 2.3 Multi-Task Learning and Property Prediction

RaptorX-Property simultaneously predicts three main properties: 3-state secondary structure (helix H, sheet E, coil C), solvent accessibility (expressed as relative accessible surface area, divided into exposed/buried or continuous values), and disordered regions (ordered/disordered). These three properties are correlated: for example, disordered regions often lack stable secondary structure and have higher solvent accessibility. The server adopts a multi-task learning strategy, sharing underlying convolutional features and setting independent output branches and loss functions for each task. Through joint training, the model can leverage complementary information between tasks to improve overall generalization ability. For disulfide bond prediction, the server uses an independent classifier based on paired residue features, combining the local environment and evolutionary conservation of cysteine residues for judgment.

 2.4 Online Service Architecture and User Interaction

RaptorX-Property is deployed on a high-performance computing cluster, with a concise web interface on the front end. Users only need to paste or upload a protein sequence in FASTA format to submit a task. The server backend automatically performs MSA construction, feature extraction, model inference, and result formatting. To improve user experience, the system supports an asynchronous task queue to avoid long waiting times; it also provides task IDs and result page links so that users can check progress or download results at any time. The output results include predicted labels for each residue, confidence scores, and visualization charts (such as secondary structure topology diagrams). The server also provides a RESTful API for batch processing and integration into automated workflows.

 3 Results and Benefit Analysis

On benchmark test sets (such as CASP and CAMEO), the Q3 accuracy of RaptorX-Property for secondary structure prediction can reach over 82%, the MAE (mean absolute error) of solvent accessibility prediction is below 0.15, and the AUC of disordered region prediction exceeds 0.90. Compared with classic servers such as SSpro and JPred, it has clear advantages in most indicators, especially showing robust performance on long sequences and low-homology sequences.

From the perspective of application benefits, the server has served thousands of researchers worldwide. In the field of drug design, predicted solvent accessibility can be used to identify binding pockets; in protein engineering, disordered region prediction helps truncate expression constructs; in structural biology, secondary structure prediction can assist model building. Its features of being free, requiring no registration, and being simple to operate lower the computational threshold, enabling experimental biologists to quickly obtain structural insights. According to incomplete statistics, hundreds of papers based on this server have been published, covering directions such as enzymology, immunology, and synthetic biology.

In addition, RaptorX-Property has high computational efficiency. For a sequence of 300 residues, the time from submission to return of results is usually within 10-20 minutes, far faster than experimental methods. Its modular design also facilitates subsequent upgrades, such as replacing the MSA generation tool with a more advanced one or introducing attention mechanisms.

 4 Conclusion

RaptorX-Property is a comprehensive and high-performance web server for predicting protein structural properties. By integrating multiple sequence alignment, deep convolutional neural networks, conditional random fields, and multi-task learning, it can accurately predict secondary structure, solvent accessibility, disordered regions, and disulfide bonds. Its online service architecture balances usability and computational efficiency, providing experimental and computational biologists with a powerful analysis tool. Future work will focus on extending predicted properties (such as post-translational modification sites), improving applicability to membrane proteins and complexes, and further optimizing the user interaction experience. The continued development of RaptorX-Property will help advance research on protein structure-function relationships.

title: Enhanced-efficiency fertilizers are not a panacea for resolving the nitrogen problem
text:
Enhanced-Efficiency Fertilizers Are Not a Panacea for Solving the Nitrogen Problem

 Abstract

Objective: Enhanced-efficiency fertilizers (EEFs) are widely regarded as an important technological pathway for mitigating agricultural nitrogen losses and improving nitrogen fertilizer use efficiency. However, their actual effectiveness varies significantly across different cropping systems, regional environments, and agro-economic conditions. This paper aims to systematically evaluate the comprehensive efficacy of EEFs in reducing nitrogen losses and increasing crop yields, and to explore their limitations as a solution to the nitrogen problem. Methods: Based on field positioning experiments conducted in major agricultural regions of China (North China Plain, Middle and Lower Yangtze River, Northeast China) from 2018 to 2023, four treatments were established: conventional urea (CU), controlled-release urea (CRU), nitrification-inhibitor urea (NIU), and urease-inhibitor urea (UIU). Crop yield, nitrogen use efficiency (NUE), ammonia volatilization, nitrous oxide emissions, and nitrate leaching were measured, and economic feasibility was assessed through cost-benefit analysis. Results: Compared with CU, CRU, NIU, and UIU increased NUE by 8.3–15.6 percentage points, reduced ammonia volatilization by 18.2%–42.7%, decreased N₂O emissions by 21.5%–38.9%, and reduced nitrate leaching by 12.4%–29.8%, respectively. However, crop yield increases were only 2.1%–6.8%, and in cash crop systems, the incremental revenue was insufficient to offset the increased fertilizer costs. Conclusion: EEFs have clear effects on reducing environmental nitrogen losses, but their yield-enhancing and efficiency-improving capacity is limited and is regulated by soil type, climatic conditions, and cropping systems. They cannot serve as a single strategy for solving agricultural nitrogen problems. It is necessary to integrate optimized nitrogen application rates, cropping structure adjustment, and regional nutrient management policies to construct a comprehensive nitrogen management system.

Keywords: enhanced-efficiency fertilizers; nitrogen use efficiency; ammonia volatilization; nitrous oxide; nitrate leaching; nitrogen management

 1 Introduction

Nitrogen is a key limiting factor for crop growth and development, and nitrogen fertilizer application plays an irreplaceable role in ensuring global food security. However, the problem of excessive nitrogen fertilizer application in China's farmland is prominent, with nitrogen use efficiency in the current season being only 30%–45%. Large amounts of nitrogen are lost through ammonia volatilization, nitrification-denitrification, and leaching, causing a series of environmental problems including air pollution, water eutrophication, and soil acidification (Zhu & Chen, 2002; Gu et al., 2023). It is estimated that agricultural ammonia emissions account for more than 80% of China's total ammonia emissions, and farmland N₂O emissions account for approximately 50% of anthropogenic N₂O emissions. Nitrogen loss has become a core bottleneck constraining green agricultural development.

Against this background, enhanced-efficiency fertilizers (EEFs), as a class of novel fertilizers capable of delaying nitrogen release or inhibiting nitrogen transformation processes, have been highly anticipated. EEFs mainly include controlled-release/slow-release fertilizers, nitrification inhibitors, and urease inhibitors. Their core principle is to synchronize nitrogen release with crop uptake through physical coating or biochemical regulation, thereby reducing losses and improving use efficiency (Trenkel, 2010). Over the past two decades, the global EEFs market has continued to expand, and China has also incorporated EEFs promotion into its action plan for fertilizer reduction and efficiency enhancement.

However, a growing number of studies indicate that the actual effectiveness of EEFs is not as significant as expected. On one hand, their emission reduction effects are strongly regulated by environmental factors such as soil temperature, moisture, pH, and microbial activity, with considerable variation under field conditions. On the other hand, EEFs generally cost more than conventional fertilizers, and their economic feasibility faces challenges in smallholder farming systems (Li et al., 2021). More critically, EEFs can only alter the transformation pathways of nitrogen in the soil-crop system and cannot fundamentally solve the core problem of excessive nitrogen input. If the total nitrogen application rate and application methods are not simultaneously optimized, the emission reduction potential of EEFs may be offset by excessive nitrogen application.

Based on multi-year and multi-site field experiments, this paper systematically evaluates the agronomic and environmental effects of EEFs in major agricultural regions of China, and explores their extension boundaries through economic analysis, aiming to provide a basis for scientifically understanding the roles and limitations of EEFs and constructing a comprehensive nitrogen management system.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Experimental Sites

Experiments were conducted from 2018 to 2023 in three typical agricultural regions: the North China Plain (Quzhou, Hebei; fluvo-aquic soil; winter wheat-summer maize rotation), the Middle and Lower Yangtze River (Nanjing, Jiangsu; paddy soil; rice-wheat rotation), and Northeast China (Gongzhuling, Jilin; black soil; spring maize monoculture). The climatic conditions and basic soil physicochemical properties of each experimental site are shown in Table 1 (data omitted).

 2.2 Experimental Design

A randomized complete block design was adopted with four treatments and three replications:

(1) CU: conventional urea, containing 46% N, applied as a single basal application or split application;
(2) CRU: controlled-release urea, resin-coated, with a release period of 60–90 days;
(3) NIU: urea + nitrification inhibitor (DMPP, added at 1% of pure nitrogen);
(4) UIU: urea + urease inhibitor (NBPT, added at 0.5% of pure nitrogen).

Nitrogen application rates for each treatment were set according to local recommended rates: North China Plain winter wheat season 180 kg N·hm⁻², summer maize season 210 kg N·hm⁻²; Middle and Lower Yangtze River rice season 195 kg N·hm⁻², wheat season 150 kg N·hm⁻²; Northeast spring maize 225 kg N·hm⁻². Phosphorus and potassium fertilizers were applied uniformly at local conventional rates.

 2.3 Measurement Items and Methods

Yield and nitrogen use efficiency: Yield was measured at maturity, and NUE was calculated using the difference method.

Ammonia volatilization: Captured using the ventilation method, measured once per week until no volatilization occurred.

N₂O emissions: Measured using the static chamber-gas chromatography method, with sampling every 7–10 days.

Nitrate leaching: Soil solution was collected using ceramic suction cups, and NO₃⁻-N concentration was determined.

Economic analysis: Fertilizer costs, yield revenue, and net revenue were calculated. EEFs prices were set at market average prices (CRU approximately 30% higher than CU, NIU and UIU approximately 15% higher).

 2.4 Data Processing

SPSS 26.0 was used for analysis of variance and multiple comparisons (LSD method, α=0.05), and figures were plotted using Origin 2021.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Crop Yield and Nitrogen Use Efficiency

Compared with CU, the three EEFs treatments all increased crop yield and NUE to some extent, but the increases were limited (Table 2). In the North China Plain winter wheat-summer maize rotation system, CRU showed the best yield-increasing effect, with a combined increase of 6.8% across two seasons and an NUE increase of 15.6 percentage points; NIU and UIU increased yield by 4.2% and 2.9%, respectively. In the Middle and Lower Yangtze River rice-wheat rotation system, CRU and NIU increased yield by 5.1% and 3.8%, respectively, while UIU increased yield by only 2.1%. In the Northeast spring maize system, CRU increased yield by 5.6%, NIU by 3.4%, and UIU by 2.5%.

Overall, the agronomic effect of CRU was superior to NIU and UIU, but the yield increase of all EEFs treatments did not exceed 7%, with considerable inter-annual variation. Under high-temperature and rainy summer conditions in the North China Plain in 2019, the controlled-release effect of CRU was suppressed, and the yield increase dropped to 2.3%.

 3.2 Nitrogen Loss Pathways

The reduction effects of EEFs on nitrogen losses varied by loss pathway (Table 3). For ammonia volatilization, UIU showed the most significant effect, reducing by 42.7% compared with CU; NIU and CRU reduced by 28.3% and 18.2%, respectively. For N₂O emissions, NIU showed the best reduction effect, decreasing by 38.9% compared with CU; CRU and UIU reduced by 26.4% and 21.5%, respectively. For nitrate leaching, CRU reduced by 29.8%, while NIU and UIU reduced by 18.6% and 12.4%, respectively.

It is noteworthy that EEFs exhibit an obvious "trade-off" phenomenon in emission reduction effects. For example, NIU reduces N₂O emissions and nitrate leaching by inhibiting nitrification, but may increase the risk of ammonia volatilization; UIU inhibits urease activity to reduce ammonia volatilization, but has limited effect on nitrate leaching. A single type of EEF is difficult to simultaneously minimize nitrogen losses across multiple pathways.

 3.3 Economic Feasibility Analysis

Economic analysis showed that the net revenue increment of EEFs was generally low or even negative in grain crop systems (Table 4). In the North China Plain winter wheat-summer maize rotation system, CRU increased net revenue by 486 yuan·hm⁻² compared with CU, NIU by 312 yuan·hm⁻², and UIU by only 98 yuan·hm⁻². In the Middle and Lower Yangtze River rice-wheat rotation system, CRU increased net revenue by 375 yuan·hm⁻², NIU by 256 yuan·hm⁻², and UIU was -42 yuan·hm⁻². In the Northeast spring maize system, CRU increased net revenue by 420 yuan·hm⁻², NIU by 285 yuan·hm⁻², and UIU by 135 yuan·hm⁻².

If the internalization of environmental benefit externalities is considered (e.g., carbon trading price of 100 yuan·t⁻¹ CO₂e), the environmental benefits of NIU and CRU could increase by approximately 180 and 150 yuan·hm⁻², respectively, but the environmental benefits of UIU are still insufficient to offset the cost increment. For smallholders, the increased initial investment and revenue uncertainty of EEFs constitute the main obstacles to extension.

 4 Discussion

 4.1 Limitations and Mechanisms of EEFs Emission Reduction Effects

The results of this study indicate that EEFs have certain effects on reducing environmental nitrogen losses, but their effects have clear boundaries. First, the emission reduction effects of EEFs are strongly regulated by environmental conditions. The release rate of CRU depends on soil temperature and moisture; under high-temperature and rainy conditions, release accelerates and the controlled-release effect weakens. The nitrification inhibition effect of NIU is more persistent in low-pH and high-organic-matter soils, but is easily degraded in alkaline soils. The urease inhibition effect of UIU is affected by the background soil urease activity, and its effectiveness decreases in soils with long-term organic fertilizer application. This is consistent with the meta-analysis results of Li et al. (2021) and Zhang et al. (2022).

Second, EEFs cannot solve the fundamental problem of excessive nitrogen input. When nitrogen application exceeds crop demand, even with EEFs, excess nitrogen will still be lost through some pathway—only the loss pathway shifts. For example, NIU reduces N₂O and nitrate leaching but may increase ammonia volatilization; CRU reduces leaching but may still release excessive nitrogen in the late crop growth stage. Therefore, the emission reduction potential of EEFs can only be fully realized under the premise of optimizing nitrogen application rates.

 4.2 Economic Feasibility and Extension Boundaries

The economic feasibility of EEFs is the key determinant of whether they can be extended on a large scale. This study shows that in grain crop systems, the yield-increasing revenue of EEFs is limited, while fertilizer costs increase by 15%–30%, resulting in small or even negative net revenue increments. This contradicts the current reality of small operational scales and weak risk-bearing capacity of smallholders in China. In contrast, in cash crop systems (e.g., fruit trees, vegetables), due to higher output value and larger nitrogen fertilizer application rates, the economic feasibility of EEFs is higher, but their environmental risks are also greater (e.g., nitrate leaching).

In addition, the extension of EEFs faces problems such as insufficient market awareness, inconsistent product quality, and lack of regulatory standards. Some controlled-release fertilizers have actual release periods that do not match their labels, and the degradation products of nitrification inhibitors in soil may pose environmental risks, all of which require further research and regulation.

 4.3 Necessity of Constructing a Comprehensive Nitrogen Management System

EEFs are not a panacea for solving the nitrogen problem, and their role should be rationally positioned as one technological option within a comprehensive nitrogen management system. To truly achieve nitrogen emission reduction and efficiency enhancement, multiple measures are needed:

(1) Optimize nitrogen application rates: Based on soil nitrogen supply capacity and crop demand, adopt recommended or reduced nitrogen application rates to reduce nitrogen input at the source;
(2) Adjust cropping structure: Reduce planting of high-nitrogen crops in nitrogen-loss-sensitive areas and develop legume crop rotations;
(3) Improve application methods: Adopt deep placement, split application, and integrated water-fertilizer techniques to reduce ammonia volatilization and leaching;
(4) Policy incentives: Internalize environmental benefits through subsidies, carbon trading, and ecological compensation mechanisms to enhance the economic attractiveness of EEFs;
(5) Regional differentiated strategies: Select appropriate EEF types and application rates based on soil, climate, and cropping system characteristics.

 5 Conclusions

(1) Enhanced-efficiency fertilizers (CRU, NIU, UIU) can increase nitrogen use efficiency by 8.3–15.6 percentage points, reduce ammonia volatilization by 18.2%–42.7%, N₂O emissions by 21.5%–38.9%, and nitrate leaching by 12.4%–29.8%, but their crop yield increases are only 2.1%–6.8%, with considerable inter-annual variation.

(2) The emission reduction effects of EEFs exhibit a "trade-off" phenomenon among pathways, and a single type of EEF is difficult to simultaneously minimize nitrogen losses across multiple pathways. Their effects are strongly regulated by soil type, climatic conditions, and cropping systems.

(3) In terms of economic feasibility, the net revenue increment of EEFs in grain crop systems is limited or even negative, making them insufficiently attractive to smallholders; in cash crop systems, economic feasibility is higher, but environmental risks require attention.

(4) EEFs are not a panacea for solving agricultural nitrogen problems and cannot replace optimized nitrogen application rates and comprehensive nutrient management. They should be positioned as one technological option within a comprehensive nitrogen management system. Only by integrating reduced nitrogen application, cropping structure adjustment, improved application methods, and policy incentives to construct regionally differentiated nitrogen management strategies can the win-win outcome of green agricultural development and food security be achieved.

title: The sequence and thresholds of leaf hydraulic traits underlying grapevine varietal differences in drought tolerance
text:
Leaf Hydraulic Trait Sequence and Thresholds Underlying Differences in Drought Tolerance Among Grapevine Cultivars

Abstract: To clarify the differences in drought tolerance mechanisms among different grapevine cultivars under drought conditions, this study used the commonly cultivated 'Cabernet Sauvignon', 'Merlot', 'Chardonnay', and 'Syrah' as materials, and systematically measured leaf hydraulic conductance, stomatal conductance, leaf water potential, turgor loss point, and leaf anatomical traits through a potted water-control experiment. The results showed that during drought, the responses of leaf hydraulic traits exhibited a clear sequence across cultivars, namely stomatal closure preceded the decline in leaf hydraulic conductance, and the decline in leaf hydraulic conductance preceded turgor loss. Differences in drought tolerance among cultivars were mainly determined by the threshold for the decline in leaf hydraulic conductance, rather than the initiation point of stomatal closure. 'Syrah' and 'Cabernet Sauvignon' maintained relatively high hydraulic conductance when leaf water potential dropped to -1.2 MPa, exhibiting strong drought tolerance; 'Chardonnay' showed a significant decline in hydraulic conductance at -0.8 MPa, exhibiting weak drought tolerance. Accordingly, it is recommended that in drought-prone regions, cultivars with lower hydraulic conductance thresholds should be preferentially selected, and irrigation or shading measures should be taken before the threshold water potential is reached in field management.

Introduction: Drought is one of the main environmental factors limiting grape yield and quality. The adaptability of different grapevine cultivars to drought differs significantly, but the underlying physiological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Leaves are the key organs for water transport and gas exchange in grapevines, and leaf hydraulic conductance reflects the efficiency of water transport from the petiole to mesophyll cells. When soil water is deficient, leaf hydraulic conductance declines, stomata close, and photosynthesis is subsequently affected. However, whether the sequence of changes in leaf hydraulic traits and the critical thresholds during drought are consistent among different cultivars lacks systematic comparison. This study aims to reveal the relationship between differences in drought tolerance among grapevine cultivars and the sequence and thresholds of leaf hydraulic traits, providing a theoretical basis for drought-tolerant cultivar selection and water-saving cultivation.

Key Technical Analysis

1. Experimental Design and Materials

The experiment was conducted in a rain shelter. Uniform two-year-old cuttings were selected and planted in 10 L pots, with a substrate of garden soil:peat:perlite = 2:1:1. Two treatments were established: normal water supply (soil relative water content 75% ± 5%) and drought treatment (natural water depletion after cessation of watering), with 6 plants per cultivar per treatment. The drought treatment lasted 14 days, and leaf hydraulic conductance, stomatal conductance, and leaf water potential were measured every 2 days. Leaf water potential was measured using the pressure chamber method, leaf hydraulic conductance was measured using the dynamic method, and stomatal conductance was measured using a porometer. Additionally, mature leaves were collected to determine the turgor loss point (PV curve method) and leaf anatomical structure (paraffin sectioning method).

2. Response Sequence of Leaf Hydraulic Conductance and Stomatal Conductance

Under normal water supply conditions, there were no significant differences in leaf hydraulic conductance among the four cultivars (12–14 mmol m⁻² s⁻¹ MPa⁻¹). On day 4 of drought treatment, stomatal conductance began to decline in all cultivars, but leaf hydraulic conductance had not yet changed significantly; on day 6, stomatal conductance dropped below 40% of the control, and leaf hydraulic conductance began to decline; on day 8, leaf hydraulic conductance dropped to approximately 50% of the control, and leaf water potential dropped to -1.0 to -1.4 MPa. This indicates that stomatal closure precedes the decline in leaf hydraulic conductance, i.e., stomata are more sensitive to drought than the leaf hydraulic system. This sequence was consistent across the four cultivars, indicating that stomatal closure is an early response of grapevines to drought.

3. Differences in Thresholds for Leaf Hydraulic Conductance Decline

Although the sequence was consistent, there were significant differences among cultivars in the threshold water potential for leaf hydraulic conductance decline. Taking the control leaf hydraulic conductance as 100%, when leaf water potential dropped to -0.8 MPa, 'Chardonnay' leaf hydraulic conductance dropped to 65%, while 'Syrah' and 'Cabernet Sauvignon' still maintained above 85%; when leaf water potential dropped to -1.2 MPa, 'Chardonnay' dropped to 35%, 'Merlot' dropped to 55%, and 'Syrah' and 'Cabernet Sauvignon' remained at approximately 70%. Defining the leaf water potential corresponding to a 50% decline in leaf hydraulic conductance as the threshold water potential, 'Chardonnay' was -0.9 MPa, 'Merlot' was -1.1 MPa, 'Cabernet Sauvignon' was -1.3 MPa, and 'Syrah' was -1.4 MPa. The lower the threshold water potential, the stronger the drought tolerance.

4. Association of Turgor Loss Point with Leaf Anatomical Traits

PV curve parameters showed that the turgor loss points of 'Syrah' and 'Cabernet Sauvignon' were -1.6 to -1.8 MPa, significantly lower than that of 'Chardonnay' (-1.2 MPa). Leaf anatomy revealed that cultivars with strong drought tolerance had greater leaf thickness, higher palisade tissue/spongy tissue ratios, and greater vein density. These structural characteristics help maintain leaf hydraulic conductance and cell turgor under low water potential. Correlation analysis showed that threshold water potential was significantly positively correlated with turgor loss point (r = 0.86) and significantly negatively correlated with vein density (r = -0.79). This indicates that leaf hydraulic trait thresholds are regulated by anatomical structure.

5. Field Verification and Implications for Water Management

In field experiments, drip irrigation was applied before leaf water potential dropped to the threshold water potential of each cultivar. The results showed that for 'Syrah' and 'Cabernet Sauvignon', irrigation before the threshold maintained leaf hydraulic conductance above 80% of the control, with no significant decline in yield or fruit quality; whereas for 'Chardonnay', if irrigation was delayed until the threshold water potential was reached, leaf hydraulic conductance was difficult to recover, and photosynthetic rate declined by more than 30%. Therefore, it is recommended to formulate irrigation schedules based on cultivar-specific threshold water potentials: cultivars with weak drought tolerance should be irrigated when leaf water potential drops to -0.6 MPa, while cultivars with strong drought tolerance can be delayed until -1.0 MPa.

Results and Benefit Analysis: This study demonstrates that the key to differences in drought tolerance among grapevine cultivars lies in the threshold water potential for leaf hydraulic conductance decline, rather than the initiation point of stomatal closure. Cultivars with strong drought tolerance have lower threshold water potentials and turgor loss points, as well as more developed veins and palisade tissue. Irrigation strategies based on threshold water potential can save 20%–30% of water while avoiding the inhibition of photosynthesis and yield caused by severe drought. Taking 'Chardonnay' as an example, irrigation based on the threshold saves approximately 80 m³ per mu per season compared with conventional irrigation, with a yield increase of 5%–8%. The drought-tolerant cultivars 'Syrah' and 'Cabernet Sauvignon' showed more than 15% improvement in yield stability in dry years. This technique is simple and easy to implement, requiring only a pressure chamber and leaf water potential monitoring, and is suitable for promotion in grape-producing regions.

Conclusion: Leaf hydraulic traits of grapevines follow the sequence of "stomatal closure—leaf hydraulic conductance decline—turgor loss" during drought. Differences in drought tolerance among cultivars are mainly determined by the threshold water potential for leaf hydraulic conductance decline; the lower the threshold water potential, the stronger the drought tolerance. Threshold water potential is closely related to turgor loss point and vein density. In production, irrigation indicators should be formulated based on cultivar-specific threshold water potentials; cultivars with weak drought tolerance require earlier irrigation, while cultivars with strong drought tolerance can be appropriately delayed. This strategy can significantly improve water use efficiency and stabilize yield and quality, and is suitable for promotion and application in arid and semi-arid regions.

title: Entrepreneurs and Environmental Sustainability in the Digital Era: Regional and Institutional Perspectives
text:
Entrepreneurs and Environmental Sustainability in the Digital Era: Regional and Institutional Perspectives

Abstract: In the era of the digital economy, the impact of entrepreneurial behavior on environmental sustainability has attracted increasing attention. Based on panel data from 30 provinces in China from 2015 to 2022, this paper constructs a comprehensive evaluation index system for entrepreneurial activity, digital infrastructure, and environmental sustainability, and employs fixed-effects models and mediation-effect models to empirically examine the influence mechanism of entrepreneurial activities on regional environmental sustainability as well as regional and institutional heterogeneity. The findings are as follows: entrepreneurial activity significantly enhances regional environmental sustainability, and this effect is more pronounced in the eastern region and regions with a better institutional environment; digital infrastructure plays a partial mediating role in this process; the institutional environment has a positive moderating effect on the environmental spillover effects of entrepreneurship. The conclusions of this study provide empirical evidence for optimizing regional entrepreneurship policies and promoting green digital transformation.

Keywords: entrepreneurs; environmental sustainability; digital economy; regional differences; institutional environment; mediation effect

1 Introduction

Against the dual backdrop of the "dual carbon" goals and the rapid development of the digital economy, entrepreneurs, as important actors in technology diffusion and market innovation, have received widespread scholarly attention for their environmental externalities. Existing studies mostly focus on the role of entrepreneurship in promoting economic growth and employment, while less attention has been paid to its impact on environmental sustainability. In particular, in the context of the digital era, the environmental effects of entrepreneurial activities through channels such as the application of digital technologies and green business model innovation remain unclear. Meanwhile, China's unbalanced regional development and differences in institutional environments may lead to significant heterogeneity in the environmental effects of entrepreneurship. This paper aims to construct an analytical framework of "entrepreneurship–digital–institution–environment," empirically examine the influence mechanism of entrepreneurial activities on environmental sustainability using provincial panel data, and explore the differentiated manifestations from regional and institutional perspectives, with the aim of providing a theoretical basis for green entrepreneurship policy formulation.

2 Materials and Methods

2.1 Data Sources

This paper selects 30 provinces in China (excluding Tibet, Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan) from 2015 to 2022 as the research objects. The data are sourced from the China Statistical Yearbook, the China Environmental Statistics Yearbook, the China Torch Statistical Yearbook, and the Peking University Digital Financial Inclusion Index, among others. A small number of missing values were filled using linear interpolation.

2.2 Variable Settings

The dependent variable is environmental sustainability (ES), and the entropy weight method is used to construct a comprehensive index from three aspects: environmental pollution, resource consumption, and ecological governance. The core explanatory variable is entrepreneurial activity (EA), measured by the natural logarithm of the number of newly registered enterprises per ten thousand people. The mediating variable is digital infrastructure (DI), synthesized from the internet penetration rate, mobile phone base station density, and the digital finance index. The moderating variable is the institutional environment (IE), which is standardized and weighted using the marketization index and the strength of intellectual property protection. Control variables include the level of economic development, industrial structure, urbanization rate, R&D investment intensity, and foreign capital dependence.

2.3 Model Construction

The baseline regression model is: ES_it = α0 + α1EA_it + ΣβX_it + μ_i + λ_t + ε_it. The mediation effect is tested using the three-step method to examine the mediating role of DI. The moderating effect is examined by introducing the EA×IE interaction term to investigate the moderating role of the institutional environment. Regional heterogeneity is examined through grouped regressions for the eastern, central, and western regions.

3 Results and Analysis

3.1 Baseline Regression Results

The fixed-effects model results show that entrepreneurial activity has a significant positive impact on environmental sustainability (β=0.213, p<0.01), indicating that entrepreneurial activities are generally conducive to regional environmental improvement. Among the control variables, R&D investment intensity and industrial structure upgrading also show significant positive correlations, while the coefficient of foreign capital dependence is negative but not significant.

3.2 Mediation Effect Analysis

Digital infrastructure plays a partial mediating role between entrepreneurial activity and environmental sustainability, with the mediation effect accounting for 18.7% of the total effect. The specific path is: increased entrepreneurial activity → improved digital infrastructure → enhanced environmental sustainability. This indicates that the application of digital technology is an important transmission channel for the environmental dividend of entrepreneurship.

3.3 Regional and Institutional Heterogeneity

The sub-regional regressions show that the environmental promotion effect of entrepreneurship is strongest in the eastern region (β=0.287), followed by the central region (β=0.174), and not significant in the western region. The test of the moderating effect of the institutional environment shows that the EA×IE interaction term is significantly positive (β=0.132, p<0.05), indicating that in regions with a higher degree of marketization and stronger intellectual property protection, the positive impact of entrepreneurship on environmental sustainability is more prominent.

4 Discussion

This paper confirms that entrepreneurs in the digital era have significant positive environmental externalities, which complements the traditional view that "entrepreneurship exacerbates resource consumption." The possible reasons are: digital entrepreneurship is mostly concentrated in low-material-consumption, high-knowledge-intensive service and platform sectors, and digital technology empowers the green transformation of traditional industries. Regional heterogeneity reflects that the digital ecosystem and institutional support in the eastern region are more mature, making it easier for entrepreneurs to translate green innovation into environmental performance. The moderating role of the institutional environment indicates that a sound market and legal environment can incentivize entrepreneurs to adopt clean technologies and green business models rather than short-term arbitrage behavior. The limitation of this paper is that it does not distinguish between types of entrepreneurship (necessity-based and opportunity-based), and future research can further refine the mechanism by incorporating micro-level firm data.

5 Conclusions

Based on provincial panel data, this paper empirically reveals the promoting effect of entrepreneurial activities on regional environmental sustainability and verifies the mediating effect of digital infrastructure and the moderating effect of the institutional environment. Regional heterogeneity indicates that the eastern region and regions with a better institutional environment benefit more significantly. The policy implications are as follows: First, the entrepreneurial environment should continue to be optimized to encourage green- and digital-oriented entrepreneurial activities; second, digital infrastructure construction in the central and western regions should be strengthened to narrow the "digital divide"; third, marketization and intellectual property systems should be improved to guide the positive environmental spillovers of entrepreneurs. The conclusions of this study provide empirical support for achieving the coordinated development of entrepreneurial vitality and ecological civilization in the era of the digital economy.

title: The individual and combined effects of hypoxia and high-fat diet feeding on nutrient composition and flesh quality in Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
text:
Effects of Hypoxia and High-Fat Diet Alone and in Combination on Nutritional Composition and Flesh Quality of Nile Tilapia

Abstract: To investigate the effects of hypoxia and high-fat diet on the flesh quality of Nile tilapia, four treatment groups were established in this experiment: normoxia + normal diet (control group), normoxia + high-fat diet, hypoxia + normal diet, and hypoxia + high-fat diet. The culture period was 8 weeks. The results showed that the high-fat diet significantly increased the crude lipid content and decreased the crude protein content of the fish. Hypoxia treatment exacerbated lipid deposition and led to a decrease in muscle water-holding capacity. Under the combined effect of both factors, the proportion of saturated fatty acids in the flesh increased, the content of n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids decreased, and the taste and nutritional value of the flesh were significantly reduced. This study can provide technical reference for healthy aquaculture and quality regulation of tilapia.

Introduction: Nile tilapia is an important freshwater aquaculture species in China, known for its tender flesh and high protein content, and is well received by the market. However, in intensive aquaculture, hypoxia in water bodies frequently occurs, and simultaneously, high-fat diets are widely used in pursuit of growth rate. Both hypoxia and high-fat diets can interfere with lipid metabolism in fish, but systematic comparisons of their individual and combined effects on the nutritional composition and flesh quality of tilapia are still lacking. Through culture experiments, this paper analyzes the changes in conventional nutritional composition, fatty acid composition, and texture characteristics of fish under different treatments, aiming to provide a basis for optimizing feeding strategies and improving aquaculture water quality.

Key Technical Analysis:

1. Experimental Design and Culture Management
The experiment was conducted in an indoor recirculating aquaculture system. A total of 240 healthy Nile tilapia with an initial body weight of approximately 50 g were selected and randomly divided into 4 groups, with 3 replicates per group. The dissolved oxygen in the normoxia groups was maintained at 6.0–7.0 mg/L, while in the hypoxia groups, the dissolved oxygen was controlled at 3.0–3.5 mg/L by adjusting aeration intensity. The normal diet had a lipid content of 6%, and the high-fat diet had a lipid content of 12%, with other nutritional components being identical. Fish were fed twice daily to apparent satiation, and the culture period was 8 weeks.

2. Determination of Conventional Nutritional Composition
After the culture period, 10 fish were sampled from each group, and dorsal muscle was collected. Moisture content was determined by atmospheric drying at 105°C, crude protein by the Kjeldahl method, crude lipid by the Soxhlet extraction method, and ash by muffle furnace combustion. The results showed that the muscle crude lipid content in the high-fat diet group increased by approximately 28% compared with the control group, while crude protein decreased by approximately 7%. In the hypoxia + high-fat group, crude lipid further increased by approximately 45% compared with the control group, and crude protein decreased by approximately 12%.

3. Analysis of Fatty Acid Composition
Muscle lipids were extracted using the chloroform-methanol method, followed by methyl esterification, and fatty acid composition was analyzed using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry. In the high-fat diet group, the proportion of saturated fatty acids (SFA) increased, and monounsaturated fatty acids (MUFA) slightly increased. In the hypoxia group, n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFA) significantly decreased. The combined treatment group had the highest SFA proportion and the lowest n-3 PUFA proportion, with the n-6/n-3 ratio increasing from 4.2 in the control group to 7.8, indicating a decline in the nutritional quality of flesh fatty acids.

4. Evaluation of Flesh Texture and Water-Holding Capacity
Muscle hardness, elasticity, and chewiness were measured using a texture analyzer, and water-holding capacity was determined by the centrifugation method. In the high-fat diet group, muscle hardness and chewiness decreased, and water-holding capacity declined. In the hypoxia group, elasticity decreased. In the combined treatment group, both hardness and elasticity were significantly lower than those in the control group, and water-holding capacity decreased by approximately 15% compared with the control group, indicating deterioration in flesh taste and reduced water retention capacity.

Results and Benefit Analysis: This study demonstrates that the high-fat diet mainly leads to excessive lipid deposition in fish, while hypoxia exacerbates lipid oxidation and deterioration of fatty acid composition. The combined effect of both factors has a greater negative impact on flesh quality than either factor alone. From the perspective of production benefits, although the high-fat diet can improve weight gain rate to some extent, under hypoxic conditions, feed conversion ratio decreases and fish quality declines, which in turn affects the selling price. If the dietary lipid level is controlled at 8%–10% and dissolved oxygen is maintained above 5 mg/L during aquaculture, both growth and quality can be balanced. According to estimates from this experiment, compared with the hypoxia + high-fat group, the optimized group showed approximately 30% lower muscle crude lipid, approximately 25% higher n-3 PUFA, and 15% higher water-holding capacity, with the market price per kilogram of fish increasing by 1–2 yuan, demonstrating good potential for promotion.

Conclusion: Both hypoxia and high-fat diet reduce the flesh quality of Nile tilapia, and their combined effect is more pronounced. It is recommended to reasonably control dietary lipid content and strengthen aeration management in aquaculture to maintain good nutritional composition and texture characteristics of flesh, achieving high-quality and efficient aquaculture.

title: Effects of phosphorylation on μ-calpain activity at different incubation temperature
text:
Effect of Phosphorylation Modification on μ-Calpain Activity at Different Incubation Temperatures

 Abstract

μ-Calpain, a core member of the calcium-dependent cysteine protease family, plays a key role in postmortem muscle protein degradation, cytoskeletal remodeling, and various physiological and pathological processes. Phosphorylation modification is an important post-translational modification that regulates calpain activity, but its interaction with temperature conditions remains unclear. In this study, μ-calpain extracted from porcine longissimus dorsi muscle was used as the research object. Exogenous protein kinase A (PKA) was employed to catalyze phosphorylation modification, and enzyme activity was measured at different incubation temperatures (4, 15, 25, and 37 °C). Autolysis characteristics and catalytic kinetics were analyzed using Western blot and fluorogenic substrate methods. The results showed that phosphorylation modification significantly inhibited μ-calpain activity, and the degree of inhibition was temperature-dependent—the inhibition rates at 4 °C and 15 °C were 18.6% and 26.3%, respectively, while at 25 °C and 37 °C, the inhibition rates reached 41.7% and 52.4%. Kinetic analysis revealed that phosphorylation decreased the maximum reaction rate (Vmax) of the enzyme, but the Michaelis constant (Km) showed no significant change, suggesting a non-competitive inhibition mechanism. Furthermore, phosphorylation delayed the autolytic activation process of μ-calpain at low temperatures. This study reveals the pattern of synergistic regulation of μ-calpain activity by phosphorylation and temperature, providing a theoretical basis for the regulation of postmortem meat tenderization and research on calpain-related disease mechanisms.

Keywords: μ-calpain; phosphorylation; incubation temperature; enzyme activity; postmortem tenderization

 1 Introduction

μ-Calpain is a widely expressed protease in the calpain family, and its activity depends on elevated intracellular Ca²⁺ concentration. In postmortem muscle, μ-calpain participates in the muscle tenderization process through limited hydrolysis of myofibrillar proteins (such as desmin, troponin T, and nebulin), making it one of the key enzymes determining meat quality. Meanwhile, μ-calpain also plays an important role in pathological processes such as neurodegenerative diseases, ischemia-reperfusion injury, and tumorigenesis, and its abnormal activity is closely associated with various diseases.

Phosphorylation modification, as one of the most prevalent post-translational modifications in eukaryotes, has been demonstrated to regulate the activity, localization, and stability of various proteases. Previous studies have shown that both the regulatory subunit and catalytic subunit of μ-calpain contain multiple potential phosphorylation sites, and protein kinase A (PKA) and protein kinase C (PKC) can influence its phosphorylation level. However, whether the regulatory effect of phosphorylation modification on μ-calpain activity is affected by environmental temperature has rarely been systematically studied. Temperature is an important factor affecting enzymatic reaction rates and protein conformational stability. During postmortem muscle maturation, the environmental temperature gradually decreases from body temperature (37 °C) to refrigeration temperature (4 °C), and this dynamic change may alter the effect intensity of phosphorylation modification.

In this study, porcine longissimus dorsi muscle was used as material to extract μ-calpain. Through in vitro phosphorylation modification treatment, the effects of phosphorylation on μ-calpain activity at different incubation temperatures were systematically investigated, aiming to elucidate the interactive regulatory pattern between phosphorylation and temperature, and to provide theoretical references for the regulation of postmortem meat tenderization and research on calpain-related disease mechanisms.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Materials and Reagents

Fresh porcine longissimus dorsi muscle was obtained from a local slaughterhouse, sampled within 30 min postmortem, and immediately transported back to the laboratory on ice. Casein, fluorogenic substrate Suc-Leu-Leu-Val-Tyr-AMC, PKA catalytic subunit, ATP, dithiothreitol (DTT), ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA), and other reagents were purchased from Sigma-Aldrich. All other reagents were of analytical grade.

 2.2 Extraction and Purification of μ-Calpain

The method of Dayton et al. was referenced with minor modifications. Fifty grams of porcine longissimus dorsi muscle was trimmed of fat and connective tissue, and 3 volumes of pre-cooled extraction buffer (20 mmol/L Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, containing 1 mmol/L EDTA, 1 mmol/L DTT, 0.1% β-mercaptoethanol) were added. After homogenization, the sample was centrifuged (10,000×g, 4 °C, 30 min). The supernatant was subjected to ammonium sulfate fractional precipitation (30%–60% saturation), dialyzed, and then loaded onto a DEAE-Sephacel anion exchange chromatography column, eluted with a linear gradient of 0–0.5 mol/L NaCl. Fractions containing μ-calpain activity were collected, concentrated by ultrafiltration, and stored at -80 °C. Purity was assessed by SDS-PAGE, and Coomassie brilliant blue staining showed a single band with a molecular weight of approximately 80 kDa.

 2.3 In Vitro Phosphorylation Modification

The phosphorylation reaction system contained: purified μ-calpain (0.5 mg/mL), PKA catalytic subunit (100 U/mL), ATP (1 mmol/L), MgCl₂ (5 mmol/L), and Tris-HCl buffer (50 mmol/L, pH 7.5). In the control group, ATP was replaced with an equal volume of buffer. The reaction was incubated at 30 °C for 30 min, then EDTA (10 mmol/L) was added to terminate the reaction. The phosphorylation level was detected using the Pro-Q Diamond phosphoprotein staining kit and expressed as the ratio of phosphorylated/total protein fluorescence intensity.

 2.4 Enzyme Activity Assay

μ-Calpain activity was measured using the fluorogenic substrate method. The reaction system (200 μL) contained: 50 mmol/L Tris-HCl (pH 7.5), 100 mmol/L NaCl, 5 mmol/L CaCl₂, 10 μmol/L Suc-Leu-Leu-Val-Tyr-AMC, and an appropriate amount of enzyme solution. Incubation was performed at 4, 15, 25, and 37 °C, respectively. Fluorescence intensity changes were continuously monitored using a fluorescence microplate reader (excitation wavelength 355 nm, emission wavelength 460 nm), recorded every 30 s for a total of 30 min. Enzyme activity was expressed as the increase in fluorescence intensity per minute (ΔFU/min). Three parallels were set for each group, with three replicates.

 2.5 Determination of Kinetic Parameters

The initial rates of enzymatic reaction were measured at different substrate concentrations (2.5–50 μmol/L), and Km and Vmax were calculated using the Lineweaver-Burk double reciprocal plot method.

 2.6 Autolysis Analysis

Phosphorylated and non-phosphorylated μ-calpain were separately placed in a reaction system containing 5 mmol/L CaCl₂, incubated at 4, 15, 25, and 37 °C, and sampled at 0, 5, 15, and 30 min. SDS-PAGE loading buffer was added, and samples were boiled for 5 min. After separation by 8% SDS-PAGE and Coomassie brilliant blue staining, the conversion of the 80 kDa full-length enzyme to 76 kDa and 78 kDa autolytic fragments was observed.

 2.7 Data Processing

Data were expressed as mean ± standard deviation. One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) was performed using SPSS 22.0, and Duncan's multiple comparison test was used to examine differences between groups, with P<0.05 considered significantly different.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Verification of Phosphorylation Modification

Pro-Q Diamond staining results showed that the phosphorylation fluorescence intensity of the PKA-treated group was significantly higher than that of the control group (P<0.05), with the phosphorylated/total protein ratio increasing from 0.21±0.03 in the control group to 0.68±0.07, indicating that μ-calpain was effectively phosphorylated. SDS-PAGE Coomassie brilliant blue staining showed no obvious degradation bands, indicating that the phosphorylation reaction did not cause significant degradation of the enzyme protein.

 3.2 Effect of Phosphorylation on μ-Calpain Activity at Different Temperatures

As shown in Table 1, the activity of non-phosphorylated μ-calpain increased with increasing temperature, from 12.4±1.1 ΔFU/min at 4 °C to 86.7±5.3 ΔFU/min at 37 °C. Phosphorylation modification significantly inhibited enzyme activity at all temperatures (P<0.05), but the inhibition rate increased with increasing temperature: the inhibition rate was 18.6% at 4 °C, 26.3% at 15 °C, 41.7% at 25 °C, and 52.4% at 37 °C. Two-way ANOVA showed a significant interaction effect between phosphorylation and temperature (P<0.01), indicating that elevated temperature enhanced the inhibitory effect of phosphorylation on enzyme activity.

Table 1 Effect of Phosphorylation on μ-Calpain Activity at Different Incubation Temperatures

| Temperature (°C) | Non-phosphorylated group (ΔFU/min) | Phosphorylated group (ΔFU/min) | Inhibition rate (%) |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 4 | 12.4±1.1 | 10.1±0.9 | 18.6 |
| 15 | 28.7±2.3 | 21.2±1.8 | 26.3 |
| 25 | 54.3±3.6 | 31.7±2.5 | 41.7 |
| 37 | 86.7±5.3 | 41.3±3.2 | 52.4 |

Note: Different lowercase letters in the same column indicate significant differences (P<0.05).

 3.3 Kinetic Parameter Analysis

Kinetic parameters were determined at 25 °C. The Km of non-phosphorylated μ-calpain was 8.6±0.7 μmol/L, and Vmax was 112.4±8.5 ΔFU/min; after phosphorylation, Km was 8.9±0.8 μmol/L (P>0.05), and Vmax decreased to 64.7±5.1 ΔFU/min (P<0.05). No significant change in Km with a significant decrease in Vmax indicated that the inhibition of μ-calpain by phosphorylation belongs to the non-competitive inhibition type, i.e., phosphorylation modification may alter the catalytic efficiency of the enzyme without affecting its affinity for the substrate.

 3.4 Autolysis Characteristics Analysis

SDS-PAGE results showed that non-phosphorylated μ-calpain exhibited obvious 76 kDa autolytic fragments after 5 min of incubation at 37 °C, and the 80 kDa full-length enzyme band essentially disappeared after 15 min; at 25 °C, the autolytic process was slightly slower, with most of the full-length enzyme converted to autolytic fragments at 30 min; at 15 °C and 4 °C, the autolytic process was significantly delayed, with obvious 80 kDa bands still visible at 30 min. Phosphorylation modification further delayed the autolytic process at all temperatures, especially at 4 °C and 15 °C, where almost no obvious autolytic fragments were generated in the phosphorylated group at 30 min, and the 80 kDa band remained intact. This indicates that phosphorylation modification can stabilize the full-length enzyme conformation of μ-calpain and inhibit its Ca²⁺-induced autolytic activation.

 4 Discussion

This study systematically revealed the inhibitory effect of phosphorylation modification on μ-calpain activity and its temperature-dependent characteristics. The study found that phosphorylation modification had a weaker inhibitory effect on enzyme activity at low temperatures, while the inhibitory effect was significantly enhanced at high temperatures. This phenomenon may be related to the conformational changes of the protein caused by phosphorylation modification and its temperature sensitivity. The introduction of phosphate groups increases the negative charge density on the protein surface, which may affect the conformational flexibility of the catalytic domain through electrostatic interactions. Under low-temperature conditions, the thermal motion of protein molecules is weak, the amplitude of conformational changes is limited, and the steric hindrance effect of phosphorylation is relatively small; whereas when temperature increases, the thermal motion of protein molecules intensifies, and the phosphorylation-induced conformational changes become more significant, thereby more effectively inhibiting catalytic activity.

Kinetic analysis showed that phosphorylation modification led to a decrease in Vmax without changing Km, suggesting a non-competitive inhibition mechanism. This is consistent with the findings of Du et al. regarding PKA phosphorylation regulation of calpain activity. The catalytic domain of μ-calpain contains multiple potential phosphorylation sites, among which Ser⁷⁶ and Thr⁷⁸ are located near the catalytic triad. Phosphorylation may reduce catalytic efficiency by altering the microenvironment of the active center without affecting the affinity of the substrate binding site.

Autolysis analysis results further indicated that phosphorylation modification can delay the Ca²⁺-induced autolytic activation of μ-calpain. Autolysis of μ-calpain is a prerequisite for its proteolytic activity, and the autolytic process involves the removal of the N-terminal propeptide and domain rearrangement. Phosphorylation may delay the autolytic process by stabilizing the full-length enzyme conformation and hindering the conformational changes induced by Ca²⁺ binding. This effect was more pronounced at low temperatures, possibly due to a synergistic effect with the inhibition of the autolytic reaction by low temperature itself.

From an application perspective, the results of this study have reference significance for the regulation of postmortem meat tenderization. The activity of μ-calpain in postmortem muscle directly affects the degree of myofibrillar protein degradation and the ultimate tenderness of meat. In the early postmortem period, muscle temperature is relatively high (close to 37 °C), at which point the inhibitory effect of phosphorylation on μ-calpain is stronger and may delay the tenderization process; as the carcass cools to 4 °C, the phosphorylation inhibitory effect weakens, and enzyme activity is partially restored. Therefore, regulating the phosphorylation level of μ-calpain in early postmortem muscle may become a potential approach for regulating meat tenderization. In addition, in the medical field, excessive activation of μ-calpain is closely associated with myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury and neurodegenerative diseases, and targeted regulation of its phosphorylation state may provide new ideas for the treatment of related diseases.

The limitation of this study is that only an in vitro phosphorylation system was used, which could not fully simulate the complex kinase-phosphatase network in vivo. Future studies can combine in vivo models to further verify the regulatory role of phosphorylation modification under different physiological and pathological conditions.

 5 Conclusion

(1) Phosphorylation modification significantly inhibited μ-calpain activity, and the inhibition rate increased with increasing incubation temperature, with inhibition rates of 18.6%, 26.3%, 41.7%, and 52.4% at 4, 15, 25, and 37 °C, respectively. (2) Phosphorylation modification significantly decreased the Vmax of μ-calpain without significant change in Km, exhibiting non-competitive inhibition characteristics. (3) Phosphorylation modification can delay the Ca²⁺-induced autolytic activation of μ-calpain, with the delaying effect being more pronounced at low temperatures. (4) There is a significant interaction effect between phosphorylation and temperature on μ-calpain activity, with elevated temperature enhancing the inhibitory effect of phosphorylation. This study provides a theoretical basis for the regulation of postmortem meat tenderization and research on calpain-related disease mechanisms.

title: Comparative pharmacokinetic study of chlorogenic acid after oral administration of Lonicerae Japonicae Flos and Shuang-Huang-Lian in normal and febrile rats
text:
Comparative pharmacokinetic study of chlorogenic acid after oral administration of Lonicerae Japonicae Flos and Shuang-Huang-Lian in normal and febrile rats

Abstract: Objective: To compare the pharmacokinetic characteristics of chlorogenic acid after oral administration of Lonicerae Japonicae Flos and Shuang-Huang-Lian in normal and febrile rats, so as to provide a reference for the rational use of Chinese herbal compound prescriptions and single herbs under pathological conditions. Methods: A yeast-induced fever model was established in rats. Lonicerae Japonicae Flos extract and Shuang-Huang-Lian oral liquid were administered by gavage respectively. Blood samples were collected at different time points, and the plasma concentration of chlorogenic acid was determined by high-performance liquid chromatography to calculate pharmacokinetic parameters. Results: Compared with the normal group, the time to peak concentration of chlorogenic acid in febrile rats after oral administration of Lonicerae Japonicae Flos was prolonged, the peak concentration was decreased, and the area under the concentration-time curve was reduced; after oral administration of Shuang-Huang-Lian, the time to peak concentration of chlorogenic acid was shortened, the peak concentration was increased, and the area under the concentration-time curve was increased. Conclusion: The febrile state can alter the absorption process of chlorogenic acid in vivo, and the influence trends of the single herb Lonicerae Japonicae Flos and the compound prescription Shuang-Huang-Lian are different, suggesting that clinical medication should be adjusted according to the body state and preparation form.

Introduction: Lonicerae Japonicae Flos is the dried flower bud of Lonicera japonica Thunb. of the family Caprifoliaceae, and chlorogenic acid is one of its main active components, possessing antibacterial, antiviral, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant effects. Shuang-Huang-Lian is composed of Lonicerae Japonicae Flos, Forsythiae Fructus, and Scutellariae Radix, and is a commonly used clinical compound preparation for clearing heat and detoxifying. Fever is a common pathological state in exogenous febrile diseases and can affect the absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of drugs in vivo. At present, pharmacokinetic studies on chlorogenic acid are mostly based on normal animals, while comparative studies under pathological conditions are relatively insufficient. In this study, chlorogenic acid was used as the index component to compare the pharmacokinetic differences after oral administration of Lonicerae Japonicae Flos and Shuang-Huang-Lian in normal and febrile rats, aiming to reveal the effects of body state and compound compatibility on the in vivo process of chlorogenic acid and to provide experimental evidence for rational clinical medication.

Key technical analysis

1. Establishment of animal model and grouping
Healthy SD rats were selected and randomly divided into a normal group and a febrile group. The febrile group was subcutaneously injected with dry yeast suspension according to body weight, while the normal group was injected with an equal volume of normal saline. After modeling, rectal temperature was measured at regular intervals, and a body temperature increase of more than 0.5°C with sustained stability was taken as the criterion for successful establishment of the fever model. Each group was further divided into a Lonicerae Japonicae Flos administration subgroup and a Shuang-Huang-Lian administration subgroup, and the corresponding preparations were administered by gavage respectively. This model is simple to operate and has good reproducibility, and can better simulate the clinical state of exogenous fever.

2. Administration regimen and sample collection
Lonicerae Japonicae Flos extract and Shuang-Huang-Lian oral liquid were converted according to chlorogenic acid content and administered by gavage at the same chlorogenic acid dose. Food was withheld but water was allowed before administration. After administration, blood was collected from the orbital venous plexus at 0.083, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, and 12 hours, placed in heparinized centrifuge tubes, centrifuged to separate plasma, and stored at -20°C until determination. The blood collection time points covered the absorption phase, distribution phase, and elimination phase, and could relatively completely reflect the concentration-time process.

3. Plasma sample processing and HPLC determination
Methanol was added to plasma samples to precipitate protein. After vortexing and centrifugation, the supernatant was taken for injection. Chromatographic conditions: C18 column, mobile phase of methanol-phosphoric acid aqueous solution with gradient elution, detection wavelength 327 nm, flow rate 1.0 mL/min, column temperature 30°C. Methodological investigation showed that chlorogenic acid had a good linear relationship in the range of 0.05-10 μg/mL, and the recovery, precision, and stability all met the requirements for biological sample determination. This method is sensitive and accurate, and is suitable for the analysis of large batches of plasma samples.

4. Calculation of pharmacokinetic parameters and statistical analysis
DAS software was used to calculate pharmacokinetic parameters by a non-compartmental model, including time to peak concentration, peak concentration, area under the concentration-time curve, half-life, and mean residence time. One-way analysis of variance was used for comparison between groups, and P<0.05 was considered statistically significant. By comparing the parameter differences between the normal and febrile groups and between the Lonicerae Japonicae Flos and Shuang-Huang-Lian groups, the effects of body state and preparation form on the in vivo process of chlorogenic acid were analyzed.

Results and benefit analysis

The results showed that in the normal group, the time to peak concentration of chlorogenic acid after oral administration of Lonicerae Japonicae Flos was about 0.5 hours, the peak concentration was relatively high, and the area under the concentration-time curve was relatively large. In the febrile group, after oral administration of Lonicerae Japonicae Flos, the time to peak concentration was prolonged to about 1 hour, the peak concentration was decreased, and the area under the concentration-time curve was reduced, suggesting that the febrile state may delay the absorption of chlorogenic acid from Lonicerae Japonicae Flos. In the normal group, the time to peak concentration of chlorogenic acid after oral administration of Shuang-Huang-Lian was about 1 hour, and in the febrile group it was shortened to about 0.5 hours, while the peak concentration and area under the concentration-time curve were both increased, indicating that the febrile state can promote the absorption of chlorogenic acid from Shuang-Huang-Lian. There were no significant differences in half-life and mean residence time among the groups, indicating that fever mainly affects the absorption process and has little effect on the elimination process.

The above differences may be related to changes in gastrointestinal motility, gastric emptying rate, intestinal blood flow, and enzyme activity under the febrile state. In the single herb Lonicerae Japonicae Flos, chlorogenic acid is mainly in free form, and inhibition of gastrointestinal function during fever may delay its absorption; components such as Scutellariae Radix and Forsythiae Fructus in the Shuang-Huang-Lian compound may alter the gastrointestinal environment or promote the dissolution and absorption of chlorogenic acid, thereby showing different trends under the febrile state. These results suggest that when clinically using Chinese herbal preparations containing chlorogenic acid, consideration should be given to whether the patient is in a febrile state and whether the preparation is a single herb or a compound prescription, and the dosage or dosing interval should be adjusted when necessary.

The benefits of this study are as follows: first, it provides a pharmacokinetic basis for the rational clinical use of Lonicerae Japonicae Flos and Shuang-Huang-Lian; second, it provides a methodological reference for comparative studies of Chinese herbal compound prescriptions and single herbs under pathological conditions; third, it suggests that pharmacokinetic studies of Chinese medicines should attach importance to the application of pathological models and avoid extrapolating to clinical practice solely based on data from normal animals. Through technical promotion, it can help primary-level medical and pharmaceutical personnel understand the impact of body state on drug absorption and improve the safety and effectiveness of the use of Chinese patent medicines.

Conclusion: This study compared the pharmacokinetic characteristics of chlorogenic acid after oral administration of Lonicerae Japonicae Flos and Shuang-Huang-Lian in normal and febrile rats. The results showed that the febrile state can alter the absorption process of chlorogenic acid, and the influence trends on the single herb Lonicerae Japonicae Flos and the compound prescription Shuang-Huang-Lian are opposite. Clinical medication should be reasonably adjusted according to the body state and preparation form. In the future, the sample size can be further expanded, and multi-component pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamic indicators can be combined to further explore the mechanism of the interaction between compound compatibility and pathological state.

title: Malate enhances survival of zebrafish against Vibrio alginolyticus infection in the same manner as taurine
text:
Malate Enhances the Survival Ability of Zebrafish Against Vibrio alginolyticus Infection in the Same Manner as Taurine

 Abstract

Objective: To investigate the effect of malate on the survival rate of zebrafish infected with *Vibrio alginolyticus*, and to compare it with the protective effect of taurine, thereby revealing the potential shared mechanism of action between the two. Methods: A total of 540 healthy zebrafish were randomly divided into a control group, an infection group, a taurine group (100 mg/L), and a malate group (100 mg/L). After 7 d of pre-immersion treatment, the fish were challenged with *Vibrio alginolyticus* via intraperitoneal injection, and the 7 d cumulative survival rate was recorded. Liver antioxidant enzyme activities, inflammatory cytokine expression, and intestinal microbiota composition were measured. Results: The 7 d cumulative survival rates of zebrafish in the malate group and taurine group were 68.5% and 70.2%, respectively, significantly higher than the 31.5% in the infection group (*P*<0.05).
