In both treatment groups, superoxide dismutase (SOD) and catalase (CAT) activities were significantly increased, malondialdehyde (MDA) content was decreased, the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and TNF-α was downregulated, and the expression of the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 was upregulated. The abundance of beneficial intestinal bacteria increased, while the relative abundance of *Vibrio* decreased. There were no significant differences between the malate and taurine groups in any indicator (*P*>0.05). Conclusion: Malate can enhance the ability of zebrafish to resist *Vibrio alginolyticus* infection through antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and intestinal microbiota-regulating pathways. Its protective effect is comparable to that of taurine, and the two may share similar metabolic regulatory mechanisms.

Keywords: malate; taurine; zebrafish; *Vibrio alginolyticus*; antioxidation; intestinal microbiota

 1 Introduction

*Vibrio alginolyticus* is a common opportunistic pathogen in aquaculture, capable of causing mass mortality of fish and shrimp, resulting in severe economic losses to China's marine aquaculture industry. The problems of drug resistance and drug residues caused by antibiotic abuse are becoming increasingly prominent, making the development of safe and efficient immunostimulants a research hotspot. Taurine, as a sulfur-containing β-amino acid, has been proven to enhance the antioxidant capacity and anti-infection ability of fish. Malate is an important intermediate of the tricarboxylic acid cycle. Recent studies have found that it possesses antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and energy metabolism-regulating functions, and has potential intersections with taurine in metabolic pathways (e.g., both participate in mitochondrial function regulation). However, whether malate can enhance the ability of fish to resist *Vibrio* infection like taurine remains unclear. Zebrafish (*Danio rerio*) is highly homologous to humans in genome and is an ideal model for infection immunity research. In this study, zebrafish were used as subjects to compare the effects of malate and taurine against *Vibrio alginolyticus* infection and to explore their mechanisms, providing a theoretical basis for the development of novel immunostimulants in aquaculture.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Experimental Animals and Strains

A total of 540 healthy AB strain zebrafish (body length 3.0±0.5 cm) were purchased from the China Zebrafish Resource Center and acclimated in a recirculating water system (28±1°C, pH 7.2±0.3) for 2 weeks. *Vibrio alginolyticus* (ATCC 17749) was preserved in our laboratory, cultured in LB medium at 28°C to the logarithmic phase (OD₆₀₀=0.8), centrifuged and washed, then resuspended in PBS to 1×10⁷ CFU/mL.

 2.2 Experimental Design

Zebrafish were randomly divided into 4 groups (3 replicates per group, 45 fish per replicate): control group (Group C, no infection and no treatment), infection group (Group V, infected without drug administration), taurine group (Group T, immersed in 100 mg/L taurine), and malate group (Group M, immersed in 100 mg/L malate). After 7 d of pre-immersion, all groups except Group C were intraperitoneally injected with 20 μL of bacterial suspension (1×10⁶ CFU/fish), while Group C was injected with an equal volume of PBS. After challenge, immersion administration was continued, and the 7 d cumulative survival rate was recorded.

 2.3 Indicator Measurement

At 48 h after challenge, 9 fish were randomly selected from each group, and the liver and intestine were dissected. SOD and CAT activities and MDA content were measured using kits (Nanjing Jiancheng); IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-10 mRNA expression was measured by RT-qPCR (β-actin as internal reference); high-throughput sequencing of the 16S rRNA V3-V4 region of intestinal microbiota was performed to analyze genus-level composition.

 2.4 Data Processing

Data were expressed as Mean±SD. One-way analysis of variance was performed using SPSS 22.0, with Duncan's multiple range test. *P*<0.05 was considered a significant difference.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Survival Rate

At 7 d after challenge, the cumulative survival rate of Group V was only 31.5%, while those of Group T and Group M were 70.2% and 68.5%, respectively, both significantly higher than that of Group V (*P*<0.05), but there was no significant difference between Group T and Group M (*P*>0.05) (Table 1). This indicates that both malate and taurine can significantly enhance the ability of zebrafish to resist *Vibrio alginolyticus* infection.

Table 1 Cumulative 7 d survival rate of zebrafish in each group

| Group | Survival rate/% |
|------|----------|
| Group C | 96.7±2.1ᵃ |
| Group V | 31.5±4.3ᶜ |
| Group T | 70.2±3.8ᵇ |
| Group M | 68.5±4.1ᵇ |

Note: Different letters in the same column indicate significant differences (*P*<0.05).

 3.2 Liver Antioxidant Indicators

Compared with Group V, SOD and CAT activities in Group T and Group M were significantly increased (*P*<0.05), and MDA content was significantly decreased (*P*<0.05); there was no significant difference between Group T and Group M (Table 2). This indicates that both malate and taurine can enhance the body's antioxidant defense and alleviate oxidative damage.

Table 2 Liver antioxidant indicators in each group

| Group | SOD/(U·mg⁻¹) | CAT/(U·mg⁻¹) | MDA/(nmol·mg⁻¹) |
|------|----------------|----------------|-------------------|
| Group C | 85.3±5.2ᵃ | 42.1±3.5ᵃ | 2.1±0.3ᶜ |
| Group V | 48.6±4.7ᶜ | 23.8±2.9ᶜ | 5.8±0.6ᵃ |
| Group T | 76.4±5.8ᵇ | 38.5±3.2ᵇ | 3.0±0.4ᵇ |
| Group M | 74.9±6.1ᵇ | 37.2±3.7ᵇ | 3.2±0.5ᵇ |

 3.3 Inflammatory Cytokine Expression

The expression of IL-1β and TNF-α in Group V was significantly higher than that in Group C, while IL-10 was significantly decreased; the expression of IL-1β and TNF-α in Group T and Group M was significantly downregulated compared with Group V, and IL-10 was significantly upregulated (*P*<0.05), with no significant difference between the two treatment groups (Figure 1). This indicates that both can inhibit excessive inflammatory responses.

 3.4 Intestinal Microbiota

The relative abundance of *Vibrio* in Group V was significantly higher than that in Group C, while the abundance of *Lactobacillus* and *Cetobacterium* was decreased. Compared with Group V, the abundance of *Vibrio* in Group T and Group M decreased by 42.3% and 40.7%, respectively, and the abundance of *Lactobacillus* increased by 1.8-fold and 1.7-fold, respectively, with no significant difference between the two treatment groups. Both malate and taurine can reshape the intestinal microbiota and inhibit pathogen colonization.

 4 Discussion

This study is the first to confirm that malate can significantly improve the survival rate of zebrafish against *Vibrio alginolyticus* infection, with an effect comparable to that of taurine. *Vibrio alginolyticus* infection induces host oxidative stress and inflammatory storms, leading to tissue damage and death. This study found that both malate and taurine can increase SOD and CAT activities and reduce MDA content, indicating that they scavenge reactive oxygen species by enhancing the antioxidant enzyme system and alleviate lipid peroxidation damage. Meanwhile, both can downregulate IL-1β and TNF-α and upregulate IL-10, inhibiting excessive inflammatory responses, which is consistent with the known anti-inflammatory effects of taurine.

Intestinal microbiota analysis further revealed that both malate and taurine can reduce the abundance of *Vibrio* and increase beneficial bacteria such as *Lactobacillus*, suggesting that they may indirectly enhance anti-infection ability through regulating the microbiota-immune axis. Notably, there is a metabolic connection between malate and taurine: taurine can be synthesized via the cysteine sulfinic acid decarboxylation pathway, while malate, as a TCA cycle intermediate, can promote mitochondrial energy metabolism. Both can maintain mitochondrial functional homeostasis and reduce ROS production. In addition, malate can be converted to oxaloacetate to participate in aspartate metabolism, and aspartate is an indirect precursor for taurine synthesis, which may be the molecular basis for their similar effects.

This study also has limitations: no different concentration gradients were set, and the mechanism exploration remains at the phenotypic level. Future studies will use gene knockout or metabolomics approaches to further elucidate the shared signaling pathways of malate and taurine.

 5 Conclusion

Immersion with malate (100 mg/L) can significantly increase the 7 d survival rate of zebrafish infected with *Vibrio alginolyticus* to 68.5%, comparable to the effect of taurine (70.2%). Its mechanism involves enhancing liver antioxidant capacity, inhibiting excessive inflammatory responses, and regulating intestinal microbiota structure. Malate is expected to serve as a substitute or supplementary aquatic immunostimulant for taurine, with promising application prospects.

title: Construction of a high-density, high-quality genetic map of cultivated lotus (Nelumbo nucifera) using next-generation sequencing
text:
Construction of a High-Density, High-Quality Genetic Map of Cultivated Lotus (*Nelumbo nucifera*) Using Next-Generation Sequencing Technology

Abstract: Lotus (*Nelumbo nucifera*) is an important aquatic economic crop in China, possessing edible, ornamental, and cultural value. However, due to the lack of a high-density genetic map, molecular breeding and genomics research in lotus have long been constrained. In this study, an F₂ population derived from a cross between the cultivated lotus varieties "Elian No. 6" and "Mantianxing" was used as material. Whole-genome resequencing was performed using next-generation sequencing (NGS) technology, generating a large number of single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) markers, and a high-density, high-quality genetic map was constructed. The map contains 8 linkage groups, covers a total genetic distance of 1,012.6 cM, with an average marker interval of 0.38 cM, and comprises a total of 2,668 SNP markers. Compared with existing maps, this map shows significantly improved marker density and more uniform distribution of markers across chromosomes. The construction of this map provides a powerful tool for QTL mapping of important traits, gene cloning, and marker-assisted breeding in lotus.

Keywords: lotus; genetic map; next-generation sequencing; SNP; molecular breeding

1 Introduction

Lotus (*Nelumbo nucifera*) is a perennial aquatic herb of the genus *Nelumbo* in the family Nelumbonaceae, with a cultivation history of over three thousand years in China. As an important aquatic vegetable and ornamental plant, the planting area and yield of lotus have been increasing year by year, and it has become an important industry for agricultural structural adjustment and farmers' income growth in many regions. However, compared with major crops such as rice and maize, genetics and genomics research in lotus started relatively late, and the level of molecular breeding lags behind. One of the key factors restricting molecular breeding in lotus is the lack of a high-density, high-quality genetic map.

Genetic maps are fundamental tools in genetics research and can be used for QTL mapping, map-based cloning, comparative genomic analysis, and marker-assisted selection. Early lotus genetic maps were mainly based on dominant markers such as AFLP, RAPD, and SRAP, which had few markers, low density, and were difficult to transfer between laboratories. With the rapid development of next-generation sequencing (NGS) technology, the development of SNP markers based on whole-genome resequencing has become the mainstream method for constructing high-density genetic maps. This method has the advantages of high throughput, low cost, and codominant markers, making it particularly suitable for genetic map construction in non-model crops.

This study aims to use NGS technology to perform whole-genome resequencing of an F₂ population of cultivated lotus, develop large-scale SNP markers, and construct a high-density, high-quality genetic map, providing foundational support for genetic research and molecular breeding in lotus.

2 Key Technical Analysis

2.1 Population Construction and Sequencing Strategy

In this study, the cultivated lotus variety "Elian No. 6" was selected as the female parent and "Mantianxing" as the male parent, which differ significantly in traits such as plant architecture, flower color, and rhizome quality. F₁ was obtained through artificial hybridization, and the F₂ population was produced by self-pollination of F₁, comprising a total of 200 individuals. This population size is moderate, ensuring effective detection of recombination events while facilitating sequencing cost control.

Regarding the sequencing strategy, deep resequencing (approximately 30×) was performed on the two parents, and low-depth resequencing (approximately 5×) was performed on F₂ individuals. Although low-depth sequencing has limited coverage for individual samples, genotype imputation can be effectively achieved through joint population analysis, improving the accuracy of marker genotyping. This "deep parent + shallow progeny" strategy significantly reduces costs while ensuring map quality, making it suitable for technology dissemination.

2.2 SNP Marker Development and Screening

BWA software was used to align sequencing reads of parents and progeny to the lotus reference genome (*Nelumbo nucifera* genome v1.1), and GATK was used for SNP calling. First, homozygous and differential SNP loci were screened in the parents, requiring clear parental genotypes, sequencing depth ≥10×, and quality value ≥30. Subsequently, genotyping was performed in the F₂ population, and markers with high missing rates (>20%), severe segregation distortion (P<0.001), and high Mendelian error rates were removed. Finally, 2,668 high-quality SNP markers were obtained for map construction.

2.3 Linkage Analysis and Map Construction

JoinMap 5.0 software was used for linkage analysis. First, recombination rates and LOD values between markers were calculated, with a LOD threshold of 6.0 and a maximum recombination rate of 0.4. The regression mapping algorithm was used for grouping and ordering, followed by the Kosambi function for calculating genetic distances. For regions with abnormal marker intervals during ordering, correction was performed in combination with the physical positions in the reference genome to ensure that marker order was consistent with the physical map. Finally, markers were divided into 8 linkage groups, consistent with the haploid chromosome number of lotus.

2.4 Map Quality Assessment

Map quality was assessed in three ways: first, marker distribution uniformity, by calculating the coefficient of variation of genetic distances between adjacent markers; second, collinearity analysis, by comparing the genetic map with the reference genome physical map to check for inversions or translocations; third, comparison with published lotus genetic maps to evaluate marker density and coverage. The results showed that the markers in this map were uniformly distributed, with good collinearity, and no obvious assembly errors were found.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

3.1 Basic Characteristics of the Map

The constructed genetic map contains 8 linkage groups, with a total genetic distance of 1,012.6 cM, an average marker interval of 0.38 cM, and a maximum interval of 3.2 cM. The length of each linkage group ranges from 98.4 cM to 156.7 cM, with the number of markers ranging from 248 to 412. Compared with existing lotus genetic maps, the number of markers increased by approximately 5-fold, and the average interval was reduced by approximately 80%. The distribution of markers on linkage groups was relatively uniform, with no obvious clustering regions.

3.2 Collinearity and Recombination Characteristics

Anchoring the genetic map markers to the reference genome revealed that 99.2% of marker orders were consistent with physical positions, indicating high map accuracy. Recombination hotspot analysis showed that recombination rates were higher at chromosome ends and lower near centromeres, consistent with general patterns of recombination distribution in plants. These results provide recombination information for candidate gene screening in subsequent QTL mapping.

3.3 Application Benefits

This map can be directly used for QTL mapping of important traits in lotus. For example, using this map for QTL analysis of traits such as rhizome enlargement, flower color, and flowering time in the F₂ population, multiple major QTL intervals have been preliminarily identified. In addition, SNP markers in the map can be used for marker-assisted selection to accelerate the breeding of superior varieties. For technology dissemination, the method used in this study has controllable costs and standardized operational procedures, making it suitable for promotion and use in provincial academies of agricultural sciences and universities.

3.4 Role in Promoting Industrial Development

The lotus industry is developing from traditional cultivation toward quality-oriented and specialized directions. The high-density genetic map provides technical support for breeding lotus varieties with high yield, disease resistance, stress tolerance, and strong ornamental value. Through marker-assisted selection, the breeding cycle can be shortened from the traditional 6–8 years to 3–4 years, significantly improving breeding efficiency. At the same time, the map can also be used for genetic diversity analysis of lotus germplasm resources and variety identification, providing a basis for intellectual property protection.

4 Conclusion

In this study, next-generation sequencing technology was used to successfully construct a high-density, high-quality genetic map of cultivated lotus. The map contains 2,668 SNP markers, covers 8 linkage groups, with an average marker interval of 0.38 cM, uniform marker distribution, and good collinearity. The construction of this map lays a solid foundation for QTL mapping, gene cloning, and marker-assisted breeding in lotus, and is of great significance for promoting technological upgrading of the lotus industry. In the future, the population size can be further expanded, marker density increased, and multi-trait joint analysis conducted in combination with phenomics to enhance the application value of the map.

title: Comparative transcriptome analysis uncovers regulatory roles of long non-coding RNAs involved in resistance to powdery mildew in melon
text:
Comparative Transcriptome Analysis Reveals the Regulatory Role of Long Non-Coding RNAs in Powdery Mildew Resistance of Melon

Abstract: To investigate the regulatory mechanism of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in powdery mildew resistance of melon, this study used the resistant cultivar 'MR-1' and the susceptible cultivar 'Top Mark' as materials, and performed transcriptome sequencing at 0, 24, 48, and 72 h after inoculation with Podosphaera xanthii. A total of 4,872 lncRNAs were identified, of which 1,263 were differentially expressed in the resistant cultivar. Functional enrichment analysis showed that the target genes of these lncRNAs were significantly enriched in plant-pathogen interaction, MAPK signaling pathway, and phenylpropanoid biosynthesis. Further construction of a ceRNA network revealed that lncRNA-MSTRG.12345 may regulate SPL transcription factors by sponging miR156a, thereby activating downstream disease resistance genes. qRT-PCR validated the expression patterns of 8 key lncRNAs and their target genes, which were consistent with the sequencing results. This study provides new candidate lncRNA resources for molecular breeding of powdery mildew resistance in melon.

Keywords: melon; powdery mildew; long non-coding RNA; comparative transcriptome; ceRNA network

1 Introduction

Melon (*Cucumis melo* L.) is an important horticultural crop worldwide, and powdery mildew (*Podosphaera xanthii*) often causes severe yield reduction. Current disease resistance breeding mostly focuses on protein-coding genes, while the role of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) in plant immunity remains unclear. lncRNAs can participate in stress responses by regulating gene transcription, splicing, and acting as miRNA sponges. In this study, by comparing the transcriptomes of resistant and susceptible melon cultivars after inoculation with Podosphaera xanthii, differentially expressed lncRNAs were systematically identified and a ceRNA regulatory network was constructed, aiming to reveal the disease resistance mechanism mediated by lncRNAs.

2 Materials and Methods

2.1 Plant Materials and Treatment
The resistant cultivar 'MR-1' and the susceptible cultivar 'Top Mark' were grown in an artificial climate chamber (25°C/18°C, 16 h light/8 h dark). At the three-leaf stage, uniform spray inoculation was performed with a spore suspension (1×10⁶ spores·mL⁻¹), and the control was sprayed with sterile water. Leaves were collected at 0, 24, 48, and 72 h, respectively, and quickly frozen in liquid nitrogen.

2.2 Transcriptome Sequencing and lncRNA Identification
Three biological replicates were used for each sample, totaling 24 libraries. Sequencing was performed using Illumina NovaSeq 6000, and after obtaining clean reads, they were aligned to the melon reference genome (Melon DHL92 v3.6.1). Transcripts were assembled using StringTie, and lncRNAs were screened through CPC, CNCI, and the Pfam database (length ≥200 nt, exon number ≥2, FPKM ≥0.5).

2.3 Differential Expression and Functional Enrichment
DESeq2 was used to identify differentially expressed lncRNAs (|log₂FC|≥1, FDR<0.05). Target genes were predicted through cis-regulation (±100 kb) and trans-regulation (Pearson |r|>0.9). GO and KEGG enrichment were performed using clusterProfiler.

2.4 ceRNA Network Construction and qRT-PCR Validation
Based on miRBase, lncRNA-miRNA-mRNA interactions were predicted, and Cytoscape was used to construct the network. Eight lncRNAs and their target genes were selected for qRT-PCR validation, with *Actin* as the internal reference, and relative expression levels were calculated using the 2⁻ΔΔCt method.

3 Results and Analysis

3.1 Transcriptome Overview and lncRNA Identification
A total of 186.4 Gb clean data were obtained, with Q30≥93.2%. A total of 4,872 lncRNAs were identified, of which 1,263 were differentially expressed in the resistant cultivar (Figure 1A). Compared with the susceptible cultivar, 487 and 392 lncRNAs were upregulated in the resistant cultivar at 24 h and 48 h, respectively.

3.2 Functional Enrichment of Target Genes of Differential lncRNAs
Cis-target genes were significantly enriched in "plant-pathogen interaction" (ko04626) and "MAPK signaling pathway" (ko04016), including *WRKY33*, *PR1*, and *EDS1*, etc. Trans-target genes were enriched in "phenylpropanoid biosynthesis" (ko00940), involving *PAL*, *C4H*, and *4CL*.

3.3 ceRNA Network Analysis
A ceRNA network containing 38 lncRNAs, 12 miRNAs, and 56 mRNAs was constructed. Among them, lncRNA-MSTRG.12345 had 6.8-fold higher expression in the resistant cultivar than in the susceptible cultivar (48 h), and its binding free energy with miR156a was the lowest (-38.6 kcal·mol⁻¹). miR156a targets *SPL6*, and *SPL6* can activate *PR1* expression.

3.4 qRT-PCR Validation
The expression trends of the 8 lncRNAs were consistent with RNA-seq (r=0.91, P<0.01). The expression level of lncRNA-MSTRG.12345 in the resistant cultivar at 48 h was 5.2 times that in the susceptible cultivar, and its target genes *SPL6* and *PR1* were upregulated by 3.8-fold and 7.1-fold, respectively.

4 Discussion

This study systematically compared, for the first time, the lncRNA expression profiles of resistant and susceptible melon cultivars in response to Podosphaera xanthii. Similar to lncRNAs regulating *PR* genes in Arabidopsis, we found that lncRNA-MSTRG.12345 may enhance resistance through the "miR156a-SPL6-PR1" module. In addition, the differential expression of lncRNAs related to the phenylpropanoid pathway suggests a synergistic role of cell wall reinforcement and phytoalexin synthesis in disease resistance. Unlike the rice lncRNA *ELE* regulating immunity, melon lncRNAs tend to be finely regulated through the ceRNA mechanism. The limitation of this study is that no genetic transformation validation was performed, and future work will use VIGS technology to silence candidate lncRNAs.

5 Conclusion

This study identified 1,263 melon lncRNAs responding to Podosphaera xanthii and revealed a new mechanism by which lncRNA-MSTRG.12345 regulates the *SPL6*-*PR1* pathway by sponging miR156a, providing a theoretical basis and candidate molecular targets for disease resistance breeding in melon.

title: ACC Deaminase from Lysobacter gummosus OH17 Can Promote Root Growth in Oryza sativa Nipponbare Plants
text:
Role of ACC Deaminase in *Lysobacter gummosus* OH17 in Promoting Root Growth of Rice Nipponbare

Abstract: To investigate the mechanism by which *Lysobacter gummosus* OH17 promotes rice root growth, this study analyzed the biological function of ACC deaminase in this strain through enzyme activity assays, gene cloning and expression analysis, combined with rice inoculation experiments. The results showed that the intracellular ACC deaminase activity of strain OH17 was 0.86 U/mg, and the expression of its encoding gene was significantly upregulated under ACC induction. After inoculation with this strain, the root length, root fresh weight, and lateral root number of rice Nipponbare seedlings increased by 28.6%, 34.2%, and 41.5%, respectively, compared with the control, and the root IAA content increased by approximately 1.6-fold. These results indicate that ACC deaminase promotes rice root growth by reducing the level of ethylene precursor and alleviating the inhibition of root elongation by ethylene. This strain can serve as a candidate strain for microbial fertilizer, providing a reference for the promotion of root growth-promoting technology in green rice production.

1 Introduction

Rice is a major food crop in China, and its root development directly affects nutrient uptake and yield formation. Excessive application of traditional chemical fertilizers leads to soil compaction and environmental pollution. The use of beneficial microorganisms to promote crop root growth has become an important direction in green agriculture. Plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) can promote plant growth through nitrogen fixation, phosphate solubilization, siderophore production, and secretion of plant hormones, among which the role of ACC deaminase has attracted particular attention.

ACC deaminase can catalyze the decomposition of 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate (ACC), the precursor of ethylene synthesis, into α-ketobutyrate and ammonia, thereby reducing the ethylene level in plants. When plants are subjected to stress or rapid growth, ethylene accumulation inhibits root elongation. PGPR with ACC deaminase activity can "intercept" ACC exuded from roots, alleviating the inhibitory effect of ethylene and indirectly promoting root development. *Lysobacter gummosus* is a biocontrol and growth-promoting bacterium that has received attention in recent years, but systematic studies on the effect of its ACC deaminase on rice roots are still limited. In this study, *Lysobacter gummosus* OH17 isolated from the rice rhizosphere was used as material to analyze its ACC deaminase characteristics and its promoting effect on the root growth of rice Nipponbare, aiming to provide a theoretical basis for the field application of this strain.

2 Analysis of Key Technologies

2.1 Strain Culture and ACC Deaminase Activity Assay

Strain OH17 was inoculated into DF minimal medium and cultured at 30°C with shaking at 180 r/min for 24 h. Cells were collected by centrifugation, disrupted by ultrasonication, and the supernatant was taken as crude enzyme extract. Using ACC as substrate, the amount of α-ketobutyrate produced in the reaction system was measured to calculate enzyme activity. The results showed that the ACC deaminase activity of strain OH17 was 0.86 U/mg, significantly higher than that of the control strain. Enzymatic characterization showed that the optimal pH of the enzyme was 7.5 and the optimal temperature was 30°C, with good stability in the range of pH 6.5–8.5 and 20–35°C, suitable for the rice rhizosphere environmental conditions.

2.2 Cloning and Expression Analysis of the ACC Deaminase Gene

Primers were designed based on the conserved sequences of reported ACC deaminase genes. The target gene fragment was amplified from the OH17 genome, and after sequencing, it was aligned with homologous sequences in GenBank, showing a similarity of over 98%. RT-qPCR was used to detect gene expression levels under different ACC concentrations. The results showed that when the ACC concentration in the medium increased from 0 to 5 mmol/L, the relative gene expression increased by approximately 4.3-fold; the expression level was very low without ACC, indicating that the gene is induced by ACC. This characteristic ensures that the strain efficiently expresses enzyme activity in the ACC-enriched region of the plant rhizosphere.

2.3 Design of Rice Inoculation Experiment

Rice Nipponbare was used as the test variety. Seeds were sterilized, germinated, and sown in nutrient pots filled with sterilized vermiculite. Two treatments were set up: control (irrigated with sterile water) and inoculation treatment (irrigated with OH17 bacterial suspension at a concentration of 1×10⁸ CFU/mL), with 30 plants per treatment and 3 replicates. The culture conditions were 28°C, 16 h light/8 h dark, and 70% relative humidity. After 14 d of culture, root length, root fresh weight, lateral root number, and root IAA content were measured.

2.4 Determination of Root Ethylene Release and IAA Content

Root ethylene release was measured by gas chromatography. The results showed that the ethylene release of rice roots inoculated with strain OH17 was reduced by 37.8% compared with the control, indicating that ACC deaminase effectively reduced ethylene production. Meanwhile, the root IAA content was measured by high-performance liquid chromatography, and the inoculation treatment increased by approximately 1.6-fold compared with the control. The decrease in ethylene and the increase in IAA jointly promoted root cell elongation and lateral root formation.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

The inoculation experiment results showed that strain OH17 significantly promoted the root growth of rice Nipponbare. Compared with the control, the root length of rice seedlings in the inoculation treatment increased by 28.6%, root fresh weight increased by 34.2%, and lateral root number increased by 41.5%, with all differences reaching significant levels (P<0.05). Root morphological observation showed that the roots of the inoculation treatment were white and bright with strong vigor, and the root tip elongation zone was significantly extended.

From a mechanistic perspective, strain OH17 decomposes rhizosphere ACC through ACC deaminase, reducing root ethylene release and relieving the inhibition of root cell elongation by ethylene; at the same time, the metabolic activity of the strain may indirectly regulate the auxin balance in roots, promoting lateral root primordium differentiation. The synergistic effect of the two forms a "ethylene reduction–growth promotion" root growth-promoting model.

From the perspective of application benefits, this strain has the following advantages: first, high enzyme activity and strong environmental adaptability, suitable for colonization in the rice rhizosphere; second, stable growth-promoting effect, which can be observed within 14 d; third, simple culture conditions, easy for large-scale fermentation production. Based on an estimated application of 1.5×10¹² CFU of bacterial agent per hectare, the amount of chemical fertilizer can be reduced by 10%–15%, with a yield increase potential of approximately 5%–8%, providing both economic and ecological benefits. This technology is suitable for supporting application during rice seedling raising and transplanting periods, especially for fields with continuous cropping obstacles and low-temperature stress.

4 Conclusion

This study clarified the ACC deaminase activity and gene expression characteristics of *Lysobacter gummosus* OH17, and confirmed that this strain significantly promotes the increase in root length, root fresh weight, and lateral root number of Nipponbare seedlings by reducing root ethylene release and increasing IAA content in rice. The optimal pH of ACC deaminase from this strain is 7.5 and the optimal temperature is 30°C, suitable for the rice rhizosphere environment. The results provide strain resources and theoretical support for the development of microbial fertilizers with ACC deaminase as the core. Next, field experiments should be carried out to verify the growth-promoting stability of this strain under different soil types and climatic conditions, and to optimize the formulation and application technology of the bacterial agent, promoting its large-scale application in green rice production.

title: Traditional Chinese Medicine for Alzheimer's Disease and Other Cognitive Impairment: A Review
text:
A Review of Research on Traditional Chinese Medicine in the Treatment of Alzheimer's Disease and Other Cognitive Impairments

Abstract: With the acceleration of population aging, the incidence of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and other cognitive impairment disorders has been rising year by year, becoming a public health issue that seriously affects the quality of life of the elderly. Modern medicine still lacks effective curative means for AD treatment, while traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), with its characteristics of multi-target, multi-pathway, and holistic regulation, has demonstrated unique advantages in the prevention and treatment of cognitive impairment. This paper systematically reviews recent research on TCM in the treatment of AD and other cognitive impairments, summarizing from the perspectives of etiology and pathogenesis, single herbs and active components, compound preparations, and acupuncture therapy, and analyzes the findings in conjunction with clinical efficacy data. Research has found that TCM can improve cognitive function through multiple mechanisms including anti-oxidative stress, inhibition of neuroinflammation, regulation of neurotransmitters, and reduction of β-amyloid deposition. This paper aims to provide a reference basis for further research and clinical application of TCM in the prevention and treatment of cognitive impairment.

Keywords: Traditional Chinese Medicine; Alzheimer's disease; cognitive impairment; acupuncture; neuroprotection

 1 Introduction

Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disease characterized primarily by progressive cognitive decline, with pathological features mainly including senile plaques formed by β-amyloid (Aβ) deposition, neurofibrillary tangles formed by hyperphosphorylated tau protein, and neuronal loss. According to statistics from the International Alzheimer's Association, there are approximately 50 million dementia patients worldwide, and this number is projected to increase to 152 million by 2050, with approximately 60%-70% being AD patients. As a populous country, China has a dementia prevalence rate of approximately 6.0% among people over 60 years old, with an AD prevalence rate of approximately 3.9%, imposing a heavy burden on families and society.

Currently, commonly used clinical AD treatment drugs mainly include cholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine, etc.) and NMDA receptor antagonists (memantine), but these drugs can only temporarily relieve symptoms and cannot stop disease progression, and they have side effects such as gastrointestinal reactions and bradycardia. In recent years, TCM has received widespread attention in the field of AD and cognitive impairment prevention and treatment due to its theoretical system of "holistic concept" and "treatment based on syndrome differentiation," as well as its pharmacological characteristics of multiple components, multiple targets, and multiple pathways. Multiple clinical studies have shown that TCM has potential value in improving patients' cognitive scores, activities of daily living, and delaying disease progression. This paper intends to systematically review the research progress of TCM in the treatment of AD and other cognitive impairments, with the aim of providing references for subsequent research.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Literature Search Strategy

This paper used "traditional Chinese medicine," "Alzheimer's disease," "cognitive impairment," "acupuncture," "Chinese herbal compound," "neuroprotection" and other terms as keywords to search for relevant literature published from January 2015 to December 2024 in databases including China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), Wanfang Database, and PubMed. Inclusion criteria: (1) clinical studies, animal experiments, or reviews on TCM treatment of AD or cognitive impairment; (2) reasonable study design with complete data; (3) published in core journals or SCI-indexed journals. Exclusion criteria: (1) duplicate publications; (2) insufficient sample size or incomplete data; (3) non-Chinese and non-English literature.

 2.2 Data Extraction and Quality Assessment

Two researchers independently extracted literature information, including authors, publication year, study type, sample size, intervention measures, and main outcome indicators. The Cochrane risk of bias assessment tool was used to evaluate the quality of randomized controlled trials, and the SYRCLE animal experiment risk of bias assessment tool was used to evaluate animal experiments. A total of 86 articles meeting the criteria were included, including 32 clinical studies, 41 animal experiments, and 13 reviews.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 TCM Understanding of the Etiology and Pathogenesis of AD

Although traditional Chinese medicine does not have the name "Alzheimer's disease," based on its clinical manifestations, it can be classified under the categories of "dementia," "idiocy," and "forgetfulness." The "Jingyue Quanshu" records: "Dementia syndrome, in cases where there is ordinarily no phlegm, but due to stagnation, or frustration, or excessive worry, or confusion, or fright, gradually leads to dementia." TCM believes that the disease location of AD is in the brain, closely related to the heart, liver, spleen, and kidney, and its basic pathogenesis is root deficiency and branch excess. Root deficiency is mainly kidney essence depletion and qi-blood insufficiency, while branch excess is mainly phlegm turbidity, blood stasis, and qi stagnation. The kidney governs bones and generates marrow; the brain is the sea of marrow. When kidney essence is depleted, the sea of marrow is insufficient, the brain loses nourishment, and the spirit-mind loses its function; when phlegm and blood stasis interconnect and obstruct the brain collaterals, the clear orifices are obscured and the spirit mechanism loses control. Therefore, tonifying the kidney and filling essence, resolving phlegm and removing blood stasis, and opening the orifices and awakening the spirit are commonly used treatment methods.

 3.2 Research on Single Herbs and Active Components

In recent years, a large number of studies have confirmed that active components of various Chinese herbs have neuroprotective effects. Ginsenoside Rg1 can improve learning and memory abilities in AD model mice by inhibiting Aβ-induced neuroinflammation and oxidative stress. An animal experiment showed that after 8 weeks of intervention with ginsenoside Rg1 (20 mg/kg), the escape latency in the Morris water maze of APP/PS1 transgenic mice was shortened by approximately 35.6%, and the neuronal apoptosis rate in the hippocampal CA1 region was reduced by 42.3%. Huperzine A is an alkaloid extracted from Huperzia serrata and is a reversible cholinesterase inhibitor. Clinical studies have shown that it can significantly improve the ADAS-cog score of AD patients, with an effective rate of approximately 68.5%. In addition, components such as curcumin, resveratrol, icariin, and astragaloside IV have all been confirmed to exert cognitive protective effects through anti-oxidation, anti-inflammation, and regulation of autophagy.

 3.3 Research on Chinese Herbal Compound Preparations

Chinese herbal compounds are based on treatment based on syndrome differentiation, conducting multi-target intervention for the complex pathogenesis of AD. Commonly used clinical compounds include Bushen Yizhi Formula, Danggui Shaoyao San, Huanglian Jiedu Tang, and Ditan Tang. A multicenter randomized controlled trial enrolled 240 patients with mild to moderate AD. The treatment group was given Bushen Yizhi Formula (composed of Rehmannia glutinosa, Cornus officinalis, Lycium barbarum, Acorus tatarinowii, etc.) combined with donepezil, while the control group was given donepezil alone. After 24 weeks of treatment, the MMSE score of the treatment group increased by 3.2 points from baseline, while the control group increased by 1.8 points, with a statistically significant difference between groups (P<0.05); the improvement in ADL scores in the treatment group was also superior to that in the control group. Another study on vascular dementia showed that Danggui Shaoyao San could improve patients' cognitive function, and its mechanism may be related to regulating brain acetylcholine levels and inhibiting platelet aggregation.

 3.4 Research on Acupuncture Therapy

Acupuncture, as a characteristic therapy of TCM, is widely used in the treatment of cognitive impairment. Commonly used acupoints include Baihui, Sishencong, Shenting, Fengchi, Zusanli, Sanyinjiao, etc. A meta-analysis included 15 randomized controlled trials with a total of 1,200 AD patients, and the results showed that acupuncture combined with medication was superior to medication alone in improving MMSE scores (WMD=1.86, 95%CI: 1.23-2.49, P<0.001). Animal experiments have shown that electroacupuncture at Baihui and Shenshu acupoints can reduce hippocampal Aβ deposition in AD model rats, inhibit tau protein phosphorylation, and upregulate synaptophysin expression, thereby improving synaptic plasticity. In addition, acupuncture can also regulate gut microbiota and exert neuroprotective effects through the "brain-gut axis" pathway.

 3.5 Analysis of Mechanisms of TCM in Treating Cognitive Impairment

Based on comprehensive literature analysis, the mechanisms of TCM in treating AD and other cognitive impairments mainly include the following aspects: (1) Anti-oxidative stress: scavenging free radicals, increasing superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity, and reducing malondialdehyde (MDA) levels; (2) Inhibiting neuroinflammation: reducing the release of pro-inflammatory factors such as IL-1β and TNF-α, and inhibiting excessive activation of microglia; (3) Regulating neurotransmitters: increasing acetylcholine levels and enhancing cholinergic neurotransmission; (4) Reducing Aβ deposition: promoting Aβ clearance and inhibiting Aβ aggregation; (5) Inhibiting tau protein phosphorylation: regulating the activity of kinases such as GSK-3β and CDK5; (6) Improving mitochondrial function: protecting neuronal energy metabolism; (7) Regulating gut microbiota: influencing central nervous system function through the brain-gut axis.

 4 Discussion

This paper reviews recent research progress on TCM in the treatment of AD and other cognitive impairments. The results indicate that TCM has unique advantages in improving cognitive function and delaying disease progression, and its mechanisms of action involve multiple targets and multiple pathways. However, current research still has the following problems: First, clinical study sample sizes are generally small, and there are few multicenter, large-sample, double-blind randomized controlled trials, so the level of evidence needs to be improved; Second, the components of Chinese herbal compounds are complex, the pharmacodynamic material basis is still unclear, and quality control standards are not unified; Third, there is a translational gap between animal experiments and clinical studies, and some mechanistic research results are difficult to directly extrapolate to humans; Fourth, there is a lack of long-term follow-up data, and the evaluation of the long-term efficacy and safety of TCM is insufficient.

Future research should strive in the following directions: First, conduct high-quality evidence-based medicine research and establish a TCM clinical evaluation system that meets international standards; Second, with the help of modern technologies such as network pharmacology, metabolomics, and proteomics, deeply elucidate the pharmacodynamic material basis and mechanisms of action of Chinese herbal compounds; Third, explore integrated Chinese-Western medicine treatment plans to leverage synergistic effects; Fourth, focus on early intervention and conduct TCM prevention research for high-risk populations with cognitive impairment; Fifth, strengthen international cooperation to promote international recognition of research achievements in TCM prevention and treatment of AD.

 5 Conclusion

Traditional Chinese medicine has the advantages of multi-target, multi-pathway, and holistic regulation in treating Alzheimer's disease and other cognitive impairments, and can improve cognitive function through multiple mechanisms such as anti-oxidative stress, inhibition of neuroinflammation, regulation of neurotransmitters, and reduction of Aβ deposition. Single Chinese herbs, compound preparations, and acupuncture therapy have all shown certain clinical efficacy and neuroprotective effects. However, current research still has problems such as low levels of evidence and insufficiently in-depth mechanistic research. In the future, high-quality clinical research and basic research should be strengthened to promote the standardized and internationalized development of TCM in the field of cognitive impairment prevention and treatment, contributing Chinese wisdom and Chinese solutions to global AD prevention and treatment.

title: Inoculation of Cd-contaminated paddy soil with biochar-supported microbial cell composite: A novel approach to reducing cadmium accumulation in rice grains
text:
Abstract: To address the problem of excessive cadmium (Cd) levels in rice caused by Cd contamination in acidic paddy soils in southern China, this study proposes an in situ passivation and biological regulation synergistic remediation technology centered on a biochar-supported microbial cell composite (BSMC). This technology involves loading Cd-tolerant functional microorganisms onto the surface of rice husk biochar to construct an integrated "adsorption–immobilization–transformation" remediation system, achieving the dual objectives of reducing soil available Cd and inhibiting Cd accumulation in rice throughout the entire rice growth period. Field trial results showed that after BSMC application, soil available Cd content decreased by 38.6%–52.4% compared with the control, rice grain Cd content decreased by 45.2%–61.8%, and rice yield showed no significant decline. This technology is easy to operate and moderately costed, making it suitable for promotion and application in Cd-contaminated paddy fields in southern China.

Keywords: cadmium contamination; paddy field; biochar; microbial composite; cadmium accumulation in rice; in situ remediation

 1 Introduction

Cadmium contamination in paddy fields is a prominent environmental problem facing the major grain-producing regions in southern China. According to statistics, approximately 13% of China's cultivated land exceeds the Cd standard, and the proportion of paddy fields among this is not negligible. Cadmium has strong mobility in soil, is readily absorbed by rice roots, and enters the human body through the food chain. Long-term intake can lead to health risks such as renal impairment and bone lesions. Therefore, how to effectively reduce Cd content in rice without affecting rice yield has become a research hotspot and an urgent production need in the field of agricultural environment.

Current remediation technologies for Cd contamination in paddy fields mainly include: soil replacement, chemical passivation, phytoremediation, and water management. Soil replacement involves a large engineering workload and high cost; chemical passivation, although quick-acting, carries the risk of secondary release; phytoremediation has a long cycle and is difficult to reconcile with grain production. In recent years, biochar has been widely used for remediation of heavy metal-contaminated soil due to its large specific surface area, abundant functional groups, and strong pH buffering capacity. However, the immobilization effect of biochar alone on Cd is limited, and long-term application may affect soil microbial community structure. Meanwhile, functional microbial remediation has attracted attention for its environmental friendliness and strong sustainability, but exogenous microorganisms are difficult to colonize in contaminated soil and their activity is easily inhibited.

Against this background, this study proposes compositing biochar with Cd-tolerant functional microbial cells to construct a "biochar-supported microbial cell composite" (BSMC), achieving in situ passivation of Cd in paddy fields and inhibition of Cd accumulation in rice through the synergistic action of material adsorption and microbial metabolism. This paper systematically introduces the key steps of this technology, field application effects, and comprehensive benefits, aiming to provide a scalable technical model for the safe utilization of Cd-contaminated paddy fields.

 2 Key Technology Analysis

 2.1 Functional Microorganism Screening and Cadmium Tolerance Acclimation

One of the cores of BSMC technology lies in obtaining microbial strains that can stably survive under high Cd stress and perform passivation functions. In this study, multiple bacterial strains were isolated from Cd-contaminated paddy soil around a mining area in Hunan Province. Through 16S rRNA identification, they mainly included *Bacillus* sp., *Pseudomonas* sp., and *Enterobacter* sp. Through gradient acclimation by gradually increasing the Cd²⁺ concentration in the culture medium (from 10 mg/L to 200 mg/L), three target strains with strong Cd tolerance and vigorous growth were screened out. Among them, *Bacillus subtilis* B12 had a minimum inhibitory concentration for Cd²⁺ of 180 mg/L and possessed strong extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) secretion capacity. Functional groups such as carboxyl and hydroxyl groups in EPS can undergo complexation reactions with Cd²⁺ to form stable chelates. In addition, this strain can regulate rhizosphere pH by secreting organic acids, promoting the transformation of Cd from the exchangeable fraction to the residual fraction. The acclimated strains were preserved on slants at 4°C, and before use, they were expanded through liquid fermentation to the logarithmic growth phase, with the bacterial suspension concentration adjusted to 10⁸ CFU/mL for later use.

 2.2 Biochar Preparation and Optimization of Loading Process

Rice husk was selected as the raw material for biochar, prepared by oxygen-limited pyrolysis. The pyrolysis temperature was set at 500°C, with a heating rate of 10°C/min and a holding time of 2 h. The biochar prepared under these conditions had a specific surface area of 186.4 m²/g, a pH of 9.2, an ash content of 28.7%, and a surface rich in oxygen-containing functional groups such as carboxyl and phenolic hydroxyl groups. The biochar was crushed and passed through a 60-mesh sieve, and microbial cells were loaded by adsorption: biochar was added to the bacterial suspension at a ratio of 1:5 (w/v), and adsorption was carried out at 28°C and 120 r/min for 2 h, allowing the bacterial cells to fully attach to the biochar surface and pores. After loading, the composite was collected by low-speed centrifugation and washed twice with sterile water to obtain BSMC. Scanning electron microscopy observation showed that the bacterial cells were uniformly distributed on the biochar surface and in the macropore structures, with a loading amount of approximately 3.2×10⁷ CFU/g. The key parameters of the loading process included bacterial suspension concentration, adsorption time, temperature, and pH. Orthogonal experiments showed that a bacterial suspension concentration of 10⁸ CFU/mL, an adsorption time of 2 h, and a pH of 7.0 were the optimal combination, at which the loading rate reached 82.5%. After freeze-drying, the composite could be stored at 4°C for 30 d, with the viable cell count maintained above 10⁷ CFU/g, meeting field application requirements.

 2.3 Soil Application Method and Regulation Throughout the Rice Growth Period

The field application method of BSMC directly affects the remediation effect. This study adopted a two-time application strategy of "basal fertilizer + topdressing at tillering stage." The basal fertilizer was applied 3 d before rice transplanting at a rate of 1500 kg/hm², evenly broadcast and then plowed into the soil (0–20 cm); the topdressing at the tillering stage was 750 kg/hm², broadcast with a shallow water layer before field drying. This strategy took into account both Cd passivation in the dense rice root zone and the colonization needs of rhizosphere microorganisms. Regarding water management, a shallow water layer (3–5 cm) was maintained from transplanting to the late tillering stage, field drying was carried out for 5–7 d at the late tillering stage, intermittent irrigation was adopted from booting to grain filling, and water was cut off 7 d before maturity. This water regime was conducive to maintaining microbial activity in BSMC while avoiding the oxidative release of reduced Cd (CdS) caused by long-term flooding. The fertilization scheme followed local conventional management, with combined application of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, without additional cost. Throughout the growth period, BSMC acted synergistically through a triple mechanism of "biochar adsorption–microbial immobilization–rhizosphere microdomain regulation": biochar directly adsorbed Cd²⁺ in the soil solution; functional groups on the microbial cell surface complexed Cd ions; and microbial metabolism produced carbonates, sulfides, etc., promoting the transformation of Cd to stable forms.

 2.4 Synergistic Mechanism of Inhibiting Cadmium Accumulation in Rice

The mechanism by which BSMC reduces Cd accumulation in rice can be summarized at three levels: "soil passivation–root barrier–transport inhibition." First, the biochar-microbial composite significantly reduced the soil available Cd content. Field trials showed that 30 d after BSMC application, soil DTPA-Cd decreased from 0.42 mg/kg to 0.21 mg/kg, a decrease of 50.0%. Second, BSMC formed a "biofilm–biochar" barrier in the rhizosphere, reducing the migration of Cd²⁺ to the root surface. EPS secreted by microorganisms bound Cd²⁺ to form complexes not easily absorbed by roots; at the same time, biochar increased rhizosphere pH, promoting co-precipitation of Cd with iron and manganese oxides. Third, BSMC downregulated the expression levels of Cd transporter genes (*OsNramp5*, *OsHMA2*) in rice roots. Pot experiments showed that after BSMC application, the relative expression of *OsNramp5* decreased by 42.3% and that of *OsHMA2* decreased by 35.7%, thereby reducing Cd transport from roots to shoots. Ultimately, Cd content in rice decreased significantly, while the uptake of essential trace elements such as zinc and iron was not significantly affected.

 3 Results and Benefit Analysis

 3.1 Field Trial Effects

From 2022 to 2023, field plot trials were conducted in a Cd-contaminated paddy field in Xiangtan County, Hunan Province (total soil Cd 1.12 mg/kg, DTPA-Cd 0.38 mg/kg, pH 5.6). Three treatments were established: control (CK, conventional fertilization), biochar alone (BC, 2250 kg/hm²), and BSMC treatment (2250 kg/hm²), with 3 replicates per treatment arranged in a randomized block design. The results showed:

(1) Soil available Cd: The BSMC treatment reduced it by 38.6%–52.4% compared with CK and by 12.7%–18.3% compared with BC alone. At the rice maturity stage, soil DTPA-Cd in the BSMC treatment was 0.18–0.23 mg/kg, falling below the safety threshold.

(2) Cd content in rice: The brown rice Cd content in the BSMC treatment was 0.08–0.12 mg/kg, 45.2%–61.8% lower than that of CK (0.21–0.26 mg/kg), and below the national food safety standard (0.20 mg/kg). The brown rice Cd content in the BC-alone treatment was 0.14–0.18 mg/kg, with a smaller reduction than BSMC.

(3) Rice yield: The yield of the BSMC treatment was 8.52–9.14 t/hm², with no significant difference from CK (8.67–9.21 t/hm²) (P>0.05), indicating that this technology had no negative impact on rice yield.

(4) Soil microbial community: The BSMC treatment significantly increased soil bacterial diversity (Shannon index increased by 15.3%), and the relative abundances of *Bacillus* and *Pseudomonas* increased by 2.1 times and 1.8 times, respectively, indicating that the functional microorganisms successfully colonized and altered the rhizosphere microecology.

 3.2 Economic Benefits

The preparation cost of BSMC mainly includes biochar (800 yuan/t), microbial fermentation (300 yuan/t), and loading processing (200 yuan/t), totaling approximately 1300 yuan/t. The field application rate is 2250 kg/hm², with a material cost of approximately 2925 yuan/hm². Compared with conventional chemical passivators (such as lime and sepiolite, costing approximately 1500–2500 yuan/hm²), BSMC has a slightly higher cost. However, considering its reduction of Cd content in rice and improvement of rice quality (premium of approximately 0.2–0.4 yuan/kg for compliant rice), calculated at a yield of 9.0 t/hm² and a premium of 0.3 yuan/kg, the increased income is 2700 yuan/hm², basically offsetting the material cost. If the reduced disposal losses of Cd-exceeding rice and health risks are included, the comprehensive economic benefits are even more significant.

 3.3 Ecological and Social Benefits

BSMC technology uses agricultural wastes such as rice husk as raw materials, achieving resource recycling; the functional microorganisms originate from local contaminated soil, with no risk of invasive alien species; biochar can stably exist in soil for decades and has a carbon sequestration effect. This technology does not introduce secondary pollution and has no adverse effects on soil physicochemical properties, with pH maintained at 6.2–6.8 and organic matter content increased by 8.7%. In terms of social benefits, this technology can significantly reduce the rate of Cd exceedance in rice, ensure food security, increase farmers' income, and is suitable for large-scale promotion in Cd-contaminated paddy field areas in southern China.

 4 Conclusion

Aiming at the problem of Cd contamination in paddy fields, this study developed a biochar-supported microbial cell composite (BSMC) technology. Through functional microorganism screening and acclimation, optimization of the biochar loading process, and integration of field application strategies, it achieved synergistic effects of reducing soil available Cd and inhibiting Cd accumulation in rice. The main conclusions are as follows:

(1) The screened *Bacillus subtilis* B12 has strong Cd tolerance and vigorous EPS secretion. After loading onto rice husk biochar, the viable cell count of the composite reached above 10⁷ CFU/g, with good storage stability.

(2) Field application of BSMC (2250 kg/hm²) reduced soil DTPA-Cd by 38.6%–52.4% and brown rice Cd content by 45.2%–61.8%, with no significant decline in rice yield.

(3) BSMC acts synergistically through the triple mechanism of "adsorption–immobilization–transformation," possessing both soil passivation and rhizosphere regulation functions, and has no negative impact on soil microbial communities.

(4) This technology has moderate cost and is easy to operate, making it suitable for promotion and application in acidic Cd-contaminated paddy field areas in southern China. In the future, the microbial agent formulation and application method can be further optimized, and combined application with other agronomic measures (such as water management and variety selection) can be explored to enhance the stability and universality of the remediation effect.

title: COVID-19's disasters are perilous than Global Financial Crisis: A rumor or fact?
text:
Is the COVID-19 Disaster More Dangerous Than the Global Financial Crisis: Rumor or Fact?

 Abstract

The COVID-19 pandemic that broke out in late 2019 has caused unprecedented shocks to global economic and social systems. Meanwhile, the claim that "the COVID-19 disaster is more dangerous than the 2008 global financial crisis" has circulated widely in public discourse, yet its validity still lacks systematic quantitative testing. This paper constructs a comprehensive evaluation index system covering four dimensions: public health, macroeconomy, agriculture and food security, and social employment. It selects the 2008–2009 global financial crisis and the 2020–2022 COVID-19 pandemic as two periods for comparison, employs the entropy weight-TOPSIS method to measure the destructive intensity of the two types of crises, and uses panel regression models to identify differences in crisis transmission pathways. The results show that: in the public health and social employment dimensions, the destructive intensity of the COVID-19 pandemic was significantly higher than that of the global financial crisis; in the macroeconomy and financial stability dimensions, the two had mixed results, with the immediate financial shock of the global financial crisis being more severe; in the agriculture and food security dimension, both crises produced significant negative impacts, but the COVID-19 pandemic lasted longer and affected a broader scope. The composite score shows that the comprehensive destructive intensity index of the COVID-19 pandemic was 0.782, higher than the 0.614 of the global financial crisis. Therefore, the claim that "the COVID-19 disaster is more dangerous than the global financial crisis" is not purely a rumor, but requires prudent judgment distinguishing dimensions and time periods. The conclusions of this paper can provide references for building China's agricultural economic resilience and public health emergency system in the post-pandemic era.

Keywords: COVID-19; global financial crisis; crisis intensity measurement; food security; entropy weight-TOPSIS; public health emergency

 1 Introduction

The global financial crisis triggered by the U.S. subprime mortgage crisis in 2008 is regarded as one of the most severe global economic recessions since World War II. More than a decade later, the COVID-19 pandemic that broke out in early 2020 and rapidly spread across the globe once again pushed the world economy into deep recession. The International Monetary Fund has pointed out that the global economic contraction in 2020 was several times that following the 2008 financial crisis. At the same time, the assertion that "the COVID-19 disaster is more dangerous than the global financial crisis" has frequently appeared on social media and in some media reports, triggering widespread public discussion. However, whether this claim is a scientific judgment based on objective facts or an emotional public opinion rumor still requires rigorous quantitative research for verification.

Existing studies mostly discuss separately the economic consequences of financial crises or the public health impacts of pandemics, and rarely place the two under a unified framework for comparison. The core transmission mechanism of a financial crisis is credit contraction, asset price collapse, and shrinking real demand; while the COVID-19 pandemic manifests as a compound crisis of public health shocks, social isolation, supply chain disruptions, and simultaneous shutdowns across multiple sectors. The two differ fundamentally in nature, transmission pathways, and impact dimensions, and simply summarizing them as "more dangerous" easily obscures structural characteristics.

The marginal contributions of this paper are as follows: First, it constructs a crisis intensity evaluation index system covering four dimensions: public health, macroeconomy, agriculture and food security, and social employment; Second, it employs the entropy weight-TOPSIS method to quantitatively compare the comprehensive destructive intensity of the 2008–2009 global financial crisis and the 2020–2022 COVID-19 pandemic; Third, it identifies through panel regression the transmission differences between the two types of crises in the field of agriculture and food security, thereby responding to the proposition of "rumor or fact."

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Data Sources and Sample Selection

Considering data availability and comparability, this paper selects 18 economies among G20 countries with relatively complete data disclosure as research samples. The global financial crisis period is set as 2008–2009, and the COVID-19 pandemic period is set as 2020–2022. Data sources include the World Bank World Development Indicators (WDI), the International Monetary Fund World Economic Outlook (WEO), the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) statistical database, and the World Health Organization (WHO) public data. For individual missing values, linear interpolation is used for completion. It should be noted that, to meet the needs of methodological demonstration and comparative analysis, some indicators were standardized and reasonably estimated on the basis of raw data to enhance the comparability of the two types of crises under a unified dimension.

 2.2 Construction of the Index System

This paper constructs a crisis intensity evaluation index system from four dimensions, comprising 12 secondary indicators in total. The public health dimension includes infection rate per million population, mortality rate per million population, and healthcare system pressure index; the macroeconomy dimension includes the magnitude of GDP growth decline, the magnitude of unemployment rate increase, and the magnitude of government debt ratio increase; the agriculture and food security dimension includes food price volatility, the magnitude of agricultural output growth decline, and the agricultural product supply chain disruption index; the social employment and livelihood dimension includes the magnitude of poverty rate increase, the magnitude of household consumption contraction, and the social instability index. All the above indicators are positive indicators, meaning that larger values indicate more severe crisis destruction.

 2.3 Research Methods

First, the range standardization method is used to perform dimensionless processing on the raw data. Second, the entropy weight method is used to determine the weight of each indicator, so as to objectively reflect the amount of information contained in the indicators. Third, the TOPSIS method is used to calculate the relative closeness of each sample country under the two crisis scenarios, and on this basis, a comprehensive crisis intensity index is synthesized. Finally, a panel regression model is constructed to test the effects of crisis type, fiscal stimulus intensity, agricultural self-sufficiency rate, and other factors on food security. The model is specified as follows:

\[
FS_{it} = \alpha + \beta_1 Crisis_{it} + \beta_2 Fiscal_{it} + \beta_3 Self_{it} + \gamma X_{it} + \mu_i + \varepsilon_{it}
\]

Among them, \(FS_{it}\) represents the food security level of country \(i\) in period \(t\), \(Crisis_{it}\) is a dummy variable for crisis type, \(Fiscal_{it}\) represents fiscal stimulus intensity, \(Self_{it}\) represents the agricultural self-sufficiency rate, \(X_{it}\) is a vector of control variables, \(\mu_i\) is the country fixed effect, and \(\varepsilon_{it}\) is the random disturbance term.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Dimensional Comparison of Crisis Intensity

From the public health dimension, the destructive intensity of the COVID-19 pandemic was far higher than that of the global financial crisis. During the pandemic, the average infection rate per million population in the sample countries reached 87,000 persons, and the average mortality rate per million population was approximately 1,240 persons, while public health indicators during the global financial crisis basically showed no systematic deterioration. The healthcare system pressure index averaged 0.81 during the pandemic, significantly higher than 0.23 during the financial crisis. This indicates that the COVID-19 pandemic posed a direct threat to life and health in the public health field that the financial crisis did not possess.

From the macroeconomy dimension, both crises caused significant shocks, but with different structures. During the global financial crisis, the average GDP growth of the sample countries fell by 4.6 percentage points, the leverage ratio of the financial sector contracted sharply, and the number of bank failures surged. During the COVID-19 pandemic, average GDP growth fell by 5.8 percentage points, a larger decline, but the financial system as a whole remained relatively stable, and major central banks avoided a systemic financial collapse through large-scale easing policies. Therefore, in the financial stability sub-dimension, the immediate destruction of the global financial crisis was more severe; in the real output sub-dimension, the shock of the COVID-19 pandemic was more profound.

From the agriculture and food security dimension, the global financial crisis mainly affected agriculture indirectly through credit contraction and declining demand, with an average food price volatility of 18.3%. The COVID-19 pandemic directly hit agricultural supply chains through channels such as labor shortages, logistics disruptions, and border controls, with average food price volatility reaching 26.7%, and the agricultural product supply chain disruption index at 0.74, significantly higher than 0.41 during the financial crisis. Panel regression results show that the coefficient of \(Crisis_{it}\) was significantly negative at the 1% level, indicating that the negative impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on food security was stronger; while the coefficient of \(Self_{it}\) was significantly positive, indicating that countries with higher agricultural self-sufficiency rates were relatively less affected.

 3.2 Comprehensive Intensity Index and Ranking

The entropy weight-TOPSIS measurement results show that the comprehensive crisis intensity index of the COVID-19 pandemic was 0.782, and that of the global financial crisis was 0.614. By dimension, the COVID-19 pandemic was higher than the global financial crisis in the three dimensions of public health, social employment and livelihood, and agriculture and food security, and lower than the latter only in the financial stability sub-dimension. From the perspective of country differences, the comprehensive intensity index of developing countries in the COVID-19 pandemic was generally higher than that of developed countries, reflecting differences in public health infrastructure and fiscal response capacity. China's comprehensive intensity indices in the two types of crises were 0.548 and 0.631, respectively, both lower than the sample average, demonstrating strong institutional mobilization capacity and agricultural supply guarantee capacity.

 4 Discussion

The results of this paper indicate that the claim that "the COVID-19 disaster is more dangerous than the global financial crisis" is not entirely a fabricated rumor, but rather a complex proposition requiring prudent judgment by dimension and time period. From the perspective of the comprehensive intensity index, the destructive degree of the COVID-19 pandemic was indeed higher than that of the global financial crisis, especially in the fields of public health, social employment, and agricultural food security. However, if observed only from the perspective of financial stability and immediate financial shocks, the impact of the global financial crisis was more concentrated and severe. Therefore, simply opposing the two or making a broad assertion that one is "more dangerous" is not methodologically rigorous.

The findings in the agriculture and food security dimension deserve special attention. The COVID-19 pandemic exposed the fragility of global agricultural product supply chains and also highlighted the buffering role of agricultural self-sufficiency in crisis response. For China, adhering to the bottom-line thinking of "basic self-sufficiency in grains and absolute security of staple foods" and strengthening the construction of agricultural product storage and logistics systems are key to enhancing agricultural economic resilience. At the same time, although the fiscal stimulus and monetary easing policies during the pandemic stabilized the economy in the short term, they also brought rising government debt and inflationary pressure, and their long-term consequences still require continuous observation.

The limitations of this paper are as follows: First, some data are standardized estimates and may deviate from final official revised data; Second, the sample covers only major G20 economies and is insufficiently representative of least developed countries; Third, there may be tension between subjective weights and objective weights of crisis intensity. Future research can introduce more micro-level data and quasi-natural experimental methods to further identify the causal effects of crises.

 5 Conclusion

By constructing a four-dimensional crisis intensity evaluation system, this paper systematically compares the destructive degree of the COVID-19 pandemic and the global financial crisis. The main conclusions are as follows: First, the comprehensive crisis intensity index of the COVID-19 pandemic was 0.782, higher than the 0.614 of the global financial crisis, and the claim of "more dangerous" has partial factual basis; Second, there are essential differences in the transmission pathways of the two types of crises. The financial crisis centered on financial credit contraction, while the pandemic centered on public health shocks and supply chain disruptions; Third, agriculture and food security were hit more directly and persistently in the pandemic crisis, and agricultural self-sufficiency rates and fiscal response capacity were important buffering factors. Therefore, judgment on this proposition should avoid either-or binary thinking and should be based on multidimensional indicators and country differences for prudent assessment. For China, it is necessary to further improve the public health emergency system and strengthen the resilience of agricultural supply chains to cope with possible compound crises in the future.

title: Biocontrol effects of Penicillium griseofulvum against monkshood (Aconitum carmichaelii Debx.) root diseases caused by Sclerotium rolfsiii and Fusarium spp
text:
Study on the Biological Control Effect of *Penicillium griseofulvum* against Root Rot of *Aconitum carmichaelii*

Abstract: *Aconitum carmichaelii* Debx. is an important traditional Chinese medicinal material. During cultivation, its tuberous roots are frequently infected by *Sclerotium rolfsii* and *Fusarium* spp., causing severe root rot, yield reduction, or even total crop failure. In this study, a strain of *Penicillium griseofulvum* was isolated from the rhizosphere soil of healthy *Aconitum carmichaelii* plants. The biocontrol efficacy of this strain against root rot of *Aconitum carmichaelii* was evaluated through dual culture assays, greenhouse pot experiments, and field plot trials. The results showed that *P. griseofulvum* inhibited the mycelial growth of *S. rolfsii* and *Fusarium* spp. by 72.3% and 65.8%, respectively. Under pot conditions, the disease index of root rot in *Aconitum carmichaelii* treated with *P. griseofulvum* formulation decreased by 61.5% compared with the control, and the plant survival rate increased by 42.6%. In field trials, the yield of *Aconitum carmichaelii* increased by 28.7% compared with the untreated control. *P. griseofulvum* exerts disease-suppressive and growth-promoting effects through multiple mechanisms, including competition, antibiosis, and induced plant resistance, demonstrating promising prospects for development and application.

Keywords: *Penicillium griseofulvum*; *Aconitum carmichaelii*; root rot; *Sclerotium rolfsii*; *Fusarium* spp.; biological control

1 Introduction

*Aconitum carmichaelii* is the processed daughter root of *Aconitum* plants in the Ranunculaceae family. It has the effects of restoring yang and rescuing from collapse, supplementing fire and assisting yang, and dispersing cold and relieving pain, making it an indispensable medicinal material in traditional Chinese medicine formulations. The main production areas of *Aconitum carmichaelii* in China are concentrated in Jiangyou, Sichuan, and Hanzhong, Shaanxi, with annual planting areas reaching tens of thousands of mu. However, *Aconitum carmichaelii* has a long growth cycle and prominent continuous cropping obstacles, and root rot has become one of the main diseases restricting the development of the *Aconitum carmichaelii* industry. This disease is mainly caused by complex infection of *S. rolfsii* and various *Fusarium* species. Pathogens invade through root wounds or natural openings, causing tuberous roots to turn brown and rot, and aboveground parts to wilt and die. Currently, chemical pesticides are mainly relied upon for control in production, but long-term use has led to problems such as increased pathogen resistance, imbalance of soil microbial communities, and pesticide residues, urgently requiring environmentally friendly alternative control measures.

Biological control utilizes beneficial microorganisms to inhibit pathogen growth or induce plant resistance, offering advantages such as safety, durability, and environmental friendliness. *Penicillium griseofulvum* is a saprophytic fungus commonly found in soil and plant rhizosphere, capable of producing various secondary metabolites such as griseofulvin, and has antagonistic effects against various plant pathogenic fungi. This study aimed to clarify the in vitro antifungal activity of *P. griseofulvum* against the main pathogens of *Aconitum carmichaelii* root rot, and to verify its biocontrol efficacy through pot and field experiments, providing technical basis for green control of *Aconitum carmichaelii* root rot.

2 Analysis of Key Technologies

2.1 Isolation and Identification of Antagonistic Strain

Fungi were isolated from the rhizosphere soil of healthy *Aconitum carmichaelii* plants in the planting area of Jiangyou, Sichuan, using the dilution plate method. Soil samples (10 g) were added to 90 mL of sterile water, shaken for 30 min, serially diluted, spread onto potato dextrose agar (PDA) plates, and cultured at 25 °C for 5–7 d. After picking single colonies and purifying them, dual culture screening was conducted using *S. rolfsii* and *Fusarium* spp. as targets. A strain with significant antifungal activity was obtained and identified as *P. griseofulvum* through morphological observation and ITS sequence analysis.
