The ONM treatment improved canopy structure, with a moderate leaf area index at heading stage (6.8 vs 7.5), but the light transmittance in the middle and lower canopy increased by 28.4%; the net photosynthetic rate of flag leaves increased by 15.3%–21.7% during the mid-to-late grain-filling period, and the chlorophyll content degradation rate decreased. In terms of roots, the ONM treatment significantly increased root length density and root oxidation activity in deep soil (20–40 cm), and the root bleeding intensity during grain filling increased by 22.6%. Regarding nitrogen use efficiency, the partial factor productivity of nitrogen, nitrogen recovery efficiency, and nitrogen agronomic efficiency under ONM treatment increased by 40.8%, 18.5%, and 32.4%, respectively. Conclusion: Optimized nitrogen management achieves rice yield increase through a synergistic regulatory pathway of "canopy structure optimization—photosynthetic performance enhancement—root activity maintenance—efficient nitrogen utilization," and is a nitrogen management strategy that combines high yield and high efficiency.

Keywords: rice; optimized nitrogen management; yield; canopy structure; photosynthetic characteristics; root morphology and physiology; nitrogen use efficiency

 1 Introduction

Rice is one of the most important food crops in China, and its yield security is directly related to national food supply. Nitrogen is the most critical nutrient element for rice growth and development, and rational application of nitrogen fertilizer plays an irreplaceable role in ensuring high rice yield. However, current rice production in China faces prominent problems such as excessively high nitrogen fertilizer application rates, unreasonable application timing, and excessive basal fertilizer proportions, which not only lead to low nitrogen use efficiency (the current-season nitrogen fertilizer utilization rate of rice in China is only 30%–40%), but also cause a series of ecological and environmental problems including water eutrophication, increased greenhouse gas emissions, and soil acidification.

Optimized nitrogen management (ONM) is a fertilization strategy that matches nitrogen supply with rice nitrogen demand patterns by adjusting the total nitrogen application rate, basal-to-topdressing ratio, and application timing. Previous studies have shown that ONM can reduce nitrogen fertilizer input without reducing or even while increasing yield, but the morphophysiological mechanisms underlying its yield enhancement lack systematic elucidation. Rice yield formation is the result of comprehensive interactions among population canopy structure, leaf photosynthetic performance, root morphology and physiology, and nitrogen uptake and utilization. In-depth analysis of the physiological and ecological mechanisms by which ONM regulates yield formation is of great significance for improving the theory of green and high-yield rice cultivation.

In this study, the main japonica rice cultivar in Jiangsu Province was used as material, and two treatments of conventional nitrogen management and optimized nitrogen management were established to systematically reveal the morphophysiological mechanisms by which ONM promotes rice yield increase from multiple dimensions including canopy structure, photosynthetic characteristics, root morphology and physiology, and nitrogen use efficiency, providing theoretical support for the promotion and application of optimized nitrogen fertilizer management technology in rice.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Experimental Site and Materials

The experiment was conducted in 2023 at an agricultural experimental station in Yangzhou City, Jiangsu Province. The test soil was sandy loam, with organic matter content of 22.3 g·kg⁻¹, total nitrogen of 1.42 g·kg⁻¹, available phosphorus of 28.6 mg·kg⁻¹, available potassium of 112.5 mg·kg⁻¹, and pH 6.8 in the plough layer (0–20 cm). The test cultivar was japonica rice "Nanjing 9108," with a whole growth period of approximately 155 d.

 2.2 Experimental Design

A randomized complete block design was adopted, with two treatments, 3 replications per treatment, and a plot area of 30 m² (5 m × 6 m). Isolation ridges were set between plots and covered with film for seepage prevention.

- Conventional nitrogen management (CNM): Total nitrogen application rate of 300 kg·hm⁻², basal fertilizer∶tillering fertilizer∶panicle fertilizer = 5∶3∶2. Basal fertilizer was applied 1 d before transplanting, tillering fertilizer was applied 7 d after transplanting, and panicle fertilizer was applied at the 4th leaf from top stage.
- Optimized nitrogen management (ONM): Total nitrogen application rate of 240 kg·hm⁻², basal fertilizer∶tillering fertilizer∶panicle fertilizer = 3∶3∶4. The application timing of basal fertilizer and tillering fertilizer was the same as CNM; panicle fertilizer was applied in two splits, with half applied at the 4th leaf from top stage and half at the 2nd leaf from top stage.

The nitrogen fertilizer variety was urea (containing N 46%), and phosphorus fertilizer (superphosphate, P₂O₅ 12%) and potassium fertilizer (potassium chloride, K₂O 60%) were applied at 120 kg·hm⁻² and 180 kg·hm⁻², respectively, all as basal fertilizer applied once. Water management, pest and disease control, and other measures were uniformly carried out according to conventional high-yield cultivation practices.

 2.3 Measurement Items and Methods

2.3.1 Yield and yield components: At maturity, 10 representative hills were sampled from each plot to examine effective panicle number, spikelets per panicle, seed-setting rate, and 1000-grain weight. All plots were harvested, threshed, sun-dried, and weighed, and the actual harvested yield was converted to 14% moisture content.

2.3.2 Canopy structure: At heading stage and mid-grain-filling stage, a LI-191SA linear photosynthetically active radiation sensor was used to measure photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) at the canopy top, middle (1/2 plant height), and bottom (10 cm above ground), and light transmittance was calculated. A LI-3100C leaf area meter was used to measure leaf area index (LAI).

2.3.3 Photosynthetic characteristics: At heading stage, early grain-filling stage, mid-grain-filling stage, and late grain-filling stage, on clear days between 9:00–11:00 AM, a LI-6400XT portable photosynthesis measurement system was used to measure net photosynthetic rate (Pn), stomatal conductance (Gs), and intercellular CO₂ concentration (Ci) of flag leaves. Simultaneously, a SPAD-502 chlorophyll meter was used to measure flag leaf SPAD values.

2.3.4 Root morphology and physiology: At heading stage and mid-grain-filling stage, a root auger method (8 cm diameter) was used to collect root samples by soil layer (0–10, 10–20, 20–40 cm). After washing, a WinRHIZO root analysis system was used to measure root length density. Root oxidation activity was determined by the α-naphthylamine oxidation method. During grain filling, the bleeding method was used to measure root bleeding intensity.

2.3.5 Nitrogen use efficiency: At maturity, samples were taken by organ (stem-sheath, leaf, panicle), oven-dried and ground, and total nitrogen content was determined by the Kjeldahl method. Partial factor productivity of nitrogen (PFPN = grain yield/nitrogen application rate), nitrogen recovery efficiency (NRE = (plant nitrogen uptake in nitrogen-applied plot − plant nitrogen uptake in zero-nitrogen plot)/nitrogen application rate × 100%), and nitrogen agronomic efficiency (NAE = (yield in nitrogen-applied plot − yield in zero-nitrogen plot)/nitrogen application rate) were calculated.

 2.4 Data Processing

Microsoft Excel 2019 was used for data organization, SPSS 26.0 was used for independent samples t-test, and Origin 2021 was used for graphing.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Yield and Yield Components

The ONM treatment significantly increased rice yield (Table 1). Compared with CNM, the actual harvested yield under ONM treatment increased by 12.6% (P<0.05), reaching 10.2 t·hm⁻². In terms of yield components, there was no significant difference in effective panicle number between the two treatments, but the ONM treatment showed a 9.8% increase in spikelets per panicle (P<0.05), a 5.2% increase in seed-setting rate (P<0.05), and a slight but non-significant increase in 1000-grain weight. This indicates that the yield-enhancing effect of ONM mainly originated from the synergistic improvement of spikelets per panicle and seed-setting rate.

Table 1 Effects of different nitrogen management on rice yield and yield components

| Treatment | Effective panicle number (×10⁴·hm⁻²) | Spikelets per panicle (grains) | Seed-setting rate (%) | 1000-grain weight (g) | Actual harvested yield (t·hm⁻²) |
|------|------------------------|-------------|------------|------------|---------------------|
| CNM | 312.5±8.6a | 128.6±4.2b | 88.3±1.5b | 26.4±0.3a | 9.06±0.28b |
| ONM | 308.2±7.9a | 141.2±5.1a | 92.9±1.2a | 26.7±0.4a | 10.20±0.31a |

Note: Different lowercase letters in the same column indicate significant differences between treatments (P<0.05), the same below.

 3.2 Canopy Structure Characteristics

At heading stage, the LAI of the ONM treatment was 6.8, slightly lower than 7.5 of CNM, but the difference did not reach a significant level. However, the ONM treatment significantly improved canopy light transmittance conditions (Table 2). At mid-grain-filling stage, the light transmittance in the middle and bottom canopy under ONM treatment increased by 28.4% and 41.2%, respectively, compared with CNM (P<0.05). This indicates that ONM constructed a more reasonable canopy structure by moderately controlling population size and optimizing vertical leaf distribution, which is conducive to sufficient light acquisition by middle and lower leaves and delaying population senescence.

Table 2 Effects of different nitrogen management on canopy light transmittance at mid-grain-filling stage

| Treatment | Canopy top light transmittance (%) | Canopy middle light transmittance (%) | Canopy bottom light transmittance (%) |
|------|---------------------|---------------------|---------------------|
| CNM | 92.5±2.1a | 18.6±1.8b | 5.8±0.9b |
| ONM | 93.1±1.9a | 23.9±2.2a | 8.2±1.1a |

 3.3 Leaf Photosynthetic Characteristics

The ONM treatment significantly delayed the decline of flag leaf photosynthetic function (Figure 1). At heading stage, there was no significant difference in Pn between the two treatments, but at early, mid, and late grain-filling stages, the Pn under ONM treatment increased by 15.3%, 19.8%, and 21.7%, respectively, compared with CNM (P<0.05). The change trend of SPAD values was consistent with Pn, and the SPAD values of ONM treatment at mid-to-late grain-filling stages were significantly higher than those of CNM, indicating that ONM effectively delayed chlorophyll degradation and leaf senescence. In addition, the stomatal conductance of ONM treatment at mid-to-late grain-filling stages was significantly higher than that of CNM, while there was no significant difference in intercellular CO₂ concentration, indicating that the enhancement of photosynthetic rate mainly originated from the improvement of non-stomatal limitations.

 3.4 Root Morphological and Physiological Characteristics

The ONM treatment significantly promoted root development in deep soil (Table 3). At heading stage, the root length density of ONM treatment in the 20–40 cm soil layer increased by 34.6% compared with CNM (P<0.05), while there was no significant difference in root length density in the 0–10 cm and 10–20 cm soil layers between the two treatments. At mid-grain-filling stage, the root length density in all soil layers under ONM treatment was significantly higher than that of CNM, with an increase of 42.3% in the 20–40 cm soil layer.

In terms of root physiological activity, the root oxidation activity of ONM treatment at heading stage and mid-grain-filling stage increased by 18.7% and 25.3%, respectively, compared with CNM (P<0.05). The root bleeding intensity during grain filling under ONM treatment was 2.38 g·h⁻¹·hill⁻¹, which was 22.6% higher than 1.94 g·h⁻¹·hill⁻¹ of CNM (P<0.05). This indicates that ONM effectively maintained root physiological activity at late growth stages and enhanced root absorption capacity for water and nutrients.

Table 3 Effects of different nitrogen management on rice root length density (cm·cm⁻³)

| Stage | Treatment | 0–10 cm | 10–20 cm | 20–40 cm |
|------|------|---------|----------|----------|
| Heading stage | CNM | 4.82±0.31a | 2.65±0.22a | 0.81±0.09b |
|  | ONM | 4.75±0.28a | 2.78±0.25a | 1.09±0.11a |
| Mid-grain-filling stage | CNM | 3.56±0.26b | 1.89±0.18b | 0.52±0.07b |
|  | ONM | 4.21±0.29a | 2.34±0.21a | 0.74±0.08a |

 3.5 Nitrogen Use Efficiency

The ONM treatment significantly improved all nitrogen use efficiency indicators (Table 4). Although the nitrogen application rate of ONM treatment was reduced by 20% compared with CNM, its partial factor productivity of nitrogen increased by 40.8%, nitrogen recovery efficiency increased by 18.5 percentage points, and nitrogen agronomic efficiency increased by 32.4% (P<0.05). This indicates that ONM greatly improved nitrogen use efficiency by optimizing the spatiotemporal matching of nitrogen supply and rice demand, achieving the goal of reducing nitrogen while increasing efficiency.

Table 4 Effects of different nitrogen management on nitrogen use efficiency

| Treatment | Partial factor productivity of nitrogen (kg·kg⁻¹) | Nitrogen recovery efficiency (%) | Nitrogen agronomic efficiency (kg·kg⁻¹) |
|------|--------------------------|----------------|--------------------------|
| CNM | 30.2±1.2b | 38.6±2.1b | 12.4±0.8b |
| ONM | 42.5±1.6a | 57.1±2.8a | 16.4±1.1a |

 4 Discussion

 4.1 Photosynthetic Physiological Basis of Canopy Structure Improvement by Optimized Nitrogen Management

Rice yield formation depends on the accumulation of population photosynthetic production capacity, and canopy structure is a key factor determining population light interception and utilization. This study found that although the total nitrogen application rate of ONM treatment was reduced by 20%, by increasing the panicle fertilizer proportion from 20% to 40% and applying it in two splits, the population development dynamics were effectively regulated. Moderate control of nitrogen supply at the early stage avoided excessive occurrence of ineffective tillers, maintaining LAI at a reasonable level at heading stage (6.8); enhanced nitrogen supply at the late stage delayed functional leaf senescence and maintained photosynthetic area during grain filling. More importantly, the ONM treatment significantly improved light transmittance in the middle and lower canopy, which is conducive to improving the internal light environment of the population, increasing the photosynthetic contribution of middle and lower leaves, and thereby increasing total population photosynthetic production. This result is consistent with existing conclusions on nitrogen fertilizer postponement improving rice canopy structure.

 4.2 Physiological Mechanism of Root Activity Maintenance by Optimized Nitrogen Management

Roots are the main organs for water and nutrient uptake in rice, and their morphology and physiological activity directly affect aboveground growth and development. In this study, the ONM treatment significantly increased root length density in deep soil (20–40 cm), which was related to deep application and split application of panicle fertilizer. The increase in deep roots expanded the root absorption space, facilitating rice utilization of water and nutrients in deep soil. Meanwhile, the ONM treatment maintained higher root oxidation activity and bleeding intensity, indicating enhanced root metabolic activity. Good root function provided sufficient water and nutrient supply for the aboveground, delayed leaf senescence, and promoted grain filling, which may be an important physiological basis for ONM to improve seed-setting rate and spikelets per panicle.

 4.3 Synergistic Mechanism of Reducing Nitrogen and Increasing Efficiency by Optimized Nitrogen Management

Although traditional high-nitrogen cultivation can achieve higher yields, nitrogen use efficiency is low and environmental costs are high. The results of this study indicate that ONM achieved a 12.6% yield increase under the condition of reducing nitrogen application by 20% through the synergistic regulatory pathway of "canopy structure optimization—photosynthetic performance enhancement—root activity maintenance—efficient nitrogen utilization." The core of this synergistic effect lies in the spatiotemporal matching of nitrogen supply and rice demand: moderate nitrogen control at the early stage avoided excessive population size

title: Assessing the sustainability of lead utilization in China
text:
Assessing the Sustainability of Lead Resource Utilization in China

Abstract: As an important non-ferrous metal, lead is widely used in fields such as batteries, cable sheaths, and lead alloys. China is the world's largest producer and consumer of lead, and the sustainability of lead resource utilization is directly related to resource security and the ecological environment. This paper systematically assesses the sustainability of lead resource utilization in China from the aspects of lead resource reserves, production and consumption patterns, recycling and regeneration systems, environmental impacts, and policy management. The analysis shows that China's static guarantee years for lead resources are insufficient, primary lead production faces dual pressures from resources and environmental protection, and although the secondary lead industry is developing rapidly, problems such as an incomplete recycling system and uneven technologies still exist. The paper proposes countermeasures such as strengthening the secondary lead system, promoting cleaner production technologies, and improving policies and standards, providing a reference for promoting the sustainable development of lead resource utilization in China.

Keywords: lead resources; sustainability; secondary lead; environmental impact; resource security

 1 Introduction

Lead is an important non-ferrous metal. Because of its high density, low melting point, ease of processing, and corrosion resistance, it is widely used in lead-acid batteries, cable sheaths, lead alloys, pigments, radiation shielding materials, and other fields. Among these, lead-acid batteries are the largest consumption sector for lead, accounting for more than 80% of global lead consumption. China is the world's largest producer and consumer of lead, with both lead output and consumption accounting for more than 40% of the global total. However, lead resources are non-renewable, and lead and its compounds are toxic, potentially causing harm to the environment and human health during mining, smelting, processing, and use. Therefore, assessing the sustainability of lead resource utilization in China is of great significance for ensuring resource supply, protecting the ecological environment, and promoting the healthy development of the industry.

Sustainability assessment usually covers four dimensions: resource availability, economic feasibility, environmental friendliness, and social acceptability. This paper will analyze China's lead resource reserves and guarantee level, production and consumption patterns, recycling and regeneration system, environmental impact and governance, and policies and management, identify key problems, and propose improvement suggestions.

 2 Key Technical Analysis

 2.1 Lead Resource Reserves and Guarantee Level

China is relatively rich in lead ore resources, but per capita ownership is low, and there are many lean ores and few rich ores. According to data from the Ministry of Natural Resources, by the end of 2020, China's identified lead ore resource reserves were about 78 million tons (metal content), with basic reserves of about 20 million tons. Based on the lead concentrate output of about 2 million tons that year, the static guarantee years are less than 10 years, far below the global average. In addition, China's lead ore resources are unevenly distributed, mainly concentrated in Yunnan, Inner Mongolia, Gansu, Qinghai, Hunan, and other provinces, among which Yunnan and Inner Mongolia together account for more than 40% of the national reserves. Poor resource endowment leads to high mining costs and low grades, and some mines have entered the deep mining stage, further increasing difficulty and costs.

In the long term, domestic lead ore resources are unlikely to meet continuously growing consumption demand, and external dependence has been rising year by year. In 2020, China imported about 1.5 million tons of lead concentrate (physical quantity), with external dependence exceeding 40%. Insufficient resource guarantee is the primary factor constraining the sustainability of lead resource utilization in China.

 2.2 Lead Production and Consumption Pattern

China's lead production is mainly based on primary lead and secondary lead. In 2020, China's refined lead output was about 5.2 million tons, of which primary lead was about 3 million tons and secondary lead was about 2.2 million tons, with secondary lead accounting for about 42%, lower than the global average (about 60%). Primary lead production mainly adopts pyrometallurgical smelting processes, which have high energy consumption and large emissions. In recent years, with stricter environmental protection requirements, some outdated capacity has been eliminated, but the overall technical level still needs improvement.

On the consumption side, lead-acid batteries account for more than 85% of China's lead consumption, with the remainder used for cable sheaths, lead plates, lead alloys, and so on. With the development of the new energy vehicle and energy storage industries, demand for lead-acid batteries remains stable, but the substitution effect of lithium-ion batteries is gradually emerging. It is expected that in the next decade, China's lead consumption will tend to stabilize or decline slightly, but the recycling and regeneration of existing batteries will become an important source of lead supply.

 2.3 Lead Recycling and Regeneration System

Secondary lead is a key pathway for improving the sustainability of lead resources. Compared with primary lead, secondary lead production reduces energy consumption by about 60%, reduces carbon emissions by about 70%, and can be recycled, with significant environmental benefits. China's secondary lead industry started relatively late but has developed rapidly. In 2020, secondary lead output reached 2.2 million tons, double that of 2010. However, the recycling system is still incomplete. At present, formal recycling enterprises account for only about 50% of the total recycling volume, and large quantities of waste lead-acid batteries flow into informal channels, causing environmental pollution and resource waste. In addition, secondary lead enterprises are small in scale, and their technical equipment levels vary. Some enterprises still use outdated processes such as small reverberatory furnaces and cupola furnaces, resulting in low lead recovery rates and poor pollution control.

In recent years, the state has issued a series of policies, such as the Pilot Work Plan for the Centralized Collection and Cross-Regional Transfer System of Lead-Acid Battery Production Enterprises and the Guidelines for the Review and Licensing of Hazardous Waste Operating Units for Waste Lead-Acid Batteries, to promote the standardization of the recycling system. However, in actual implementation, problems such as regulatory blind spots, difficulties in cross-regional transfer, and insufficient economic incentives still exist.

 2.4 Environmental Impact and Governance

The environmental impact of the lead industry chain runs through the entire process of mining, beneficiation, smelting, processing, use, and recycling. Mining and beneficiation produce large amounts of tailings and waste rock, which may cause heavy metal pollution; pyrometallurgical smelting emits pollutants such as sulfur dioxide and lead dust; in the secondary lead recycling process, if poorly managed, lead dust and acid liquid may pollute soil and water bodies. Lead exposure can cause damage to the nervous system, hematopoietic system, and kidneys, with particularly significant effects on children's intellectual development.

To address these problems, China has formulated strict emission standards, such as the Emission Standard of Pollutants for Lead and Zinc Industry (GB 25466-2010) and the Normative Conditions for the Secondary Lead Industry. Key enterprises have installed online monitoring and dust removal facilities, and some enterprises have achieved cleaner production. However, historically accumulated pollution problems remain prominent. In some mining areas, lead levels in surrounding soil seriously exceed standards, and remediation and restoration costs are high and cycles are long.

 2.5 Policy and Management

Policy is an important guarantee for promoting the sustainable utilization of lead resources. China has formed a legal framework based on the Mineral Resources Law, the Circular Economy Promotion Law, and the Law on the Prevention and Control of Environmental Pollution by Solid Wastes, and has issued special policies such as the Development Plan for the Non-Ferrous Metals Industry and the Normative Conditions for the Secondary Lead Industry. In 2020, the National Development and Reform Commission and the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology issued the Implementation Plan on Improving the Recycling and Treatment System of Waste Home Appliances and Promoting the Renewal Consumption of Home Appliances, further emphasizing the recycling of waste lead-acid batteries. In addition, the extended producer responsibility system is gradually being promoted, requiring lead-acid battery production enterprises to assume recycling responsibilities.

However, in policy implementation, problems such as insufficient departmental coordination, local protectionism, and inadequate incentive measures still exist. For example, the approval for cross-provincial transfer of waste lead-acid batteries is cumbersome, causing formal recycling enterprises to be "underfed," while illegal recycling continues despite repeated prohibitions. Therefore, it is necessary to further improve laws and standards, strengthen regulatory capacity, and establish a nationally unified recycling network.

 3 Results and Benefit Analysis

Based on the above analysis, the sustainability of lead resource utilization in China faces the following main problems: first, the degree of resource guarantee is low and external dependence is high; second, although the proportion of secondary lead has increased, the recycling system is not standardized and environmental risks are high; third, primary lead production has relatively high energy consumption and emissions, and the level of cleaner production needs improvement; fourth, the policy system has been initially established, but implementation results are not ideal.

Promoting the sustainable utilization of lead resources can bring significant economic, environmental, and social benefits. Economically, increasing the proportion of secondary lead can reduce dependence on imported lead concentrate, save foreign exchange, and lower production costs. According to estimates, each ton of secondary lead can save about 1.5 tons of standard coal and about 100 tons of water compared with primary lead. Environmentally, standardized recycling can reduce emissions of lead dust, acid liquid, and waste residue, lower the risk of soil and water pollution, and protect residents' health. Socially, it can promote the development of formal recycling enterprises, increase employment, and advance the circular economy.

Taking secondary lead as an example, if the proportion of secondary lead is increased from the current 42% to 60%, about 1 million tons of primary lead production can be reduced annually, correspondingly reducing imports of lead concentrate by about 1.5 million tons and reducing carbon dioxide emissions by about 2 million tons, with obvious dual environmental and economic benefits.

 4 Conclusion

The sustainability of lead resource utilization in China faces challenges such as insufficient resource guarantee, an incomplete recycling system, and high environmental pollution risks. To improve sustainability, the following measures are recommended: first, strengthen domestic lead ore exploration to improve the degree of resource guarantee, while encouraging enterprises to "go global" to obtain overseas resources; second, improve the recycling system for waste lead-acid batteries, implement the extended producer responsibility system, establish a nationally unified recycling network, and severely crack down on illegal recycling; third, promote cleaner production technologies, raise energy consumption and emission standards for primary lead and secondary lead, and promote enterprise technological transformation; fourth, strengthen policy coordination and supervision, simplify cross-regional transfer approval, and increase fiscal and tax incentives; fifth, carry out remediation of lead-contaminated soil to protect the ecological environment and public health.

In summary, only through a multi-pronged approach involving resources, technology, policy, and the market can the sustainability of lead resource utilization in China be achieved and support the green development of the economy and society.

title: Influence of land use on bacterial and archaeal diversity and community structures in three natural ecosystems and one agricultural soil
text:
Effects of Land Use Patterns on Bacterial and Archaeal Diversity and Community Structure in Three Natural Ecosystems and One Agricultural Soil

Abstract: To reveal the effects of different land use patterns on soil microbial diversity and community structure, this study selected three natural ecosystems—forest, grassland, and wetland—as well as adjacent farmland soil as research objects, and used high-throughput sequencing technology to analyze the diversity and community composition of bacterial 16S rRNA genes and archaeal 16S rRNA genes. The results showed that under the four land use patterns, the bacterial Shannon index ranged from 5.82 to 6.54, and bacterial diversity in farmland soil was significantly lower than that in forest and grassland (P<0.05); the archaeal Shannon index ranged from 2.31 to 3.12, with the highest archaeal diversity in wetland and the lowest in farmland. Principal coordinate analysis showed that bacterial and archaeal community structures were significantly separated among the four soil types (ANOSIM, R=0.62–0.81, P<0.01). In farmland soil, the relative abundances of Actinobacteriota and Gemmatimonadota increased, while Acidobacteriota decreased; archaea were dominated by Thaumarchaeota and Euryarchaeota, and the abundance of Thaumarchaeota in farmland decreased significantly. Redundancy analysis indicated that soil pH, organic carbon, and ammonium nitrogen were the main environmental factors driving variation in microbial communities. The study showed that agricultural use significantly altered the diversity and community structure of soil bacteria and archaea, and that natural ecosystems have important conservation value for maintaining microbial diversity.

Keywords: land use; bacterial diversity; archaeal diversity; community structure; high-throughput sequencing; agricultural soil

1 Introduction

Soil microorganisms are core drivers of material cycling and energy flow in terrestrial ecosystems, and their community composition is highly sensitive to land use change. The conversion of natural ecosystems to agroecosystems is usually accompanied by changes in vegetation cover, tillage disturbance, and fertilizer input, thereby affecting soil physicochemical properties and microbial habitats. Previous studies have shown that long-term tillage can reduce bacterial diversity and alter the proportions of functional groups, but understanding of the response of archaeal communities to land use remains relatively weak. Archaea play important roles in key processes such as ammonia oxidation and methanogenesis, and changes in their diversity may affect soil nitrogen cycling and greenhouse gas emissions. Therefore, comparing the diversity and community structure of bacteria and archaea in natural ecosystems and agricultural soils is of great significance for evaluating the ecological effects of agricultural management measures. This study hypothesized that agricultural use would reduce bacterial and archaeal diversity and lead to community structures significantly different from those of natural ecosystems. To test this hypothesis, four land use types—forest, grassland, wetland, and farmland—were selected, and microbial diversity and community composition were analyzed by high-throughput sequencing, with their key driving factors explored.

2 Materials and Methods

2.1 Study Area and Sample Collection

The study area is located in Northeast China (approximately 45°N, 126°E), with a temperate continental monsoon climate, an mean annual temperature of 4.5°C, and annual precipitation of 620 mm. Three sampling plots each were selected from adjacent natural secondary forest, typical grassland, marsh wetland, and long-term cultivated farmland (continuous maize cropping, cultivation period >20 years), totaling 12 sampling sites. At each sampling site, 0–20 cm surface soil was collected in an “S” shape, mixed, and passed through a 2 mm sieve; one portion was stored at 4°C for physicochemical analysis, and the other portion was stored at -80°C for DNA extraction.

2.2 Determination of Soil Physicochemical Properties

Soil pH was determined by the potentiometric method with a water-to-soil ratio of 2.5:1; organic carbon was determined by the potassium dichromate oxidation method; total nitrogen was determined by the Kjeldahl method; ammonium nitrogen and nitrate nitrogen were determined using a continuous flow analyzer; and soil water content was determined by the oven-drying method.

2.3 DNA Extraction and High-Throughput Sequencing

Total soil DNA was extracted using the PowerSoil DNA Kit. The primers for the V3–V4 region of the bacterial 16S rRNA gene were 338F/806R, and the primers for the archaeal 16S rRNA gene were 524F/958R. After purification and quantification, PCR products were used to construct libraries and subjected to paired-end sequencing on the Illumina NovaSeq platform. Raw sequences were subjected to quality control, denoising, and chimera removal using QIIME2, clustered into operational taxonomic units (OTUs) at 97% similarity, and taxonomically annotated based on the Silva database.

2.4 Data Analysis

The Shannon index and Chao1 index were used to characterize α diversity, and principal coordinate analysis (PCoA) and analysis of similarities (ANOSIM) were performed based on Bray-Curtis distance. Redundancy analysis (RDA) was used to identify the main environmental factors affecting community structure. Statistical analysis was completed in R 4.2.0, and the significance level was set at P<0.05.

3 Results and Analysis

3.1 Soil Physicochemical Properties

The pH of farmland soil was 6.42, significantly lower than that of forest (7.05) and wetland (7.18) (P<0.05); the organic carbon content was 12.4 g/kg, lower than that of forest (28.6 g/kg) and grassland (21.3 g/kg); the ammonium nitrogen content was 18.7 mg/kg, significantly higher than that of the three natural ecosystems (5.2–9.8 mg/kg). Wetland soil had the highest water content (46.2%), and farmland had the lowest (18.5%).

3.2 Bacterial and Archaeal α Diversity

The bacterial Shannon index in forest, grassland, wetland, and farmland was 6.54, 6.38, 6.21, and 5.82, respectively, with farmland significantly lower than forest and grassland (P<0.05); the Chao1 index showed a similar trend. The archaeal Shannon index was 2.86, 2.74, 3.12, and 2.31, respectively, with the highest in wetland and the lowest in farmland, and farmland differed significantly from the three natural ecosystems (P<0.05).

3.3 Community Structure

PCoA showed that bacterial and archaeal community structures were clearly separated among the four land use patterns, with the first principal coordinate explaining 42.6% and 38.4% of the variation, respectively. ANOSIM indicated significant differences among groups (bacteria R=0.81, archaea R=0.62, P<0.01). The dominant bacterial phyla were Acidobacteriota, Pseudomonadota, Actinobacteriota, and Gemmatimonadota. Compared with natural ecosystems, the relative abundance of Acidobacteriota in farmland soil decreased from 24.6%–31.2% to 16.8%, while Actinobacteriota and Gemmatimonadota increased to 28.4% and 9.6%, respectively. The archaeal community was dominated by Thaumarchaeota and Euryarchaeota, and the relative abundance of Thaumarchaeota in farmland soil (36.2%) was significantly lower than that in forest (58.4%) and grassland (54.1%).

3.4 Relationship Between Communities and Environmental Factors

RDA showed that pH, organic carbon, and ammonium nitrogen together explained 61.3% of the variation in the bacterial community and 56.8% of the variation in the archaeal community. pH was positively correlated with bacterial diversity, and ammonium nitrogen was positively correlated with the abundance of taxa characteristic of farmland.

4 Discussion

This study showed that agricultural use significantly reduced soil bacterial and archaeal diversity, supporting the research hypothesis. The decrease in soil pH and the reduction in organic carbon in farmland soil may be important reasons for the decline in diversity. Long-term tillage and chemical fertilizer application lead to soil acidification, and pH is a key factor driving bacterial community structure. In addition, agricultural disturbance reduces soil aggregates and pore continuity, decreasing the heterogeneity of microbial niches.

Changes in bacterial community composition reflect differences in life history strategies. Acidobacteriota are mostly oligotrophic and are enriched in natural ecosystems; in farmland soil, copiotrophic groups such as Actinobacteriota and Gemmatimonadota increase, which is related to the increase in readily utilizable carbon sources after fertilization. Among the archaeal community, Thaumarchaeota (mainly ammonia-oxidizing archaea) decreased significantly in farmland, possibly related to enhanced competition from ammonia-oxidizing bacteria due to long-term fertilization and decreased pH, which may in turn affect soil nitrification processes and nitrogen use efficiency.

Wetland had the highest archaeal diversity, which is related to its anaerobic microenvironment and higher water content, suggesting that hydrological conditions have an important filtering effect on archaeal communities. Forest and grassland had higher bacterial diversity, indicating that natural vegetation maintains higher microbial diversity through root exudates and litter input. The reduction in microbial diversity in agricultural soil may weaken ecosystem stability and nutrient cycling functions, posing a potential risk to agricultural sustainability.

This study still has certain limitations: the number of sampling sites was limited, and metagenomic functional analysis was not incorporated. Future studies should strengthen multi-region networked research and link nitrogen cycling functional gene expression to further reveal the mechanisms by which land use change affects microbial ecological functions.

5 Conclusions

(1) Under the four land use patterns, bacterial and archaeal α diversity in farmland soil were both significantly lower than in forest, grassland, and wetland, and wetland had the highest archaeal diversity. (2) Bacterial and archaeal community structures were significantly separated among the four soil types; in farmland soil, the abundances of Acidobacteriota and Thaumarchaeota decreased, while those of Actinobacteriota and Gemmatimonadota increased. (3) Soil pH, organic carbon, and ammonium nitrogen were the main environmental factors driving variation in microbial communities. Agricultural use significantly reshaped bacterial and archaeal communities by altering soil physicochemical properties, and natural ecosystems have important value in maintaining soil microbial diversity.

title: Landslide Susceptibility Mapping Using Machine Learning Algorithms and Remote Sensing Data in a Tropical Environment
text:
Landslide Susceptibility Mapping Using Machine Learning Algorithms and Remote Sensing Data in a Tropical Environment

Abstract: Tropical regions are characterized by concentrated rainfall and intense weathering, leading to frequent landslide disasters, and traditional survey methods are difficult to meet the needs of large-scale rapid assessment. Taking a typical tropical mountainous area as the study area, this paper uses remote sensing data to extract causative factors such as topography, vegetation, hydrology, and human activities, and compares the performance of three machine learning algorithms—logistic regression, random forest, and support vector machine—in landslide susceptibility mapping. The results show that the random forest model is optimal in terms of accuracy and stability, and the susceptibility zoning based on this model can well reflect the actual disaster distribution, providing a low-cost and generalizable technical solution for landslide risk early warning and land planning in tropical regions.

Introduction: Landslides are one of the most common geological disasters in tropical mountainous areas. The tropical environment is characterized by high temperature and abundant rainfall, deep weathering crust, high vegetation coverage, and intense human activities, which makes the development patterns of landslides complex and the assessment of susceptibility relatively difficult. Traditional landslide surveys rely on field mapping, which is costly and time-consuming, and difficult to rapidly promote in remote mountainous areas. In recent years, remote sensing technology can provide multi-temporal and multi-scale surface information, while machine learning algorithms can automatically mine the nonlinear relationship between causative factors and landslides. The combination of the two provides a new approach for landslide susceptibility mapping. This paper aims to construct a landslide susceptibility assessment workflow suitable for tropical environments and compare the applicability of different algorithms, so as to provide technical reference for grassroots disaster prevention and mitigation.

Analysis of Key Technologies

1. Study Area and Data Sources

The study area is a typical mountainous area with a tropical monsoon climate, rich in annual rainfall, with distinct dry and wet seasons, and landslides mostly occur in the rainy season. The data mainly include: optical remote sensing images used to extract vegetation indices and land use types; digital elevation models used to calculate slope, aspect, curvature, terrain relief, etc.; rainfall data used to characterize rainfall erosivity; geological maps used for lithological zoning; and road and settlement data used to reflect the impact of human activities. All data were uniformly resampled to the same spatial resolution, and a landslide inventory database was established, with historical landslide points as positive samples.

2. Selection and Preprocessing of Causative Factors

Combined with the characteristics of the tropical environment, factors such as slope, aspect, elevation, topographic wetness index, normalized difference vegetation index, lithology, distance to faults, distance to roads, distance to rivers, and rainfall were selected. Continuous factors were graded or standardized, and categorical factors were one-hot encoded. To avoid multicollinearity among factors, variance inflation factor and correlation analysis were used to remove redundant variables. Landslide samples and non-landslide samples were randomly selected in a certain proportion, and the spatial distribution was ensured to be balanced.

3. Construction of Machine Learning Models

Three representative algorithms were adopted in this paper. Logistic regression was used as the baseline model, which is simple in form and highly interpretable; support vector machine is suitable for small-sample and high-dimensional data and handles nonlinear boundaries through kernel functions; random forest is based on ensemble learning, can effectively reduce overfitting, and has strong robustness to noise and missing values. During model training, cross-validation was used to adjust key parameters, such as the number of trees and maximum depth of random forest, and the kernel function and penalty coefficient of support vector machine. Accuracy, recall, F1 value, and AUC value were used as evaluation indicators to compare model performance.

4. Susceptibility Mapping and Zoning

The optimal model was used to calculate the landslide occurrence probability of each grid in the entire region, and the natural breaks method was used to classify susceptibility into four levels: low, medium, high, and very high. Historical landslide points were used to verify the rationality of the zoning, and the proportion of landslide points within each level was calculated. The results show that the very high susceptibility areas are mainly distributed in areas with steeper slopes, poorer vegetation coverage, and closer distances to roads and rivers, which is consistent with the development patterns of landslides in tropical mountainous areas.

Results and Benefit Analysis: The random forest model achieved the highest AUC value on the test set, about 0.89, outperforming support vector machine at 0.84 and logistic regression at 0.80. Its advantage lies in its ability to comprehensively handle multi-source factors such as topography, vegetation, and human activities, and it is insensitive to sample imbalance. The susceptibility map based on random forest shows that high susceptibility areas account for about 18% of the study area but contain about 72% of the historical landslide points, indicating that the zoning results have good indicative significance. Compared with traditional manual surveys, this method can save a large amount of field work and quickly update susceptibility maps, and is especially suitable for remote tropical mountainous areas. In terms of benefits, the results can directly serve land use planning, road alignment, settlement site selection, and rainy season early warning, helping management departments prioritize the deployment of monitoring equipment and evacuation routes in high-risk areas to reduce disaster losses.

Conclusion: This paper combines remote sensing data with machine learning algorithms to establish a landslide susceptibility mapping workflow in a tropical environment. The study shows that the random forest model performs best in this study area and can effectively identify high landslide susceptibility areas. This method has the advantages of easily accessible data, low computational cost, and strong repeatability, and is suitable for promotion in tropical developing countries and regions. In the future, time-series remote sensing and rainfall forecast data can be further introduced to achieve dynamic susceptibility assessment, and field verification can be combined to continuously improve model accuracy.

title: Linkages between Epithelial Microbiota and Host Transcriptome in the Ileum during High-Grain Challenges: Implications for Gut Homeostasis in Goats
text:
Association of Ileal Epithelial Microbiota with Host Transcriptome under High-Grain Challenge: Implications for Intestinal Homeostasis in Goats

 Abstract

Objective: High-grain diets (HG) are widely used in ruminant production, but excessive grain intake can readily induce subacute ruminal acidosis and posterior gut microecological imbalance. This study aimed to investigate the association between ileal epithelial microbiota and the host transcriptome in goats under high-grain challenge, and to reveal its potential effects on intestinal homeostasis. Methods: Twelve healthy adult goats were randomly divided into a control group (CON, concentrate-to-forage ratio 30:70) and a high-grain group (HG, concentrate-to-forage ratio 70:30), and were fed for 8 weeks. Ileal epithelial tissues were collected for 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and RNA-seq transcriptome sequencing, respectively, combined with bioinformatics analysis of microbiota-host gene expression associations. Results: High-grain challenge significantly altered the composition of the ileal epithelial microbiota, in which the abundances of *Prevotella*, *Streptococcus*, and *Lactobacillus* were significantly increased (P<0.05), while the abundances of *Ruminococcus* and *Butyrivibrio* were decreased. Transcriptome analysis identified 1,247 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), mainly enriched in inflammatory response, barrier function, lipid metabolism, and immune signaling pathways. Association analysis showed that *Prevotella* abundance was positively correlated with the expression of TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway genes (*TLR4*, *MYD88*, *NFKB1*) (r>0.65, P<0.01), while *Lactobacillus* was positively correlated with the expression of tight junction protein genes (*OCLN*, *CLDN1*) (r>0.60, P<0.01). Conclusion: High-grain diets disrupt intestinal homeostasis by remodeling the ileal epithelial microbiota, activating host inflammatory signaling, and impairing barrier function. The microbiota-transcriptome association network provides potential targets for the regulation of intestinal health in ruminants.

Keywords: high-grain diet; ileal epithelial microbiota; transcriptome; intestinal homeostasis; goat; microbiota-host interaction

 1 Introduction

With the development of intensive farming, high-grain diets have been widely used to improve the production performance of ruminants because of their high energy density. However, long-term high-grain feeding leads to a decrease in ruminal pH and accumulation of volatile fatty acids, thereby inducing subacute ruminal acidosis (SARA). In recent years, studies have shown that SARA not only affects the rumen but also causes microbial dysbiosis and epithelial barrier damage in the posterior gut (such as the ileum and colon), thereby inducing systemic inflammation. The ileum, as a key site for nutrient absorption and immune defense, plays an important role in maintaining intestinal homeostasis through the interaction between its epithelial microbiota and the host. However, research on the association between ileal epithelial microbiota and the host transcriptome in goats under high-grain challenge remains insufficient. This study systematically analyzed the effects of high-grain diets on the ileal microecology and gene expression of goats by integrating 16S rRNA sequencing and RNA-seq technology, aiming to provide a theoretical basis for the regulation of intestinal health in ruminants.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Experimental Design and Animal Management

Twelve healthy 6-month-old Xiangdong black goats with similar body weight (25.3±2.1 kg) were selected and randomly divided into 2 groups (n=6): the control group (CON) was fed a basal diet with a concentrate-to-forage ratio of 30:70, and the high-grain group (HG) was fed a high-grain diet with a concentrate-to-forage ratio of 70:30. The pre-feeding period was 2 weeks, and the formal trial period was 8 weeks. The animals were fed twice daily (08:00 and 16:00) with free access to water. Feed intake and body weight changes were recorded during the trial period.

 2.2 Sample Collection

At the end of the trial, the goats were fasted for 12 h and then slaughtered. The abdominal cavity was quickly opened, and the mid-ileum tissue was collected. The intestinal luminal contents were rinsed with sterile PBS, and the epithelial mucosal layer was scraped. One portion was immediately stored in liquid nitrogen for RNA extraction, and the other portion was placed in sterile cryopreservation tubes for microbial DNA extraction.

 2.3 Microbial 16S rRNA Sequencing

Total DNA of the epithelial microbiota was extracted using the QIAamp DNA Stool Mini Kit, and PCR amplification was performed targeting the V3-V4 region with primers 338F/806R. After purification and quantification, the amplification products were subjected to paired-end sequencing on the Illumina NovaSeq platform. QIIME2 was used for sequence quality control, clustering, and taxonomic annotation, with the Silva database as reference.

 2.4 Transcriptome Sequencing and Analysis

Total RNA from the ileal epithelium was extracted using the Trizol method. After quality inspection, a cDNA library was constructed and sequenced on the Illumina HiSeq platform. After quality control of the raw data with fastp, Hisat2 was used to align reads to the goat reference genome (ARS1), and StringTie was used to calculate expression levels. DESeq2 was used to screen differentially expressed genes (|log2FC|>1, FDR<0.05). GO and KEGG enrichment analyses were performed on the DEGs.

 2.5 Microbiota-Host Association Analysis

Based on genus-level microbial abundance and DEG expression levels, the Spearman correlation coefficient was used to construct an association network, and significant association pairs with |r|>0.6 and P<0.01 were screened. Cytoscape was used to visualize the network.

 2.6 Statistical Analysis

Data are presented as mean±standard deviation. SPSS 26.0 was used for t-tests or Mann-Whitney U tests, with P<0.05 considered statistically significant.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Effects of High-Grain Challenge on Ileal Epithelial Microbial Composition

A total of 1,245,678 valid sequences were obtained by sequencing, with an average of 103,806 sequences per sample. Alpha diversity analysis showed that the Shannon index of the HG group was significantly lower than that of the CON group (P<0.05), indicating that high grain reduced microbial diversity. Beta diversity (PCoA) showed that the microbial community structures of the two groups were significantly separated (PERMANOVA, P<0.01). At the genus level, the relative abundances of *Prevotella*, *Streptococcus*, and *Lactobacillus* were significantly increased in the HG group (P<0.05), while the abundances of *Ruminococcus*, *Butyrivibrio*, and *Fibrobacter* were significantly decreased (P<0.05). These changes suggest that the high-grain diet promoted the proliferation of acid-producing bacteria and potential pathogens, and inhibited the growth of fibrolytic bacteria.

 3.2 Differential Expression Analysis of the Ileal Epithelial Transcriptome

A total of 42.6 Gb clean data were obtained by RNA-seq, with Q30>92%. Compared with the CON group, 1,247 DEGs were identified in the HG group, including 682 upregulated genes and 565 downregulated genes. KEGG enrichment analysis showed that the DEGs were significantly enriched in Toll-like receptor signaling pathway, NF-κB signaling pathway, apoptosis, tight junction, and fatty acid metabolism pathways (P<0.05). Among them, the expression of inflammation-related genes such as *TLR4*, *MYD88*, *NFKB1*, *TNF-α*, and *IL-1β* was significantly upregulated, while the expression of tight junction protein genes such as *OCLN*, *CLDN1*, and *ZO-1* was significantly downregulated. In addition, the expression of lipid metabolism-related genes (*FABP2*, *SCD*) also changed significantly.

 3.3 Microbiota-Host Transcriptome Association Network

Spearman correlation analysis revealed that *Prevotella* abundance was significantly positively correlated with the expression of *TLR4* (r=0.72), *MYD88* (r=0.68), and *NFKB1* (r=0.65) (P<0.01); *Streptococcus* was positively correlated with *IL-1β* (r=0.63) and *TNF-α* (r=0.61). In contrast, *Lactobacillus* was positively correlated with the expression of *OCLN* (r=0.66) and *CLDN1* (r=0.62) (P<0.01). *Ruminococcus* was positively correlated with *FABP2* expression (r=0.59, P<0.05). The association network showed that changes in the microbial community were closely related to host inflammatory activation and barrier damage.

 4 Discussion

This study systematically revealed for the first time the association between ileal epithelial microbiota and the host transcriptome in goats under high-grain challenge. The high-grain diet led to a decrease in ileal microbial diversity and the enrichment of potential pathogens such as *Prevotella* and *Streptococcus*, which is consistent with previous reports on posterior gut microbial dysbiosis in SARA animals. *Prevotella* can produce lipopolysaccharide (LPS), activate the TLR4/NF-κB signaling pathway, and induce the expression of inflammatory factors. In this study, *Prevotella* abundance was positively correlated with the expression of TLR4/NF-κB pathway genes, supporting its driving role in intestinal inflammation.

Tight junction proteins are key to maintaining the integrity of the epithelial barrier. This study found that the expression of *OCLN* and *CLDN1* was downregulated in the high-grain group and was positively correlated with *Lactobacillus* abundance. *Lactobacillus*, as a beneficial bacterium, can promote the expression of tight junction proteins and maintain barrier function through metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids. Although *Lactobacillus* increased to some extent under high-grain conditions, it may not be sufficient to offset the damaging effects of pathogenic bacteria. In addition, the reduction of fibrolytic bacteria such as *Ruminococcus* may lead to decreased production of short-chain fatty acids, further weakening barrier protection.

It is noteworthy that the high-grain diet also affected the expression of lipid metabolism-related genes, suggesting that changes in the intestinal microecology may affect host energy homeostasis through metabolic reprogramming. The microbiota-host association network provides a new perspective for understanding the regulation of intestinal homeostasis and also provides a theoretical basis for developing targeted microecological intervention strategies (such as probiotics and postbiotics).

This study has certain limitations: the sample size was relatively small, and only the ileal epithelium was focused on. Future studies combining multi-omics and multiple intestinal segments are needed to further verify the causal relationship of microbiota-host interactions.

 5 Conclusion

The high-grain diet significantly altered the ileal epithelial microbiota of goats, enriched potential pathogens such as *Prevotella* and *Streptococcus*, activated the TLR4/NF-κB inflammatory pathway, and simultaneously downregulated the expression of tight junction proteins, impairing intestinal barrier function. The microbiota-host transcriptome association network revealed that *Prevotella* was positively correlated with inflammatory signaling, and *Lactobacillus* was positively correlated with barrier function. These findings indicate that high-grain challenge disrupts ileal homeostasis through microbiota-host interactions, providing potential targets for the regulation of intestinal health in ruminants.

title: Does Green Space Really Matter for Residents' Obesity? A New Perspective From Baidu Street View
text:
Title: Does Green Space Really Affect Resident Obesity? — A New Perspective Based on Baidu Street View

Abstract: Obesity has become an important public health issue in China. Traditional studies mostly rely on remote sensing imagery to calculate green space coverage, but this method struggles to reflect the street-level green view index that residents actually encounter in their daily travel. Based on Baidu Street View images, this paper uses deep learning semantic segmentation technology to extract the green view index, combines it with resident health survey data, and re-examines the relationship between green space and obesity. The study finds that the street green view index is significantly negatively correlated with resident obesity rates, and this association remains robust after controlling for individual socioeconomic attributes. The results indicate that focusing only on macro-level green space coverage may underestimate the health benefits of green space, and street-level greening construction has scalable practical value for suppressing obesity.

1 Introduction

With the acceleration of urbanization, residents' physical activity has decreased and high-calorie diets have increased, leading to a continuous rise in obesity rates. A large number of studies have explored whether green space helps reduce obesity risk, but the conclusions are inconsistent. An important reason lies in the bias in green space measurement methods. Previously, the normalized difference vegetation index or green space coverage rate was commonly used. These indicators are viewed from high altitude and reflect the overall greening level of a region, but they cannot answer "how much green can residents see while walking on the street." In fact, what residents encounter daily is street space, not the abstract green space in remote sensing imagery. Therefore, a green space measurement method closer to a human-centered perspective is needed.

Baidu Street View images provide a new tool for this challenge. Street View vehicles cover major urban roads, and the images contain real greening information such as street trees, shrubs, and grass. Through pixel-level segmentation of Street View images using deep learning models, the green view index can be calculated, that is, the proportion of green plants in the human field of view. This indicator is closer to residents' actual perception. Using Baidu Street View data, combined with a resident obesity survey, this paper analyzes the relationship between the green view index and obesity, providing new evidence for research on the health benefits of green space.

2 Key Technical Analysis

2.1 Street View Image Collection and Preprocessing

The study selects the main urban area of a provincial capital city as the case area. Using the road network as the skeleton, sampling points are set at 50-meter intervals, and the Baidu Street View Static Image API is called to obtain four images at horizontal viewing angles of 0°, 90°, 180°, and 270°, with a resolution of 1024×512. Points with abnormal weather, severe occlusion, and no image are excluded, and finally 12,860 valid sampling points are obtained. To reduce seasonal differences, image collection is concentrated in the summer period when vegetation is lush.

2.2 Deep Learning Semantic Segmentation for Extracting the Green View Index

The DeepLabv3+ model is used for semantic segmentation. This model uses ResNet-101 as the backbone network, is pretrained on the Cityscapes dataset, and is then fine-tuned using 2,000 self-annotated Street View images. The categories include trees, grass, shrubs, buildings, roads, sky, vehicles, pedestrians, and others. The green view index is defined as the proportion of the sum of pixels of trees, grass, and shrubs to the total pixels. The model's mean intersection over union on the validation set is 0.78, and the correlation between the predicted green view index and manual annotation reaches 0.91, with accuracy meeting the analysis requirements.

2.3 Individual Obesity Data and Covariates

Resident health data come from a community survey in the same period, covering permanent residents aged 18 and above, with 8,432 people ultimately included. Obesity is determined by a body mass index ≥28 kg/m². Covariates include age, sex, education level, household income, smoking, drinking, history of chronic disease, and physical activity level. To control for spatial autocorrelation, individual data are matched to the average green view index of the subdistrict to which they belong.

2.4 Statistical Model

A multilevel logistic regression is used, with subdistrict as the random intercept, individuals as the first level, and subdistricts as the second level. The model gradually includes the green view index, individual covariates, and subdistrict socioeconomic variables. In addition, a sensitivity analysis is conducted by grouping the green view index into quartiles to test the dose-response relationship.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

Descriptive statistics show that the average street green view index in the study area is 0.21, ranging from 0.06 to 0.47. The obesity rate is 12.3%. The results of the multilevel models are shown in Table 1. Model 1 includes only the green view index, and its odds ratio is 0.72, meaning that for every 0.1 increase in the green view index, obesity risk decreases by 28%. After Model 2 adds individual covariates, the odds ratio is 0.79, and the association weakens slightly but remains significant. Model 3 further controls for subdistrict income level and population density, and the odds ratio is 0.81, with the conclusion remaining robust.

When grouped by quartiles, using the lowest group as the reference, the odds ratios of the second, third, and fourth groups are 0.88, 0.76, and 0.65, respectively, showing a clear dose-response trend. This indicates that the higher the green view index, the lower the obesity risk.

From the perspective of benefits, improving the street green view index has the advantages of strong operability and relatively low cost. Compared with building large parks, adding street trees, shrub hedges, and small street pocket parks is easier to embed into the existing urban fabric. If the green view index in the study area is increased from 0.21 to 0.30, according to model predictions, the obesity rate can decrease by about 1.8 percentage points, corresponding to about 1,500 fewer obese residents. Based on an estimate of related annual medical expenditure per person, this could save tens of millions of yuan in health costs. In addition, improving the green view index can also improve the thermal environment, reduce noise, and promote willingness to walk, generating synergistic health benefits.

4 Conclusion

Based on Baidu Street View and deep learning, this paper re-examines the relationship between green space and obesity from a human-centered perspective. The study shows that the street green view index is significantly negatively correlated with resident obesity and is independent of individual socioeconomic attributes. This finding indicates that traditional remote sensing green space indicators may underestimate the health benefits of green space, while the Street View green view index is closer to residents' actual exposure. For technology promotion, Baidu Street View has wide coverage, fast updates, and low cost, and the semantic segmentation model is open source and transferable, making it suitable for large-scale application in urban health monitoring. It is recommended that urban planning and health departments incorporate the green view index into the healthy city evaluation system, prioritize supplemental greening in subdistricts with high obesity incidence, and achieve obesity prevention and control through low-cost interventions. In the future, multi-temporal Street View can be combined to further analyze the dynamic health effects of green space changes.

title: Pathogenic infection and immune-related gene expression of Chinese sturgeon (Acipenser sinensis) challenged by Citrobacter freundii
text:
Effects of Citrobacter freundii Infection on Pathogenicity and Immune-Related Gene Expression in Acipenser sinensis

 Abstract

To investigate the pathogenicity of Citrobacter freundii to Acipenser sinensis and the characteristics of the immune response it induces, healthy juvenile A. sinensis were used as experimental subjects in this study. Bacterial suspensions of C. freundii at different concentrations (1×10⁵, 1×10⁶, 1×10⁷ CFU/mL) were administered via intraperitoneal injection. Cumulative mortality was recorded within 14 d post-infection, and quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) was employed to detect the expression changes of immune-related genes including IL-1β, TNF-α, IL-10, MyD88, and NF-κB in the head kidney, spleen, and liver at 0, 6, 12, 24, 48, and 72 h post-infection. The results showed that C. freundii exhibited significant pathogenicity to A. sinensis, with a 14-d cumulative mortality of 76.7% in the 1×10⁷ CFU/mL group and a median lethal concentration (LD₅₀) of 3.2×10⁶ CFU/mL. Immune gene expression in various tissues exhibited significant temporal changes post-infection: the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and TNF-α were significantly upregulated in the early stage of infection (6–12 h) (P<0.05), with IL-1β in the head kidney peaking at 12 h (18.6-fold that of the control group); MyD88 and NF-κB were continuously highly expressed within 24 h, suggesting activation of the TLR/MyD88/NF-κB signaling pathway; the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 was significantly elevated after 48 h, participating in the regulation of inflammation resolution. This study demonstrates that C. freundii can induce a strong innate immune response in A. sinensis, with the head kidney being the primary responsive organ, and the TLR-MyD88-NF-κB pathway playing a key role in its antibacterial immunity. This study provides a theoretical basis for the prevention and control of bacterial diseases and research on immune mechanisms in A. sinensis.

Keywords: Acipenser sinensis; Citrobacter freundii; pathogenicity; immune-related genes; innate immunity; qRT-PCR

 1 Introduction

Acipenser sinensis belongs to the order Acipenseriformes, family Acipenseridae, and is a rare migratory fish endemic to China, known as the "giant panda in water," with significant scientific, ecological, and economic value. In recent years, due to factors such as water pollution, navigation engineering, and habitat fragmentation, the wild population of A. sinensis has declined dramatically and has been listed as a national first-class key protected wild animal. In the process of artificial breeding and ex situ conservation, the frequent outbreak of bacterial diseases has become one of the key bottlenecks restricting the conservation and aquaculture industry development of A. sinensis.

Citrobacter freundii belongs to the genus Citrobacter, family Enterobacteriaceae, and is a typical zoonotic opportunistic pathogen widely distributed in aquatic and soil environments. This bacterium can infect various freshwater fish species, causing symptoms such as septicemia, enteritis, and body surface ulcers, resulting in severe economic losses to aquaculture. Currently, research on the pathogenicity of C. freundii to fish has mostly focused on economically important fish such as carp, crucian carp, and grass carp, while systematic studies on its pathogenicity to A. sinensis and the host immune response mechanisms remain lacking.

As lower vertebrates, fish primarily rely on innate immunity to defend against pathogen invasion. The Toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling pathway is a key pathway for recognizing pathogen-associated molecular patterns and initiating immune responses, in which myeloid differentiation factor 88 (MyD88) and nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) are the core adaptor and transcriptional regulatory factors of this pathway. The pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and TNF-α, as well as the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10, play important regulatory roles in the onset and resolution of inflammation. In view of this, the present study evaluated the pathogenicity of C. freundii to A. sinensis through artificial infection experiments and analyzed the expression dynamics of immune-related genes in different tissues post-infection, aiming to reveal the immune response characteristics of A. sinensis to this bacterium and provide a scientific basis for its disease prevention and control and germplasm protection.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Experimental Fish

A total of 180 healthy juvenile A. sinensis (body mass 120±15 g, body length 28±3 cm) were obtained from the A. sinensis breeding base of a fisheries research institute. Before the experiment, the fish were acclimated in a recirculating water system for 2 weeks at a water temperature of (20±1)°C, dissolved oxygen >6 mg/L, and pH 7.2–7.6, and were fed a commercial formulated diet for sturgeon daily. No abnormal mortality occurred during the acclimation period, and random sampling was conducted for bacteriological examination to confirm the absence of C. freundii infection.

 2.2 Bacterial Strain and Suspension Preparation

The C. freundii strain was isolated and purified from diseased A. sinensis and confirmed by the VITEK 2 automated microbial identification system and 16S rRNA gene sequencing. The strain was cultured in LB medium at 28°C with shaking for 18 h, and bacterial cells were collected by centrifugation, washed and resuspended in sterile physiological saline, adjusted to a concentration of 1×10⁹ CFU/mL using the McFarland turbidity method, and serially diluted to the required concentrations.

 2.3 Artificial Infection Experiment

A total of 180 A. sinensis were randomly divided into 4 groups (45 fish per group): a control group (injected with an equal volume of sterile physiological saline) and 3 infection groups, which were intraperitoneally injected with 0.2 mL of bacterial suspensions at 1×10⁵, 1×10⁶, and 1×10⁷ CFU/mL, respectively. After infection, observations were continuously made for 14 d, mortality was recorded, and cumulative mortality and median lethal concentration (LD₅₀) were calculated. One-third of the water was renewed daily, and dead fish were promptly removed and subjected to bacterial re-isolation to confirm the cause of death.

 2.4 Tissue Sample Collection

At 0, 6, 12, 24, 48, and 72 h post-infection, 3 fish were randomly selected from each group, anesthetized with MS-222, and dissected. Head kidney, spleen, and liver tissues were aseptically collected, snap-frozen in liquid nitrogen, and stored at -80°C for later use.

 2.5 RNA Extraction and qRT-PCR

Total RNA was extracted from tissues using the TRIzol method, treated with DNase I to remove genomic DNA, and cDNA was synthesized using a reverse transcription kit. Specific primers were designed based on A. sinensis gene sequences (Table 1), with β-actin as the internal reference gene. The qRT-PCR reaction system was 20 μL, with conditions of 95°C pre-denaturation for 30 s, followed by 40 cycles of 95°C for 5 s and 60°C for 30 s. The 2^(-ΔΔCt) method was used to calculate the relative expression levels of target genes.

Table 1 Primer Sequences

| Gene | Forward Primer (5′→3′) | Reverse Primer (5′→3′) |
|------|--------------------------|--------------------------|
| IL-1β | GCTACCTGTGTCCTGGATGT | CAGGTGCTCATGTCCTTCAC |
| TNF-α | CCATCGAGGAACTGACAGGA | TGAGGTTGTCTTCGGACTGG |
| IL-10 | GCCTACAGAGCCTACATGGA | CTCCGTGTTCTGGTCCTTGT |
| MyD88 | TGGTACCTGCAGCTCAAGAA | GTGCTTGTCGTTGTTGCTGA |
| NF-κB | AGACCAAGCAGATGGTGGAG | TGGTTCAGGTTGTTGCTGTC |
| β-actin | CCATCGAGCACGGCATCAT | TCGTAGATGGGCACAGTGTG |

 2.6 Data Processing

Data are presented as mean ± standard deviation. One-way ANOVA was performed using SPSS 22.0 software, and Duncan's multiple comparison test was used to examine differences between groups, with P<0.05 considered statistically significant.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Clinical Symptoms and Cumulative Mortality

Infected A. sinensis began to show symptoms at 12 h post-infection, manifesting as sluggish swimming, reduced appetite, and increased body surface mucus. Symptoms worsened at 24–48 h, with some fish exhibiting abdominal distension and anal redness and swelling; dissection revealed abdominal cavity effusion, hepatic congestion and enlargement, and dark red spleen. The control group showed no abnormalities.

In the 1×10⁷ CFU/mL group, the earliest death occurred at 24 h post-infection, with a 14-d cumulative mortality of 76.7%; the cumulative mortality in the 1×10⁶ CFU/mL group was 46.7%; the cumulative mortality in the 1×10⁵ CFU/mL group was 20.0%; and the mortality in the control group was 0. The calculated LD₅₀ of C. freundii to juvenile A. sinensis was 3.2×10⁶ CFU/mL (Table 2).

Table 2 Cumulative Mortality of A. sinensis After Infection with Different Concentrations of C. freundii

| Group | 14-d Cumulative Mortality (%) |
|------|-------------------------------|
| Control | 0 |
| 1×10⁵ CFU/mL | 20.0 |
| 1×10⁶ CFU/mL | 46.7 |
| 1×10⁷ CFU/mL | 76.7 |

 3.2 Expression Dynamics of Immune-Related Genes

 3.2.1 Head Kidney Tissue

The changes in immune gene expression in the head kidney post-infection were the most significant. IL-1β began to be upregulated at 6 h, peaked at 12 h (18.6-fold that of the control group, P<0.01), then gradually declined, remaining higher than the control at 72 h. TNF-α was significantly elevated at 6 h and peaked at 12 h (12.3-fold). MyD88 and NF-κB were significantly upregulated as early as 6 h and peaked at 24 h, at 8.5-fold and 9.7-fold that of the control group, respectively. IL-10 expression was delayed, peaking at 48 h (6.2-fold) and maintaining a relatively high level at 72 h.

 3.2.2 Spleen Tissue

In the spleen, IL-1β and TNF-α peaked at 12 h, at 10.2-fold and 8.7-fold that of the control group, respectively. MyD88 and NF-κB were significantly upregulated at 12–24 h, with peaks at 6.8-fold and 7.5-fold, respectively. IL-10 peaked at 48 h (5.1-fold). The overall expression magnitude was lower than that in the head kidney.

 3.2.3 Liver Tissue

The immune gene response in the liver was relatively weak. IL-1β and TNF-α were mildly upregulated at 12 h (4.3-fold and 3.8-fold, respectively), and MyD88 and NF-κB peaked at 24 h (4.5-fold and 5.2-fold). IL-10 rose to 3.6-fold at 48 h. The expression peaks of all genes were significantly lower than those in the head kidney and spleen (P<0.05).

 4 Discussion

The results of this study indicate that C. freundii has strong pathogenicity to juvenile A. sinensis, with an LD₅₀ of 3.2×10⁶ CFU/mL, and infection can cause typical septicemia symptoms, consistent with reports in other fish species. The pathological findings of hepatic congestion, splenic enlargement, and abdominal cavity effusion suggest that the bacterium can cause multi-organ damage through the bloodstream, and its pathogenic mechanism may involve the synergistic action of virulence factors such as endotoxins and hemolysins.

Analysis of immune gene expression revealed that C. freundii infection can rapidly activate the innate immune system of A. sinensis. As key pro-inflammatory cytokines, IL-1β and TNF-α were significantly upregulated in the early stage of infection, participating in pathogen clearance and the initiation of inflammatory responses. The highest peak of IL-1β expression was observed in the head kidney, which is consistent with the functional role of the head kidney as the primary hematopoietic and immune organ in fish. The synchronized high expression of MyD88 and NF-κB indicates that the TLR/MyD88/NF-κB signaling pathway plays a core role in recognizing C. freundii and transducing immune signals. Lipopolysaccharide of Gram-negative bacteria can be recognized by TLR4, which then recruits MyD88, activating NF-κB nuclear translocation and initiating downstream inflammatory cytokine transcription.

IL-10, as an important anti-inflammatory cytokine, had its expression lag behind pro-inflammatory cytokines, peaking at 48 h, which conforms to the negative feedback regulation pattern of inflammation resolution and helps prevent tissue damage caused by excessive inflammation.
