As one of the core elements of processing technology, processing adjuvants typically include wine, vinegar, honey, ginger juice, salt water, wheat bran, etc., and possess functions such as guiding drugs to specific meridians, enhancing efficacy, reducing toxicity, and altering drug properties [1]. In recent years, with the deepening of research on the modernization of TCM, the effects of processing adjuvants on the chemical composition and pharmacological activity of TCM have gradually become a research hotspot. However, systematic comparative studies on the effects of different adjuvants on the same medicinal material or the same adjuvant on different medicinal materials remain relatively insufficient.

Scutellaria baicalensis Georgi possesses the effects of clearing heat and drying dampness, and purging fire and detoxifying, with baicalin as its main active ingredient; Coptis chinensis Franch. clears heat and dries dampness, and purges fire and detoxifies, mainly containing berberine; Glycyrrhiza uralensis Fisch. tonifies the spleen and replenishes qi, and clears heat and detoxifies, mainly containing glycyrrhizic acid. All three are commonly used TCMs in clinical practice, with diverse processing methods. In this paper, these three medicinal materials were used as research subjects and processed with wine, ginger juice, and honey adjuvants, respectively. The changes in active ingredient content, antioxidant activity, and cytotoxicity before and after processing were systematically compared, aiming to reveal the patterns of the effects of processing adjuvants on TCM quality and to provide data support for the scientific and standardized processing of TCM.

2 Materials and Methods

2.1 Medicinal materials and reagents

Raw Scutellaria baicalensis, Coptis chinensis, and Glycyrrhiza uralensis were purchased from a Chinese medicinal materials market and identified as meeting the standards of the Chinese Pharmacopoeia 2020 edition. Yellow wine (15% alcohol content), ginger juice (self-prepared), and honey (commercially available) were all food-grade. Baicalin, berberine, and glycyrrhizic acid reference standards (purity ≥98%) were purchased from the National Institutes for Food and Drug Control. DPPH, MTT, DMSO, and other reagents were of analytical grade.

2.2 Processing methods

Wine-processed Scutellaria baicalensis: 100 g of raw Scutellaria baicalensis was mixed with 20 mL of yellow wine, moistened for 2 h, stir-fried at 160°C for 10 min, removed, and cooled. Ginger-processed Coptis chinensis: 100 g of raw Coptis chinensis was mixed with 15 mL of ginger juice, moistened for 1 h, and stir-fried at 140°C for 8 min. Honey-processed Glycyrrhiza uralensis: 100 g of raw Glycyrrhiza uralensis was mixed with 25 g of refined honey (diluted with an appropriate amount of water), moistened for 2 h, and stir-fried at 150°C for 12 min. Three batches of each processed product were prepared in parallel.

2.3 Determination of active ingredient content

High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) was used to determine the content of baicalin, berberine, and glycyrrhizic acid. Chromatographic column: C18 column (4.6 mm × 250 mm, 5 μm); mobile phase: methanol–0.1% phosphoric acid aqueous solution (gradient elution); detection wavelength: baicalin 274 nm, berberine 345 nm, glycyrrhizic acid 250 nm; flow rate 1.0 mL/min; column temperature 30°C.

2.4 Determination of antioxidant activity

The DPPH free radical scavenging method was used. 2 mL of each sample extract (0.1–2.0 mg/mL) was mixed with 2 mL of 0.1 mmol/L DPPH ethanol solution, reacted in the dark for 30 min, and the absorbance was measured at 517 nm. The scavenging rate and IC₅₀ value were calculated.

2.5 Cytotoxicity experiment

The MTT method was used. HepG2 cells were cultured in DMEM medium (containing 10% FBS). Cells in the logarithmic growth phase were seeded in 96-well plates, and samples at different concentrations (0.1–1.0 mg/mL) were added. After 48 h of culture, MTT was added, and the absorbance at 570 nm was measured to calculate the cell inhibition rate.

2.6 Data processing

Experimental data were expressed as mean ± standard deviation. One-way analysis of variance was performed using SPSS 22.0, with P<0.05 considered a significant difference.

3 Results and Analysis

3.1 Effects of processing adjuvants on active ingredient content

As shown in Table 1, after processing with different adjuvants, the active ingredient content of all three TCMs increased to varying degrees. The baicalin content in wine-processed Scutellaria baicalensis was (12.45±0.32)%, an increase of 18.6% compared with the raw product (10.50±0.28)%; the berberine content in ginger-processed Coptis chinensis was (8.72±0.21)%, an increase of 12.4% compared with the raw product (7.76±0.19)%; the glycyrrhizic acid content in honey-processed Glycyrrhiza uralensis was (5.68±0.15)%, an increase of 15.2% compared with the raw product (4.93±0.13)%. All differences were statistically significant (P<0.05). It is speculated that components such as organic acids and sugars in the adjuvants can promote the dissolution or transformation of active ingredients.

Table 1 Changes in active ingredient content before and after processing (%, n=3)

| Sample | Active ingredient | Raw product | Processed product | Increase rate |
|------|----------|------|--------|--------|
| Scutellaria baicalensis | Baicalin | 10.50±0.28 | 12.45±0.32* | 18.6% |
| Coptis chinensis | Berberine | 7.76±0.19 | 8.72±0.21* | 12.4% |
| Glycyrrhiza uralensis | Glycyrrhizic acid | 4.93±0.13 | 5.68±0.15* | 15.2% |

Note: *Compared with the raw product, P<0.05.

3.2 Effects of processing adjuvants on antioxidant activity

The DPPH scavenging experiment results showed that the antioxidant activity of all processed products was superior to that of the raw products. The IC₅₀ of honey-processed Glycyrrhiza uralensis was (0.42±0.03) mg/mL, 31.1% lower than that of the raw product (0.61±0.04) mg/mL; the IC₅₀ of wine-processed Scutellaria baicalensis was (0.55±0.04) mg/mL, 29.5% lower than that of the raw product (0.78±0.05) mg/mL; the IC₅₀ of ginger-processed Coptis chinensis was (0.68±0.05) mg/mL, 23.6% lower than that of the raw product (0.89±0.06) mg/mL. The enhancement of antioxidant activity after processing may be related to the inherent antioxidant properties of the adjuvants and the increased content of active ingredients.

3.3 Effects of processing adjuvants on cytotoxicity

The MTT experiment showed that the inhibitory effects of all three processed TCMs on HepG2 cells were stronger than those of the raw products. At a concentration of 1.0 mg/mL, the inhibition rate of wine-processed Scutellaria baicalensis was (62.3±3.1)%, compared with (48.7±2.8)% for the raw product; the inhibition rate of ginger-processed Coptis chinensis was (55.6±2.9)%, compared with (43.2±2.5)% for the raw product; the inhibition rate of honey-processed Glycyrrhiza uralensis was (49.8±2.6)%, compared with (38.4±2.2)% for the raw product. All differences were significant (P<0.05). This suggests that processing adjuvants can enhance the antitumor activity of TCM.

4 Discussion

This study systematically compared the effects of three processing adjuvants—wine, ginger, and honey—on the quality of Scutellaria baicalensis, Coptis chinensis, and Glycyrrhiza uralensis. The results showed that processing adjuvants can significantly increase the content of active ingredients and enhance antioxidant activity and cytotoxicity. The mechanisms may include: (1) components such as organic acids and sugars in the adjuvants form complexes with the active ingredients in the medicinal materials, promoting dissolution; (2) during heating, the adjuvants participate in the Maillard reaction, generating antioxidant active substances; (3) the adjuvants alter the cell wall permeability of the medicinal materials, facilitating the release of components [2-3].

It is noteworthy that the effects of different adjuvants on the same medicinal material or the same adjuvant on different medicinal materials differ. The effect of wine-processed Scutellaria baicalensis in increasing baicalin content was superior to the effect of ginger-processed Coptis chinensis in increasing berberine, which may be related to the better solubility of baicalin in ethanol in yellow wine than that of berberine in ginger juice. In addition, the enhancement of antioxidant activity was most significant in honey-processed Glycyrrhiza uralensis, which may be related to the abundant phenolic compounds in honey.

This study also has certain limitations: only three medicinal materials and three adjuvants were selected, with a limited sample size; the interactive effects of processing parameters such as temperature and time were not investigated; and only a single cell line was used in the cell experiments. Future research can expand the combinations of medicinal materials and adjuvants, and combine metabolomics, proteomics, and other technologies to further explore the mechanisms of action of processing adjuvants.

5 Conclusion

Through systematic research on the effects of three processing adjuvants—wine, ginger, and honey—on the active ingredients, antioxidant activity, and cytotoxicity of Scutellaria baicalensis, Coptis chinensis, and Glycyrrhiza uralensis, the following conclusions were drawn: (1) processing adjuvants can significantly increase the content of active ingredients in TCM, with baicalin in wine-processed Scutellaria baicalensis increasing by 18.6%, berberine in ginger-processed Coptis chinensis increasing by 12.4%, and glycyrrhizic acid in honey-processed Glycyrrhiza uralensis increasing by 15.2%; (2) the antioxidant activity of all processed products was superior to that of the raw products, with the IC₅₀ of honey-processed Glycyrrhiza uralensis decreasing by 31.1%; (3) the inhibitory effects of the processed products on HepG2 cells were enhanced. This study provides experimental evidence for the scientific selection of processing adjuvants and the standardization of processing technology for TCM, and is of great significance for promoting the modernization of TCM.

References:

[1] Wang Xiaotao. Science of Traditional Chinese Medicine Processing [M]. Beijing: China Press of Traditional Chinese Medicine, 2018: 45-52.

[2] Li Wei, Zhang Tao, Liu Yang. Research progress on the effects of processing adjuvants on the chemical composition of traditional Chinese medicine [J]. China Journal of Chinese Materia Medica, 2021, 46(12): 3056-3063.

[3] Chen Jing, Zhao Ming, Sun Li. Effects of honey processing on the chemical composition and antioxidant activity of Glycyrrhiza uralensis [J]. Chinese Traditional and Herbal Drugs, 2022, 53(8): 2412-2419.

title: Cellular function of chicken FOXO3 and its associations with chicken growth
text:
Cellular Functions of Chicken FOXO3 and Its Association with Chicken Growth

Abstract: FOXO3 is an important transcription factor of the forkhead box O subfamily, playing key roles in cell cycle regulation, apoptosis, antioxidant stress response, and metabolic regulation. This study investigated the cellular functions of chicken FOXO3 and its association with growth traits in chickens. The coding region sequence of chicken FOXO3 was cloned, and a eukaryotic expression vector was constructed. FOXO3 was overexpressed in chicken myoblasts and fibroblasts, and changes in cell proliferation, apoptosis, and related gene expression were detected. Meanwhile, polymorphism site screening and growth trait association analysis were performed using a commercial chicken population. The results showed that chicken FOXO3 inhibited cell proliferation, promoted apoptosis, and downregulated the expression of growth-related genes such as IGF1 and MyoD. Two SNP sites were identified in the promoter region of the chicken FOXO3 gene, among which g.-1256A>G was significantly associated with body weight at 8 weeks of age (P<0.05). This study provides a theoretical basis for molecular marker-assisted selection of chicken growth traits.

1 Introduction

Chicken growth traits are among the core economic traits affecting breeding profitability and are regulated by multiple factors including genetics, nutrition, and environment. In recent years, with the development of molecular biology techniques, elucidating growth regulatory mechanisms at the gene level has become a hotspot in poultry genetic breeding research. FOXO3 (Forkhead box O3) is an important member of the FOXO transcription factor family and is widely involved in biological processes such as cell cycle arrest, apoptosis induction, oxidative stress resistance, and energy metabolism. In mammals, FOXO3 has been confirmed to affect muscle development and fat deposition by regulating downstream target genes. However, studies on the cellular functions of chicken FOXO3 and its association with growth traits remain insufficient.

This study aimed to clone the chicken FOXO3 gene, analyze its functions in chicken cells, and screen for polymorphic sites associated with growth traits, thereby providing candidate genes and molecular markers for genetic improvement of chicken growth traits.

2 Analysis of Key Techniques

2.1 Cloning and Sequence Analysis of the Chicken FOXO3 Gene

Total RNA was extracted from chicken liver tissue, and cDNA was obtained by reverse transcription. Specific primers were designed based on the predicted sequence from NCBI, and the FOXO3 coding region was amplified by PCR. The amplified products were detected by agarose gel electrophoresis, recovered and purified, and then ligated into the pMD18-T vector. The constructs were transformed into DH5α competent cells, and positive clones were selected for sequencing. Sequencing results showed that the chicken FOXO3 coding region is 1896 bp in full length, encoding 631 amino acids, and contains a typical forkhead box DNA-binding domain. Sequence alignment indicated that chicken FOXO3 has high homology with mammals, especially in the forkhead box region, which is highly conserved.

2.2 Construction of Eukaryotic Expression Vector and Cell Transfection

The correctly sequenced FOXO3 coding region was subcloned into the pcDNA3.1(+) vector to construct the recombinant plasmid pcDNA3.1-FOXO3. Chicken myoblasts and chicken embryonic fibroblasts were used as research subjects, and the recombinant plasmid was introduced into cells using liposome transfection. Forty-eight hours after transfection, FOXO3 expression levels were detected by RT-qPCR and Western blot to confirm overexpression efficiency. An empty vector control group was also set up to exclude non-specific effects.

2.3 Detection of Cell Proliferation and Apoptosis

Cell proliferation ability was detected using the CCK-8 assay. The results showed that the proliferative activity of myoblasts overexpressing FOXO3 was significantly lower than that of the control group (P<0.05), indicating that FOXO3 inhibits cell proliferation. Flow cytometry was used to detect the apoptosis rate, and the apoptosis rate of the overexpression group was significantly higher than that of the control group (P<0.05). Further RT-qPCR detection of apoptosis-related genes revealed that the expression of Bax and Caspase-3 was upregulated, while the expression of Bcl-2 was downregulated, suggesting that FOXO3 promotes apoptosis through the mitochondrial pathway.

2.4 Analysis of Growth-Related Gene Expression

In myoblasts overexpressing FOXO3, the expression of growth and myogenesis-related genes such as IGF1, MyoD, and MyoG was detected. The results showed that IGF1 and MyoD mRNA levels were significantly decreased (P<0.05), while MyoG showed no significant change. This indicates that FOXO3 may negatively regulate muscle development by inhibiting the IGF1 signaling pathway and the expression of myogenic determination factors.

2.5 Population Polymorphism Screening and Association Analysis

A total of 300 commercial broilers were selected, and blood samples were collected for DNA extraction. The FOXO3 promoter region and partial intron regions were amplified by PCR, and SNP sites were screened by sequencing. A total of 2 SNPs were identified: g.-1256A>G and g.2345C>T. PCR-RFLP was used for genotyping of the population, and association analysis was conducted in combination with growth traits such as body weight at 8 weeks of age and breast muscle percentage. The results showed that the g.-1256A>G site was significantly associated with body weight at 8 weeks of age (P<0.05), and individuals with the AA genotype had significantly higher body weight than those with the AG and GG genotypes. The g.2345C>T site had no significant association with growth traits.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

This study systematically revealed the cellular functions of chicken FOXO3 and its association with growth. At the cellular level, FOXO3 exerts a negative regulatory effect on growth by inhibiting proliferation, promoting apoptosis, and downregulating IGF1/MyoD expression. At the population level, the g.-1256A>G site in the promoter region was significantly associated with body weight and can be used as a molecular marker for assisted selection.

From the perspective of application benefits, this marker can be used for early selection, improving breeding efficiency and shortening the generation interval. For commercial broiler breeds, selecting individuals with the AA genotype is expected to improve body weight traits and increase breeding returns. At the same time, as a growth regulatory node, functional studies of FOXO3 provide targets for the subsequent development of gene editing or nutritional regulation strategies. It is estimated that incorporating this marker into breeding programs can achieve a 5%–10% increase in genetic progress for body weight traits, with favorable economic and social benefits.

4 Conclusion

This study cloned the chicken FOXO3 gene and confirmed its cellular functions of inhibiting cell proliferation, promoting apoptosis, and downregulating growth-related genes. A SNP site g.-1256A>G in the promoter region was screened and found to be significantly associated with body weight at 8 weeks of age. This site can serve as a candidate marker for molecular marker-assisted selection of chicken growth traits, providing new ideas and a theoretical basis for chicken genetic improvement. Future studies will further verify the general applicability of this marker in different populations and explore the specific molecular mechanisms by which FOXO3 regulates growth.

title: Effects of light quality on leaf growth and photosynthetic fluorescence of Brasenia schreberi seedlings
text:
Effects of Light Quality on Leaf Growth and Photosynthetic Fluorescence Characteristics of Water Shield (Brasenia schreberi) Seedlings

Abstract: To investigate the effects of different light qualities on leaf growth and photosynthetic fluorescence characteristics of water shield (Brasenia schreberi) seedlings, this study used one-year-old water shield seedlings as experimental materials and set up five treatments: white light (W, control), blue light (B), red light (R), red-blue mixed light (RB, red:blue = 3:1), and green light (G). Leaf morphological indicators, chlorophyll content, photosynthetic gas exchange parameters, and chlorophyll fluorescence parameters of seedlings under each treatment were measured. The results showed that: compared with the white light control, the leaf area, leaf number, chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, and total chlorophyll content of water shield seedlings under blue light and red-blue mixed light treatments were significantly increased (P<0.05), with the red-blue mixed light treatment showing the best effect; the red light treatment was second, and the green light treatment significantly inhibited seedling leaf growth. In terms of photosynthetic parameters, the net photosynthetic rate (Pn), stomatal conductance (Gs), and transpiration rate (Tr) under blue light and red-blue mixed light treatments were significantly higher than those of the control, while intercellular CO₂ concentration (Ci) was significantly reduced; the green light treatment showed the opposite trend. Chlorophyll fluorescence parameters showed that under blue light and red-blue mixed light treatments, the maximum photochemical efficiency of PSⅡ (Fv/Fm), actual photochemical efficiency of PSⅡ (ΦPSⅡ), and photochemical quenching coefficient (qP) were all significantly higher than those of the control, while the non-photochemical quenching coefficient (NPQ) was significantly reduced. The study indicates that blue light and red-blue mixed light (3:1) can effectively promote leaf growth and enhance photosynthetic capacity of water shield seedlings, with red-blue mixed light showing the best effect, while green light produces an inhibitory effect. This study provides a theoretical basis for light environment regulation in facility cultivation of water shield.

Keywords: water shield; light quality; leaf growth; photosynthetic characteristics; chlorophyll fluorescence

 1 Introduction

Water shield (Brasenia schreberi) is a perennial aquatic herbaceous plant of the genus Brasenia in the family Nymphaeaceae. It is a precious aquatic vegetable unique to China. Its tender stems and leaves are rich in polysaccharides, proteins, vitamins, and various trace elements, possessing high nutritional and medicinal value. Water shield prefers warm, humid, and semi-shaded environments and is relatively sensitive to light conditions. Direct intense light can easily cause leaf scorching, while insufficient light affects photosynthetic matter accumulation, thereby reducing yield and quality. In recent years, with the development of facility agriculture, the artificial cultivation area of water shield has been continuously expanding. How to promote robust growth of water shield seedlings through light environment regulation has become an urgent problem to be solved in production.

Light quality is one of the important environmental factors affecting plant growth and development. It not only provides energy for photosynthesis but also acts as a signal molecule regulating plant morphogenesis, physiological metabolism, and gene expression. Studies have shown that blue light can promote stomatal opening and chloroplast development, while red light is beneficial for the construction of photosynthetic organs and the accumulation of assimilates. Red-blue mixed light often exhibits synergistic effects. However, systematic studies on the effects of light quality on the growth and photosynthetic fluorescence characteristics of water shield seedlings are still rarely reported. Based on this, this study used water shield seedlings as materials, set up different light quality treatments, and investigated their effects on leaf growth, photosynthetic gas exchange, and chlorophyll fluorescence parameters, aiming to provide theoretical reference for the optimization of light environment in facility cultivation of water shield.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Experimental Materials

The experiment was conducted from March to June 2024 in an artificial climate chamber of a certain agricultural university. Healthy, uniformly sized one-year-old water shield seedlings were selected and transplanted into plastic pots (diameter 20 cm, height 15 cm) filled with garden soil and river sand (volume ratio 3:1), with 3 plants per pot, maintaining a water depth of 3–5 cm. After 7 d of acclimatization, light quality treatments were applied.

 2.2 Experimental Design

LED light sources were used to set up 5 light quality treatments: white light (W, control, spectral range 400–700 nm), blue light (B, peak 450 nm), red light (R, peak 660 nm), red-blue mixed light (RB, red:blue = 3:1), and green light (G, peak 530 nm). The light intensity for all treatments was uniformly set at 100 μmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹, with a photoperiod of 12 h·d⁻¹, temperature (25±2)°C, and relative humidity (75±5)%. Each treatment had 3 replicates, with 10 pots per replicate, and the treatment period was 30 d.

 2.3 Measurement Indicators and Methods

2.3.1 Leaf Growth Indicators

After the treatment period, 15 plants were randomly selected from each treatment. Leaf length and leaf width were measured with a ruler, and leaf area was calculated (leaf area = leaf length × leaf width × 0.75); the number of leaves per plant was counted; leaf fresh weight was weighed with an electronic balance, then blanched at 105°C for 30 min and dried at 80°C to constant weight, and dry weight was measured.

2.3.2 Chlorophyll Content

Chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, and total chlorophyll content were determined by the ethanol-acetone (1:1) mixed solution extraction method, and the chlorophyll a/b ratio was calculated.

2.3.3 Photosynthetic Gas Exchange Parameters

On the 30th day of treatment, between 9:00–11:00 AM, a LI-6400 portable photosynthesis system was used to measure net photosynthetic rate (Pn), stomatal conductance (Gs), intercellular CO₂ concentration (Ci), and transpiration rate (Tr). The measurement light intensity was 1000 μmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹, CO₂ concentration was 400 μmol·mol⁻¹, and 5 plants were measured per treatment, with averages taken.

2.3.4 Chlorophyll Fluorescence Parameters

A FMS-2 pulse-modulated fluorometer was used to measure chlorophyll fluorescence parameters. After 30 min of dark adaptation, initial fluorescence (Fo) and maximum fluorescence (Fm) were measured, and the maximum photochemical efficiency of PSⅡ (Fv/Fm) was calculated; under actinic light, steady-state fluorescence (Fs) and maximum fluorescence under light (Fm′) were measured, and the actual photochemical efficiency of PSⅡ (ΦPSⅡ), photochemical quenching coefficient (qP), and non-photochemical quenching coefficient (NPQ) were calculated.

 2.4 Data Processing

Excel 2019 was used for data organization, SPSS 26.0 was used for one-way analysis of variance (One-way ANOVA), and Duncan's new multiple range test was used for multiple comparisons, with the significance level set at P<0.05.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Effects of Light Quality on Leaf Growth of Water Shield Seedlings

As shown in Table 1, different light quality treatments had significant effects on leaf growth of water shield seedlings. Compared with the white light control (W), under blue light (B) and red-blue mixed light (RB) treatments, leaf area increased by 23.6% and 35.2%, leaf number increased by 18.4% and 26.3%, leaf fresh weight increased by 21.7% and 32.5%, and dry weight increased by 25.3% and 38.6%, respectively, all significantly higher than the control (P<0.05), and all indicators under RB treatment were significantly better than those under B treatment. Under red light (R) treatment, growth indicators increased slightly compared with the control, but the differences did not reach a significant level. Under green light (G) treatment, leaf area, leaf number, fresh weight, and dry weight decreased by 15.8%, 12.1%, 14.3%, and 16.7%, respectively, compared with the control, all significantly lower than the control (P<0.05). This indicates that blue light and red-blue mixed light have obvious promoting effects on leaf growth of water shield seedlings, with red-blue mixed light showing the best effect, while green light exhibits an inhibitory effect.

 3.2 Effects of Light Quality on Chlorophyll Content in Leaves of Water Shield Seedlings

As shown in Table 2, blue light and red-blue mixed light treatments significantly increased chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, and total chlorophyll content in leaves of water shield seedlings. Compared with the control, under B treatment, chlorophyll a, b, and total content increased by 18.6%, 22.4%, and 19.8%, respectively; under RB treatment, they increased by 27.3%, 31.5%, and 28.6%, respectively, all significantly higher than the control (P<0.05). Under red light treatment, chlorophyll content was slightly higher than the control, but the difference was not significant. Under green light treatment, chlorophyll a, b, and total content decreased by 13.2%, 10.5%, and 12.4%, respectively, compared with the control, significantly lower than the control (P<0.05). There was no significant difference in chlorophyll a/b ratio among treatments, indicating that light quality mainly affects total chlorophyll synthesis rather than component proportion.

This indicates that blue light and red-blue mixed light can effectively enhance the gas exchange capacity of water shield seedling leaves, with red-blue mixed light showing a better effect.

title: Mechanism and application of Sesbania root-nodulating bacteria: an alternative for chemical fertilizers and sustainable development
text:
Mechanisms and Applications of Sesbania Rhizobia: A New Pathway for Fertilizer Substitution and Sustainable Development

Abstract: Long-term excessive application of chemical nitrogen fertilizer has brought about a series of problems such as soil degradation, water pollution, and greenhouse gas emissions. Finding environmentally friendly biological nitrogen fixation alternatives has become an urgent need for green agricultural development. Sesbania, as a salt-tolerant and waterlogging-tolerant leguminous green manure plant, can form root nodules through symbiosis with rhizobia and carry out efficient biological nitrogen fixation. This paper reviews the key mechanisms of Sesbania rhizobia, including symbiotic recognition, nitrogen fixation regulation, growth-promoting effects, and stress adaptation, and analyzes the feasibility and comprehensive benefits of substituting part of chemical nitrogen fertilizer in combination with application scenarios such as saline-alkali land improvement, green manure return, and rotation/intercropping. The results show that inoculation with matching Sesbania rhizobia can significantly increase Sesbania biomass and nitrogen fixation, increase soil organic matter and alkaline hydrolyzable nitrogen content, improve soil aggregate structure, and demonstrate good effects in saline-alkali land improvement. This technology is low-cost, easy to operate, and has low environmental risk. It is suitable for promotion in saline-alkali lands, medium- and low-yield fields, and green manure planting areas, and is an important technical pathway for promoting fertilizer reduction and efficiency enhancement and sustainable agricultural development.

Keywords: Sesbania; rhizobia; biological nitrogen fixation; saline-alkali land improvement; green manure; chemical fertilizer reduction

1 Introduction

Nitrogen is a key limiting factor for crop yield formation. Over the past decades, the massive application of chemical nitrogen fertilizer has supported the rapid growth of grain yields, but it has also brought about problems such as soil acidification, compaction, water eutrophication, and nitrous oxide emissions. China's fertilizer application rate has long been relatively high, with nitrogen use efficiency being only 30%–40%, and a large amount of nitrogen being lost through leaching, runoff, and gaseous forms. Under the policy background of "zero growth in chemical fertilizers" and green agricultural development, using biological nitrogen fixation to partially replace chemical nitrogen fertilizer has become a realistic and feasible technical route.

The symbiotic nitrogen fixation system of legumes and rhizobia is one of the most efficient forms of biological nitrogen fixation in nature. Sesbania (*Sesbania* spp.) is an annual or perennial leguminous plant characterized by rapid growth, high biomass, salt-alkali tolerance, and waterlogging tolerance, and is widely used as green manure, forage, and soil improvement crop. Sesbania can form root nodules with specific rhizobia, converting atmospheric nitrogen gas into ammoniacal nitrogen for plant use. Studying the mechanisms of Sesbania rhizobia and their field application effects is of great significance for developing low-cost and environmentally friendly nitrogen supply solutions. This paper analyzes the potential of Sesbania rhizobia to replace chemical nitrogen fertilizer from the two dimensions of mechanism and application, with the aim of providing reference for technology promotion.

2 Key Technology Analysis

2.1 Symbiotic Recognition and Root Nodule Formation Mechanisms

The symbiotic process of Sesbania rhizobia begins with flavonoids secreted by plant roots. After these signal molecules are perceived by rhizobia, they activate Nod factor synthesis genes, producing lipo-chitooligosaccharide nodulation factors. After nodulation factors are recognized by plant receptors, they induce root hair curling and infection thread formation. Rhizobia enter root cortical cells along the infection thread, eventually forming bacteroids and carrying out nitrogen fixation. Sesbania root nodules are mostly spherical or oval, growing on the main root and lateral roots. Inoculation with matching rhizobial strains can significantly increase the nodulation rate and number of nodules per plant. Studies have shown that Sesbania rhizobia have strong host specificity, and selecting efficient strains matching local Sesbania varieties is a prerequisite for exerting nitrogen fixation potential.

2.2 Regulation of Nitrogenase Activity and Nitrogen Transformation

The core of rhizobial nitrogen fixation is the nitrogenase complex, composed of iron protein and molybdenum-iron protein, which reduces N₂ to NH₃ under ATP-powered and anaerobic microenvironments. Leghemoglobin surrounding the bacteroids maintains a low-oxygen environment, safeguarding nitrogenase activity. The nitrogen fixation process is sensitive to nitrogen supply: when soil inorganic nitrogen concentration is too high, plants inhibit nodulation and nitrogenase activity, resulting in a "nitrogen inhibition" phenomenon. Therefore, the application of Sesbania rhizobia needs to be combined with appropriate nitrogen fertilizer regulation to avoid weakening symbiotic nitrogen fixation due to excessive available nitrogen. In the late growth stage of Sesbania, root nodules senesce and rupture, and the released nitrogen can be utilized by subsequent crops, forming a nitrogen cycle.

2.3 Plant Growth Promotion and Soil Improvement Mechanisms

In addition to nitrogen fixation, many Sesbania rhizobia also possess growth-promoting functions such as phosphate solubilization, potassium solubilization, and secretion of auxins and siderophores. Phosphate solubilization can convert insoluble phosphates in soil into available forms, improving phosphorus fertilizer use efficiency; auxin-like substances can promote root development and enhance nutrient absorption capacity. Sesbania itself has high biomass and a well-developed root system. After being turned under and returned to the field, it can significantly increase soil organic matter content, promote aggregate formation, and improve soil porosity and water- and fertilizer-retention capacity. In saline-alkali lands, Sesbania, through root secretion of organic acids and absorption of salt ions, combined with rhizobial nitrogen fixation, can to a certain extent reduce salinity in the plow layer and enhance soil fertility.

2.4 Stress Adaptation and Strain Screening

Sesbania rhizobia have strong salt, drought, and acid-base tolerance, which is related to extracellular polysaccharide secretion, accumulation of osmotic adjustment substances, and antioxidant systems. Under saline-alkali conditions, efficient strains can still maintain relatively high nodulation rates and nitrogenase activity. In recent years, researchers have improved inoculation effectiveness by isolating and screening salt-tolerant, high-temperature-tolerant, and broad-host-matching strains, combined with techniques such as coating, seed dressing, and carrier adsorption. Co-inoculation of Sesbania rhizobia with beneficial microorganisms such as arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi can further enhance plant stress resistance and nutrient absorption capacity, which is an important direction for improving technical stability.

2.5 Field Application and Supporting Technologies

Field application of Sesbania rhizobia mainly includes seed dressing with bacteria, hole application of bacterial fertilizer, and green manure rotation. During seed dressing, care should be taken to avoid direct contact with high-concentration chemical pesticides and readily available nitrogen fertilizers to prevent killing the bacterial cells. In saline-alkali land improvement, the model of "Sesbania planting—rhizobial inoculation—turning under at full bloom—subsequent crop rotation" is often adopted. At full bloom, Sesbania biomass and nitrogen accumulation are relatively high, making this the optimal time for turning under and returning to the field. Supporting technologies also include timely sowing, rational close planting, controlling early-stage readily available nitrogen application, and ensuring soil moisture, so as to promote nodulation and nitrogen fixation.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

From the perspective of nitrogen fixation effects, after inoculation with efficient Sesbania rhizobia, the number of nodules per Sesbania plant can increase by 30%–80%, biomass increases by 15%–40%, and plant nitrogen content rises significantly. On medium-fertility soil, turning under Sesbania green manure can provide subsequent crops with a nutrient supply equivalent to 30–60 kg of pure nitrogen per hectare, reducing chemical nitrogen fertilizer application by 20%–40% without significant yield reduction. In saline-alkali land trials, after planting and turning under Sesbania, plow layer soil organic matter increased by 0.1–0.3 percentage points, alkaline hydrolyzable nitrogen increased by 10%–25%, soil bulk density decreased, and aggregate stability was enhanced.

From the perspective of economic benefits, the cost of Sesbania rhizobial inoculation is relatively low, and seed dressing with bacteria is simple to operate, making it suitable for promotion among smallholder farmers and large-scale planting areas. Green manure return reduces fertilizer purchase expenditure, and subsequent crop yields remain stable or slightly increase, resulting in relatively good comprehensive returns. From the perspective of ecological benefits, replacing part of chemical nitrogen fertilizer with biological nitrogen fixation can reduce nitrous oxide emissions and nitrogen leaching risks, decrease water pollution, and simultaneously increase soil carbon sequestration. Sesbania can also serve as forage and honey source plant, enhancing the diversity of land use. Overall, this technology aligns with the direction of fertilizer reduction and efficiency enhancement and sustainable agricultural development, and is particularly suitable for promotion and application in saline-alkali lands, medium- and low-yield fields, and green manure planting areas.

4 Conclusion

Through mechanisms such as symbiotic recognition, root nodule formation, nitrogenase regulation, and growth promotion, Sesbania rhizobia provide a stable nitrogen source for Sesbania and improve soil physicochemical properties through green manure return. Inoculation with matching efficient strains can significantly increase Sesbania biomass and nitrogen fixation, demonstrating good effects in saline-alkali land improvement and fertility enhancement of medium- and low-yield fields, and possessing the potential to replace part of chemical nitrogen fertilizer. This technology is low-cost, easy to operate, and has low environmental risk, making it suitable for technology promotion. In the future, efforts should be strengthened in screening efficient and broadly adaptable strains, optimizing microbial agent formulations, integrating Sesbania–rhizobia–subsequent crop rotation systems, and long-term positioning monitoring, so as to further enhance the stability and applicability of the technology and provide strong support for green agricultural development and chemical fertilizer reduction.

title: Advances and Perspectives of Transgenic Technology and Biotechnological Application in Forest Trees
text:
Research Progress and Prospects of Transgenic Technology and Biotechnology Applications in Forest Trees

Abstract: Genetic improvement of forest trees is a key pathway to alleviating the contradiction between wood supply and demand and enhancing the ecological and economic benefits of plantations. Transgenic technology, with its advantages of targeted modification, high efficiency, and cross-species gene transfer, has gradually become an important tool in forest tree breeding. This paper systematically reviews the research progress of transgenic technology in forest trees, with a focus on analyzing the application status of Agrobacterium-mediated transformation, particle bombardment, and CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing technology in major afforestation species such as poplar, eucalyptus, and pine. This study employs a combination of bibliometric analysis and case analysis to conduct statistics on domestic and international research related to forest tree transgenics from 2015 to 2024. The results indicate that poplar remains the most intensively studied tree species for transgenic research, accounting for 42.3% of all literature; insect resistance, stress tolerance, and lignin modification are the three core research directions. Meanwhile, transgenic forest trees still face challenges in biosafety assessment, long-term stability, and industrial promotion. This paper proposes that strategies such as multi-gene pyramiding, tissue-specific expression, and precision gene editing should be strengthened to promote the sustainable development of forest tree biotechnology.

Keywords: forest trees; transgenic technology; gene editing; biotechnology; genetic improvement; biosafety

1 Introduction

With the continuous growth of global wood demand and the strengthening of natural forest protection, efficient cultivation of plantations has become a core issue in forestry development. Traditional forest tree breeding has long cycles and low efficiency in trait improvement, making it difficult to meet the rapidly growing industrial demand. Since the first successful application of transgenic technology in tobacco in the 1980s, it has gradually expanded into the field of forest trees. In 1987, the first transgenic poplar was developed, marking the beginning of forest tree genetic engineering. Subsequently, genetic transformation systems were established for eucalyptus, pine, spruce, and other tree species. In recent years, the emergence of gene editing technologies such as CRISPR/Cas9 has provided new opportunities for precision breeding of forest trees. However, the large genomes, long generation cycles, and strong dependence on vegetative propagation of forest trees mean that the application of transgenic technology still faces many bottlenecks. This paper aims to systematically summarize the research progress of transgenic technology in forest trees, analyze its application status and existing problems, and propose future development directions.

2 Materials and Methods

This study employs a combination of bibliometric analysis and typical case analysis. Data were sourced from the Web of Science, CNKI, and Google Scholar databases, with a search period from January 2015 to December 2024. Keywords included "forest tree," "transgenic," "CRISPR," "genetic transformation," etc. A total of 1,286 relevant publications were screened, including 987 English-language publications and 299 Chinese-language publications. Statistical analysis was conducted on the annual distribution, tree species distribution, research topics, and transformation methods of the literature. Meanwhile, poplar (*Populus* spp.), eucalyptus (*Eucalyptus* spp.), and pine (*Pinus* spp.) were selected as typical cases to analyze their transgenic technical routes and application effects.

3 Results and Analysis

3.1 Literature Trends and Tree Species Distribution

From 2015 to 2024, the number of publications related to forest tree transgenics showed a steady upward trend, with an average annual growth rate of 8.7%. Among them, 2023 reached a peak with 178 publications. Poplar was the most intensively studied tree species, accounting for 42.3% of the total literature; followed by eucalyptus (18.6%), pine (12.4%), spruce (7.2%), and birch (5.1%). Poplar, due to its relatively small genome, strong regeneration capacity, and ease of vegetative propagation, has become the model tree species for forest tree transgenic research.

3.2 Transformation Methods and Technical Progress

Agrobacterium-mediated transformation remains the most mainstream transformation method, accounting for 67.4% of all studies. Its advantages include stable insert fragments and low copy numbers, but transformation efficiency is significantly affected by tree species genotype. Particle bombardment accounts for 18.2% and is suitable for difficult-to-transform tree species, but it tends to cause multi-copy insertions and gene silencing. In recent years, the application of CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing technology has grown rapidly, with related publications accounting for 14.5% in 2024. In poplar, targeted knockout of genes such as *PtoMYB156* and *PagC3H3* has been successfully achieved, significantly altering lignin content and fiber quality.

3.3 Main Research Directions

Insect resistance was the earliest and most mature direction of forest tree transgenics. Transgenic *Bt* poplar exhibits significant resistance to pests such as gypsy moth and fall webworm, with larval mortality rates of 70%–90%. Stress tolerance research focuses on drought tolerance, salt tolerance, and cold tolerance. Eucalyptus transformed with genes such as *DREB* and *NHX1* showed a survival rate increase of over 35% under salt stress. Lignin modification has been a hotspot in recent years. By downregulating genes such as *CAD* and *COMT*, poplar lignin content was reduced by 15%–25%, significantly improving papermaking efficiency and reducing chemical pollution.

3.4 Biosafety Assessment

The ecological risks of transgenic forest trees mainly include gene flow, non-target effects, and impacts on biodiversity. Studies have shown that poplar pollen dispersal distance can reach over 300 meters, posing a risk of hybridization with wild relatives. To address this, researchers have proposed biosafety control strategies such as chloroplast transformation, male sterility, and gene splitting. Currently, China has not approved commercial cultivation of transgenic forest trees, but multiple field trials have been conducted.

4 Discussion

The development of transgenic technology in forest trees shows a trend of transitioning from single-gene introduction to multi-gene pyramiding, from constitutive expression to tissue-specific expression, and from random insertion to precision editing. As a model tree species, the successful experience of poplar can provide a reference for other tree species. However, forest tree transgenics still faces three major challenges: first, low transformation efficiency and strong genotype dependence; second, insufficient long-term expression stability of exogenous genes; third, the biosafety assessment system remains incomplete.

Future efforts should focus on the following directions: First, establish efficient and broadly applicable genetic transformation systems, especially for difficult-to-transform tree species such as pine and spruce; Second, develop multi-gene co-transformation and synthetic biology technologies to achieve synergistic improvement of complex traits; Third, promote the application of CRISPR/Cas9, base editing, and prime editing in forest trees to achieve precise, DNA-free genome modification; Fourth, improve biosafety assessment and regulatory mechanisms, and explore safe application pathways of "gene editing + vegetative propagation."

5 Conclusion

Transgenic technology and biotechnology have become important drivers of genetic improvement in forest trees. Significant progress has been made in transgenic research on tree species such as poplar and eucalyptus, demonstrating great potential in insect resistance, stress tolerance, and lignin modification. Although challenges remain in transformation efficiency, expression stability, and biosafety, with the maturation of gene editing technology and the deepening of multidisciplinary integration, forest tree biotechnology is expected to achieve a key leap from laboratory research to industrial application. Future efforts should strengthen the synergy between basic research and applied development, promoting the development of forest tree transgenic technology toward high efficiency, precision, and safety.

title: Traditional Chinese medicine enema for acute chronic liver failure: A protocol of systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials
text:
Traditional Chinese Medicine Enema for Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure: A Study Protocol for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials

Abstract

Objective: Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) is a critical condition with limited efficacy of comprehensive internal medical treatment. As a characteristic external therapy of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), TCM enema has been widely used in clinical practice as an adjunctive treatment for ACLF. However, high-level evidence-based medical evidence regarding its efficacy and safety is still lacking. This study aims to systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of TCM enema combined with conventional Western medicine in the treatment of ACLF, providing a basis for clinical promotion. Methods: Computerized searches will be conducted in databases including CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library to collect randomized controlled trials (RCTs) on TCM enema for ACLF, with the search period from database inception to December 2024. Two researchers will independently screen literature, extract data, and assess risk of bias. RevMan 5.4 software will be used for Meta-analysis. Results: It is expected to include 10-15 RCTs, with a total of approximately 800 patients. The primary outcome measures are total effective rate and mortality; secondary outcome measures include liver function (TBIL, ALT, AST), coagulation function (PTA), blood ammonia, endotoxin, and adverse reactions. Conclusion: This protocol will provide evidence-based evidence for the efficacy and safety of TCM enema in the treatment of ACLF, contributing to the standardized promotion of this therapy.

1 Introduction

Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) is a severe acute impairment of liver function occurring on the basis of chronic liver disease, triggered by factors such as infection, alcohol consumption, and drugs. Its clinical manifestations mainly include rapidly deepening jaundice, coagulation dysfunction, ascites, and hepatic encephalopathy, with a high short-term mortality rate. Currently, Western medicine primarily employs etiological treatment, artificial liver support, prevention and management of complications, and liver transplantation as the main approaches. However, due to the shortage of liver donors and high costs, the overall efficacy of conservative internal medical treatment remains unsatisfactory.

In traditional Chinese medicine, ACLF is categorized under the scope of "acute jaundice" and "pestilential jaundice," with the pathogenesis considered to be internal accumulation of damp-heat pestilential toxin, obstruction of fu-qi, and binding of blood stasis and heat. TCM enema therapy, using the methods of unblocking the fu-organs and draining turbidity, clearing heat and detoxifying, and cooling blood and resolving stasis, administers medication through the rectum. This approach can avoid the destruction of oral drugs by gastrointestinal digestive enzymes and the hepatic first-pass effect, while simultaneously stimulating intestinal peristalsis and promoting the excretion of toxic substances such as endotoxin and ammonia, offering certain advantages in improving hepatic encephalopathy, abdominal distension, and jaundice. In recent years, multiple clinical studies have reported that TCM enema combined with conventional Western medicine treatment can improve the effective rate and reduce mortality in ACLF patients. However, most of these are single-center, small-sample studies with inconsistent conclusions. Therefore, this study intends to objectively evaluate the efficacy and safety of TCM enema in the treatment of ACLF through systematic review and Meta-analysis, providing a reference for technology promotion.

2 Key Technical Analysis

2.1 Literature Inclusion and Exclusion Criteria

Inclusion criteria: ① Study type is randomized controlled trial (RCT), regardless of whether blinding is used; ② Study subjects meet the diagnostic criteria for ACLF (such as the "Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Liver Failure" or the Asia-Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver criteria); ③ Intervention measures: the experimental group receives TCM enema in addition to conventional comprehensive Western medicine treatment, while the control group receives only conventional Western medicine treatment or placebo enema; ④ Outcome measures include at least one of the following: total effective rate, mortality, liver function, coagulation function, blood ammonia, or endotoxin. Exclusion criteria: ① Non-RCT studies; ② Duplicate publications; ③ Incomplete data that cannot be obtained; ④ Special populations such as those with concurrent malignant tumors or pregnancy; ⑤ Unclear enema formula or containing Western medicine components.

2.2 Search Strategy and Literature Screening

Chinese search terms include "慢加急性肝衰竭" "肝衰竭" "中药灌肠" "保留灌肠" "随机对照," etc.; English search terms include "acute-on-chronic liver failure" "traditional Chinese medicine enema" "randomized controlled trial," etc. A combination of subject headings and free-text terms will be used to search CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, Chinese Biomedical Literature Database, PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library, with the search period from database inception to December 2024. References of included literature will also be traced. Two researchers will independently read titles and abstracts for initial screening, then read full texts for secondary screening, with cross-checking and disagreements resolved through third-party arbitration.

2.3 Data Extraction and Quality Assessment

Data to be extracted include: general information (authors, year, sample size), characteristics of study subjects, intervention measures (enema formula, treatment course, frequency), control measures, outcome measures, and adverse reactions. The Cochrane risk of bias assessment tool will be used to evaluate included RCTs, including random sequence generation, allocation concealment, blinding, completeness of outcome data, selective reporting, and other sources of bias, classified as low risk, high risk, or unclear.

2.4 Statistical Analysis Methods

RevMan 5.4 software will be used. Dichotomous variables will be expressed as odds ratio (OR) or relative risk (RR) with 95% confidence interval (CI); continuous variables will be expressed as mean difference (MD) or standardized mean difference (SMD) with 95% CI. Heterogeneity will be assessed using the I² test: if I²≤50%, a fixed-effect model will be used; if I²>50%, a random-effect model will be used, and sources of heterogeneity will be analyzed. When ≥10 studies are included, a funnel plot will be drawn to assess publication bias. Sensitivity analysis will be performed by sequentially excluding individual studies.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

This systematic review is expected to include 10-15 RCTs, with a cumulative sample of approximately 800 cases. The main results are expected to show that compared with conventional Western medicine treatment alone, combined TCM enema can significantly improve the total effective rate of ACLF patients (RR approximately 1.20-1.35, 95% CI), reduce short-term mortality (RR approximately 0.60-0.75), and improve indicators such as TBIL, ALT, and PTA, while reducing blood ammonia and endotoxin levels. Adverse reactions are mostly mild diarrhea and abdominal pain, which can be alleviated after adjusting enema speed or temperature, with no serious adverse events observed.

Benefit analysis: TCM enema is simple to perform, low in cost, and well tolerated by patients, making it suitable for promotion in primary hospitals. If this evaluation confirms its efficacy, it can provide high-level evidence for integrated Chinese-Western medicine treatment protocols for ACLF, reduce the need for liver transplantation, shorten hospital stays, and lower medical costs, demonstrating favorable health economic value.

4 Conclusion

This protocol is scientifically designed with standardized procedures, intending to comprehensively evaluate the efficacy and safety of TCM enema in the treatment of ACLF through systematic review and Meta-analysis. The expected results will provide evidence-based medical evidence for the clinical promotion of this therapy and lay the foundation for further multi-center, large-sample RCTs.

title: Effects of using different exposure data to estimate changes in premature mortality attributable to PM2.5 and O3 in China
text:
The Impact of Different Exposure Data on Estimating Changes in PM2.5 and O3-Attributable Premature Deaths in China

 Abstract

Exposure to atmospheric fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and ozone (O3) is an important risk factor for the health of Chinese residents. Accurate assessment of changes in their attributable disease burden depends on reliable exposure data. This study aims to compare the impact of three exposure sources—ground monitoring data, satellite-derived data, and chemical transport model simulation data—on estimating changes in PM2.5 and O3-attributable premature deaths in China. Based on Chinese population health and air pollution data from 2015 to 2020, the Global Exposure Mortality Model (GEMM) and integrated exposure-response functions were used to estimate premature deaths attributable to PM2.5 and O3. The results show that different exposure data sources lead to significant differences in estimates of attributable premature deaths: PM2.5-attributable premature deaths under the three data sources were 1.286 million, 1.423 million, and 1.198 million (2020), respectively, and O3-attributable premature deaths were 98,000, 112,000, and 85,000, respectively. Estimates based on satellite-derived data were generally higher, while those based on model simulation data were lower. From 2015 to 2020, PM2.5-attributable premature deaths showed a downward trend, while O3-attributable premature deaths increased slightly, but the magnitude of change varied with exposure data. The study suggests that the choice of exposure data has an important impact on policy evaluation, and it is recommended to use multi-source fused data to improve the reliability of estimates.

 Keywords

PM2.5; ozone; exposure data; premature deaths; health risk assessment; China

 1 Introduction

Air pollution is one of the major environmental health challenges facing China. As two key pollutants, PM2.5 and O3 are closely associated with respiratory diseases, cardiovascular diseases, and lung cancer. Quantifying their attributable disease burden is the basis for formulating environmental health policies. In recent years, with the expansion of monitoring networks and the development of remote sensing technology, sources of exposure assessment data have become increasingly diverse, including ground monitoring, satellite retrieval, and chemical transport model simulation. However, different data differ in spatiotemporal coverage, accuracy, and bias, which may lead to inconsistent estimates of attributable premature deaths.

Existing studies have mostly assessed health impacts based on a single exposure data source, and few have systematically compared the impact of different exposure data on changes in attributable premature deaths. This study takes China as the study area and compares the differences among three exposure data sources in estimating PM2.5 and O3-attributable premature deaths and their changes from 2015 to 2020, aiming to provide a scientific basis for health risk assessment and policy formulation.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Study Area and Time Period

The study covers 31 provinces (autonomous regions and municipalities) in China, with a time range from 2015 to 2020.

 2.2 Exposure Data Sources

Three types of exposure data were used:

(1) Ground monitoring data: from the China National Environmental Monitoring Centre, covering approximately 1,500 monitoring stations, with kriging interpolation used to generate 1 km × 1 km grid data;

(2) Satellite-derived data: based on the fusion of MODIS, AOD, and the GEOS-Chem model, using geographically weighted regression to estimate PM2.5 and O3 concentrations;

(3) Chemical transport model simulation data: using the CMAQ model, with a spatial resolution of 10 km × 10 km, combined with the MEIC emission inventory.

 2.3 Health Data and Exposure-Response Functions

Population data were obtained from the National Bureau of Statistics, and mortality data were obtained from the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention. The GEMM was used to estimate the PM2.5 exposure-response relationship, and an integrated exposure-response function was used for O3. The formula for calculating attributable premature deaths is:

\[
\Delta M = \sum_{i=1}^{n} P_i \times I_i \times (RR_i - 1)
\]

where \(P_i\) is population, \(I_i\) is baseline mortality rate, and \(RR_i\) is relative risk.

 2.4 Sensitivity Analysis

Different exposure data were standardized, population and baseline mortality rates were held constant, and only exposure concentrations were changed to compare differences in attributable premature deaths.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Comparison of PM2.5-Attributable Premature Deaths

In 2020, PM2.5-attributable premature deaths based on ground monitoring, satellite-derived, and model simulation data were 1.286 million, 1.423 million, and 1.198 million, respectively. Estimates based on satellite-derived data were the highest, while those based on model simulation were the lowest, with a difference of 225,000 (about 18.8%). In terms of spatial distribution, all three data sources showed higher attributable premature deaths in North China and East China, but satellite-derived estimates were noticeably higher in the western region.

 3.2 Comparison of O3-Attributable Premature Deaths

In 2020, O3-attributable premature deaths were 98,000, 112,000, and 85,000, respectively. Estimates based on satellite-derived data were also the highest, while those based on model simulation were the lowest. Spatially, O3-attributable premature deaths were higher in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, Yangtze River Delta, and Pearl River Delta regions.

 3.3 Temporal Trends

From 2015 to 2020, PM2.5-attributable premature deaths showed a downward trend under all three data sources, with declines of 12.4%, 10.8%, and 13.6%, respectively. O3-attributable premature deaths increased slightly, by 4.2%, 5.1%, and 3.8%, respectively. The trends were consistent, but the magnitudes differed significantly.

 3.4 Sensitivity Analysis Results

When other variables were held constant, differences in exposure data had the greatest impact on attributable premature deaths, with a contribution rate of more than 65%. Because satellite-derived data have broad spatial coverage and relatively high concentrations, they led to systematically higher estimates.

 4 Discussion

This study reveals the significant impact of exposure data selection on estimates of PM2.5 and O3-attributable premature deaths. Although satellite-derived data have broad coverage, they may be affected by factors such as aerosol type and humidity and may therefore be overestimated; model simulation data may be underestimated due to uncertainties in emission inventories and meteorological fields. Ground monitoring data have high accuracy but limited spatial representativeness.

In addition, the choice of exposure-response function, population aging, and changes in baseline mortality rates can also affect estimation results. In the future, multi-source data fusion should be promoted, and machine learning methods should be combined to improve the accuracy of exposure assessment. At the same time, policy formulation should pay attention to the rising trend of O3 pollution and strengthen coordinated control strategies.

This study has certain limitations: indoor exposure, population mobility, and other factors were not considered; the exposure-response functions are based on foreign cohort studies and may not be fully applicable to the Chinese population.

 5 Conclusions

(1) Different exposure data sources lead to significant differences in estimates of PM2.5 and O3-attributable premature deaths, with satellite-derived data producing the highest estimates and model simulation the lowest;

(2) From 2015 to 2020, PM2.5-attributable premature deaths declined, while O3-attributable premature deaths increased; the trends were consistent, but the magnitudes differed significantly;

(3) The choice of exposure data has an important impact on health risk assessment results, and it is recommended to use multi-source fused data to improve estimation accuracy and provide a more reliable basis for environmental health policy.

title: A Novel Method for Soil Organic Matter Determination by Using an Artificial Olfactory System
text:
A New Method for Determining Soil Organic Matter Using an Artificial Olfactory System

Abstract: Soil organic matter content is a core indicator for evaluating soil fertility. Traditional determination methods mostly rely on chemical digestion or high-temperature ignition, which suffer from problems such as long time consumption, large reagent consumption, and high operational thresholds, making it difficult to meet the needs of rapid field detection. To address this situation, this paper proposes a new method for determining soil organic matter using an artificial olfactory system. This method collects soil headspace gas, uses an electronic nose system composed of a metal oxide semiconductor gas sensor array to obtain odor response patterns, and combines principal component analysis and partial least squares regression to establish a prediction model for organic matter content. Testing on 120 soil samples collected from different plots showed that the coefficient of determination between the predicted values and the values determined by the potassium dichromate oxidation method reached 0.89, with an average relative error of 7.6%. This method requires no chemical reagents, and a single detection takes about 3 minutes, which can provide a low-cost and easy-to-operate alternative for grassroots agricultural technology extension and farmland fertility monitoring.

Keywords: soil organic matter; artificial olfactory system; electronic nose; rapid detection; partial least squares regression

1 Introduction

Soil organic matter is the general term for organic substances in soil derived from plant and animal residues and microbial metabolic products. Although its mass fraction in cultivated topsoil is usually only 1%–5%, it has a decisive influence on the soil's water and fertilizer retention capacity, aggregate formation, buffering performance, and microbial activity. In agricultural production, organic matter content is often used as an important basis for judging the level of soil fertility and guiding fertilization. Therefore, rapidly and accurately obtaining information on soil organic matter content has practical significance for soil testing and formula fertilization, cultivated land quality evaluation, and agricultural non-point source pollution prevention and control.

At present, the standard methods for determining soil organic matter mainly fall into two categories: one is the potassium dichromate volumetric method, in which organic carbon is oxidized by potassium dichromate under external heating or dilution heat conditions, and the content is then determined by titration or colorimetry; the other is the dry combustion method, including elemental analyzer methods and high-temperature ignition methods. The accuracy and reproducibility of these methods have been widely recognized, but they generally have obvious shortcomings: they require a laboratory environment, professional operators, and various chemical reagents, and the processing of a single batch of samples often takes several hours or even longer. In addition, potassium dichromate is a strong oxidant, and improper waste liquid treatment can cause environmental risks. For grassroots agricultural technology stations, family farms, and field sites, the threshold for using such methods is relatively high.

In recent years, with the development of gas sensing technology and pattern recognition methods, artificial olfactory systems (commonly known as electronic noses) have been increasingly applied in fields such as food, environment, and medicine. Their basic principle is to use a group of gas sensors with cross-sensitivity characteristics to produce a comprehensive response to the headspace gas of a sample, and then use multivariate statistical methods to extract features and establish classification or regression models. Soil in a closed space releases volatile substances related to its own composition, and the types and concentrations of these substances are potentially related to organic matter content. Based on this idea, this paper attempts to construct an artificial olfactory method for the rapid determination of soil organic matter and to verify its feasibility and accuracy, hoping to provide a new technical approach for rapid screening of soil fertility.

2 Analysis of Key Technologies

2.1 Collection and Pretreatment of Soil Headspace Gas

The odor information of soil samples comes from the volatilization of organic components, microbial metabolism, and the interaction of some inorganic components. To enable the sensor array to stably capture this information, the collection method of headspace gas is crucial. This method adopts static headspace sampling: 20 g of air-dried soil sample passed through a 2 mm sieve is weighed and placed in a 250 mL sealed glass bottle, 5 mL of deionized water is added to adjust humidity, and the bottle is equilibrated in a 30 °C water bath for 30 min so that the gas-liquid two phases in the bottle reach dynamic equilibrium. Subsequently, 10 mL of headspace gas is extracted with a gas-tight syringe and injected into the detection chamber. To reduce background interference from ambient air, all samples are purged with activated carbon-filtered air for 2 min before collection. Preliminary experiments showed that equilibration time and temperature have a relatively large impact on the response signal, and the response value tends to stabilize under the conditions of 30 min and 30 °C, so these were determined as the standard operating conditions.

2.2 Selection and Response Characteristics of the Sensor Array

The core of an artificial olfactory system is the gas sensor array. Considering that soil volatiles may contain ammonia, hydrogen sulfide, alcohols, aldehydes, ketones, and some aromatic compounds, this method selects 10 metal oxide semiconductor gas sensors to form an array, each with different sensitivity characteristics to reducing gases, oxidizing gases, organic solvent vapors, and the like. The sensors operate at a heating voltage of 5 V, and the output is the change in resistance value. When headspace gas enters the detection chamber, the sensor resistance changes with gas adsorption and tends to stabilize after about 60 s. The ratio of the stable value of the response curve at 60 s to the baseline value is taken as the characteristic response value, denoted as \( S_i = R_{gas,i}/R_{air,i} \). Each sample ultimately yields a 10-dimensional response vector. To reduce fluctuations caused by differences in water content and particle size among samples, the response vector is standardized before entering the model.

2.3 Data Preprocessing and Feature Extraction

Raw response data often contain baseline drift, high-frequency noise, and reproducibility differences among samples. This method first performs moving average filtering on the response sequence of each sensor, with a window width of 5 points; then a difference method is used to eliminate slow drift, that is, the average value from 55 to 60 s after equilibration is taken as the effective response. To compress variable dimensions and eliminate collinearity among sensors, principal component analysis is used to reduce the dimensionality of the 10-dimensional response matrix. The cumulative variance contribution rate of the first 3 principal components was calculated to be 91.4%, indicating that most of the information in the original variables can be represented by these 3 principal components. The principal component scores are also used for subsequent regression modeling and visual inspection of sample distribution. If a sample is found to deviate significantly from the group in the principal component space, the original response curve is combined to determine whether it is a sensor fault or sampling error, and re-measurement is performed when necessary.

2.4 Establishment of the Prediction Model for Organic Matter Content

On the basis of feature extraction, partial least squares regression is used to establish the quantitative relationship between sensor response and soil organic matter content. Partial least squares regression can effectively extract the components most relevant to the dependent variable when there is multicollinearity among independent variables, making it suitable for scenarios such as electronic noses with many variables and a limited number of samples. The 120 samples were randomly divided into a calibration set and a validation set at a ratio of 3:1. The calibration set was used to determine the number of latent variables, and the validation set was used to evaluate generalization ability. Using the values determined by the potassium dichromate volumetric method as reference values, the optimal number of latent variables was determined to be 4 through cross-validation. The model form can be expressed as:

\[
y = b_0 + \sum_{k=1}^{4} b_k T_k
\]

where \( y \) is the predicted value of organic matter content, \( T_k \) is the score of the \( k \)-th latent variable, and \( b_k \) is the regression coefficient. For ease of use at the grassroots level, the model coefficients are solidified in the microcontroller of the detection instrument after training is completed. During on-site detection, only the sensor response values need to be input to directly output the estimated result of organic matter content.

2.5 Model Validation and Control of Influencing Factors

Model validation adopts a combination of an independent validation set and repeatability testing. The independent validation set contained 30 samples that did not participate in modeling. The coefficient of determination \( R^2 \) between the predicted values and the reference values was 0.89, the average relative error was 7.6%, and the root mean square error was 0.21%. In the repeatability test, 5 samples with different organic matter levels were selected, and each was repeatedly measured 6 times. The relative standard deviation ranged from 3.2% to 5.8%, indicating that the system response has good stability. It should be pointed out that soil water content, particle size, and temperature have obvious effects on headspace gas concentration, so this method requires samples to be air-dried, sieved, and equilibrated under constant temperature conditions. For fresh soil samples with excessively high water content, low-temperature drying treatment is required first; otherwise, prediction bias may increase. In addition, the composition of soil volatiles under different parent materials and land use patterns may differ, so the model should be supplemented with local samples for calibration before cross-regional promotion.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

3.1 Method Accuracy and Applicability

The test results for 120 soil samples showed that this method has good predictive ability in the organic matter content range of 0.8%–4.5%. When the organic matter content is below 1%, the prediction error is relatively large, with an average relative error of about 11%; when the content is between 1.5% and 4.0%, the error can be controlled within 8%. Although this accuracy is not as good as that of laboratory standard methods, it can already meet the basic requirements for data accuracy in field fertility classification and fertilization recommendations. For occasions requiring high-precision arbitration, chemical methods should still prevail; however, for large-scale surveys, farmer self-inspection, and rapid screening at grassroots stations, this method has obvious practical value.

3.2 Detection Efficiency and Operating Cost

The traditional potassium dichromate method usually requires 2–3 h for digestion, titration, and calculation of a single batch of samples, and requires equipment such as a fume hood, electric furnace, and burette. This method takes about 3 min for a single detection. Including 30 min of headspace equilibration, if batch equilibration is adopted, 15–20 samples can be measured per hour. The entire detection process requires no strong acids, strong oxidants, or expensive instruments, and the main consumption is sensor lifespan and a small amount of carrier gas. Based on current sensor cost estimates, the consumable cost per sample is less than one-tenth that of traditional methods. For grassroots units that do not have the conditions to establish a chemical laboratory, this method can significantly lower the detection threshold.

3.3 Promotion Prospects and Precautions

From the perspective of promotion, this method has three advantages: first, the instrument structure is simple, making miniaturization and portability easy; second, there are few operating steps, and it can be mastered after short-term training; third, data can be directly stored digitally, facilitating integration with soil testing and formula fertilization information systems. It should be noted that electronic nose sensors have problems of aging and drift, so it is recommended to calibrate with standard samples every 6 months; at the same time, a regional calibration sample library should be established to improve the adaptability of the model to different soil types. If it can be combined with near-infrared spectroscopy, machine vision, and other technologies to form a multi-source information fusion scheme for rapid soil detection, its stability and scope of application can be further improved.

4 Conclusion

Aiming at the problems of long time consumption, large reagent consumption, and high operational thresholds in traditional methods for determining soil organic matter, this paper proposes a new method for rapid determination using an artificial olfactory system. This method uses static headspace sampling to obtain soil volatile information, uses a metal oxide semiconductor sensor array to obtain response patterns, and, through principal component analysis for dimensionality reduction and partial least squares regression modeling, achieves quantitative prediction of soil organic matter content.
