Wheat (*Triticum aestivum* L.) is one of the most important food crops globally, but its genetic basis has become increasingly narrow during modern breeding, which has become a bottleneck for further improvement of yield and resistance. Thinopyrum ponticum (2n=70) is a wild relative of wheat that possesses excellent traits such as resistance to rust and powdery mildew, tolerance to salinity and alkalinity, drought tolerance, and high protein content, making it an important donor of alien genes for wheat genetic improvement. However, due to cross incompatibility and abnormal chromosome pairing, the efficiency of introducing beneficial genes from Th. ponticum into wheat through sexual hybridization is low.

Somatic hybridization technology, through protoplast fusion, can overcome sexual hybridization barriers and achieve the transfer of genetic material between distant species. In recent years, this technology has been successfully applied to the creation of introgression lines between wheat and various related wild species. However, the introduction of alien chromosomes or chromosome fragments not only causes genomic structural variation but may also induce changes in epigenetic modifications of the host genome, thereby affecting gene expression and phenotype. Currently, systematic studies on genetic and epigenetic variation in somatic hybrid introgression lines of wheat and Th. ponticum remain insufficient.

In this study, 12 wheat-Th. ponticum somatic hybrid introgression lines previously created by our research group were used as materials. By comprehensively employing molecular markers, cytogenetics, and epigenetics approaches, we systematically dissected their genomic composition, DNA methylation variation, and gene expression characteristics, aiming to reveal the patterns of coordinated genetic and epigenetic variation during distant somatic hybridization and to provide theoretical support for alien gene introduction and germplasm innovation in wheat.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Plant Materials

The materials used included the common wheat cultivar "Jimai 22" (recipient parent), Th. ponticum (donor parent), and 12 introgression lines (IL1–IL12) obtained through somatic hybridization, all preserved by our laboratory. The introgression lines had been self-pollinated for more than 6 consecutive generations with stable traits. All materials were planted at the experimental farm of Shandong Agricultural University during the 2022–2023 growing season with conventional field management.

 2.2 Genomic In Situ Hybridization (GISH)

Root tip meristems were collected, pretreated with colchicine, fixed with Carnoy's fixative, enzymatically digested, and then slide preparations were made. Total genomic DNA of Th. ponticum was used as a probe and labeled with biotin by nick translation, with wheat genomic DNA as a blocker. Hybridization signals were detected with anti-biotin-FITC, counterstained with DAPI, and observed and photographed under a fluorescence microscope.

 2.3 SSR Analysis

Leaf genomic DNA was extracted using the CTAB method. Three hundred pairs of SSR primers distributed across the 21 wheat chromosomes were selected for PCR amplification. The products were separated by 8% non-denaturing polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis and visualized by silver staining. Clearly distinguishable bands were recorded, and the proportion of polymorphic loci and genetic similarity coefficients were calculated.

 2.4 MSAP Analysis

DNA was extracted using a modified CTAB method. Two enzyme combinations, EcoRI/HpaII and EcoRI/MspI, were used for double digestion, followed by adapter ligation, pre-amplification, and selective amplification. The products were separated by 6% denaturing polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis and silver-stained. Methylation-sensitive loci were scored, and the total methylation rate, full methylation rate, and hemi-methylation rate were calculated.

 2.5 Transcriptome Sequencing and Data Analysis

Flag leaf samples were collected from introgression lines IL3, IL7, and the wheat parent, with 3 biological replicates per sample. RNA-seq libraries were constructed and sequenced on the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform. After quality control, raw data were aligned to the wheat reference genome (IWGSC RefSeq v2.1). Differentially expressed genes were identified using DESeq2 (|log2FC|≥1, FDR<0.05), and GO and KEGG enrichment analyses were performed.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Chromosome Composition of Introgression Lines

GISH analysis revealed that among the 12 introgression lines, 8 (IL1, IL2, IL4, IL5, IL6, IL8, IL10, IL12) carried 1–2 complete Th. ponticum chromosomes, appearing as whole-chromosome addition lines; 4 (IL3, IL7, IL9, IL11) were detected with only Th. ponticum chromosome fragments, mostly located at the terminal regions of wheat chromosomes, appearing as small-fragment translocation lines. The translocation fragments of IL3 and IL7 were located on the long arms of chromosomes 5A and 7B, respectively, with fragment sizes of approximately 85 Mb and 62 Mb.

 3.2 SSR Polymorphism Analysis

Among the 300 pairs of SSR primers, 56 pairs amplified Th. ponticum-specific bands in the introgression lines, with a polymorphic locus proportion of 18.7%. The number of polymorphic loci varied considerably among different introgression lines. IL3 and IL7 had 21 and 18 polymorphic loci, respectively, significantly higher than the whole-chromosome addition lines (average 9.3). Genetic similarity coefficient analysis showed that the similarity coefficients between the introgression lines and the wheat parent ranged from 0.73 to 0.89, with IL3 being the lowest (0.73) and IL12 the highest (0.89), indicating that the small-fragment translocation lines deviated further from the wheat parent in genetic background.

 3.3 DNA Methylation Variation

A total of 1,024 clear loci were detected by MSAP analysis. The total methylation rate of the wheat parent was 28.6%, while that of the introgression lines averaged 35.0%, an increase of 6.4 percentage points (P<0.01). Among these, the CG site methylation rate increased from 15.2% in the parent to 21.8%, an increase of 6.6 percentage points; CHG sites increased from 8.9% to 10.7%; CHH sites showed no significant change. Among the introgression lines, IL3 and IL7 showed the greatest increases in methylation, at 8.9 and 8.1 percentage points, respectively, consistent with their carrying alien chromosome fragments. In addition, 47 loci were detected as demethylated in the introgression lines, of which 12 were in the promoter regions of stress response-related genes.

 3.4 Differentially Expressed Gene Analysis

Transcriptome sequencing yielded a total of 42.6 Gb of high-quality reads, with alignment rates of 82.3%–88.7%. Compared with the wheat parent, 1,486 and 1,261 differentially expressed genes were identified in IL3 and IL7, respectively, with 812 and 697 upregulated genes, respectively. GO enrichment analysis showed that differentially expressed genes were significantly enriched in terms such as "stress response," "oxidation-reduction process," "transcriptional regulation," and "secondary metabolism"; KEGG analysis indicated significant enrichment in plant hormone signal transduction, phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, and glutathione metabolism pathways. Notably, among the 37 genes located on the alien translocation fragments, 24 were expressed in the introgression lines, of which 11 showed significantly higher expression levels than the homologous genes in the wheat parent, presumably related to promoter region demethylation.

 4 Discussion

This study systematically revealed the variation characteristics of wheat-Th. ponticum somatic hybrid introgression lines at the genetic and epigenetic levels. GISH and SSR results consistently indicated that somatic hybridization can produce two main types: whole-chromosome addition and small-fragment translocation. The latter, due to the smaller alien fragment, is more easily stably inherited and has less negative impact on the wheat background, making it an ideal form for alien gene introduction.

Increased DNA methylation is a common feature of the introgression lines, particularly more pronounced in lines carrying alien chromosome fragments. This phenomenon may be related to "genomic shock" triggered by the introduction of alien chromosomes, similar to the epigenetic remodeling commonly observed during distant hybridization and allopolyploidization. Increased methylation may suppress the activity of some repetitive sequences and transposons, thereby maintaining genomic stability; however, demethylation in the promoter regions of some stress response genes may activate their expression, conferring new stress tolerance to the introgression lines.

Transcriptome results further support the role of epigenetic regulation in alien gene expression. The high expression of some genes on alien fragments was associated with demethylation in their promoter regions, suggesting that DNA methylation variation may affect the expression levels of alien genes through cis-regulatory mechanisms. In addition, a large number of wheat genes not on alien fragments also showed differential expression, indicating that the introduction of alien chromosomes may also affect host gene networks through trans-regulation.

This study provides new insights into the genetic and epigenetic mechanisms of wheat distant somatic hybrid introgression lines. However, the causal relationship between DNA methylation variation and phenotype still needs further verification through methylation inhibitor treatment and gene editing approaches. Future studies can combine multi-omics integrative analysis to further dissect the application potential of epigenetic variation in distant hybridization breeding.

 5 Conclusion

(1) Wheat-Th. ponticum somatic hybrid introgression lines exhibit two types of chromosome composition: whole-chromosome addition and small-fragment translocation. The latter has a genetic background closer to wheat but carries alien gene fragments.

(2) The genomic DNA methylation level of the introgression lines is significantly elevated, predominantly at CG sites, and is closely associated with small-fragment translocations.

(3) The introduction of alien chromosomes causes extensive gene expression reprogramming, and the high expression of some alien genes is related to promoter region demethylation.

(4) Somatic hybrid introgression lines can serve as important resources for wheat genetic improvement, and their epigenetic variation provides a new research perspective for distant hybridization breeding.

title: Effect of long-term fertilisation on the weed community of a winter wheat field
text:
Effects of Long-Term Fertilization on Weed Communities in Winter Wheat Fields

Abstract: To clarify the effects of different long-term fertilization regimes on the weed community structure in winter wheat fields, this study was based on a 10-year positioned fertilization experiment with four treatments: no fertilization (CK), chemical fertilizer alone (NPK), organic fertilizer alone (M), and combined application of organic and inorganic fertilizers (MNPK). Weed species, density, biomass, and community diversity were investigated at the wheat maturity stage. The results showed that long-term fertilization significantly altered weed community composition. The CK treatment had the highest number of weed species, dominated by Descurainia sophia, Capsella bursa-pastoris, and Veronica polita; in the NPK treatment, the dominance of grass weeds Bromus japonicus and Aegilops tauschii increased; the M and MNPK treatments significantly reduced total weed density and biomass, with MNPK showing the best weed suppression, reducing total weed density by 62.3% and total biomass by 68.7% compared with CK. Fertilization also indirectly affected weed communities by altering wheat canopy closure and soil nutrient status. Combined application of organic and inorganic fertilizers effectively suppressed dominant weed species and increased community diversity while ensuring wheat yield, making it a fertilization strategy that balances production and ecology.

Keywords: long-term fertilization; winter wheat; weed community; combined application of organic and inorganic fertilizers; biodiversity

1 Introduction

Winter wheat is a major grain crop in northern China, with a long growth cycle and widespread weed occurrence in fields. Weeds compete with wheat for light, water, and nutrients, and are one of the important factors affecting wheat yield and quality. Traditional weed control methods are mainly based on chemical herbicides, but long-term single use of herbicides leads to increased weed resistance, accelerated community succession, and environmental pollution risks. Therefore, exploring the regulation of weed communities through agronomic measures has become an important direction for green agricultural production.

Fertilization is the most basic cultivation measure in wheat production. It not only directly affects wheat growth but also indirectly affects weed occurrence and succession by changing soil nutrients, canopy structure, and the microenvironment. The effects of different fertilization types and rates on weed communities differ markedly: excessive application of chemical fertilizers may promote the growth of certain nutrient-tolerant weeds, while organic fertilizers may suppress some weeds by altering the soil seed bank and microbial environment. However, current studies on the effects of long-term positioned fertilization on weed communities in winter wheat fields mostly focus on a single fertilization level or short-term effects, lacking systematic comparison under different long-term fertilization regimes.

Based on a 10-year long-term positioned fertilization experiment, this study systematically analyzed the structural characteristics of weed communities in winter wheat fields under four regimes: no fertilization, chemical fertilizer alone, organic fertilizer alone, and combined application of organic and inorganic fertilizers, aiming to provide a theoretical basis and technical reference for ecological weed regulation through optimized fertilization.

2 Analysis of Key Technologies

2.1 Experimental Design and Fertilization Treatments

The experimental site is located in a typical winter wheat planting area of the Huang-Huai-Hai Plain, with fluvo-aquic soil of medium fertility. The long-term positioned experiment began in 2013, using a randomized block design with 4 treatments, 3 replicates per treatment, and a plot area of 30 m². The treatments were: no fertilization control (CK); chemical fertilizer alone (NPK), applying 180 kg/hm² pure nitrogen, 90 kg/hm² phosphorus pentoxide, and 90 kg/hm² potassium oxide per season; organic fertilizer alone (M), applying 30 t/hm² decomposed cow manure per season; and combined application of organic and inorganic fertilizers (MNPK), with the organic fertilizer rate at 50% of the M treatment and the chemical fertilizer rate at 50% of the NPK treatment. The wheat variety was a locally dominant cultivar, sown in early October and harvested in early June of the following year. Field management was identical except for fertilization, and no herbicides were applied throughout the growth period.

2.2 Weed Survey and Calculation of Community Indicators

At the wheat maturity stage (7 days before harvest), a five-point sampling method was used in each plot, with each point covering 0.25 m². Weed species and plant numbers within the sampling frame were recorded, and aboveground parts were clipped by species, oven-dried, and weighed. Weed density (plants/m²), biomass (g/m²), relative density, relative biomass, importance value, Shannon-Wiener diversity index, Pielou evenness index, and Simpson dominance index were calculated. Importance value = (relative density + relative biomass)/2.

2.3 Effects of Fertilization on Weed Species Composition

Long-term fertilization significantly changed the species composition of weed communities. A total of 12 weed species were recorded in the CK treatment, mainly broadleaf weeds Descurainia sophia, Capsella bursa-pastoris, and Veronica polita, and the grass weed Poa annua, with the highest community diversity. The number of weed species in the NPK treatment decreased to 9, but the importance values of the grass weeds Bromus japonicus and Aegilops tauschii increased significantly, becoming dominant species, while the proportion of broadleaf weeds decreased. The M treatment had 8 weed species, with Descurainia sophia and Capsella bursa-pastoris still holding some dominance, but total density was significantly reduced. The MNPK treatment had the fewest weed species, only 6, and the importance values of all species were relatively low, with no single dominant species. This indicates that combined application of organic and inorganic fertilizers had the strongest suppressive effect on weed communities and could avoid outbreaks of a single species.

2.4 Effects of Fertilization on Weed Density and Biomass

Total weed density and total biomass both followed the order CK > NPK > M > MNPK. Compared with CK, the NPK treatment reduced total weed density by 28.5% and total biomass by 31.2%; the M treatment reduced them by 51.7% and 56.4%, respectively; and the MNPK treatment reduced them by 62.3% and 68.7%, respectively. By category, the biomass proportion of grass weeds in the NPK treatment reached 54.6%, significantly higher than in other treatments; broadleaf weeds had a relatively higher proportion in the M and MNPK treatments, but their absolute amounts were low. This indicates that chemical fertilizer alone favored the growth of grass weeds, while combined application of organic fertilizer provided better suppression of both weed categories.

2.5 Ecological Mechanisms by Which Fertilization Affects Weed Communities

The effects of long-term fertilization on weed communities were mainly realized through three pathways. First, it changed soil nutrient supply. The NPK treatment had high available nitrogen content, favoring the growth of nitrogen-loving grass weeds such as Bromus japonicus and Aegilops tauschii; organic fertilizer treatments released nutrients slowly and had high organic matter content and strong soil microbial activity, causing some weed seeds to be decomposed or consumed by microorganisms. Second, it changed wheat canopy structure. In the M and MNPK treatments, wheat plants were robust, had more tillers, and closed the canopy earlier, reducing light transmittance and inhibiting the emergence and growth of light-demanding weeds. Third, it changed the soil seed bank. Under long-term conditions without herbicide application, organic fertilizer introduced fewer weed seeds and killed some seeds through high-temperature decomposition, while chemical fertilizer treatments had no direct seed input but the original weed seeds had a higher germination rate under suitable nutrients. The combined action of these three factors formed the differentiation of weed communities under different fertilization regimes.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

3.1 Effects on Wheat Yield

Long-term fertilization significantly increased wheat yield. Compared with CK, wheat yields under the NPK, M, and MNPK treatments increased by 86.4%, 72.1%, and 112.5%, respectively. The MNPK treatment had the highest yield, indicating that combined application of organic and inorganic fertilizers, while improving soil fertility, could better coordinate nutrient supply and promote wheat growth. Although the yield of the M treatment was slightly lower than that of NPK, its weed suppression effect was better, and soil organic matter content was significantly increased.

3.2 Effects on Weed Community Diversity

The Shannon-Wiener diversity index followed the order CK > M > NPK > MNPK, but the difference between MNPK and NPK was not significant. The Pielou evenness index was highest in MNPK, and the Simpson dominance index was highest in NPK. This indicates that chemical fertilizer alone led to community simplification and prominent dominant species, whereas combined application of organic and inorganic fertilizers, although reducing species richness, increased community evenness and made dominant species less obvious, which was beneficial for reducing the risk of a single weed outbreak.

3.3 Comprehensive Benefit Analysis

From the perspective of production benefits, the MNPK treatment had the highest yield and the lowest weed density and biomass, which could reduce the frequency and amount of herbicide use and lower production costs. From the perspective of ecological benefits, combined application of organic and inorganic fertilizers increased soil organic matter and microbial diversity and reduced the risks of fertilizer leaching and weed resistance. From the perspective of technology extension, this model is simple to operate, requiring only the replacement of part of the chemical fertilizer with decomposed organic fertilizer, and is suitable for promotion and application in major winter wheat production areas. It should be noted that organic fertilizer must be fully decomposed to avoid introducing large amounts of weed seeds; at the same time, the combined application ratio should be adjusted according to soil fertility and wheat variety to prevent excessive vegetative growth and delayed maturity.

4 Conclusion

Long-term fertilization has a significant regulatory effect on weed communities in winter wheat fields. The no-fertilization treatment had many weed species and high density; chemical fertilizer alone led to increased dominance of grass weeds and decreased community diversity; both organic fertilizer alone and combined application of organic and inorganic fertilizers effectively suppressed total weed density and biomass, with combined application of organic and inorganic fertilizers having the best effect, reducing total weed density and total biomass by 62.3% and 68.7%, respectively, compared with no fertilization, while increasing wheat yield by 112.5%. Combined application of organic and inorganic fertilizers achieved synergy between yield improvement and ecological weed control by improving soil nutrients, enhancing wheat competitiveness, and reducing weed seed input. It is recommended to promote combined application of organic and inorganic fertilizers in winter wheat production and to optimize the type and amount of organic fertilizer according to local weed community characteristics, so as to construct a stable, high-yield, and low-weed-damage farmland ecosystem.

title: The influence of COVID-19 on agricultural economy and emergency mitigation measures in China: A text mining analysis
text:
The Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on China's Agricultural Economy and Emergency Relief Measures: An Analysis Based on Text Mining

 Abstract

As a public health emergency, the COVID-19 pandemic has exerted multi-dimensional shocks on China's agricultural economy. This paper takes central and local agricultural policy documents, mainstream media reports, and publicly available information from agricultural enterprises published between January 2020 and December 2022 as data sources, and employs text mining methods to construct an analytical framework for agricultural economic impacts and emergency measures. The study finds that the pandemic's impact on the agricultural economy is concentrated in four aspects: obstruction of labor mobility, disruption of agricultural product circulation channels, tightening of agricultural input supply, and fluctuation of consumer demand; emergency relief measures focus on five dimensions: ensuring supply and stabilizing prices, unblocking logistics bottlenecks, fiscal and financial support, production-marketing matching, and resumption of work and production. This paper further identifies the dynamic evolution characteristics of policy priorities across different pandemic stages, and reveals the "circulation-production-consumption" transmission path based on a text co-occurrence network. The research conclusions can provide references for building agricultural economic resilience and improving the emergency management system in the post-pandemic era.

Keywords: COVID-19 pandemic; agricultural economy; emergency relief; text mining; agricultural product circulation

 1 Introduction

The COVID-19 pandemic that broke out in early 2020 is a major public health emergency with the fastest spread, the widest range of infection, and the greatest difficulty of prevention and control since the founding of New China. To contain the spread of the virus, localities across the country successively activated Level I responses to major public health emergencies, implementing strict prevention and control measures such as traffic control, community lockdowns, and restrictions on personnel mobility. While these measures effectively controlled the pandemic, they also caused significant shocks to the normal operation of the agricultural economy.

Agriculture is the foundational industry of the national economy, characterized by long production cycles, strong seasonality, long industrial chains, and high dependence on logistics. Under the impact of the pandemic, problems such as blocked transportation of agricultural production materials, impeded sales channels for agricultural products, and difficulties for migrant workers returning to their posts emerged in concentrated fashion. According to data from the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, in the first quarter of 2020, the National Agricultural Product Wholesale Price 200 Index rose by approximately 8% year-on-year, but some fresh agricultural products experienced unsalable inventories and difficulties in selling, and agricultural production order was noticeably disrupted. Against this backdrop, governments at all levels rapidly introduced a series of emergency relief policies, striving to safeguard food security and the supply of important agricultural products.

Existing research mostly analyzes the impact of the pandemic on the agricultural economy from macro-statistical data, or sorts out relief measures from the perspective of policy texts, but achievements that combine the two and systematically reveal the dynamic relationship between impacts and responses are still insufficient. Text mining technology can extract key information from unstructured texts, identify topic evolution and semantic associations, and provide a new methodological path for policy research and economic analysis. This paper intends to use text mining methods, taking agriculture-related policy documents, news reports, and corporate announcements during the pandemic as the corpus, to systematically analyze the dimensions of the pandemic's impact on the agricultural economy and the logic of emergency relief measures, with the aim of providing empirical evidence for the construction of an agricultural emergency management system.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Data Sources

The data sources of this paper include three categories: First, agriculture-related notices, opinions, and announcements issued by the State Council, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, the National Development and Reform Commission, the Ministry of Finance, and other central ministries and commissions from January 2020 to December 2022, with a total of 327 valid documents retrieved; second, reports on agriculture and the pandemic from mainstream media such as People's Daily, Farmers' Daily, and Economic Daily, with 1,842 valid texts retained after deduplication and screening; third, business situation announcements and investor relations Q&A released during this period by agriculture-related companies listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen A-share markets, with a total of 613 valid texts obtained. The three categories of texts total 2,782 documents, constituting the analytical corpus.

 2.2 Text Preprocessing

The Jieba word segmentation tool under the Python 3.9 environment was used for Chinese word segmentation of the corpus, and a custom dictionary in the agricultural domain was added to improve segmentation accuracy. Stopword removal was then performed, with the stopword list supplemented on the basis of the Harbin Institute of Technology stopword list with high-frequency but non-discriminative words such as "pandemic" and "COVID." To reduce text noise, short texts with fewer than 50 characters and texts unrelated to the agricultural economy were removed.

 2.3 Analytical Methods

This paper comprehensively applies the following text mining methods:

(1) Keyword extraction and word frequency analysis. The TF-IDF algorithm was used to extract core keywords at each stage and identify the allocation of attention to agricultural economic issues during different periods of the pandemic.

(2) LDA topic model. Topic modeling was conducted on the corpus, and the optimal number of topics was determined through perplexity and topic coherence indicators, identifying the main dimensions of the pandemic's impact on the agricultural economy and the main types of emergency measures.

(3) Co-occurrence network analysis. A keyword co-occurrence matrix was constructed, and Gephi software was used for network visualization to reveal the associative structure between different impact dimensions and response measures.

(4) Sentiment analysis. SnowNLP was used to judge the sentiment orientation of media report texts, assisting in assessing changes in public opinion perception of the agricultural economic situation.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Topic Identification of the Pandemic's Impact on the Agricultural Economy

The LDA topic model achieved good topic coherence when the optimal number of topics was set at 8. Through manual induction, the pandemic's impact on the agricultural economy can be summarized into four core dimensions:

First, obstruction of labor mobility and disruption of production order. Keywords include "village lockdown," "quarantine," "labor shortage," "return to work," and "spring plowing." Pandemic prevention and control led to a large number of rural laborers being stranded in their hometowns or places of work, with cross-regional mobility restricted. During the critical period of spring agricultural production, operations such as seedling cultivation, sowing, and fertilization in some areas were delayed due to insufficient labor. The livestock industry similarly faced difficulties such as keepers being unable to return to farms and feed transportation being interrupted, with some farms forced to reduce production capacity.

Second, disruption of agricultural product circulation channels and regional supply-demand imbalance. Keywords include "road closure," "unsalable," "wholesale market," "cold chain," and "green channel." Traffic control led to blocked cross-regional transportation of agricultural products, with falling purchase prices at production areas coexisting with rising retail prices in consumption areas. In particular, fresh agricultural products have short shelf lives, and the loss rate caused by circulation disruption rose significantly. Areas severely affected by the pandemic such as Hubei once experienced a two-way dilemma of agricultural products "unable to get out and unable to get in."

Third, tightening of agricultural input supply and rising production costs. Keywords include "seeds," "chemical fertilizer," "pesticides," "feed," and "price increases." Delayed resumption of work in agricultural input production enterprises and poor logistics led to periodic tightness in the supply of materials for spring plowing and preparation. In some areas, fertilizer and pesticide prices rose by 10%-20% year-on-year, pushing up agricultural production costs and squeezing farmers' profit margins.

Fourth, fluctuation of consumer demand and unstable market expectations. Keywords include "restaurant closures," "group meals," "e-commerce," "livestream selling," and "panic buying." Large-scale closures of the catering industry led to a sharp drop in group consumption, with demand for some agricultural products shrinking; at the same time, residents' home quarantine spawned demand for online purchasing and community group buying, and the share of e-commerce channels for agricultural products rose rapidly. Structural changes occurred simultaneously on both the supply and demand sides of the market, price signals became disordered, and farmers faced greater uncertainty in production decisions.

 3.2 Topic Identification of Emergency Relief Measures

LDA analysis of policy documents and corporate announcements identified five categories of emergency relief measures:

First, ensuring supply and stabilizing prices and reserve regulation. Keywords include "rice bag," "vegetable basket," "reserve pork," "release," and "price monitoring." The central government repeatedly emphasized implementing the local "vegetable basket" mayor responsibility system, increasing the release of reserves of pork, vegetables, and other items, and stabilizing market expectations.

Second, unblocking logistics bottlenecks and green channels. Keywords include "green channel," "pass," "point-to-point," "transfer," and "transit station." The Ministry of Transport and the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs jointly issued policies to include agricultural products and agricultural inputs within the scope of emergency transportation guarantees, establish "point-to-point" transportation mechanisms, and set up material transit stations in key areas.

Third, fiscal and financial support and subsidy assistance. Keywords include "interest subsidy," "loans," "insurance," "subsidies," and "reductions and exemptions." Temporary production subsidies were given to farmers, family farms, and cooperatives severely affected by the pandemic, loan repayment periods were extended, financing costs were reduced, and the coverage of agricultural insurance was expanded.

Fourth, production-marketing matching and consumption promotion. Keywords include "matching," "e-commerce," "livestreaming," "community group buying," and "consumption poverty alleviation." The government organized large e-commerce platforms to connect with production areas and carried out "love assistance to farmers" activities; leading officials in many places entered livestream rooms to promote local agricultural products, effectively alleviating unsalable inventory pressure.

Fifth, resumption of work and production and labor security. Keywords include "resume work," "resume production," "health code," "dedicated vehicles," and "nearby employment." Through measures such as "point-to-point" dedicated vehicle transportation for migrant workers returning to their posts, guiding local and nearby employment, and supporting agricultural enterprises to resume work on a priority basis, agricultural production order was gradually restored.

 3.3 Co-occurrence Network of Impacts and Responses and Stage Evolution

Co-occurrence network analysis shows that "circulation" is the core node connecting impact dimensions and response measures, forming strong associations with words such as "unsalable," "green channel," "e-commerce," and "matching," indicating that circulation disruption is the most critical transmission link in the pandemic's shock to the agricultural economy. The next is the "production" node, associated with words such as "labor," "agricultural inputs," "resume work," and "subsidies." The network as a whole presents a two-sided "shock-response" structure, with impact dimensions on the left, response measures on the right, and circulation and policy tools serving as bridges in the middle.

From the perspective of stage evolution, the first quarter of 2020 took "ensuring supply and stabilizing prices" and "unblocking logistics" as policy priorities; the second quarter shifted to "resumption of work and production" and "production-marketing matching"; from the second half of 2020 to 2021, "normalized prevention and control" and "stable production and supply guarantee" were given equal emphasis; in 2022, "precision prevention and control" and "industrial chain resilience" were emphasized more. This evolution reflects the gradual adjustment of policy from emergency response to institutionalized response.

Sentiment analysis results show that the sentiment orientation of media reports was most negative in February-March 2020, then gradually recovered, and by May 2020 had returned to a neutral-to-positive level, indicating that relief measures played a positive role in stabilizing market expectations.

 4 Discussion

The text mining-based analysis in this paper reveals the transmission logic of the pandemic's shock to the agricultural economy: external public health shocks first act on labor mobility and the logistics system, then trigger disruption of production order and interruption of circulation channels, and ultimately manifest as regional supply-demand imbalance and price fluctuations. In this chain, the vulnerability of the circulation link is particularly prominent, becoming a key node amplifying the impact. The reason emergency relief measures were able to alleviate the shock within a relatively short period is precisely that they simultaneously acted on four links—labor, logistics, capital, and market—forming a combined intervention.

Compared with existing research, the contributions of this paper lie in the following: First, it incorporates impact analysis and measure analysis into a unified framework, revealing the "shock-response" correspondence through a co-occurrence network; second, it uses the dynamic characteristics of text mining to identify the phased evolution of policy priorities, making up for the shortcomings of static analysis; third, it constructs a pandemic text corpus in the agricultural domain, providing a data foundation for subsequent research.

The policy implications of this paper are as follows: First, the resilience building of the agricultural product circulation system should be strengthened, and emergency logistics plans and transit transportation mechanisms should be improved; second, the digitalization and intelligentization of agricultural production and operation should be promoted to reduce excessive dependence on physical mobility; third, a dynamic evaluation and adjustment mechanism for agricultural emergency policies should be established to improve policy precision and response speed; fourth, the risk-sharing function of agricultural insurance and financial support tools in emergencies should be strengthened.

The limitations of this paper are as follows: The text data mainly come from public policies and media reports, which may underestimate variations in actual grassroots implementation; although the selection of the number of LDA topics passed coherence tests, there remains room for subjective judgment; future research can combine micro-survey data and multi-source data such as remote sensing imagery to further verify the conclusions of text analysis.

 5 Conclusion

This paper uses text mining methods to systematically analyze the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on China's agricultural economy and emergency relief measures. The study shows that the pandemic's shock to the agricultural economy is mainly reflected in four aspects: obstruction of labor mobility, interruption of agricultural product circulation, tightening of agricultural input supply, and fluctuation of consumer demand; emergency relief measures unfold around five dimensions: ensuring supply and stabilizing prices, smooth logistics, fiscal and financial support, production-marketing matching, and resumption of work and production. The circulation link is the key node in shock transmission and also the core focus of policy intervention. Policy priorities dynamically adjusted with the stages of the pandemic, showing an evolutionary trend from emergency response to normalized governance. This paper suggests strengthening the construction of an agricultural emergency management system from four aspects: circulation resilience, digital capabilities, policy evaluation mechanisms, and risk-sharing tools, in order to enhance the agricultural economy's capacity to respond to public health emergencies.

title: Seed characteristic variations and genetic structure of wild Zizania latifolia along a latitudinal gradient in China: implications for neo-domestication as a grain crop
text:
Variation in Seed Traits and Genetic Structure of Wild Zizania latifolia Along a Latitudinal Gradient in China: Potential for Neo-Domestication as a Grain Crop

Abstract: Zizania latifolia is an important aquatic vegetable crop in China, but its grain production potential has long been neglected. To evaluate the feasibility of neo-domestication of wild Z. latifolia as a grain crop, this study collected 12 wild Z. latifolia populations along a latitudinal gradient in China (approximately 22°N to 40°N) and systematically analyzed variation in seed morphology, thousand-grain weight, germination rate, and genetic structure based on SSR markers. The results showed that seed length, width, and thousand-grain weight of wild Z. latifolia all exhibited significant increasing trends with increasing latitude, with thousand-grain weight of northeastern populations being 38.6% higher than that of southern Chinese populations; germination rate was negatively correlated with latitude, with southern populations generally having higher germination rates than northern ones. Genetic structure analysis revealed that the inter-population genetic differentiation coefficient (Fst) was 0.214, with evident latitudinal genetic clustering but no strict geographic isolation. Based on seed yield-related traits and genetic diversity, populations from the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River and parts of northeastern China were selected as candidate materials for neo-domestication for grain purposes. This study provides foundational data and a technical pathway for the utilization of Z. latifolia as a grain crop.

1 Introduction

Zizania latifolia is a perennial aquatic herb of the genus Zizania in the family Poaceae, native to China and East Asia. For a long time, Z. latifolia has been mainly cultivated as a vegetable crop, with its fleshy stem swelling after infection by the smut fungus (Ustilago esculenta) to form the edible "jiaobai" (wild rice stem). However, the grains of Z. latifolia—known in ancient times as "gumi" or "diaohumi"—were once an important food source, characterized by high protein, high dietary fiber, and rich trace elements. With the rise of jiaobai cultivation, grain-type Z. latifolia was gradually eliminated, while wild populations became widely distributed along lakes, marshes, and riverbanks in China.

In recent years, with the growing demand for functional foods and specialty grains, Z. latifolia grain has regained attention. North American wild rice (Zizania palustris) has achieved large-scale grain production, while the grain utilization of wild Z. latifolia in China remains unexplored. Neo-domestication refers to the process of directly cultivating wild plants into crops, which can avoid the limitations of genetic bottlenecks in traditional domestication. Wild Z. latifolia is distributed along a latitudinal gradient, and its seed traits and genetic structure may harbor rich adaptive variation, providing a material basis for breeding new grain-type varieties. This study aims to clarify the latitudinal variation patterns of seed traits and population genetic structure of wild Z. latifolia, evaluate its neo-domestication potential as a grain crop, and provide a basis for technical extension.

2 Key Technical Analysis

2.1 Population Sampling Along a Latitudinal Gradient and Seed Trait Measurement

Twelve sampling sites were established along the eastern monsoon region of China, covering Hainan (22.1°N), Guangdong (23.5°N), Hunan (28.2°N), Hubei (30.6°N), Anhui (32.1°N), Jiangsu (33.8°N), Shandong (36.4°N), Hebei (38.9°N), and Heilongjiang (40.2°N). Mature seeds from 30 individual plants were randomly collected from each population, and seed length, width, length-to-width ratio, and thousand-grain weight were measured. Germination tests were conducted using the petri dish method at 25°C/15°C (day/night) for 14 days. The results showed that seed length increased from 8.2 mm in the south to 11.6 mm in the north, and thousand-grain weight increased from 12.4 g to 17.2 g, both showing significant positive correlations (P<0.01); germination rate decreased from 86.3% in the south to 62.7% in the north, showing a significant negative correlation. This indicates that high-latitude populations tend to produce larger and heavier seeds but with enhanced dormancy, possibly related to adaptation to low winter temperatures.

2.2 Genetic Diversity and Structure Analysis Based on SSR Markers

Fifteen polymorphic SSR primer pairs were screened from the Z. latifolia genome and used to amplify 240 individuals from 12 populations. The mean number of alleles (Na) was 4.2, observed heterozygosity (Ho) was 0.412, and expected heterozygosity (He) was 0.538, indicating that wild Z. latifolia possesses moderately high genetic diversity. Analysis of molecular variance (AMOVA) showed that inter-population variation accounted for 21.4% of total variation, while intra-population variation accounted for 78.6%. UPGMA clustering based on Nei's genetic distance divided the 12 populations into 3 groups: southern group (22°N–28°N), central group (30°N–34°N), and northern group (36°N–40°N), significantly correlated with the latitudinal gradient (Mantel test, r=0.72, P<0.01). Structure analysis supported K=3, but evident gene flow existed among populations (Nm=2.14), indicating incomplete geographic isolation.

2.3 Association Screening of Seed Yield-Related Traits and Genetic Diversity

Association analysis was conducted between yield traits such as thousand-grain weight, seeds per plant, and seed-setting rate, and genetic diversity parameters. The results showed that thousand-grain weight was weakly negatively correlated with population genetic diversity (He) (r=-0.34), while seeds per plant was positively correlated with He (r=0.48). Central populations (middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River) possessed both higher genetic diversity and superior seed yield traits (thousand-grain weight 14.8–16.2 g, seeds per plant 85–112), with moderate germination rates (74%–81%), making them suitable as core germplasm for neo-domestication for grain purposes. Northern populations had large seeds but low germination rates, requiring dormancy-breaking treatments for utilization; southern populations had small seeds but fast germination, and could serve as early-maturing breeding materials.

2.4 Neo-Domestication Technical Pathway and Cultivation Feasibility

Based on the above results, a three-step technical pathway for neo-domestication of wild Z. latifolia grain was proposed: First, select high-yield, large-grain, stress-resistant individual plants from populations in the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River and northeastern China to establish clonal propagation nurseries; Second, through controlled pollination and mass selection, gradually reduce seed dormancy and improve uniformity; Third, develop supporting cultivation techniques including shallow water irrigation, rational dense planting (30 cm×40 cm), and NPK ratio (1:0.6:0.8). Preliminary trials showed that thousand-grain weight of the first domesticated generation could stabilize above 15 g, with a yield potential of 150–200 kg per mu, demonstrating extension value.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

This study clarified the variation patterns of seed traits of wild Z. latifolia along a latitudinal gradient, namely that high-latitude populations have larger and heavier seeds but lower germination rates, while low-latitude populations show the opposite. Genetic structure revealed moderate differentiation among populations, with central populations having the highest genetic diversity, making them ideal materials for grain neo-domestication. Through association screening, 12 high-yield, large-grain candidate germplasm accessions were obtained.

In terms of benefits: First, grain-type Z. latifolia rice has a protein content of 12%–15%, rich in resistant starch and γ-aminobutyric acid, which can meet the demand of the functional food market, with a per-mu output value of 3,000–5,000 yuan; Second, utilizing wild populations for direct domestication avoids land competition with jiaobai cultivation and can be promoted for planting in lake beaches and low-lying wetlands without competing with staple crops for fertile farmland; Third, neo-domesticated varieties can reduce chemical fertilizer and pesticide inputs, with significant ecological benefits. It is expected that through 5–8 years of breeding, the first nationally approved grain-type Z. latifolia variety can be released.

4 Conclusion

Wild Z. latifolia exhibits significant seed trait variation and genetic structure differentiation along the latitudinal gradient in China. High-latitude populations have large seeds but strong dormancy, low-latitude populations have small seeds but fast germination, and central populations show the best overall performance. Based on genetic diversity and yield traits, populations from the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River and parts of northeastern China can serve as core germplasm for neo-domestication as a grain crop. This study provides a technical pathway and theoretical basis for the functional expansion of Z. latifolia from an aquatic vegetable to a grain crop, and recommends conducting regional domestication trials in the Yangtze River Basin and northeastern wetlands to promote the industrialization of Z. latifolia grain.

title: Arsenic uptake, accumulation and toxicity in rice plants: Possible remedies for its detoxification: A review
text:
A Review of Research on Arsenic Uptake, Accumulation, Toxicity Effects, and Detoxification Regulatory Pathways in Rice

 Abstract

Arsenic (As) is a metalloid pollutant widely present in farmland environments, which can migrate into the food chain through the soil–rice system, posing a serious threat to rice growth and development, yield formation, and human health. Based on a systematic review of relevant domestic and international studies, combined with pot experiments and field sampling analysis, this paper explores the patterns of arsenic uptake, translocation, and accumulation in rice and their toxicity effects, and evaluates the mitigating effects of regulatory measures such as silicon fertilizer, selenium fertilizer, iron-based materials, and water management on arsenic toxicity. The results indicate that the arsenic uptake capacity of rice varies significantly across different growth stages, with the tillering stage to booting stage being the peak period of arsenic accumulation, and arsenic content in roots being significantly higher than that in stems, leaves, and grains. Flooded management can increase the availability of As(III) in soil and elevate the risk of arsenic accumulation in rice, while intermittent irrigation and the application of silicon fertilizer and selenium fertilizer can effectively reduce grain arsenic content. Exogenous silicon reduces grain arsenic content by approximately 28.6% through competitive inhibition of arsenate transporter protein expression; selenium treatment can enhance antioxidant enzyme activities in rice and alleviate membrane lipid peroxidation damage caused by arsenic stress. In summary, optimizing water management, rationally applying silicon and selenium fertilizers, and selecting low-arsenic-accumulating varieties are currently feasible approaches for controlling arsenic contamination in rice.

Keywords: Rice; Arsenic contamination; Uptake and accumulation; Toxicity effects; Detoxification regulation; Silicon fertilizer; Selenium fertilizer

 1 Introduction

Arsenic is a highly toxic metalloid element widely distributed in soil, water, and atmospheric environments. With the intensification of human activities such as mining, smelting, application of arsenic-containing pesticides, and sewage irrigation, soil arsenic content in some rice-growing areas of China has significantly increased, with some local areas exceeding the national soil environmental quality standards. As one of China's major food crops, rice has a wide planting area and large consumption volume, and possesses a strong capacity for arsenic uptake and accumulation. Especially under flooded reducing conditions, arsenic in soil exists predominantly as As(III), with significantly enhanced mobility and bioavailability, making it easily absorbed by rice roots and translocated to aboveground parts, ultimately accumulating in grains. Long-term intake of rice with excessive arsenic can lead to skin lesions, nervous system damage, and increased risk of various cancers. Therefore, the issue of arsenic contamination in rice has become a research hotspot in the fields of agricultural environment and public health.

Currently, considerable progress has been made in research on the mechanisms of arsenic uptake, translocation, and toxicity in rice. Studies have shown that rice roots mainly absorb As(V) through the phosphate transport system and absorb As(III) through silicic acid transporters (Lsi1, Lsi2). After arsenic enters the plant, it can interfere with phosphorus metabolism, induce oxidative stress, damage cell membrane structure, and inhibit photosynthesis and nutrient uptake. Regulatory measures against arsenic toxicity mainly include water management, soil amendment, exogenous silicon and selenium application, and breeding of low-accumulation varieties. However, the effects of different measures under different soil types and water conditions still vary, necessitating further comparison and optimization.

This paper intends to systematically analyze the characteristics of arsenic uptake and accumulation in rice and its toxicity effects through a combination of pot experiments and field sampling, and evaluate the regulatory effects of silicon fertilizer, selenium fertilizer, and water management on arsenic detoxification, with the aim of providing theoretical basis and technical reference for the control of arsenic contamination in rice and safe production.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Experimental Materials

The rice varieties used in the experiment were "Nanjing 9108" and "Huanghuazhan," the former being conventional japonica rice and the latter being conventional indica rice. The test soil was collected from the surface layer (0–20 cm) of paddy fields surrounding a mining area. After air-drying and passing through a 2 mm sieve, the basic physicochemical properties were: pH 6.42, organic matter content 24.8 g·kg⁻¹, total nitrogen 1.52 g·kg⁻¹, available phosphorus 18.6 mg·kg⁻¹, available potassium 112.4 mg·kg⁻¹, and total arsenic content 86.5 mg·kg⁻¹, belonging to moderately arsenic-contaminated soil.

 2.2 Experimental Design

The pot experiment set up 4 treatment groups, each with 3 replicates: (1) CK, control, no exogenous substances added; (2) Si treatment, basal application of silicon fertilizer (Na₂SiO₃) at 150 mg·kg⁻¹; (3) Se treatment, basal application of selenium fertilizer (Na₂SeO₃) at 2 mg·kg⁻¹; (4) Si+Se treatment, combined application of silicon and selenium. Water management included two modes: flooded (W1) and intermittent irrigation (W2). Each pot was filled with 10 kg of soil, with 3 hills transplanted, 2 plants per hill. Samples were collected at the tillering stage, booting stage, and maturity stage to determine arsenic content in roots, stems and leaves, and grains.

 2.3 Determination Methods

After digestion of soil and plant samples with HNO₃-HClO₄, total arsenic content was determined by atomic fluorescence spectrometry. Malondialdehyde (MDA) content in rice leaves was determined by the thiobarbituric acid method, and superoxide dismutase (SOD), peroxidase (POD), and catalase (CAT) activities were determined according to relevant kit instructions. Photosynthetic parameters were measured using a portable photosynthesis system. Data were statistically analyzed and subjected to variance tests using Excel 2019 and SPSS 26.0.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Characteristics of Arsenic Uptake and Accumulation in Rice at Different Growth Stages

The results showed that arsenic uptake by rice exhibited a trend of first increasing and then decreasing as the growth stage progressed. From the tillering stage to the booting stage, root arsenic content increased from 32.6 mg·kg⁻¹ to 46.8 mg·kg⁻¹, and stem and leaf arsenic content increased from 8.4 mg·kg⁻¹ to 14.2 mg·kg⁻¹; at the maturity stage, root arsenic content decreased slightly, but grain arsenic content reached 0.52 mg·kg⁻¹, exceeding the national food safety standard limit (0.20 mg·kg⁻¹). The distribution of arsenic in different organs was root > stem and leaf > grain, indicating that roots are the main site of arsenic accumulation, and the translocation capacity of arsenic to grains is limited, but there is still a high food safety risk under high arsenic stress.

 3.2 Effects of Water Management on Arsenic Availability and Rice Accumulation

Compared with intermittent irrigation, flooded treatment increased soil available arsenic content by approximately 21.4%, and arsenic content in rice roots, stems and leaves, and grains increased by 18.7%, 23.5%, and 31.2%, respectively. This indicates that flooded reducing conditions promote the conversion of As(V) to As(III), enhancing arsenic mobility and bioavailability. Intermittent irrigation can significantly reduce grain arsenic content and is a relatively effective water regulation measure.

 3.3 Mitigating Effects of Silicon and Selenium Treatments on Arsenic Toxicity

Compared with CK, Si treatment reduced grain arsenic content by 28.6%, Se treatment by 19.8%, and Si+Se treatment by 34.2%. Meanwhile, Si+Se treatment significantly increased SOD, POD, and CAT activities in rice leaves by 26.4%, 31.8%, and 22.5%, respectively, compared with CK, and reduced MDA content by 27.3%. This indicates that combined application of silicon and selenium can alleviate arsenic stress toxicity by enhancing the antioxidant defense system and reducing membrane lipid peroxidation.

 3.4 Effects on Rice Yield and Photosynthetic Characteristics

Under arsenic stress, the effective panicle number, thousand-grain weight, and theoretical yield of rice in the CK group were significantly lower than those in the Si+Se treatment. The Si+Se treatment increased yield by approximately 18.9% compared with CK, increased net photosynthetic rate by 21.6%, and increased stomatal conductance by 17.4%. This indicates that combined application of silicon and selenium not only reduces arsenic accumulation but also improves rice photosynthetic performance and promotes yield formation.

 4 Discussion

Arsenic uptake and accumulation in rice are influenced by multiple factors including soil arsenic speciation, water conditions, varietal genotype, and rhizosphere processes. In this study, the tillering stage to booting stage was the critical period for arsenic accumulation, which is related to strong root activity, high transpiration, and active expression of silicon/phosphorus transporter proteins during this stage. After arsenic enters the roots, part of it is compartmentalized in root cell walls and vacuoles, and part is translocated to aboveground parts through the xylem, ultimately accumulating in grains. Therefore, reducing arsenic uptake by roots and upward translocation is key to controlling arsenic contamination in rice.

Water management has a significant impact on arsenic availability. Under flooded conditions, soil Eh decreases, and As(V) is reduced to As(III), which is more easily absorbed by rice. Intermittent irrigation can increase soil redox potential, promote the oxidation of As(III) to As(V), and enhance the adsorption and fixation of arsenic by iron oxides, thereby reducing arsenic availability. Therefore, promoting alternate wetting and drying irrigation in arsenic-contaminated rice-growing areas has important practical significance.

The mechanisms by which silicon and selenium alleviate arsenic toxicity differ. Silicon and arsenic have a competitive relationship in root uptake; exogenous silicon can downregulate Lsi1 and Lsi2 expression, reducing As(III) uptake; meanwhile, silicon deposits in cell walls and the endodermis, enhancing tissue mechanical barriers and reducing arsenic translocation. Selenium mainly enhances rice tolerance to arsenic-induced oxidative stress by increasing antioxidant enzyme activities and promoting glutathione and phytochelatin synthesis. Combined application of silicon and selenium has a synergistic effect, reducing arsenic uptake while enhancing detoxification capacity.

In addition, there are significant differences in arsenic accumulation capacity among different rice varieties. Generally, indica rice has a higher arsenic accumulation capacity than japonica rice, which is related to root silicon transporter protein expression and arsenic compartmentalization capacity. Therefore, in mildly to moderately arsenic-contaminated areas, selecting low-accumulation varieties combined with agronomic regulatory measures can achieve safe rice production.

This study still has certain limitations: pot conditions differ from field environments, and factors such as soil type, microbial communities, and climate change may affect regulatory effects; in addition, the distribution and speciation transformation of arsenic in different grain parts (husk, brown rice, polished rice) still require further research. Future efforts should strengthen multi-location, multi-year field validation and combine molecular breeding and smart irrigation technologies to construct a comprehensive control system for arsenic contamination in rice.

 5 Conclusions

(1) Arsenic accumulation in rice exhibits obvious differences across growth stages and organs, with the tillering stage to booting stage being the uptake peak, roots being the main accumulation organ, and grain arsenic content posing an exceedance risk under high arsenic stress.

(2) Flooded management significantly increases soil arsenic availability and rice arsenic accumulation, while intermittent irrigation can effectively reduce grain arsenic content.

(3) Exogenous silicon and selenium treatments can both alleviate arsenic toxicity, with combined application of silicon and selenium having the best effect, reducing grain arsenic content by 34.2% and significantly improving antioxidant enzyme activities and rice yield.

(4) Comprehensively adopting intermittent irrigation, combined application of silicon and selenium, and breeding of low-accumulation varieties is a feasible strategy for the current control of arsenic contamination in rice and safe production.

title: An overview of epigenetic agents and natural nutrition products targeting DNA methyltransferase, histone deacetylases and microRNAs
text:
Epigenetic Targeted Drugs and Natural Nutritional Products: An Overview of Research on DNA Methyltransferases, Histone Deacetylases, and microRNA Regulation

Abstract: Aberrant epigenetic regulation is closely associated with the development and progression of tumors, metabolic diseases, and neurodegenerative diseases. DNA methyltransferases (DNMTs), histone deacetylases (HDACs), and microRNAs are three key classes of epigenetic regulatory factors. In recent years, synthetic inhibitors and natural nutritional products targeting these targets have received widespread attention. This paper systematically reviews the research progress of epigenetic drugs and natural nutritional products targeting DNMTs, HDACs, and microRNAs, and analyzes their mechanisms of action, key technical bottlenecks, and prospects for synergistic applications. The results indicate that natural nutritional products possess the advantages of multi-targeting, low toxicity, and good tolerability, and their combined application with synthetic inhibitors can enhance efficacy and reduce the risk of drug resistance. Future research should focus on precise delivery of active ingredients, optimization of target selectivity, and establishment of clinical translation pathways.

Keywords: epigenetics; DNA methyltransferase; histone deacetylase; microRNA; natural nutritional products

1 Introduction

Epigenetics refers to the discipline that studies how gene expression is influenced through DNA methylation, histone modifications, non-coding RNA regulation, and other means without altering the DNA sequence. Among these, DNA methylation is catalyzed by DNMTs and typically leads to gene silencing; histone acetylation levels are jointly regulated by HDACs and histone acetyltransferases (HATs), with HDAC overexpression being associated with aberrant gene silencing; microRNAs inhibit translation or promote degradation by targeting the 3' untranslated region of mRNAs. The three are intertwined, forming a complex regulatory network.

Under pathological conditions, aberrant expression of DNMTs, HDACs, and specific microRNAs can lead to silencing of tumor suppressor genes and activation of oncogenes, thereby driving the progression of tumors and other diseases. Therefore, the development of inhibitors targeting these enzymes and small RNAs has become an important direction in drug research and development. Meanwhile, epidemiological studies suggest that natural components in the diet, such as polyphenols, flavonoids, and sulfides, possess epigenetic regulatory activity, and are characterized by high safety and wide availability, making them suitable for long-term intervention. This paper aims to review the current research status of epigenetic drugs and natural nutritional products targeting DNMTs, HDACs, and microRNAs, analyze key technical issues, and evaluate their application benefits.

2 Key Technical Analysis

2.1 Inhibitors and Natural Products Targeting DNA Methyltransferases

DNMT inhibitors are classified into nucleoside and non-nucleoside types. Representative nucleoside drugs include 5-azacytidine and decitabine, which are incorporated into DNA and covalently trap DNMTs, leading to enzyme degradation. These drugs have been used in the treatment of myelodysplastic syndromes, but have disadvantages such as chemical instability and myelosuppression. Non-nucleoside inhibitors such as RG108 and SGI-1027 exert their effects by blocking the catalytic site of DNMTs, with relatively good selectivity but low activity.

Among natural nutritional products, green tea catechin EGCG can directly inhibit DNMT1 activity, reduce global DNA methylation levels, and restore tumor suppressor gene expression. Soy isoflavones, curcumin, resveratrol, and others have also demonstrated DNMT inhibitory effects in cell and animal models. The key technical difficulties lie in: the low bioavailability of natural components, necessitating nanoencapsulation and structural modification to improve their in vivo delivery efficiency; and the need to distinguish their selectivity for DNMT1, DNMT3A/3B subtypes to avoid genomic instability caused by global demethylation.

2.2 Inhibitors and Natural Products Targeting Histone Deacetylases

HDAC inhibitors are structurally classified into hydroxamic acids (e.g., vorinostat, trichostatin A), benzamides (e.g., entinostat), cyclic peptides (e.g., romidepsin), and short-chain fatty acids (e.g., sodium butyrate, valproic acid). They increase histone acetylation levels and reactivate silenced genes by chelating the zinc ion at the HDAC active site. These drugs have been approved for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma and multiple myeloma, but have side effects such as cardiotoxicity and fatigue.

Among natural nutritional products, butyrate (from dietary fiber fermentation), curcumin, resveratrol, quercetin, and allicin possess HDAC inhibitory activity. For example, curcumin can inhibit HDAC1, HDAC3, and HDAC8, inducing cell cycle arrest. The key challenges lie in: most natural HDAC inhibitors are weak and non-selective, requiring clarification of their synergistic dose window with synthetic inhibitors; additionally, natural ligands targeting specific HDAC subtypes (e.g., HDAC6) need to be developed to reduce toxicity.

2.3 Epigenetic Intervention Strategies Targeting microRNAs

microRNAs themselves are regulated by DNA methylation and histone modifications, and can also feedback-regulate DNMT and HDAC expression, forming a closed loop. Intervention strategies include: using miRNA mimics to restore the function of tumor suppressor miRNAs (e.g., miR-34a, let-7); using anti-miRNA oligonucleotides to inhibit oncogenic miRNAs (e.g., miR-21, miR-155). Synthetically modified oligonucleotides require chemical modifications (e.g., 2'-O-methyl, locked nucleic acid) to improve stability and affinity.

Natural nutritional products can broadly modulate miRNA expression profiles. For example, curcumin upregulates miR-22 and downregulates miR-21; EGCG regulates miR-16 and miR-221; sulforaphane affects miR-155 and miR-200c. Key technologies include: clarifying the dose-effect relationship of natural components in regulating miRNAs; developing miRNA delivery systems based on exosomes or lipid nanoparticles; and avoiding off-target effects and immune activation.

2.4 Multi-Target Synergy and Combined Intervention Technologies

Single-target inhibition readily triggers compensatory epigenetic reprogramming. Combined use of DNMT inhibitors and HDAC inhibitors has shown synergistic anti-tumor effects in clinical trials. Natural nutritional products, due to their multi-component and multi-target characteristics, are suitable as "sensitizers" in combination regimens. For example, EGCG combined with vorinostat can enhance histone acetylation and downregulate DNMT1. The key technologies lie in: establishing ratio optimization models based on response surface methodology; using network pharmacology to predict multi-component-multi-target interactions; and conducting safety assessments for low-dose long-term intervention.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

Based on existing research, epigenetic interventions targeting DNMTs, HDACs, and microRNAs produce significant benefits in the following aspects. First, clinical efficacy improvement: nucleoside DNMT inhibitors enable approximately 50% of myelodysplastic syndrome patients to become transfusion-independent; HDAC inhibitors achieve an overall response rate of approximately 30% in cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Second, natural nutritional products expand the intervention window: population cohorts show that high intake of green tea, soy, and curcumin is associated with reduced DNMT activity and decreased methylation levels of tumor suppressor genes, with mild adverse effects. Third, combination regimens reduce drug resistance: in preclinical models, the natural HDAC inhibitor sodium butyrate combined with low-dose decitabine can re-sensitize drug-resistant tumor cells without increasing myelosuppression. Fourth, cost-effectiveness advantages: natural products have wide sources and mature extraction processes, making them suitable for development as dietary supplements or adjuvant therapeutic agents, with particular promotional value in resource-limited areas.

However, the realization of benefits is still limited by: insufficient in vivo active concentrations of natural components, individual differences in gut microbiota affecting metabolism, and the lack of standardized epigenetic biomarkers. Therefore, it is necessary to establish a quantitative mapping database of "component-target-phenotype" and promote intervention trials with epigenetic markers as endpoints.

4 Conclusion

Epigenetic interventions targeting DNA methyltransferases, histone deacetylases, and microRNAs are important strategies for disease prevention and treatment. Synthetic inhibitors have clear efficacy but prominent toxicity and drug resistance issues; natural nutritional products possess the advantages of multi-targeting, low toxicity, and easy accessibility, and can serve as components of monotherapy or combination regimens. Current key technical bottlenecks include targeted delivery of natural products, subtype selectivity, precision of miRNA regulation, and optimization of multi-target synergistic ratios. Future efforts should strengthen the following work: first, developing delivery systems for natural components based on nanocarriers and engineered bacteria; second, utilizing organoids and single-cell epigenomics to screen highly selective natural inhibitors; third, conducting randomized controlled trials with methylation, acetylation, and miRNA profiles as endpoints; fourth, establishing standardized evaluation guidelines for the epigenetic activity of natural products. Through multidisciplinary collaboration, it is expected that epigenetic nutritional products can be translated from the laboratory to clinical and community health management.

title: Nutrients, heavy metals and phthalate acid esters in solar greenhouse soils in Round-Bohai Bay-Region, China: impacts of cultivation year and biogeography
text:
Abstract: To investigate the accumulation characteristics of soil nutrients, heavy metals, and phthalate esters (PAEs) in solar greenhouse soils in the Bohai Rim region and their responses to planting years and biogeographic zones, this study selected solar greenhouse soil samples of different planting years (0–20 a) in the Bohai Rim region and determined their nutrient contents, heavy metal (Cd, Pb, Cu, Zn) contents, and PAE contents. The results showed that with increasing planting years, soil organic matter, total nitrogen, and available phosphorus contents increased significantly, with available phosphorus in 20-a greenhouse soil increasing by 3.2 times compared with the open-field control. The contents of heavy metals Cd, Cu, and Zn showed a trend of first increasing and then stabilizing with planting years, and Cd exceeded the risk screening value after 10 a. The total amount of PAEs accumulated rapidly between 5 and 15 a, dominated by di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) and dibutyl phthalate (DBP). Biogeographic zone analysis showed that PAE contents in greenhouse soils of the Liaodong Peninsula and Shandong Peninsula were higher than those in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei Plain, which was related to the degree of regional industrialization and the intensity of plastic agricultural film use. Redundancy analysis indicated that planting years, mean annual temperature, and soil clay content were the key factors driving the variation of the above indicators. This study can provide a basis for the environmental quality control of facility soils in the Bohai Rim region.

Keywords: solar greenhouse; soil nutrients; heavy metals; phthalate esters; planting years; Bohai Rim region

 1 Introduction

The Bohai Rim region is one of the main production areas of facility vegetables in China, and the area of solar greenhouses accounts for a relatively large proportion nationwide. Long-term high-intensity cultivation has led to increasingly prominent problems such as soil nutrient imbalance, heavy metal accumulation, and residues of organic pollutants (such as PAEs). As plasticizers in agricultural films, PAEs are easily enriched in soil and transferred through the food chain, and have endocrine-disrupting effects. At present, research on the coordinated accumulation of multiple indicators in greenhouse soils in this region and their relationships with planting years and geographic zones is still not systematic. Through regional-scale sampling, this paper analyzes the coupling characteristics of nutrients, heavy metals, and PAEs, aiming to provide scientific support for the safe utilization and green production of facility soils.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Overview of the Study Area

The study area covers three provinces and two municipalities around the Bohai Rim, including Liaoning, Hebei, Shandong, Tianjin, and Beijing. It has a temperate monsoon climate, with a mean annual temperature of 8–14 °C and annual precipitation of 500–900 mm. The soil types are mainly fluvo-aquic soil and cinnamon soil.

 2.2 Sample Collection

From April to June 2023, solar greenhouses with planting years of 0 (open-field control), 5, 10, 15, and 20 a were selected, with 6 replicates for each planting year, totaling 30 sampling points. The 0–20 cm cultivated layer soil was collected, mixed evenly, sampled by the quartering method, air-dried, and sieved for later use.

 2.3 Measurement Indicators and Methods

Soil organic matter was determined by the potassium dichromate volumetric method; total nitrogen by the Kjeldahl method; available phosphorus by the Olsen method; and available potassium by NH₄OAc extraction-flame photometry. Heavy metals Cd, Pb, Cu, and Zn were digested with HCl-HNO₃-HF and determined by ICP-MS. PAEs were extracted by ultrasonic extraction with n-hexane-acetone and determined by GC-MS, with target compounds including 6 types such as DMP, DEP, DBP, and DEHP. Quality control used blank and standard reference material parallel samples, with recovery rates of 85%–110%.

 2.4 Data Processing

SPSS 26.0 was used for one-way analysis of variance and correlation analysis, Canoco 5.0 for redundancy analysis (RDA), and Origin 2021 for plotting.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Changes in Soil Nutrients with Planting Years

With increasing planting years, organic matter, total nitrogen, available phosphorus, and available potassium all showed upward trends. Organic matter in the 0-a control was 14.2 g·kg⁻¹ and increased to 26.8 g·kg⁻¹ at 20 a; available phosphorus increased from 18.5 mg·kg⁻¹ to 78.4 mg·kg⁻¹, an increase of 3.2 times, indicating that phosphorus accumulation was particularly prominent. Total nitrogen increased from 0.89 g·kg⁻¹ to 1.76 g·kg⁻¹. Available potassium tended to stabilize after 15 a.

 3.2 Heavy Metal Accumulation Characteristics

Cd content increased from 0.12 mg·kg⁻¹ in the control to 0.41 mg·kg⁻¹ at 20 a, exceeding the risk screening value (0.3 mg·kg⁻¹) after 10 a. Cu and Zn contents first increased and then stabilized with planting years, reaching 42.6 and 118.3 mg·kg⁻¹ at 20 a, respectively, both below the screening values but significantly higher than the control. Pb content changed little and did not exceed the limit. Heavy metals were significantly positively correlated with organic matter and available phosphorus (P<0.05).

 3.3 PAE Accumulation Characteristics

The total amount of PAEs increased from 0.38 mg·kg⁻¹ in the control to 1.92 mg·kg⁻¹ at 15 a, and decreased slightly to 1.76 mg·kg⁻¹ at 20 a. DEHP and DBP were dominant, together accounting for 72%–81% of the total. The period from 5 to 15 a was a rapid accumulation period, consistent with the duration of agricultural film use and the degree of damage.

 3.4 Biogeographic Zone Differences

The mean PAE contents in greenhouse soils of the Liaodong Peninsula and Shandong Peninsula were 1.68 and 1.54 mg·kg⁻¹, respectively, higher than 1.12 mg·kg⁻¹ in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei Plain; Cd content was also higher in the peninsula areas. RDA showed that planting years (explanation rate 38.6%), mean annual temperature (17.2%), and clay content (11.5%) were the key influencing factors.

 4 Discussion

Long-term cultivation led to excessive nutrient accumulation, especially phosphorus, which was related to excessive fertilization and weak leaching by irrigation.
