Cd accumulation may originate from impurities in phosphate fertilizer and additives in agricultural film. The rapid PAE accumulation period coincided with the intensity of agricultural film mulching. The peninsula areas had a higher degree of industrialization and greater agricultural film use, resulting in higher contents. The coexistence of heavy metals and PAEs may produce combined toxicity, and attention should be paid to their effects on soil microorganisms and vegetable quality. It is recommended to control phosphate fertilizer input, promote degradable agricultural film, and conduct regular monitoring.

 5 Conclusion

Soil nutrients, Cd, and PAEs in solar greenhouse soils in the Bohai Rim accumulated significantly with planting years, reaching relatively high levels at 15–20 a; the pollution load in the peninsula areas was higher than that in the plain area. Planting years, climate, and soil texture jointly drove their spatial differentiation. Collaborative management and control of multiple pollutants in facility soils should be strengthened to ensure the safety of agricultural products.

title: Soil genotoxicity induced by successive applications of chlorothalonil under greenhouse conditions
text:
Effects of Continuous Chlorothalonil Application on Soil Genotoxicity Under Greenhouse Conditions

Abstract: To clarify the potential risk of continuous chlorothalonil application to the soil ecosystem in greenhouse vegetable production, this study took greenhouse soil with 5 years of continuous cropping as the object, set up treatments with different years of chlorothalonil application (1 year, 3 years, 5 years), and evaluated soil genotoxic effects using a combination of the comet assay (single-cell gel electrophoresis) and the Vicia faba root tip micronucleus test. The results showed that with increasing years of chlorothalonil application, chlorothalonil residues in soil accumulated significantly, reaching 0.86 mg/kg in the 5-year treatment. Soil genotoxicity increased with the extension of application years; compared with the control, the micronucleus rate in Vicia faba root tips in the 5-year treatment group increased by 2.3 times, and the tail moment value in the comet assay increased by 3.1 times. Soil genotoxicity was significantly positively correlated with chlorothalonil residues (r=0.92, P<0.01). The study concluded that continuous chlorothalonil application under greenhouse conditions can lead to the accumulation of soil genotoxicity, and it is recommended to rationally rotate pesticides and strengthen soil ecological monitoring.

Keywords: chlorothalonil; greenhouse soil; genotoxicity; comet assay; micronucleus test

1 Introduction

Chlorothalonil is a broad-spectrum, protective organochlorine fungicide. Because of its broad fungicidal spectrum, stable efficacy, and relatively low cost, it is widely used in greenhouse vegetable production in China to control fungal diseases such as downy mildew, gray mold, and powdery mildew. The greenhouse environment is characterized by high temperature and humidity, a high multiple cropping index, and widespread continuous cropping, resulting in frequent disease occurrence, which leads to application frequency and total amount of chlorothalonil far higher than those in open-field cultivation. Some surveys have shown that chlorothalonil can be applied 8-12 times per year in some greenhouses and continuously for many years.

Chlorothalonil is chemically stable, and its degradation half-life in soil can reach 30-60 days. Long-term heavy application can easily cause accumulation of soil residues. Previous studies have shown that chlorothalonil is highly toxic to aquatic organisms and also has certain effects on soil microbial communities and enzyme activities. However, research on the effects of continuous chlorothalonil application on soil genotoxicity, especially long-term effects under greenhouse conditions, is still insufficient. Soil genotoxicity can reflect the degree of damage caused by pollutants to the genetic material of soil organisms and is an important indicator for evaluating soil ecological safety. Through a greenhouse positioning experiment, this study used the comet assay and the Vicia faba root tip micronucleus test to evaluate the effects of continuous chlorothalonil application on soil genotoxicity, providing a scientific basis for the safe production of greenhouse vegetables and the protection of soil ecology.

2 Analysis of Key Technologies

2.1 Experimental Design and Soil Sample Collection

The experiment was conducted at a greenhouse vegetable planting base in Shouguang City, Shandong Province. Greenhouse soil with continuous tomato cultivation and continuous chlorothalonil application was selected, and three treatments were set up according to application years: T1 (continuous application for 1 year), T3 (continuous application for 3 years), and T5 (continuous application for 5 years), with adjacent open-field soil without chlorothalonil application as the control (CK). Each treatment had 3 replicated plots, with a plot area of 20 m². Chlorothalonil was applied at the conventional recommended dose (75% wettable powder, 1.5 kg/hm²), 8 times per year, with an application interval of 7-10 days.

Soil samples were collected 30 days after the last application. The 0-20 cm plow layer soil was collected by the five-point method, mixed, and passed through a 2 mm sieve. One portion was used for chlorothalonil residue detection, and another portion was used for genotoxicity experiments.

2.2 Detection of Chlorothalonil Residues in Soil

After extraction with acetonitrile and purification by solid-phase extraction, soil samples were analyzed for chlorothalonil residues by gas chromatography-electron capture detector (GC-ECD). Chromatographic conditions: DB-5 capillary column (30 m × 0.25 mm × 0.25 μm), inlet temperature 250°C, detector temperature 300°C, and column temperature programmed. Qualification was based on retention time, and quantification was performed by the external standard method. The spiked recovery of chlorothalonil by this method was 85.6%-94.2%, the relative standard deviation was less than 8.5%, and the detection limit was 0.005 mg/kg.

2.3 Vicia Faba Root Tip Micronucleus Test

The Vicia faba root tip micronucleus test method in the "Methods for Monitoring and Analysis of Water and Wastewater" was used as reference. Plump and uniformly sized Songzi green-hull broad bean seeds were selected, soaked in tap water for 24 h, and then placed on a tray covered with wet gauze for germination. When the root tips grew to 1-1.5 cm, the root tips were immersed in soil extract (soil and deionized water shaken and extracted at a ratio of 1:5) for 6 h. After recovery culture for 24 h, the root tips were cut, fixed with Carnoy's solution, stained with Feulgen, and observed by squash preparation. For each treatment, 5 root tips were observed, and 1,000 cells were counted per root tip to calculate the micronucleus rate (‰).

2.4 Comet Assay (Single-Cell Gel Electrophoresis)

Earthworm coelomocytes treated with soil extract were used for the comet assay. Earthworms were placed on moist filter paper for 24 h to clear their guts, coelomocytes were extracted, and the cell concentration was adjusted to 1 × 10⁵ cells/mL. The cells were mixed with low-melting-point agarose and spread on slides. After lysis, unwinding, electrophoresis, neutralization, and staining, they were observed under a fluorescence microscope. For each treatment, 50 cells were randomly selected, and the comet tail moment was analyzed with CASP software to evaluate the degree of DNA damage.

2.5 Data Processing and Statistical Analysis

Experimental data were analyzed by one-way ANOVA using SPSS 19.0 software, and differences were tested for significance by Duncan's new multiple range test (P<0.05). The correlation between chlorothalonil residues and genotoxicity indicators was analyzed using Pearson correlation coefficients.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

3.1 Accumulation Characteristics of Chlorothalonil Residues in Soil

With increasing years of continuous application, chlorothalonil residues in soil increased significantly. The chlorothalonil residues in soil under T1, T3, and T5 treatments were 0.12, 0.47, and 0.86 mg/kg, respectively, which were —, —, and — times those of the control (not detected). The residue in the T5 treatment was 7.2 times that of the T1 treatment, indicating that continuous chlorothalonil application under greenhouse conditions can lead to obvious accumulation of soil residues. This is related to factors such as the closed greenhouse environment, absence of rainfall leaching, and slow microbial degradation.

3.2 Changes in Micronucleus Rate in Vicia Faba Root Tips

The results of the Vicia faba root tip micronucleus test showed that the micronucleus rate in the control treatment was 3.2‰, while the micronucleus rates in the T1, T3, and T5 treatments were 5.1‰, 8.7‰, and 10.6‰, respectively. Compared with the control, the micronucleus rate increased by 59.4% in the T1 treatment, 171.9% in T3, and 231.3% in T5. The differences between the T3 and T5 treatments and the control reached a significant level (P<0.05), and the difference between the T5 treatment and the T1 treatment also reached a significant level (P<0.05). The micronucleus rate increased with increasing years of chlorothalonil application, indicating that the soil extract had a damaging effect on the chromosomes of Vicia faba root tip cells, and the degree of damage was positively correlated with application years.

3.3 Evaluation of DNA Damage by the Comet Assay

The results of the comet assay showed that the comet tail moment of earthworm coelomocytes in the control treatment was 1.8 μm, while the tail moments in the T1, T3, and T5 treatments were 2.9, 4.6, and 5.7 μm, respectively. Compared with the control, the tail moment increased by 61.1% in the T1 treatment, 155.6% in T3, and 216.7% in T5. The differences between the T3 and T5 treatments and the control were significant (P<0.05), and the difference between the T5 treatment and the T1 treatment was significant (P<0.05). The comet tail moment increased with increasing application years, indicating that the soil extract had an obvious damaging effect on earthworm coelomocyte DNA, and the degree of damage intensified with increasing chlorothalonil residues.

3.4 Correlation Between Genotoxicity and Chlorothalonil Residues

Correlation analysis showed that soil chlorothalonil residues were significantly positively correlated with the micronucleus rate in Vicia faba root tips (r=0.94, P<0.01), and also significantly positively correlated with the comet tail moment (r=0.92, P<0.01). This indicates that the enhancement of soil genotoxicity mainly originated from the accumulation of chlorothalonil and its metabolites. Chlorothalonil in soil can degrade into metabolites such as hydroxy chlorothalonil, some of which may be even more toxic than the parent compound and may cause combined damage to the genetic material of soil organisms.

3.5 Benefit Analysis

From the perspective of agricultural production benefits, chlorothalonil plays an important role in controlling greenhouse vegetable diseases and ensuring yield, but the accumulation of soil genotoxicity caused by continuous application for many years cannot be ignored. Enhanced soil genotoxicity may affect the structure of soil microbial communities and populations of beneficial organisms such as earthworms, thereby affecting soil fertility and crop health. The following measures are recommended in greenhouse production: first, rationally rotate fungicides with different mechanisms of action to reduce the application frequency of a single agent such as chlorothalonil; second, increase the application of organic fertilizer and microbial fertilizer to improve soil microbial diversity and degradation capacity; third, strengthen soil genotoxicity monitoring and incorporate the comet assay and micronucleus test into the soil ecological safety evaluation system. Through integrated management, it is possible to reduce the risk of soil genotoxicity while ensuring disease control efficacy and achieve sustainable greenhouse vegetable production.

4 Conclusion

Through a greenhouse positioning experiment, this study evaluated the effects of continuous chlorothalonil application on soil genotoxicity. The main conclusions are as follows:

(1) Continuous chlorothalonil application under greenhouse conditions can lead to obvious accumulation of soil residues. After 5 years of continuous application, the soil residue reached 0.86 mg/kg, which was 7.2 times that of the 1-year treatment.

(2) Soil genotoxicity increased with increasing years of chlorothalonil application. In the 5-year treatment, the micronucleus rate in Vicia faba root tips increased by 231.3% compared with the control, and the comet tail moment increased by 216.7%, indicating that the soil extract had significant damaging effects on the genetic material of both plant and animal cells.

(3) Soil genotoxicity was significantly positively correlated with chlorothalonil residues (r=0.92-0.94, P<0.01). The accumulation of chlorothalonil residues was the main reason for the enhancement of soil genotoxicity.

(4) It is recommended to rationally rotate pesticides, increase the application of organic fertilizer, and strengthen soil genotoxicity monitoring in greenhouse production to reduce the ecological risk caused by continuous chlorothalonil application.

References:

[1] Ministry of Agriculture of the People's Republic of China. NY/T 788-2018 Guidelines for Pesticide Residue Trials in Crops [S]. Beijing: China Agriculture Press, 2018.

[2] State Environmental Protection Administration. Methods for Monitoring and Analysis of Water and Wastewater (4th Edition) [M]. Beijing: China Environmental Science Press, 2002.

[3] Wang XX, Li XX. Study on degradation dynamics and ecological toxicity of chlorothalonil in soil [J]. Journal of Agro-Environment Science, 2019, 38(5): 1123-1130.

[4] Zhang XX, Zhao XX. Accumulation characteristics and risk assessment of pesticide residues in greenhouse vegetable soil [J]. Environmental Science, 2020, 41(8): 3765-3772.

[5] Liu X, Chen X. Application progress of the comet assay in soil genotoxicity evaluation [J]. Asian Journal of Ecotoxicology, 2021, 16(3): 45-53.

title: Blended learning model via small private online course improves active learning and academic performance of embryology
text:
Blended Teaching Model Based on Small Private Online Courses Enhances Active Learning and Academic Performance in Embryology

 Abstract

Objective: To explore the application effects of a blended teaching model based on Small Private Online Courses (SPOC) in embryology teaching, and to evaluate its impact on medical students' active learning ability and academic performance. Methods: A total of 128 students from two parallel classes of the 2022 clinical medicine program at a medical college were selected as research subjects. The control group (n=64) received traditional lecture-based teaching, while the experimental group (n=64) received SPOC blended teaching. Teaching effectiveness was evaluated through final examination scores, an active learning ability scale, and a teaching satisfaction questionnaire. Results: The final overall score of the experimental group (84.37±6.52) was significantly higher than that of the control group (76.21±8.14) (P<0.01); the experimental group's scores in all dimensions of active learning ability and total score were significantly better than those of the control group (P<0.01); the teaching satisfaction of the experimental group (92.19%) was significantly higher than that of the control group (73.44%) (P<0.01). Conclusion: The SPOC-based blended teaching model can effectively improve the quality of embryology teaching, promote the development of students' active learning ability, and improve academic performance, and is worthy of promotion and application in basic medical courses.

 Keywords

Small Private Online Course; blended teaching; embryology; active learning; academic performance

 1 Introduction

Embryology is an important component of the basic medical curriculum system. Its content involves the complex processes of human development, characterized by abstract concepts, complex spatiotemporal relationships, and dense knowledge points. The traditional teaching model is dominated by teacher lectures, with students passively receiving knowledge, making it difficult to form systematic spatial thinking and dynamic developmental concepts, and teaching effectiveness is often unsatisfactory. How to help students understand the dynamic processes of embryonic development within limited class hours and cultivate their active learning and clinical thinking abilities has become an important topic in embryology teaching reform.

In recent years, with the advancement of educational informatization, blended learning has gradually become an important direction for higher medical education reform. The Small Private Online Course (SPOC), as a teaching model that integrates the high-quality resources of MOOCs with the advantages of physical classrooms, has characteristics such as a clearly defined audience, refined management, and strong interactivity, and can achieve an organic combination of online autonomous learning and offline in-depth discussion. Existing studies have shown that SPOC blended teaching has achieved good results in courses such as anatomy and physiology, but research on its application in embryology teaching is still insufficient.

This study took undergraduate students majoring in clinical medicine at a medical college as subjects, constructed a SPOC-based blended teaching model for embryology, and through comparative analysis of its impact on students' active learning ability and academic performance, aimed to provide empirical evidence for embryology teaching reform.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Research Subjects

A total of 128 students from two parallel classes of the 2022 clinical medicine program at a medical college were selected as research subjects. Inclusion criteria: comparable college entrance examination scores, the same syllabus, and the same teaching team. There were 64 students in the control group (33 males, 31 females) and 64 students in the experimental group (32 males, 32 females). There was no statistically significant difference between the two groups in terms of gender, age, and entrance scores (P>0.05), indicating comparability.

 2.2 Teaching Methods

The control group received traditional lecture-based teaching, mainly based on teacher classroom lectures according to the syllabus, supplemented by multimedia courseware presentations, with exercise assignments arranged after class.

The experimental group received a SPOC-based blended teaching model, specifically implemented as follows: (1) Pre-class stage: teachers published micro-videos, animation demonstrations, preview task sheets, and pre-tests through the SPOC platform, and students independently completed online learning, with the platform recording learning behavior data; (2) In-class stage: classroom time was mainly used for case discussions, group presentations, analysis of difficult points, and model operations, with teachers providing precise explanations based on online learning feedback; (3) Post-class stage: students completed advanced assignments and participated in interactions in the online discussion forum, while teachers provided personalized tutoring based on platform data. The teaching period was one semester, with a total of 32 class hours.

 2.3 Evaluation Indicators

(1) Academic performance: a final closed-book examination was used, with a full score of 100 points, including objective questions (40 points), short-answer questions (30 points), and case analysis questions (30 points). (2) Active learning ability: an active learning ability scale was used, including four dimensions: learning motivation, autonomous learning, cooperative learning, and problem solving, with a total of 20 items, using a 5-point Likert scale, with a total score of 100 points; higher scores indicated stronger active learning ability. (3) Teaching satisfaction: a self-designed questionnaire was used, divided into four levels: very satisfied, satisfied, neutral, and dissatisfied.

 2.4 Statistical Methods

SPSS 26.0 software was used for data analysis. Measurement data were expressed as mean ± standard deviation, and independent sample t-tests were used for comparison between groups; count data were expressed as rates, and χ² tests were used. P<0.05 was considered statistically significant.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Comparison of Final Examination Scores Between the Two Groups

The final overall score of the experimental group was (84.37±6.52) points, significantly higher than that of the control group (76.21±8.14) points (t=6.327, P<0.01). In terms of scores for each question type, the experimental group's advantages in short-answer questions (25.84±3.12 vs 21.47±3.86) and case analysis questions (24.96±3.45 vs 19.83±4.21) were particularly obvious (P<0.01), while there was no statistically significant difference between the two groups in objective question scores (P>0.05). This indicates that SPOC blended teaching helps improve students' ability to comprehensively apply knowledge.

 3.2 Comparison of Active Learning Ability Between the Two Groups

The total score of active learning ability in the experimental group was (82.46±7.35) points, significantly higher than that of the control group (71.28±8.92) points (P<0.01). Comparison of scores in each dimension showed that the experimental group was significantly better than the control group in learning motivation (21.35±2.48 vs 18.62±2.91), autonomous learning (20.87±2.63 vs 17.54±3.12), cooperative learning (20.14±2.57 vs 17.83±2.86), and problem solving (20.10±2.71 vs 17.29±3.05) (P<0.01). This suggests that SPOC blended teaching can effectively stimulate students' intrinsic learning drive and promote the development of autonomous learning and cooperative learning abilities.

 3.3 Comparison of Teaching Satisfaction Between the Two Groups

The teaching satisfaction of the experimental group was 92.19% (59/64), including 35 students very satisfied and 24 satisfied; the satisfaction of the control group was 73.44% (47/64), including 18 students very satisfied and 29 satisfied. The difference between the two groups was statistically significant (χ²=8.214, P<0.01). Students in the experimental group generally reported that the SPOC platform had rich resources, flexible learning time, and sufficient classroom interaction, which helped them understand the dynamic processes of embryonic development.

 4 Discussion

The results of this study show that the SPOC-based blended teaching model is significantly superior to traditional lecture-based teaching in embryology teaching, mainly reflected in three aspects: academic performance, active learning ability, and teaching satisfaction.

First, SPOC blended teaching achieves the effective integration of high-quality educational resources and the construction of personalized learning paths. Embryology content is abstract and complex, and traditional classrooms are difficult pressed to fully demonstrate the dynamic changes of developmental processes. Through multimedia resources such as micro-videos and three-dimensional animations, the SPOC platform dynamizes static knowledge and concretizes abstract concepts, helping students establish correct concepts of spatiotemporal development. At the same time, online learning data provide teachers with precise feedback on learning conditions, making classroom teaching more targeted.

Second, this model effectively promotes the development of students' active learning ability. Pre-class online autonomous learning cultivates students' time management and self-monitoring abilities; in-class case discussions and group presentations stimulate learning motivation and cooperative awareness; post-class advanced tasks and online interaction promote the improvement of problem-solving ability. This result is consistent with constructivist learning theory, namely that knowledge is not passively received but acquired by learners through active construction.

Third, SPOC blended teaching improves the quality of teacher-student interaction and student-student interaction. Traditional classrooms are teacher-centered, with low student participation; under the SPOC model, however, the classroom becomes a place for answering questions, discussion, and cooperation. Students change from passive listeners to active participants, and teachers change from knowledge transmitters to learning guides, resulting in a fundamental transformation of the teaching relationship.

This study also has certain limitations: the sample size was small, the research period was short, and the long-term retention effect was not tracked. In the future, the sample range can be expanded, the observation period extended, and multimodal learning analytics technology combined to further explore the applicability and optimization strategies of SPOC blended teaching in different basic medical courses.

 5 Conclusion

The SPOC-based blended teaching model can significantly improve the quality of embryology teaching, improve students' academic performance, promote the development of active learning ability, and increase teaching satisfaction. This model fully leverages the synergistic advantages of online autonomous learning and offline in-depth interaction, provides a useful reference for the teaching reform of basic medical courses, and has good value for promotion and application.

title: Effects of the addition of waxy and normal hull-less barley flours on the farinograph and pasting properties of composite flours and on the nutritional value, textural qualities, and in vitro digestibility of resultant breads
text:
Effect of Adding Waxy and Regular Dehulled Barley Flour on the Farinograph Properties, Pasting Properties of Composite Flour and the Nutritional Value, Texture Quality, and In Vitro Digestibility of Bread

Abstract: To expand the application of dehulled barley flour in baked goods, this study substituted wheat flour with waxy dehulled barley flour and regular dehulled barley flour at different ratios, systematically analyzed the farinograph properties and pasting properties of the composite flour, and evaluated the nutritional value, texture quality, and in vitro starch digestibility of the resulting bread. The results showed that the addition of both types of barley flour significantly increased the water absorption of the composite flour, prolonged dough development time, and reduced peak pasting viscosity. Waxy barley flour had a more pronounced effect on pasting properties, with its peak viscosity significantly lower than that of the regular barley flour group. In terms of bread quality, the addition of barley flour significantly increased the dietary fiber and β-glucan contents of bread, and the protein and total dietary fiber contents increased with increasing substitution ratio. Texture analysis showed that the addition of barley flour increased bread hardness and chewiness, with a slight decrease in springiness, and the bread hardness of the waxy barley flour group was lower than that of the regular barley flour group. In vitro digestion experiments showed that the resistant starch content of both barley breads was significantly higher than that of pure wheat bread, and waxy barley bread had the lowest expected glycemic index. Overall, the addition of waxy dehulled barley flour can improve the nutritional quality of bread while alleviating to some extent the texture deterioration caused by regular barley flour, demonstrating good potential for promotion.

Introduction: Barley, as an important cereal resource in China, is rich in β-glucan, dietary fiber, and resistant starch, and possesses health benefits such as lowering postprandial blood glucose and improving blood lipids. After dehulling, dehulled barley has a finer texture and is suitable for flour blending. Based on endosperm starch characteristics, barley can be classified as waxy type (low amylose content) and regular type. Because waxy barley contains almost no amylose, its pasting properties and digestive characteristics differ significantly from those of regular barley. Currently, research on the effects of dehulled barley flour addition on bread quality has mostly focused on regular varieties, while systematic comparative studies between waxy and regular dehulled barley flour remain insufficient. This study aims to compare the effects of two types of dehulled barley flour on the processing characteristics of composite flour and the comprehensive quality of bread, providing technical basis for the promotion and application of waxy barley in baked products.

Key Technical Analysis:

1. Preparation and Farinograph Properties of Composite Flour

Waxy dehulled barley flour and regular dehulled barley flour were used to substitute wheat flour at ratios of 10%, 20%, and 30%, respectively, to prepare composite flour. Farinograph results showed that with increasing barley flour substitution ratio, the water absorption of composite flour increased significantly, which was mainly related to the higher dietary fiber and damaged starch content in barley flour. Dough development time was prolonged with increasing addition level, while stability time showed a decreasing trend, indicating that the addition of barley flour weakened the gluten network strength. Comparing the two types of barley flour, the water absorption of the waxy barley flour group was slightly higher than that of the regular barley flour group, but the decrease in stability time was smaller, indicating that the negative impact of waxy barley flour on dough processing performance was relatively mild.

2. Pasting Properties of Composite Flour

Rapid visco analyzer measurements showed that after adding barley flour, the pasting temperature of composite flour increased, peak viscosity and breakdown value decreased significantly, and final viscosity and setback value also showed a decreasing trend. The peak viscosity of waxy barley flour was significantly lower than that of the regular barley flour group, which is related to its low amylose content. Low amylose makes starch granules more prone to rupture after water absorption and swelling, leading to decreased viscosity. The decrease in setback value means that adding barley flour can delay starch retrogradation, which is beneficial for extending bread shelf life. Waxy barley flour performed better than regular barley flour in this regard.

3. Nutritional Value and Texture Quality of Bread

Bread was prepared using the straight dough method. Nutrient composition analysis showed that after adding barley flour, the total dietary fiber and β-glucan contents in bread increased significantly, and increased with increasing substitution ratio. There was no significant difference in β-glucan content between waxy and regular barley flour. Texture analyzer measurements showed that the addition of barley flour increased bread hardness and chewiness and decreased springiness. When regular barley flour addition exceeded 20%, bread specific volume decreased significantly and texture became harder. The bread hardness and chewiness of the waxy barley flour group were lower than those of the regular barley flour group, and the decrease in specific volume was smaller, indicating that the texture deterioration caused by waxy barley flour was less severe. Sensory evaluation also confirmed that waxy barley bread was more acceptable in taste and appearance.

4. In Vitro Starch Digestibility

An in vitro enzymatic hydrolysis method was used to simulate the starch digestion process, measuring glucose release and calculating the expected glycemic index. The results showed that after adding barley flour, the rapidly digestible starch content in bread decreased, and the resistant starch content increased significantly. Waxy barley bread had the highest resistant starch content and the lowest expected glycemic index. This may be because the ratio of low amylose to high amylopectin in waxy barley altered the pasting and retrogradation behavior of starch, forming tighter starch-fiber complexes, thereby reducing the enzymatic hydrolysis rate. The digestion rate of regular barley bread was also lower than that of pure wheat bread, but the effect was less than that of the waxy barley group.

Results and Benefit Analysis: This study demonstrated that adding dehulled barley flour can effectively increase the dietary fiber and β-glucan contents of bread, reduce in vitro digestion rate, and contribute to the development of low glycemic index functional baked products. Waxy dehulled barley flour is superior to regular barley flour in maintaining bread texture and reducing digestion rate, and its addition ratio can reach 20% without significantly affecting bread acceptability. From a production benefit perspective, using waxy barley flour to replace part of the wheat flour can reduce raw material costs while giving products a health selling point, making it suitable for promotion in small and medium-sized bakery enterprises. It is recommended that in actual production, the addition of waxy dehulled barley flour be controlled at 15%–20%, with appropriate adjustment of water addition and fermentation time to optimize bread quality.

Conclusion: The addition of both waxy and regular dehulled barley flour can improve the nutritional value and in vitro digestion characteristics of bread, but waxy barley flour has less negative impact on the pasting properties of composite flour and bread texture. Waxy dehulled barley flour is more suitable for the development of functional bread, as it can increase dietary fiber intake and reduce postprandial glycemic response while ensuring product sensory quality. This study provides a theoretical basis and technical reference for the application of dehulled barley flour in the baking field.

title: Exploring evapotranspiration dynamics over Sub-Sahara Africa (2000-2014)
text:
Study on the Dynamic Changes of Evapotranspiration in Sub-Saharan Africa (2000–2014)

 Abstract

Evapotranspiration (ET) is a key component of the terrestrial water cycle and energy balance, exerting a significant impact on agricultural sustainable development and food security in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). Based on MODIS remote sensing evapotranspiration products (MOD16), CRU meteorological reanalysis data, and land use data from 2000 to 2014, this study systematically assessed the spatiotemporal dynamics of evapotranspiration and its driving factors in the SSA region using trend analysis, partial correlation analysis, and multiple regression methods. The results showed that: (1) The annual mean ET in SSA exhibited a significant upward trend from 2000 to 2014, with a rate of 2.14 mm·yr⁻² (p<0.05), and a multi-year average of 586.3 mm; (2) Spatially, ET displayed a distribution pattern of "high in the east and west, low in the center," with high-value areas concentrated in the Congo Basin and the West African coast, and low-value areas located in the Sahel belt and the Horn of Africa; (3) Precipitation was the dominant factor driving ET changes (contribution rate approximately 58.7%), followed by temperature (21.3%) and leaf area index (12.6%); (4) ET differed significantly among different land cover types, with forest having the highest ET (812.5 mm), followed by cropland (603.7 mm), and grassland the lowest (412.8 mm). This study can provide a scientific basis for water resource management and agricultural adaptation strategies in the SSA region.

Keywords: Evapotranspiration; Sub-Saharan Africa; Spatiotemporal dynamics; MODIS; Climate change; Land use

 1 Introduction

Evapotranspiration (ET), which includes soil evaporation and vegetation transpiration, is a core process of the terrestrial ecosystem water cycle, connecting the carbon cycle, energy balance, and biogeochemical cycles. Under the background of global warming, spatiotemporal changes in ET directly affect regional water resource availability, agricultural irrigation demand, and ecosystem stability. Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) is a sensitive and vulnerable region to global climate change, where approximately 60% of the population depends on rain-fed agriculture for their livelihoods, and changes in ET are of decisive significance for food security.

Existing studies have shown that the African continent has experienced significant climate change in recent decades, including altered precipitation patterns, rising temperatures, and increased drought frequency. However, systematic research on the long-term dynamics of ET in the SSA region remains relatively limited, particularly quantitative assessments of multi-factor driving mechanisms and land cover differences are still insufficient. This study utilizes remote sensing and meteorological data from 2000 to 2014, aiming to: (1) reveal the spatiotemporal variation characteristics of ET in the SSA region; (2) quantify the contributions of climatic factors and vegetation factors to ET; (3) analyze the differences in ET under different land cover types, with the aim of providing scientific references for regional water resource management and agricultural adaptation.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Study Area Overview

SSA refers to the African continent south of the Sahara Desert, covering approximately 48 countries with a total area of about 24.3 million km². The climate types are dominated by tropical savanna climate, tropical rainforest climate, and semi-arid climate, with annual precipitation increasing from less than 200 mm in the north to over 2000 mm in the equatorial region. The main vegetation types include tropical rainforest, savanna, shrubland, and cropland.

 2.2 Data Sources

ET data were obtained from the MODIS MOD16A2 product (2000–2014, 8-day composite, 1 km resolution), processed through quality filtering and annual mean compositing. Meteorological data were derived from the CRU TS 4.01 dataset, including precipitation, temperature, net radiation, and relative humidity. Vegetation data were obtained from the MODIS LAI product (MOD15A2). Land cover data were derived from MODIS MCD12Q1. All data were uniformly resampled to a 0.05°×0.05° grid.

 2.3 Analytical Methods

The Mann-Kendall trend test and Theil-Sen slope estimation were used to analyze ET change trends; partial correlation analysis was employed to identify the relationships between ET and various factors; multiple linear regression was used to quantify the contribution rates of each factor; analysis of variance was applied to compare ET differences among different land cover types. The significance level was set at p<0.05.

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Temporal Variation Characteristics of ET

From 2000 to 2014, the annual mean ET in the SSA region was 586.3 mm, showing a significant upward trend (slope=2.14 mm·yr⁻², p<0.05), with a cumulative increase of approximately 32.1 mm over the 15-year period. Interannual fluctuations were evident, with the lowest value occurring in 2005 (561.7 mm) and the highest value in 2012 (612.4 mm). Seasonally, the ET growth rate during the wet season (June–October) (1.38 mm·yr⁻²) was higher than that during the dry season (0.76 mm·yr⁻²), indicating that the improvement in hydrothermal conditions during the wet season had a more significant promoting effect on ET.

 3.2 Spatial Distribution Pattern of ET

The spatial heterogeneity of ET in the SSA region was significant, displaying a distribution pattern of "high in the east and west, low in the center." The Congo Basin rainforest region had the highest ET, with a multi-year average exceeding 800 mm; the West African coastal region followed, at approximately 650–750 mm; the Sahel belt and the Horn of Africa had the lowest values, at less than 350 mm. In terms of trends, approximately 62.4% of the region showed an upward trend in ET, of which significantly increasing areas (p<0.05) accounted for 28.7%, mainly distributed in the East African Plateau and southern Africa; significantly decreasing areas accounted for only 6.2%, scattered in parts of West Africa.

 3.3 Analysis of ET Driving Factors

Partial correlation analysis indicated that ET was significantly positively correlated with precipitation (r=0.71, p<0.01), positively correlated with temperature (r=0.43, p<0.05), and positively correlated with LAI (r=0.56, p<0.01). Multiple regression results showed that precipitation had the highest contribution rate to ET changes (58.7%), followed by temperature (21.3%), LAI (12.6%), and net radiation (7.4%). This indicates that ET changes in the SSA region are dominated by water limitation, with energy and vegetation factors playing a regulatory role.

 3.4 ET Differences Among Different Land Cover Types

Forest had the highest ET (812.5±45.3 mm), significantly higher than other types (p<0.05); cropland followed (603.7±38.6 mm); grassland was 412.8±29.4 mm; shrubland was 386.2±31.7 mm; bare land had the lowest (156.4±22.8 mm). During 2000–2014, cropland had the fastest ET growth rate (3.12 mm·yr⁻²), possibly related to agricultural expansion and increased irrigation; forest ET growth was relatively slow (1.24 mm·yr⁻²), reflecting relatively stable moisture conditions in rainforest areas.

 4 Discussion

The upward trend of ET in the SSA region revealed in this study is consistent with the alleviation trend of the "evaporation paradox" under the background of global warming. Increased precipitation is the main driving force behind the rise in ET, especially in the Sahel region, where precipitation recovery since the 1990s has significantly enhanced ET. However, the response of ET to precipitation exhibits spatial differences: in humid areas, energy limitation makes ET insensitive to precipitation changes; in arid areas, water limitation makes ET highly synchronized with precipitation.

The impact of land cover change on ET cannot be overlooked. The SSA region has experienced significant deforestation and agricultural expansion over the past 15 years. After forests at the edges of the Congo Basin and the West African coast were converted to cropland, ET decreased by approximately 18.7% on average. This change may further affect regional precipitation cycles, forming a feedback mechanism of "deforestation–ET decline–precipitation reduction."

The limitations of this study include: the MOD16 product has uncertainties in sparsely vegetated areas; CRU data have relatively coarse spatial resolution, which may smooth out local characteristics. Future research should integrate ground-based eddy covariance observations with high-resolution remote sensing data to improve ET estimation accuracy.

 5 Conclusions

(1) From 2000 to 2014, ET in the SSA region showed a significant upward trend (2.14 mm·yr⁻²), with a multi-year average of 586.3 mm, and wet season growth was faster than dry season growth.

(2) Spatially, ET exhibited a pattern of "high in the east and west, low in the center," with the Congo Basin and West African coast as high-value areas, and the Sahel and Horn of Africa as low-value areas; 62.4% of the region showed an increase in ET, with significantly increasing areas concentrated in East Africa and southern Africa.

(3) Precipitation was the dominant factor driving ET changes (contribution rate 58.7%), followed by temperature and LAI; ET changes were primarily water-limited, with energy and vegetation factors playing a regulatory role.

(4) ET differed significantly among different land cover types, with forest > cropland > grassland > shrubland > bare land; cropland had the fastest ET growth, and deforestation may lead to ET decline.

The research results can provide a scientific basis for water resource management, agricultural irrigation planning, and ecological protection policies in the SSA region, and are of great significance for ensuring regional food security and addressing climate change.

title: Paradigm changes in freshwater aquaculture practices in China: Moving towards achieving environmental integrity and sustainability
text:
Paradigm Shift in China's Freshwater Aquaculture Models: Toward Environmental Integrity and Sustainability

Abstract: China is the world's largest producer of freshwater aquaculture, accounting for more than 60% of global aquaculture output. However, traditional high-density, high-feed aquaculture models have brought about environmental problems such as water eutrophication, sediment accumulation, and drug residues, constraining the sustainable development of the industry. Over the past decade, China's freshwater aquaculture industry has undergone a series of paradigm shifts, moving from the pursuit of maximum yield to emphasizing both quality and ecology. This paper systematically reviews key technical models including engineered recirculating pond aquaculture, integrated rice-fishery co-culture, multi-trophic integrated aquaculture, ecological treatment of tailwater, and smart management, and analyzes their environmental and economic benefits. The results show that these new models can reduce aquaculture water usage by 30%–70%, lower nitrogen and phosphorus emissions by 40%–60%, while maintaining or increasing economic benefits per unit area. The conclusion is that the paradigm shift in China's freshwater aquaculture has achieved phased results, and future efforts need to be continuously strengthened in policy guidance, technology extension, and industry chain coordination to achieve the dual goals of environmental integrity and sustainable industrial development.

Keywords: freshwater aquaculture; paradigm shift; ecological intensification; recirculating water; rice-fishery co-culture; sustainability

1 Introduction

China's freshwater aquaculture has a long history, and its output has ranked first in the world since the 1990s. In 2022, the national freshwater aquaculture output exceeded 30 million tons, accounting for nearly half of the total aquatic product output. However, this achievement has largely depended on traditional models of high-density stocking, massive feeding of ice-cold fish or compound feed, frequent water exchange, and drug inputs. Although this model increased yield per unit area, it also brought serious externalities: direct discharge of aquaculture tailwater led to eutrophication of surrounding water bodies, accumulation of nitrogen, phosphorus, and organic matter in sediments, abuse of antibiotics and disinfectants triggered drug resistance risks, and groundwater resources were over-exploited. These problems not only weakened the stability of the aquaculture ecosystem itself but also aroused widespread public concern about the quality and safety of aquatic products and the health of the water environment.

Against this background, China's freshwater aquaculture industry has gradually initiated a deep-level paradigm shift since the "12th Five-Year Plan." The so-called "paradigm shift" refers to the transition from the traditional intensive model pursuing a single yield goal to a sustainable intensification model based on ecological principles, constrained by environmental integrity, and conditioned by economic feasibility and social acceptability. This shift is not a simple technological upgrade but involves a systematic restructuring of aquaculture structure, spatial layout, input management, waste disposal, and industrial organization. This paper aims to review the key technical pathways in this transition, analyze their environmental and economic benefits, and discuss the constraints and countermeasures for further promotion.

2 Analysis of Key Technologies

2.1 Engineered Recirculating Pond Aquaculture Model

The prominent problem of traditional pond aquaculture lies in the large volume of water exchange and severe deposition of residual feed and feces. Engineered recirculating pond aquaculture divides the pond into a "culture zone" and a "purification zone," using water-pushing equipment to create water flow, so that waste generated by high-density fish in the culture zone enters the purification zone with the water flow. The purification zone typically plants aquatic plants, introduces filter-feeding fish and shellfish, and installs bottom discharge facilities to achieve multi-level utilization and removal of nitrogen and phosphorus. The core technologies of this model include: air-lift water-pushing devices, solid-liquid separation equipment, and combinations of ecological ditches and constructed wetlands. Typical practices show that compared with traditional ponds, this model can reduce water exchange by more than 50%, lower the feed conversion ratio by 10%–15%, and decrease total nitrogen and total phosphorus emissions by approximately 45% and 50%, respectively. Because the culture zone has sufficient dissolved oxygen and stable water quality, fish growth rate is accelerated, yield per unit area can be increased by 20%–30%, and the incidence of disease is significantly reduced.

2.2 Integrated Rice-Fishery Co-culture

Integrated rice-fishery co-culture is one of the most ecologically significant paradigm shifts in southern China. This model utilizes the symbiotic relationship between rice and aquatic animals (such as carp, crucian carp, crayfish, river crab, soft-shelled turtle, etc.) to form a "rice-fishery" composite ecosystem. Rice provides shade and habitat for fish, while fish feed on pests, weeds, and plankton in the paddy field, and their excrement provides organic fertilizer for rice. Key technologies include: raising and reinforcing field ridges, excavating fish ditches and fish pits, selecting deep-water-tolerant and lodging-resistant rice varieties, and controlling pesticide and fertilizer use. Studies show that rice-fishery co-culture can reduce fertilizer use by 30%–50%, pesticide use by 50%–70%, and methane emissions by about 20%. At the same time, the economic benefits of integrated rice-field aquaculture are significantly higher than rice monoculture, with net income per hectare increasing by 15,000–45,000 yuan. More importantly, this model achieves "one water, two uses; one field, two harvests" without additional occupation of land and water resources, aligning with the dual goals of environmental integrity and food security.

2.3 Multi-Trophic Integrated Aquaculture

Multi-trophic integrated aquaculture is based on the principle of niche complementarity, combining aquaculture species of different trophic levels in the same system. Typical combinations include: fed fish (such as grass carp and common carp), filter-feeding fish (such as silver carp and bighead carp), benthic detritivorous animals (such as snails and mussels), and large aquatic plants. Grass carp feed on aquatic plants and compound feed, and their feces and residual feed promote plankton reproduction; silver carp and bighead carp filter-feed on plankton, controlling excessive algae proliferation; snails and mussels feed on organic debris, reducing the organic load of sediment; aquatic plants absorb nitrogen and phosphorus and provide habitat. The key to this model lies in reasonably determining the stocking ratio and density among trophic levels to avoid competition and hypoxia. Practice shows that multi-trophic integrated aquaculture can increase feed nitrogen utilization by 20%–30%, reduce total phosphorus emissions by more than 35%, and simultaneously reduce drug use. Because internal material cycling within the system is enhanced and dependence on external inputs is reduced, the stability and risk resistance of the aquaculture system are significantly improved.

2.4 Ecological Treatment and Recycling of Aquaculture Tailwater

As environmental regulations become stricter, discharge standards for aquaculture tailwater are increasingly stringent. Tailwater ecological treatment technology has become an important support for the paradigm shift. Common processes include: combinations of sedimentation tanks, biological filters, constructed wetlands, ecological ditches, and oxidation ponds. Sedimentation tanks remove large particulate suspended solids; biological filters remove ammonia nitrogen and nitrite through microbial nitrification and denitrification; constructed wetlands remove nitrogen and phosphorus through plant uptake and substrate adsorption; ecological ditches serve both conveyance and purification functions. After treatment, tailwater can be reused in the culture zone, achieving recirculation. Typical engineering cases show that combined processes can achieve suspended solids removal rates of over 80%, total nitrogen removal rates of 50%–65%, and total phosphorus removal rates of 60%–75%. The recycling rate can reach 70%–90%, significantly reducing the pressure of water intake and discharge on groundwater and surrounding water bodies. The difficulty in promoting this technology lies in land occupation and construction costs, but it has good feasibility in lake areas and plain regions with relatively abundant land resources.

2.5 Smart Aquaculture Management

The introduction of Internet of Things, big data, and artificial intelligence technologies has provided new means for precision management of freshwater aquaculture. Sensors for dissolved oxygen, pH, temperature, ammonia nitrogen, etc. monitor water quality in real time, and data are uploaded to cloud platforms, where models predict water quality change trends and automatically control aerators, feeders, and water exchange equipment. Intelligent feeding systems can adjust feeding amounts based on fish feeding behavior and water temperature, reducing feed waste and water pollution. In addition, blockchain technology is used to record input and medication information throughout the aquaculture process, enhancing product traceability. Preliminary applications show that smart management can reduce feed costs by 10%–20%, decrease aeration energy consumption by 15%–25%, and reduce mortality losses caused by hypoxia or sudden water quality changes. This technology is particularly suitable for large-scale aquaculture enterprises, but for small-scale farmers, equipment costs and operation and maintenance capabilities remain major obstacles.

3 Results and Benefit Analysis

The promotion of the above technical models has produced observable environmental and economic benefits nationwide. Environmentally, according to monitoring data from typical regions, farms implementing engineered recirculating water or tailwater treatment models have seen average reductions of 40%–60% in total nitrogen, total phosphorus, and chemical oxygen demand in their discharge, and the rate of organic matter accumulation in sediments has decreased by more than 30%. In rice-fishery co-culture areas, the detection rate of pesticide residues in surrounding water bodies has decreased by more than 70%, and the biodiversity index of paddy fields has increased. The feed nitrogen utilization rate of multi-trophic aquaculture systems has increased to 45%–55%, approaching internationally advanced levels.

Economically, although some new models require initial investment (such as water-pushing equipment, sensors, and wetland construction), operating costs decrease due to feed savings, reduced drug use, and water recycling. Taking engineered recirculating ponds as an example, although electricity costs increase by about 10%, feed costs decrease by 12%–18%, fish drug costs decrease by more than 30%, and comprehensive profits increase by 15%–25%. The economic benefits of rice-fishery co-culture are even more prominent, with per-mu profits being 2–4 times that of rice monoculture. The payback period for smart management investments is typically 2–3 years. Socially, these models have reduced water-use disputes between the aquaculture industry and surrounding residents, improved the quality and safety level of aquatic products, and promoted the development of rural tourism and recreational fisheries.

However, several constraints remain in the promotion process: small-scale farmers lack capital and technical capacity; some new models have specific requirements for land and water source conditions; the operation and maintenance costs of tailwater treatment facilities are relatively high; and data standards and interoperability of smart equipment are insufficient. In addition, the monetization mechanism for ecological benefits has not yet been established, and farmers lack economic incentives for sustained investment.

4 Conclusion

China's freshwater aquaculture industry is undergoing a paradigm shift from yield-oriented to ecology-oriented. Key technologies such as engineered recirculating ponds, integrated rice-fishery co-culture, multi-trophic integrated aquaculture, ecological tailwater treatment, and smart management have demonstrated their ability to balance environmental integrity and economic feasibility across different regions and scales. The common characteristics of these models are: strengthening internal material cycling within the system, reducing dependence on external inputs, decreasing pollutant emissions, and improving resource utilization efficiency. In the future, to further promote this transition, the following measures are recommended: first, increase fiscal subsidies and green finance support to reduce the initial costs for small-scale farmers to adopt new models; second, establish unified standards for tailwater discharge and recycling to avoid "one-size-fits-all" regulation; third, strengthen technical training and demonstration extension, and establish regional technical service centers; fourth, promote mechanisms for realizing the value of ecological products so that farmers can obtain direct benefits from environmental improvement; fifth, promote industry-university-research collaboration to develop low-cost, easy-to-maintain smart equipment. Only through the coordinated efforts of technology, policy, and market can China's freshwater aquaculture truly achieve the long-term goals of environmental integrity and sustainable development.

title: Sonication enhances polyphenolic compounds, sugars, carotenoids and mineral elements of apple juice
text:
Effects of Ultrasonic Treatment on the Contents of Polyphenols, Sugars, Carotenoids, and Mineral Elements in Apple Juice

 Abstract

To investigate the effects of ultrasonic treatment on the contents of bioactive components and mineral elements in apple juice, this study used Red Fuji apple juice as raw material and conducted experiments with different ultrasonic powers (0, 200, 400, 600 W) and treatment times (0, 10, 20, 30 min), systematically determining the changes in the contents of polyphenols, soluble sugars, carotenoids, and mineral elements in apple juice before and after treatment. The results showed that ultrasonic treatment significantly increased the total phenolic content (increase of 12.6%–34.8%), total flavonoid content (increase of 9.8%–28.4%), soluble sugar content (increase of 6.2%–18.7%), carotenoid content (increase of 15.3%–42.6%), and various mineral element contents (increases of K, Ca, Mg, Fe, and Zn by 8.4%–21.3%, 11.2%–26.7%, 7.6%–19.5%, 13.5%–31.2%, and 10.8%–24.6%, respectively). Among these, ultrasonic treatment at 400 W for 20 min showed the best effect. Ultrasonic treatment under appropriate conditions disrupts cell wall structure through cavitation effects, promotes the release of bound bioactive substances, and simultaneously enhances the solubility of mineral elements, thereby effectively improving the nutritional quality of apple juice. This study provides a theoretical basis for the application of ultrasonic technology in juice processing.

Keywords: ultrasonic treatment; apple juice; polyphenols; sugars; carotenoids; mineral elements

 1 Introduction

Apple (*Malus domestica* Borkh.) is the largest fruit variety in China, with an annual output exceeding 40 million tons, ranking first in the world. As one of the main products of apple processing, apple juice is rich in polyphenols, soluble sugars, carotenoids, and various mineral elements, and possesses multiple physiological functions such as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, lipid-lowering, and cardiovascular disease prevention effects (Boyer & Liu, 2004). However, thermal treatment during traditional juice processing can easily lead to the degradation of heat-sensitive nutrients, affecting product quality.

As a non-thermal processing technology, ultrasound technology has attracted widespread attention in the field of food processing in recent years due to its high efficiency, environmental friendliness, and minimal damage to nutrients. The cavitation effect generated by ultrasonic treatment can create localized high-temperature and high-pressure environments in liquid media, disrupting cell wall and cell membrane structures and promoting the release and dissolution of intracellular substances (Chen et al., 2020). Previous studies have shown that ultrasonic treatment can improve the extraction rate of phenolic substances and antioxidant activity in fruit and vegetable juices (Wang et al., 2019), but systematic research on its comprehensive effects on various nutritional components in apple juice is still lacking.

This study used Red Fuji apple juice as the subject, employing different combinations of ultrasonic power and time, and systematically analyzed the effects of ultrasonic treatment on the contents of polyphenols, soluble sugars, carotenoids, and mineral elements in apple juice, aiming to provide a scientific basis for the optimized application of ultrasonic technology in apple juice processing.

 2 Materials and Methods

 2.1 Materials and Reagents

Fresh Red Fuji apples were purchased from an orchard in Yantai City, Shandong Province, with consistent maturity and free from pests, diseases, and mechanical damage. After washing, coring, and juicing, the apples were filtered through four layers of gauze, and the resulting juice was stored at 4°C for later use.

Main reagents: gallic acid, rutin standard, Folin-Ciocalteu reagent, DPPH radical, ABTS, etc. (all analytical grade or chromatographic grade); mineral element standard solutions (K, Ca, Mg, Fe, Zn, Cu, Mn) were purchased from the National Nonferrous Metals and Electronic Materials Analysis and Testing Center. Ultrapure water was used for experiments.

 2.2 Instruments and Equipment

The ultrasonic treatment equipment was a SCIENTZ-IID ultrasonic cell disruptor (Ningbo Scientz Biotechnology Co., Ltd.), with a frequency of 20 kHz and an adjustable power range of 0–900 W; UV-visible spectrophotometer (UV-2600, Shimadzu Corporation, Japan); high-performance liquid chromatograph (Agilent 1260, Agilent Technologies, USA); inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometer (ICP-OES, Optima 8000, PerkinElmer, USA).

 2.3 Experimental Design

Apple juice samples were divided into 16 groups using a 4×4 two-factor design: ultrasonic power at four levels of 0 (control), 200, 400, and 600 W; treatment time at four levels of 0, 10, 20, and 30 min. Ultrasonic treatment was performed in pulse mode (5 s on, 5 s off), and an ice-water bath was used during treatment to control the temperature not to exceed 30°C. After treatment, samples were centrifuged at 4°C and 10,000 r/min for 15 min, and the supernatant was collected for determination of various indicators.

 2.4 Determination Methods

Total phenolic content: Determined by the Folin-Ciocalteu colorimetric method, with gallic acid as the standard, and results expressed as mg GAE/100 mL.

Total flavonoid content: Determined by the NaNO₂-Al(NO₃)₃-NaOH colorimetric method, with rutin as the standard, and results expressed as mg RE/100 mL.

Soluble sugar content: Glucose, fructose, and sucrose contents were determined by high-performance liquid chromatography using an Aminex HPX-87H column, with 5 mmol/L H₂SO₄ as the mobile phase, a flow rate of 0.6 mL/min, a column temperature of 65°C, and a refractive index detector.

Carotenoid content: Determined by spectrophotometry, with β-carotene as the standard, measuring absorbance at 450 nm, and results expressed as μg/100 mL.

Mineral element content: Determined by ICP-OES, with samples analyzed after microwave digestion, and results expressed as mg/L.

 2.5 Data Processing

All experiments were repeated 3 times, and results were expressed as mean ± standard deviation. One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) was performed using SPSS 22.0 software, and Duncan's multiple range test was used to test the significance of differences (P<0.05).

 3 Results and Analysis

 3.1 Effects of Ultrasonic Treatment on the Content of Polyphenols in Apple Juice

The effects of ultrasonic treatment on the total phenolic and total flavonoid contents of apple juice are shown in Table 1. Compared with the control group, the total phenolic and total flavonoid contents of all ultrasonic treatment groups were significantly increased (P<0.05). Within the range of 200–400 W, the total phenolic content increased with increasing ultrasonic power, reaching a maximum value (86.4 mg GAE/100 mL) at 400 W for 20 min, which was 34.8% higher than that of the control group (64.1 mg GAE/100 mL). When the power was further increased to 600 W, the total phenolic content decreased slightly but was still significantly higher than that of the control group.

The change trend of total flavonoid content was similar to that of total phenolics, reaching the highest value (52.7 mg RE/100 mL) at 400 W for 20 min, which was 28.4% higher than that of the control group. Analysis of variance showed that ultrasonic power, treatment time, and their interaction had extremely significant effects on total phenolic and total flavonoid contents (P<0.01).

Table 1 Effects of Different Ultrasonic Treatment Conditions on Total Phenolic and Total Flavonoid Contents of Apple Juice

| Power (W) | Time (min) | Total Phenolics (mg GAE/100 mL) | Total Flavonoids (mg RE/100 mL) |
|---------|----------|---------------------|---------------------|
| 0       | 0        | 64.1±2.3f           | 41.0±1.8e           |
| 200     | 10       | 72.3±2.8d           | 45.2±2.1d           |
| 200     | 20       | 76.8±3.1c           | 48.6±2.3c           |
| 200     | 30       | 75.4±2.6cd          | 47.9±2.0cd          |
| 400     | 10       | 80.2±3.4b           | 50.3±2.5b           |
| 400     | 20       | 86.4±3.7a           | 52.7±2.8a           |
| 400     | 30       | 83.1±3.2b           | 51.4±2.6ab          |
| 600     | 20       | 78.5±3.0c           | 49.1±2.4c           |

Note: Different lowercase letters in the same column indicate significant differences (P<0.05), the same below.

 3.2 Effects of Ultrasonic Treatment on the Content of Soluble Sugars in Apple Juice

The soluble sugars in apple juice mainly consist of fructose, glucose, and sucrose. After ultrasonic treatment, the contents of all three sugars increased to varying degrees (Table 2). At 400 W for 20 min, the total sugar content reached a maximum value (112.6 g/L), which was 18.7% higher than that of the control group (94.8 g/L). Among these, fructose showed the largest increase (21.3%), followed by glucose (17.6%) and sucrose (14.2%).

Table 2 Effects of Ultrasonic Treatment on Soluble Sugar Content of Apple Juice (g/L)

| Treatment Condition | Fructose | Glucose | Sucrose | Total Sugar |
|---------|------|--------|------|------|
| Control | 52.3±2.1e | 28.6±1.4e | 13.9±0.8e | 94.8±4.2e |
| 400W/20min | 63.4±2.8a | 33.6±1.7a | 15.9±0.9a | 112.6±5.1a |
| 600W/20min | 58.7±2.5b | 31.2±1.5b | 14.8±0.8b | 104.7±4.6b |

 3.3 Effects of Ultrasonic Treatment on the Content of Carotenoids in Apple Juice

Ultrasonic treatment significantly increased the carotenoid content in apple juice (P<0.05). At 400 W for 20 min, the carotenoid content reached the highest value (186.3 μg/100 mL), which was 42.6% higher than that of the control group (130.7 μg/100 mL). At the same power, the carotenoid content showed a trend of first increasing and then decreasing with prolonged treatment time, with 20 min being the optimal treatment time.

 3.4 Effects of Ultrasonic Treatment on the Content of Mineral Elements in Apple Juice

The effects of ultrasonic treatment on the contents of K, Ca, Mg, Fe, Zn, Cu, Mn, and other mineral elements in apple juice are shown in Table 3. Compared with the control group, the contents of all mineral elements were significantly increased after ultrasonic treatment (P<0.05). Under the condition of 400 W for 20 min, the contents of K, Ca, Mg, Fe, and Zn increased by 21.3%, 26.7%, 19.5%, 31.2%, and 24.6%, respectively, compared with the control group. The increases in Cu and Mn contents were relatively smaller, at 12.4% and 15.8%, respectively.

Table 3 Effects of Ultrasonic Treatment (400W/20min) on Mineral Element Contents of Apple Juice (mg/L)

| Element | Control | Ultrasonic Treatment | Increase (%) |
|------|------|---------|---------|
| K | 986.4±32.5 | 1196.5±38.7 | 21.3 |
| Ca | 56.8±2.4 | 72.0±3.1 | 26.7 |
| Mg | 48.3±2.1 | 57.7±2.6 | 19.5 |
| Fe | 1.28±0.08 | 1.68±0.11 | 31.2 |
| Zn | 0.61±0.04 | 0.76±0.05 | 24.6 |
| Cu | 0.105±0.008 | 0.118±0.009 | 12.4 |
| Mn | 0.152±0.011 | 0.176±0.013 | 15.8 |

 4 Discussion

The results of this study indicate that ultrasonic treatment under appropriate conditions can significantly increase the contents of polyphenols, soluble sugars, carotenoids, and mineral elements in apple juice. The enhancement effect of ultrasonic treatment is mainly attributed to the mechanical force and microjet action generated by its cavitation effect. The localized high temperature and high pressure generated at the moment of cavitation bubble collapse can disrupt plant cell wall and cell membrane structures, promoting the release of bound bioactive substances from cells (Chemat et al., 2017).

Polyphenols in apples mainly exist in bound forms combined with cell wall polysaccharides and proteins. Ultrasonic treatment promotes the release of bound phenolic substances by disrupting cellulose and hemicellulose structures in cell walls, thereby increasing the free polyphenol content (Vilkhu et al., 2008). In this study, the total phenolic content showed the greatest increase at 400 W for 20 min, but decreased at 600 W, which may be related to the oxidative degradation of some phenolic substances caused by excessively high power.

The increase in soluble sugar content may be related to the promotion of polysaccharide hydrolysis by ultrasonic treatment. The shear force generated by ultrasonic cavitation can break glycosidic bonds, releasing some bound sugars into free forms, while also promoting the hydrolysis of polysaccharides such as starch (Zhu et al., 2021). The increase in carotenoid content may be related to the disruption of pigment-protein complexes by ultrasonic treatment, promoting the release of carotenoids from the cell matrix.

The increase in mineral element content may originate from two aspects: first, ultrasonic treatment disrupts cell structures, releasing mineral elements bound to organic acids, proteins, etc., into free forms; second, the cavitation effect enhances solvent permeability, improving the dissolution rate of mineral elements (Khan et al., 2018). The significant increases in macroelements such as K, Ca, and Mg may be related to their existence in cells in ionic or easily dissociable forms.

It is worth noting that the effect of ultrasonic treatment is closely related to power and time. Too low power or too short time is insufficient to fully disrupt cell structures; while too high power or too long time may lead to degradation of heat-sensitive components or generation of free radicals that trigger oxidation reactions. In this study, 400 W and 20 min were the optimal treatment conditions, basically consistent with previous research results in other fruit and vegetable juices (Deng et al., 2020).

 5 Conclusion

This study systematically investigated the effects of ultrasonic treatment on the contents of polyphenols, soluble sugars, carotenoids, and mineral elements in apple juice. The main conclusions are as follows:

(1) Ultrasonic treatment can significantly increase the total phenolic and total flavonoid contents in apple juice. At 400 W for 20 min, the total phenolic and total flavonoid contents increased by 34.8% and 28.4%, respectively, compared with the control group.

(2) Ultrasonic treatment significantly increased the contents of fructose, glucose, and sucrose in apple juice, with the maximum increase in total sugar content reaching 18.7%.

(3) Ultrasonic treatment increased the carotenoid content by 15.3%–42.6%, with the best effect under the condition of 400 W/20 min.

(4) Ultrasonic treatment significantly increased the contents of K, Ca, Mg, Fe, Zn, and other mineral elements, with increases ranging from 8.4% to 31.2%.

(5) Considering all indicators comprehensively, ultrasonic treatment at 400 W for 20 min is the optimal process condition for improving the nutritional quality of apple juice.

The results of this study provide a theoretical basis for the industrial application of ultrasonic technology in apple juice processing, but the effects of ultrasonic treatment on flavor compounds and storage stability of apple juice still require further research.
